title: The Egg and the Earth
text:
On the first afternoon of the geography club, our new teacher, Ms. Lin, walked in carrying a boiled egg, a small {{magnet}}, and a {{plate}} piled with stones. "Today," she announced, "you are going to hold the Earth in your hands."

She tapped the egg gently against the plate. "This thin shell is the {{crust}} — the hard surface we all live on. Beneath it lies the {{mantle}}, a layer of hot, slowly moving rock, and here, in the centre, sits the {{core}}, as dense and firm as this yolk." We laughed, but everyone leaned forward for a closer look.

"And wrapped around everything," she went on, waving her hand through the air, "is the {{atmosphere}}, a thin blanket of gases. Without it, there would be no air to breathe and no {{oxygen}} for creatures like us."

"But what is most of the Earth made of?" Leo asked.

"Good question. Water — the {{hydrosphere}} — covers most of the surface, while the solid, rocky shell beneath it is the {{lithosphere}}." She rolled the egg slowly across the plate. "And water itself is nothing but two gases holding hands: {{hydrogen}} and {{oxygen}}."

"Then why do rocks all look so different?" I asked, pointing at her collection.

"Because they truly are different." She picked up a grey stone. "This one is {{granite}} — you can see the fine grains in it. The white block is {{marble}}, and the shiny crystal is {{quartz}}." Then she held up a tiny round stone. "And this little fellow is a {{pebble}}, polished smooth by water over thousands of years."

She passed the {{magnet}} over the stones, and one jumped up to meet it. "Every rock is a mixture of {{mineral|minerals}}," she explained, "and when a mineral holds enough metal to be worth digging out, we call it an {{ore}}."

"Like iron?" said Leo.

"Exactly. And when iron meets the {{oxygen}} in the air, it slowly changes into an {{oxide}} — that reddish rust you see on old bicycles."

"Before you go," she said at the door, "remember this: every year we burn huge amounts of coal and oil, adding a {{gas}} called {{carbon dioxide}} to the atmosphere. That is why {{geology}} — the science of the Earth — matters more than ever. The planet in your hands is the only one you will ever get."

We walked out feeling that we had just made a new friend: the Earth itself.
tr:
地理社团第一次活动的下午，新老师林老师走了进来，手里拿着一个煮鸡蛋、一块小磁铁（magnet），还有一个堆满石头的盘子（plate）。“今天，”她宣布，“你们要把地球捧在手心里。”

她把鸡蛋在盘子上轻轻一敲。“这层薄薄的壳就是地壳（crust）——我们所有人生活的坚硬表面。它的下面是地幔（mantle），一层炽热、缓慢流动的岩石，而正中心坐落着地核（core），像这个蛋黄一样致密结实。”我们笑了，但每个人都凑近想看个清楚。

“而包裹着这一切的，”她挥了挥手，继续说，“是大气（atmosphere），一层薄薄的气体毯子。没有它，就没有可呼吸的空气，也没有供我们这类生物呼吸的氧气（oxygen）。”

“可是地球主要是由什么构成的呢？”利奥问。

“问得好。水——也就是水圈（hydrosphere）——覆盖了大部分地表，而它下面坚硬的岩石外壳叫岩石圈（lithosphere）。”她让鸡蛋在盘子里慢慢滚过。“而水本身不过是两种气体手拉着手：氢（hydrogen）和氧（oxygen）。”

“那为什么岩石长得各不相同呢？”我指着她的收藏问。

“因为它们本来就不同。”她拿起一块灰色的石头。“这是花岗岩（granite）——你能看见里面细密的颗粒。那块白色的是大理石（marble），那块亮晶晶的晶体是石英（quartz）。”然后她举起一颗小小的圆石。“而这小家伙是一颗鹅卵石（pebble），被水流打磨了几千年才变得这么光滑。”

她把磁铁（magnet）从石头上方掠过，一块石头跳起来迎向它。“每块岩石都是矿物（mineral）的混合体，”她解释说，“当某种矿物（mineral）所含的金属多到值得挖出来时，我们就把它叫做矿石（ore）。”

“像铁那样？”利奥说。

“正是。而当铁遇到空气中的氧气（oxygen），它会慢慢变成一种氧化物（oxide）——就是你在旧自行车上看到的那种红色锈迹。”

“走之前，”她在门口说，“记住这个：每年我们都燃烧掉巨量的煤和石油，往大气里添加一种叫做二氧化碳（carbon dioxide）的气体（gas）。这就是为什么地质学（geology）——研究地球的科学——比以往任何时候都重要。你们手里的这颗星球，是你们唯一能拥有的一颗。”

走出教室时，我们都觉得自己刚刚交了一位新朋友：地球本身。

quiz.q: In the story, Ms. Lin compares the shell of the egg to the Earth's crust. The crust is —
o: the hard outer layer of the Earth
the hot liquid metal in the Earth's centre
the blanket of air around the Earth
the deepest part of the ocean floor
quiz.ex: crust 本义是"硬外皮"（如面包皮），地质学中指地球最外层的"地壳"。故事里林老师用鸡蛋作比喻：蛋壳 = 地壳（crust），蛋白 = 地幔（mantle），蛋黄 = 地核（core）。搭配：the Earth's crust 地壳；a thin crust of ice 一层薄冰。

quiz.q: According to Ms. Lin, the mantle lies —
o: between the crust and the core
quiz.ex: mantle 指"地幔"，位于地壳与地核之间，是炽热、缓慢流动的岩层。它另一个常见意思是"披风、覆盖物"（the mantle of night 夜幕）。记忆：地幔像给地球裹上了一层厚披风。

quiz.q: In this story, the atmosphere is best described as —
o: the solid rock under our feet
all the water on the Earth's surface
a thin blanket of gases surrounding the Earth
quiz.ex: atmosphere = 大气（层）。它也是雅思高频的引申义"气氛、氛围"：a friendly atmosphere 友好的气氛、the atmosphere of the meeting 会议气氛。故事中"毯子（blanket）的比喻"正是它最核心的意象：thin but essential。

quiz.q: The hydrosphere refers to —
o: all the gases in the air
the layer of rock beneath our feet
all the water on the Earth
quiz.ex: hydrosphere 由 hydro-（水）+ sphere（圈层）构成，指地球的"水圈"——海洋、河流、冰川等一切水体的总称。同族词对照记忆：atmo-（空气）→ atmosphere 大气圈；hydro-（水）→ hydrosphere 水圈；litho-（石）→ lithosphere 岩石圈。-sphere 系列是雅思地理话题的常客。

quiz.q: In the story, the tiny round stone is called a pebble because it —
o: was polished smooth by water over long ages
can be attracted by a magnet
quiz.ex: pebble 指"鹅卵石、小圆石"，强调被水流长期冲刷而变得小而圆滑。近义辨析：stone 泛指石头；rock 指成块的岩石；pebble 特指小巧光滑的卵石。搭配：a pebble beach 卵石滩、pebbles on a riverbed 河床上的卵石。

quiz.q: When is a mineral called an ore?
o: When it holds enough metal to be worth mining
When it is found near a volcano
quiz.ex: ore = 矿石，指金属含量高、值得开采的岩石。注意 mineral 与 ore 的层级关系：所有岩石都由矿物（mineral）组成，但只有富含金属、值得开采的才升级叫 ore。搭配：iron ore 铁矿石、ore mining 采矿。

quiz.q: According to the story, the reddish rust on old bicycles is an example of —
o: an oxide formed when iron meets oxygen
quiz.ex: oxide = 氧化物，即某元素与氧结合生成的化合物。铁生锈（rust）本质就是铁的氧化物（iron oxide）。构词联想：oxide → oxidize（v. 氧化）→ oxidation（n. 氧化）；carbon dioxide（二氧化碳）中的 dioxide = "两个氧"。

quiz.q: The lithosphere is —
o: the solid, rocky outer shell of the Earth
the gaseous envelope of the Earth
the hot core of the planet
quiz.ex: litho- 来自希腊语"石头"，加 sphere（圈层）构成"岩石圈"，指地球固态的岩石外壳。三个圈层一起记：atmosphere 大气圈、hydrosphere 水圈、lithosphere 岩石圈——雅思阅读地理类文章的标配三兄弟。

title: Night on the Mountain of Fire
text:
My aunt Mei watches {{volcano|volcanoes}} for a living. Last August, she took me to spend a night with her research team on the slopes of Mount Etna in Sicily. "The mountain has been restless all week," she warned me on the drive up. "Our {{seismic}} sensors have recorded more than three hundred small {{earthquake|earthquakes}} since Monday."

I felt my knees {{tremble}} slightly at the news, but her calm voice made me feel safer somehow.

We reached the camp just before dark. The ground was covered with black rock from older eruptions, and thin rivers of steam rose into the cold {{atmosphere}}. Around ten o'clock, the instruments began to chatter. "Something is moving under the {{crust}}," said one of the researchers, staring at the screen. "Magma is climbing."

At midnight, the mountain finally began to {{erupt}}. Far above us, a fountain of glowing orange {{magma}} burst from a {{crack}} near the summit. Light {{emerge|emerged}} from the crack like a door opening onto a furnace. Sparks and hot stones shot into the sky, then fell back as grey {{debris}} on the upper slopes. Part of the crater wall gave way, and a small {{avalanche}} of loose rock and ash slid down towards a valley where nobody lived. Nobody spoke; we simply stood there, watching, while the cameras recorded everything.

"What actually pushes the magma up?" I finally whispered.

"Heat and pressure," said my aunt. "Call it a {{thermodynamic}} problem if you like — the same physics that makes the lid dance on a pot of boiling soup. The Earth is a pot, and tonight we are watching its lid."

At dawn we drove down through villages dusted with grey {{sediment}}. Fine {{silt}} had settled on the rooftops and on the leaves of the lemon trees, like strange grey snow. "Is all this dangerous?" I asked.

"Not this kind," she said. "But when heavy rain mixes with fresh ash, the flowing mud can {{endanger}} whole villages downstream. That is why we stay and measure the {{intensity}} of every tremor. A warning only works if someone is awake to send it."

I looked back at the quiet, smoking mountain and understood, for the first time, why my aunt had chosen to spend her life on its dangerous slopes.
tr:
我的梅阿姨以观察火山（volcano）为业。去年八月，她带我上了西西里岛埃特纳火山的山坡，和她的研究团队一起过夜。“这座山整个星期都不安分，”上山路上她提醒我，“我们的地震（seismic）传感器从周一起已经记录了三百多次小地震（earthquake）。”

听到这个消息，我的膝盖微微发颤（tremble），但她平静的声音不知怎么让我安下心来。

天黑前我们抵达营地。地面覆盖着早期喷发留下的黑色岩石，几缕细细的蒸汽升入寒冷的大气（atmosphere）。十点左右，仪器开始咔嗒作响。“地壳（crust）下面有东西在移动，”一位研究员盯着屏幕说，“岩浆正在上升。”

午夜时分，大山终于开始喷发（erupt）。远在我们上方，一股亮橙色的岩浆（magma）从山顶附近的一道裂缝（crack）中喷涌而出。光从裂缝里涌现（emerge）出来，像一扇通往熔炉的门被打开了。火星和滚烫的石头射向天空，又化作灰色的碎屑（debris）落回上方的山坡。一部分火山口壁坍塌了，一小场由松散岩石和火山灰组成的雪崩（avalanche）滑向一座无人居住的山谷。没有人说话，我们只是站在那里注视着，摄像机记录下一切。

“到底是什么把岩浆推上来的？”我终于小声问。

“热量和压力，”阿姨说，“你要是愿意，可以把它叫作一个热力学（thermodynamic）问题——和让一锅沸水把锅盖顶得直跳的是同一种物理。地球就是一口锅，今晚我们正在看它的锅盖。”

黎明时分，我们驱车穿过蒙着灰色沉积物（sediment）的村庄。细密的淤泥（silt）落在屋顶上和柠檬树的叶子上，像一场奇怪的黑雪。“这些都很危险吗？”我问。

“这一种不危险，”她说，“但暴雨遇上新鲜的火山灰时，流动的泥浆可能危及（endanger）下游的整座村庄。所以我们留在这里，测量每一次震动的强度（intensity）。预警只有在有人清醒着把它发出去时才有用。”

我回头望向那座安静冒烟的大山，第一次明白了阿姨为什么选择在它危险的山坡上度过一生。

quiz.q: In the story, "the mountain finally began to erupt" means the volcano —
o: made a soft noise and fell silent
burst out with magma and ash
quiz.ex: erupt 指火山"喷发"，也常用于战争、暴力、情绪的"爆发"：Violence erupted in the city.（城市里爆发了暴力冲突。）名词形式是 eruption（volcanic eruption 火山喷发）。辨析：erupt 强调物质从内部喷涌而出；explode 泛指爆炸。

quiz.q: In this story, magma refers to —
o: the grey ash that falls on rooftops
molten rock beneath the Earth's surface
quiz.ex: magma = 岩浆，指地壳之下处于熔融状态的岩石物质。雅思地质类阅读的经典区分：magma 是"地下"的岩浆；一旦喷出地表，习惯改称 lava（熔岩）。故事中"heat and pressure pushes it up"正是 magma 的定义性特征。

quiz.q: The seismic sensors in the story are instruments that —
o: detect movements and vibrations in the ground
record the direction of the wind
test the quality of drinking water
quiz.ex: seismic 来自希腊语 seismos（地震），意为"地震的、与地震有关的"。高频搭配：seismic waves 地震波、seismic activity 地震活动、seismic zone 地震带。地质与工程类话题的常客形容词。

quiz.q: In the story, sparks and hot stones fell back as debris. Debris means —
o: pieces of broken rock and scattered material
new plants growing on the slope
quiz.ex: debris 指"碎片、残骸、散落的碎屑"。注意发音：最后的 s 不发音，读 /dəˈbriː/。搭配：volcanic debris 火山碎屑、debris from the plane crash 坠机残骸、clear the debris 清理瓦砾。

quiz.q: In the story, the small avalanche was a —
o: sudden slide of snow, rock or earth down a slope
quiz.ex: avalanche 最常见的意思是"雪崩"，也可指岩石、泥沙沿山坡崩落，故事中即火山碎屑的滑落。它还有个生动的引申义"纷至沓来"：an avalanche of emails 铺天盖地而来的邮件。发音注意：第二个 a 发 /ə/。

quiz.q: Fine silt had settled on the rooftops. Silt is —
o: fine particles of earth or sand carried by water or wind
quiz.ex: silt = 淤泥、泥沙，指被水流或风力搬运的细颗粒泥土，常沉积在河床与河口——三角洲（delta）正是 silt 长年堆积的产物。与 sediment（沉积物）是近亲：silt 是 sediment 中颗粒最细的一类。

quiz.q: "I felt my knees tremble slightly." To tremble is to —
o: shake slightly because of fear, cold or strong feeling
quiz.ex: tremble 指因恐惧、寒冷或激动而"发抖、打颤"，故事中"knees tremble"是紧张的经典写照。近义辨析：tremble 泛指微微发抖；shiver 专指冷得哆嗦；shake 最通用（shake hands 握手 / shake with fear 吓得发抖）。

quiz.q: In the last paragraph, the team measures the intensity of every tremor. Intensity means —
o: the strength or force of something
quiz.ex: intensity = 强度、剧烈程度。搭配：the intensity of the light 光的强度、high-intensity training 高强度训练、the intensity of the storm 风暴的猛烈程度。同族词：intensive（adj. 密集的、强化的）——intensive reading 精读。

title: A Week at the Weather Station
text:
For my work-experience week, our school sent me to the local weather station. A cheerful {{meteorology|meteorologist}} named Mr. Rossi met me at the gate. "By Friday," he promised, "you will know how a {{forecast}} is really made."

"Lesson one," he began, handing me a notebook. "Never confuse {{weather}} with {{climate}}. Weather is what you get; climate is what you expect. One cold week proves nothing — climate is the average of a thousand weeks."

On Tuesday he showed me the instruments. The {{temperature}} at seven was a {{mild}} fourteen degrees {{celsius}} — gentle for late October. "Days like this are a gift," he said. "Wait for January, and the same field will be frozen white." By noon, in the {{warm}} afternoon sunshine, we were checking the soil sensors.

Wednesday was forecast day. Mr. Rossi studied three screens at once, drawing lines with a pencil like an artist. "A {{moderate}} wind from the southwest tomorrow," he murmured, "cloudy but dry, with a chance of light {{shower|showers}} near the coast. If the {{condition|conditions}} hold, Saturday will be perfect for the football final."

On Thursday we launched the weather balloon at five in the morning. I was glad of my {{thermal}} underwear — the field was silver with {{frost}}, and my breath hung in the air like smoke. Back in the office, the old {{heating}} rattled and hummed while the data poured in.

"Is the weather the same everywhere?" I asked, rubbing my cold hands.

"Not at all," he laughed. "In the {{tropics}}, it pours almost every afternoon at four o'clock, regular as a clock. Here, we take whatever the sky decides to give us. That is why every place needs its own forecast."

On Friday, Mr. Rossi checked Saturday's predictions against the real sky. "A moderate southwest wind, light showers near the coast — and look, that is exactly what arrived." He seemed as pleased as if he had painted the weather himself.

"One last thing before you go," he said, tapping a chart where the line of world {{temperature|temperatures}} has been climbing for decades. "We keep adding {{carbon dioxide}} to the air, and the {{climate}} is slowly answering back. Mark my words — the people who will fix that problem are sitting in school right now. Perhaps in your classroom."
tr:
学校把我的职业体验周安排在了本地气象站。一位开朗的气象学家（meteorology→meteorologist）罗西先生在大门口迎接我。“到星期五，”他许诺，“你就会知道天气预报（forecast）到底是怎么做出来的。”

“第一课，”他递给我一个笔记本，开口说道，“永远别把天气（weather）和气候（climate）弄混。天气是你眼前得到的；气候是你长期预期的。一个寒冷的星期什么都证明不了——气候是一千个星期的平均。”

星期二，他带我认识各种仪器。七点钟的气温（temperature）是温和（mild）的十四摄氏度（celsius）——对十月底来说十分宜人。“这样的日子是礼物，”他说，“等到一月，同一片田野就会冻成白色。”到了中午，在温暖（warm）的午后阳光里，我们检查了土壤传感器。

星期三是预报日。罗西先生同时研究着三块屏幕，像画家一样用铅笔画线。“明天有一股和缓（moderate）的西南风，”他低声说，“多云但干燥，沿海地区可能有零星小阵雨（shower）。如果天气条件（condition）保持稳定，周六将是足球决赛的完美天气。”

星期四凌晨五点，我们放飞了探空气球。我很庆幸自己穿了保暖（thermal）内衣——田野被霜（frost）染成了银白色，我的呼吸像烟一样悬在空气里。回到办公室，老旧的暖气（heating）一边咔嗒作响一边嗡嗡运转，数据不断涌入。

“各地的天气都一样吗？”我搓着冻僵的手问。

“完全不是，”他笑了，“在热带（tropics），几乎每天下午四点都下大雨，准得像时钟。在这里，我们只能接受天空的安排。所以每个地方都需要自己的预报。”

星期五，罗西先生把周六的预测和真实的天空做了核对。“和缓的西南风，沿海零星阵雨——你看，分毫不差。”他高兴得就像这天气是他亲手画出来的一样。

“走之前最后一件事，”他敲了敲一张图表，上面全球温度（temperature）的曲线几十年来一直在攀升，“我们不断往空气中排放二氧化碳（carbon dioxide），气候（climate）正在慢慢回应我们。记住我的话——将来解决这个问题的人，现在正坐在学校里。也许就在你们的教室里。”

quiz.q: Mr. Rossi works at a weather station as a meteorologist. Meteorology is the science of —
quiz.ex: meteorology = 气象学；从业者叫 meteorologist（气象学家）。词尾 -ology 表示"学科、研究"：geology 地质学、biology 生物学、psychology 心理学。气象报告可说 a meteorological report。

quiz.q: In the story, a forecast is —
o: a record of last year's weather
a strong wind from the southwest
a statement about what the weather will probably be like
quiz.ex: forecast 可作名词（预报、预测）和动词（预测）。构词：fore-（预先）+ cast（投放、播）。常见搭配：weather forecast 天气预报、forecast economic growth 预测经济增长。注意过去式 forecast 不双写：forecast – forecast – forecast。

quiz.q: According to Mr. Rossi, which sentence uses climate correctly?
o: The climate today is sunny with light showers.
The climate is the average weather of a place over many years.
One cold week proves that the climate is changing.
The climate at five o'clock was freezing cold.
quiz.ex: 本题专考 weather 与 climate 的辨析——雅思写作环境类话题的经典对比。weather（天气）是短期的、当日的状况；climate（气候）是长期（通常三十年）的平均状况。climate 还有引申义"风气、氛围"：the political climate 政治气候、a favourable climate for investment 有利的投资环境。

quiz.q: "A mild fourteen degrees — gentle for late October." Mild means —
quiz.ex: mild = 温和的、和缓的，用途极广：天气（a mild winter 暖冬）、味道（mild cheese 淡味奶酪）、性格（a mild man 性情温和的人）、病症（a mild fever 低烧）。反义词：severe、harsh、extreme。

quiz.q: In the story, a moderate wind is a wind that is —
o: neither strong nor weak, about average in strength
quiz.ex: moderate = 中等的、适度的（程度居中，不过分）。搭配：moderate exercise 适度锻炼、a moderate income 中等收入、moderate prices 适中的价格。辨析：mild 侧重"温和不刺激"，moderate 侧重"数量或程度居中"。moderate 还可作动词，意为"主持（会议、讨论）"。

quiz.q: Why was the writer glad of thermal underwear?
o: It protected him from the rain.
It keeps body heat in and keeps you warm.
quiz.ex: thermal = 热的、保暖的、与热相关的。高频搭配：thermal underwear 保暖内衣、thermal energy 热能、thermal springs 温泉、thermal power station 火力发电站。雅思能源类话题必会词。

quiz.q: In the tropics, according to Mr. Rossi, —
o: the temperature drops below zero at night
it rains heavily almost every afternoon
quiz.ex: the tropics 指南北回归线之间的"热带地区"，惯用复数并加 the。形容词是 tropical：a tropical climate 热带气候、tropical rainforest 热带雨林。环保与生态类话题的高频区域概念。

quiz.q: "If the conditions hold, Saturday will be perfect." Here, conditions refers to —
o: the rules of the football game
the state of the weather at a given time
quiz.ex: conditions（复数）指"（天气、生活等的）状况、条件"：weather conditions 天气状况、living conditions 生活条件、road conditions 路况。condition 不可数时指"状态、状况"：in good condition 状态良好。雅思听力机场、航班场景中 weather conditions 出镜率极高。

title: The Storm Chasers
text:
Every spring, Dr. Patel and her students drive out onto the wide plains of the American Midwest to meet {{stormy}} weather face to face. Last May, I was allowed to join them for a single day. "We don't chase danger," she told me before we set off. "We chase understanding. And today, the {{forecast}} says, understanding will arrive with a storm."

The morning began calmly enough, with a soft {{breeze}} moving the grass and white clouds {{puff}}ing up like cotton. By eleven, however, the wind had begun to {{blow}} harder. A sudden {{gust}} rocked the van, and dust ran across the road like a living thing. "She is building," said Dr. Patel quietly, watching the sky darken in the west.

We parked on a hill at a safe distance and watched the clouds spin. The {{temperature}} dropped five degrees in ten minutes. Rain began as a light {{sprinkle}}, then thickened into a {{downpour}} so heavy that the fields disappeared. {{Thunder}} rolled overhead like furniture being dragged across the floor of the sky, and every {{flash}} of {{lightning}} turned the whole world white for a second.

"Is that a — is that a tornado?" I asked, pointing at a dark finger of cloud touching the ground far away.

"It is," said Dr. Patel, her eyes bright. "A small one, luckily. We measure them — wind speed, air pressure, total {{rainfall}} — so that the people in their path can be warned in time."

On the drive back, the sky washed itself clean. One heavy {{shower}} chased us for a mile, then gave up, and a huge {{rainbow}} stood over the wet fields like a painted bridge.

That evening, over soup, the team argued happily about storms around the world. "Same engine, different names," said one student. "In the Atlantic they call it a {{hurricane}}; in the western Pacific, a {{typhoon}}; and the {{monsoon}} rains of Asia are its gentler cousin. In the old days, sailors called any wild sea wind a {{gale}} and feared it like a wolf."

"And here on the plains," said Dr. Patel, "we see more {{tornado|tornadoes}} than anywhere else on Earth. Tomorrow, if the sky is willing, we will go out and meet another one." I laughed — and then noticed that I was already hoping the sky would be willing.
tr:
每年春天，帕特尔博士和她的学生们都会驱车进入美国中西部的广阔平原，与暴风雨（stormy）天气面对面。去年五月，我获准跟了他们一整天。“我们追逐的不是危险，”出发前她对我说，“我们追逐的是理解。而今天，天气预报（forecast）说，理解会随一场风暴一起到来。”

清晨还算平静，微风（breeze）吹动着草地，白云像棉花一样一团团地鼓（puff）起来。然而到了十一点，风开始越刮（blow）越猛。一阵狂风（gust）摇撼着面包车，尘土像活物一样窜过路面。“它在积聚力量，”帕特尔博士望着西边渐渐变暗的天空，轻声说。

我们在一座小山上、隔着安全的距离停好车，看着云团旋转。十分钟内，气温（temperature）骤降了五度。雨起先只是一阵细细的小雨（sprinkle），随后加粗成一场倾盆大雨（downpour），密得连田野都消失不见了。雷声（thunder）在头顶滚动，像有人在天国的地板上拖动家具，每一次闪电（lightning）的闪光（flash）都让整个世界白上一秒钟。

“那是一——那是龙卷风吗？”我指着远处一根触到地面的黑色云柱问。

“是的，”帕特尔博士眼睛发亮，“小型的，万幸。我们测量它们——风速、气压、总降雨量（rainfall）——好让处于它们路径上的人能及时得到警报。”

返程路上，天空把自己洗刷干净。一阵大雨（shower）追了我们一英里，然后放弃了，一道巨大的彩虹（rainbow）像一座画出来的桥，立在湿润的田野上空。

那天晚上喝汤时，团队开心地争论着世界各地的风暴。“同一台发动机，不同的名字，”一个学生说，“在大西洋人们叫它飓风（hurricane）；在西太平洋叫台风（typhoon）；亚洲的季风（monsoon）雨是它温和些的表亲。旧时的水手把任何狂暴的海风都叫作大风（gale），怕它像怕狼一样。”

“而在我们这片平原上，”帕特尔博士说，“我们见到的龙卷风（tornado）比地球上任何地方都多。明天，要是天空愿意，我们就再去会一会下一个。”我笑了——随即发现自己已经在盼着天空愿意了。

quiz.q: In the story, a soft breeze moved the grass. A breeze is —
o: a very strong and dangerous wind
a flash of light in the sky
quiz.ex: breeze = 微风、和风。风力从小到大排队：breeze（微风）< gust（阵风）< gale（大风）< storm（风暴）< hurricane（飓风）。搭配：a sea breeze 海风、a light breeze 一缕微风。习语 shoot the breeze = 闲聊。

quiz.q: A sudden gust rocked the van. A gust is —
o: a long period of steady rain
a short, sudden, strong rush of wind
quiz.ex: gust = 一阵狂风、阵风，强调突然而猛烈，但持续时间短。天气预报常用：gusts of up to 100 km/h 阵风时速高达 100 公里。注意与 gale 的区别：gust 是"一阵"，gale 是"持续的大风"。

quiz.q: The sprinkle thickened into a downpour. A downpour is —
o: a very heavy fall of rain
a gentle wind from the sea
quiz.ex: downpour = 倾盆大雨。故事里雨的强度递进堪称教科书：sprinkle（零星小雨）→ shower（一阵雨）→ downpour（倾盆大雨）。搭配：be caught in a downpour 被一场大雨淋了。同义表达 torrential rain。

quiz.q: Thunder rolled overhead like furniture being dragged across the floor of the sky. Thunder is —
o: the loud noise that follows a flash of lightning
quiz.ex: thunder = 雷、雷声，也可作动词表示"轰鸣、打雷"。固定搭配 thunder and lightning 电闪雷鸣。习语 steal someone's thunder = 抢某人的风头。形容词 thunderous 雷鸣般的。

quiz.q: Every flash of lightning turned the world white. Lightning is —
o: the rumbling sound a storm makes
a sudden bright flash of electricity in the sky during a storm
quiz.ex: lightning = 闪电，通常作不可数名词，"一道闪电"说 a flash/bolt of lightning。别与 lighting（照明、灯光）混淆——只差一个字母，雅思听力陷阱常客。形容词用法：lightning-fast 闪电般迅速的。

quiz.q: The dark finger of cloud touching the ground was —
o: a hurricane forming over warm oceans
a tornado — a violently spinning column of air
quiz.ex: tornado = 龙卷风，从云底延伸至地面的高速旋转气柱，常见于美国中西部平原。辨析：hurricane（大西洋）/ typhoon（西太平洋）生成于海上、规模达数百公里；tornado 通常只有几十至几百米宽，但风速更快。搭配：tornado warning 龙卷风警报。

quiz.q: In the Atlantic they call it a hurricane. A hurricane is —
o: a seasonal wind that brings rain to Asia
a small spinning wind found on plains
a huge storm that forms over warm oceans with violent winds
quiz.ex: hurricane = 飓风（大西洋生成）。同一个现象在西北太平洋叫 typhoon（台风），在印度洋叫 cyclone（气旋）——"same engine, different names"，雅思阅读天气类文章爱考这个知识点。搭配：hurricane season 飓风季。

quiz.q: Sailors feared the gale like a wolf. A gale is —
quiz.ex: gale = 大风（气象学上指 8—9 级风），强调持续而猛烈的海风。搭配：gale-force winds 疾风／大风力。近义阶梯记忆：breeze < gust < gale < storm。

title: The Morning the Wave Came
text:
I grew up in a small town on the coast of Chile, where the {{ocean}} is part of every family. My uncle Tomás works in the town's {{disaster}}-prevention office, which mostly means organising drills and checking sirens.

One March morning, just after six, every phone in town began to scream. An undersea {{earthquake}} had struck two hundred kilometres away, and the national warning system said a {{tsunami}} was possible within the hour.

Uncle Tomás was already in the street, waving people up the hill. "Forget your cars!" he shouted. "Walk! Ten minutes up, and you can watch the sea from safety!" Nobody panicked; we had practised that walk twice a year since primary school, so the {{situation}}, though serious, stayed under control. A few tourists, however, tried to drive down to the beach to film the wave. He blocked the road and refused to move. "You would {{jeopardise}} your own lives — and the lives of the people who would have to rescue you — for a video that nobody needs."

From the hill we watched the sea pull back, breathe, and return as a {{torrent}} of dark water that climbed the streets, lifted cars like toys and pushed fishing boats into gardens. It was the most {{destructive}} thing I had ever seen. Yet nobody in our town died that morning. In 1960, before warnings existed, hundreds of people {{drown}}ed in these same streets.

That evening the president called it a national {{calamity}}, and the newspapers wrote about {{catastrophic}} damage. Uncle Tomás shook his head slowly. "People spend their big words too easily," he said. "A {{mishap}} is when you drop your phone in the soup. A disaster is when the sea comes to visit. Both are bad days, but they are not the same animal. A wave destroys what it destroys — the sirens and the drills decide how much."

Over the following weeks I learned how everything on Earth is connected. That year, {{El Nino}} — a warming of the Pacific that appears every few years — had brought {{abnormal}} weather to half the planet: {{drought}} in some countries, sudden {{flooding}} in others. Scientists explained that the {{greenhouse}} effect, growing stronger year by year, was making such wild {{phenomenon|phenomena}} more likely, and that the situation in coastal towns like ours would keep getting harder to manage.

I asked Uncle Tomás whether another wave was {{inevitable}} — whether it would surely come again.

"The wave, yes," he said. "The deaths, no. That part is up to us."
tr:
我在智利一座海滨小镇长大，在那里，海洋（ocean）是每个家庭的一部分。我的叔叔托马斯在镇上的灾害（disaster）预防办公室工作，工作内容主要就是组织演练、检查警报器。

三月的一个清晨，刚过六点，镇上所有的手机都开始尖叫。一场海底地震（earthquake）在两百公里外发生了，国家预警系统说，一小时内可能出现海啸（tsunami）。

托马斯叔叔已经站在街上，挥着手让大家上山。“别管你们的车了！”他喊道，“走上去！十分钟的脚程，你们就能在安全的地方看海了。”没有人惊慌——我们从小学起每年都演练两次这条撤离路线，所以情况（situation）虽然严重，却始终在掌控之中。然而几个游客却想开车下山去海滩拍海浪。他堵在路口，说什么也不让开。“你们这是在拿自己的性命冒险（jeopardise）——还搭上那些不得不去救你们的人的命——就为了一段谁都不需要的视频。”

从山上，我们看着海水先向后退去、深吸一口气，然后化作一股黑色的急流（torrent）折返，漫上街道，像拎玩具一样掀起汽车，把渔船推进花园。那是我见过的最具破坏性（destructive）的景象。但那天早上，镇上没有一个人遇难。而在 1960 年，还没有预警系统的年代，数百人就在这些街道上被淹死（drown）了。

当天晚上，总统称其为一场全国性的大灾祸（calamity），报纸上写满了灾难性（catastrophic）损失。托马斯叔叔缓缓摇头。“人们太随便地挥霍大词了，”他说，“小意外（mishap）是你把手机掉进汤里；灾难是大海来登门。两者都是倒霉的一天，但根本不是同一种动物。海浪摧毁它所摧毁的——而警报器和演练决定它摧毁多少。”

接下来的几个星期，我明白了地球上的一切是如何环环相扣的。那一年，厄尔尼诺现象（El Nino）——每隔几年出现一次的太平洋变暖——给半个地球带来了反常（abnormal）天气：一些国家遭遇干旱（drought），另一些国家突发洪水泛滥（flooding）。科学家们解释说，逐年增强的温室（greenhouse）效应正让这类狂野的现象（phenomenon）变得更常见，而像我们这样的海滨小镇，处境会越来越难。

我问托马斯叔叔，下一场巨浪是否不可避免（inevitable）——它是不是注定还会再来。

“巨浪，是的，”他说，“死亡，不是。那一部分，取决于我们自己。”

quiz.q: In the story, the undersea earthquake might cause a tsunami. A tsunami is —
o: a strong seasonal wind from the sea
a series of huge ocean waves caused by an undersea earthquake
quiz.ex: tsunami = 海啸，由海底地震、火山喷发引发的一系列巨浪。注意两点：①不是普通的风暴潮；②发音 /tsuːˈnɑːmi/，第一个 t 几乎不送气。雅思听力拼写在 Section 4 地质话题出现过。

quiz.q: Uncle Tomás stopped the tourists because they would jeopardise their lives. To jeopardise something is to —
o: put it in danger of being harmed or lost
quiz.ex: jeopardise = 危及、使处于危险中，是 endanger 的高级同义词，雅思阅读同义替换常客（endanger / jeopardise / put at risk / threaten 互换）。美式拼写 jeopardize。搭配：jeopardise one's career 危及职业生涯。

quiz.q: The sea returned as a torrent of dark water. A torrent is —
o: a violently rushing stream of water
a small earthquake under the ground
quiz.ex: torrent = 急流、激流（迅猛奔涌的水流）。高频衍生词 torrential rain = 倾盆大雨（相当于 downpour 的形容词版本）。引申用法：a torrent of abuse 连珠炮似的辱骂、a torrent of questions 一连串的提问。

quiz.q: "A mishap is when you drop your phone in the soup." A mishap is —
o: a small accident or piece of bad luck
quiz.ex: mishap = 小事故、小意外（轻微、可以一笑而过的那种）。程度阶梯：mishap（小意外）→ accident（事故）→ disaster（灾难）→ calamity / catastrophe（特大灾祸）。故事里叔叔用"手机掉进汤里"对比"大海登门"，正是这个词义梯度的最好注解。

quiz.q: El Nino brought abnormal weather: drought in some countries. A drought is —
o: a long period with little or no rain
quiz.ex: drought = 旱灾、干旱期。两个易错点：①发音 /draʊt/（中间没有 f 音）；②拼写别写成 draught（气流、一饮）。搭配：severe drought 严重干旱、drought-resistant crops 抗旱作物（雅思农业话题高频）、combat drought 抗旱。

quiz.q: The narrator asks whether another wave is inevitable. Inevitable means —
o: certain to happen and impossible to avoid
quiz.ex: inevitable = 不可避免的 = unavoidable / certain。故事中叔叔的名言区分了两件事：巨浪（inevitable）与死亡（not inevitable）——预防决定后果。雅思写作高频句型：It is inevitable that... / an inevitable consequence of modern life。副词 inevitably。

quiz.q: El Nino had brought abnormal weather. Abnormal means —
o: different from what is usual or expected
quiz.ex: abnormal = 反常的、不正常的。构词：ab-（偏离）+ normal（正常的）。反义词 normal。搭配：abnormal weather patterns 反常的天气模式、abnormal behaviour 异常行为。近义：unusual、irregular、uncommon。

quiz.q: In the story, the greenhouse effect makes wild phenomena more likely. The greenhouse effect refers to —
o: the pulling back of the sea before a wave
the natural cooling of the Pacific Ocean
gases in the air trapping heat and warming the planet
quiz.ex: greenhouse effect = 温室效应：二氧化碳等气体像温室的玻璃一样把热量困在大气层里。第一高频搭配 greenhouse gases（GHGs）温室气体（carbon dioxide、methane 甲烷等）。本义 greenhouse = 温室（种菜的玻璃暖房），所以 greenhouse effect 才叫"温室"效应。

title: The Road to the Oasis
text:
After graduation, my cousin Wei decided to spend a year teaching in a village so {{remote}} that the nearest city was a nine-hour drive away. Last spring I went to visit him. The final three hours of the journey ran along a {{dirt}} road through pure {{wilderness}} — no towns, no phone signal, only sand and stone as far as the eye could see.

The land was {{arid}} beyond anything I had imagined. For hour after hour we crossed {{sandy}} dunes and {{stony}} flats where nothing green survived. "It was not always like this," said the driver, an old man with a face like walnut bark. "When my grandfather was young, there were forests on those hills. Then people {{deforest|deforested}} the slopes for firewood and farmland, and the rain left with the trees. Eight years of {{drought}} finished the job. Without roots to hold it, the soil blew away, and the fields turned {{barren}}."

He looked out at the empty land. "{{Nature}} keeps the score," he said. "Cut the trees, and she sends the sand."

Then, in the late afternoon, we came over a low ridge — and I finally understood why travellers in old stories wept at the sight of an {{oasis}}. Green fields, tall poplar trees and a small lake lay in the middle of the dead land like a promise. Children were racing paper boats along the water's edge, and the air smelled of melons.

The fields around the village were astonishingly {{fertile}}. Every farming family {{fertilise|fertilised}} its soil carefully with sheep manure, and meltwater from the mountains arrived through channels older than the village itself. "Up on the hills, they planted trees to hold the sand," Wei explained. "Down here, the farmers practise {{intensive}} farming — every square metre is used, because every drop of water is precious."

At dusk we walked out to the edge of the fields, where the green simply stopped and the {{desolate}} land began again without apology. Wei saw my face and smiled. "The {{desert}} isn't evil," he said. "It is just patient. So are we."
tr:
毕业后，表哥韦决定去一个偏僻（remote）得连最近的城市都要开九个小时车才能到达的村庄支教一年。去年春天我去探望他。旅程的最后三个小时是一条穿过纯粹荒野（wilderness）的土路（dirt）——没有城镇，没有手机信号，只有一望无际的沙与石。

这片土地的干旱（arid）超出了我的全部想象。一个又一个小时，我们穿过沙质（sandy）的沙丘和多石（stony）的平地，那里没有任何绿色的生命能够存活。“这里从前不是这样的，”司机说——一位脸像核桃皮似的老人，“我爷爷年轻的时候，那些山丘上还有森林。后来人们为了柴火和农田把山坡上的树砍光了（deforest），雨水就跟着树一起走了。连续八年的干旱（drought）则完成了剩下的破坏。没有树根抓住土壤，土被风吹走，田地就变成了贫瘠的（barren）荒地。”

他望着窗外空旷的大地。“大自然（nature）是记账的，”他说，“你砍了树，她就派沙子来。”

随后，傍晚时分，我们翻过一道低矮的山脊——我终于明白了古老故事里的旅人为什么见到绿洲（oasis）会流泪。绿色的田野、高大的杨树和一面小小的湖泊躺在死寂大地的中央，像一个承诺。孩子们正在水边比赛放纸船，空气里飘着甜瓜的香味。

村庄周围的田地肥沃（fertile）得令人惊讶。每户农家都用羊粪仔细地给土壤施肥（fertilise），山上的融雪水顺着比村庄本身还古老的水渠流进田里。“山上，他们种树来固定流沙，”韦解释说，“山下，农民们实行集约（intensive）耕作——每一平方米都被利用，因为每一滴水都很珍贵。”

黄昏时我们走到田野尽头，绿色在那里戛然而止，荒凉（desolate）的土地毫无歉意地重新开始。韦看出了我的心思，笑了。“沙漠（desert）不邪恶，”他说，“它只是有耐心。我们也是。”

quiz.q: In the story, the green fields and the lake in the middle of the dead land were —
o: an oasis — fertile, watered land in a desert
a plateau high in the mountains
quiz.ex: oasis = 绿洲，沙漠中水源充足、草木丰美之地；复数形式 oases。引申义非常好用：a peaceful oasis in the heart of the busy city 忙碌都市中心的一片宁静绿洲。故事中"像承诺一样的绿"是它的经典意象。

quiz.q: The land was arid beyond anything I had imagined. Arid means —
o: extremely dry, with little rain or plant life
quiz.ex: arid = 干旱的、干燥贫瘠的，是描述沙漠气候的标准学术用词。搭配：arid land / arid regions 干旱地区、an arid climate 干旱气候。引申义：an arid discussion 枯燥乏味的讨论。雅思环境类阅读高频形容词。

quiz.q: Without roots to hold the soil, the fields turned barren. Barren means —
o: unable to produce plants or crops
quiz.ex: barren = 贫瘠的、不毛的。搭配：barren land 荒地、a barren hillside 光秃秃的山坡。近义 infertile；反义 fertile（肥沃的）。故事逻辑链：deforestation → drought → barren fields，正是雅思环境类写作的标准因果链。

quiz.q: The fields around the village were astonishingly fertile. Fertile means —
o: rich in nutrients and able to grow crops well
quiz.ex: fertile = 肥沃的、多产的。搭配：fertile soil 肥沃的土壤。两个高频引申：fertile ground for new ideas 新思想的沃土；a fertile imagination 丰富的想象力。名词 fertility（肥力、生育力），动词 fertilise（施肥），名词 fertiliser（肥料）——fertile 一词族在雅思农业话题中全家上阵。

quiz.q: People deforested the slopes for firewood and farmland. To deforest an area is to —
o: cut down the trees covering it
quiz.ex: deforest = 滥伐（某地的）森林。构词：de-（去除、降低）+ forest。名词 deforestation 是雅思环保话题超高频词：Deforestation destroys habitats and speeds up soil erosion.（森林砍伐破坏栖息地并加速水土流失。）同族对照：desertification 荒漠化。

quiz.q: Where the green stopped, the desolate land began again. Desolate means —
quiz.ex: desolate = 荒凉的、凄凉的（既形容地方空旷荒芜，也形容心境孤寂凄凉）：a desolate landscape 荒凉的景色；She felt utterly desolate after the news. 听到消息后她感到无比凄凉。近义 bleak。名词 desolation 荒芜、凄凉。

quiz.q: The farmers practise intensive farming. Intensive farming means —
o: letting fields rest unused for years
using every metre of land as productively as possible
quiz.ex: intensive = 密集的、集约的、强化的。经典对比：intensive farming 集约农业（小面积高投入）vs extensive farming 粗放农业（大面积低投入）；intensive reading 精读 vs extensive reading 泛读；intensive care（ICU）重症监护。这组反义词是雅思阅读农业类文章的常客。

quiz.q: The village was so remote that the nearest city was nine hours away. Remote means —
o: very close to a big city
far from other places and hard to reach
quiz.ex: remote = 偏远的、遥远的。搭配：remote areas / villages / regions 偏远地区；in the remote past 遥远的过去。还有一个生活化义项：remote control 遥控器（把控制信号"传到远处"）。近义 isolated、distant、out-of-the-way。

title: The Journey of a Raindrop
text:
I was born in the warm ocean on a bright afternoon, when the sun quietly {{evaporate|evaporated}} me into {{vapour}} and lifted me into the sky. As vapour I {{float}}ed high above the waves, too small and light to fall back.

The wind carried me for days. Water never rests: it rises, travels, cools and falls, then rises again — {{circulate|circulating}} around the planet like blood through a body. Old drops like to say that the {{atmosphere}} is simply a river that flows above our heads.

One cold night I settled on a mountain meadow — not as rain, but as {{dew}}, a silver coat on every blade of grass. By dawn the valley below had filled with a {{dense}} {{mist}}, and the air hung {{moist}} and {{damp}} around the pines. Later, drifting south, I felt the air grow warm and {{humid}} again — the breath of the {{tropics}}.

Then came the day when I grew too heavy to float. The cloud darkened, and I {{precipitate|precipitated}} — that is the grand word scientists use; you would simply say I fell as rain. It {{pour}}ed for an hour. I landed on a leaf, hung at its tip for a moment, then {{drip}}ped onto the road below.

In the city I slid along the gutter until a {{drain}} swallowed me. For a while I travelled in darkness under the streets. When I next saw the sky, I was flying out of a park {{fountain}}, and later I rose again from a mountain {{spring}}, where the water {{gush}}es cold and sweet from between the rocks.

The city air was not always kind. Some mornings a brown {{smog}} lay over the rooftops, thick with the {{fume}}s of a million cars, and I fell through it as grey rain, carrying its dirt on my back. Water forgives, but it also remembers.

After many turns through fountains and rivers, clouds and drains, I came at last to the sea again — the same warm ocean where I was born. Somewhere above me, the sun was already reaching down for the next drop. I did not mind. Falling, I had learned, is only the beginning of rising.
tr:
我出生在温暖的海水里，那是一个晴朗的下午，太阳悄悄把我蒸发（evaporate）成了水蒸气（vapour），托举上了天空。作为水汽，我漂浮（float）在海浪上空，小得、轻得落不回去。

风带着我旅行了许多天。水从不停歇：升起、旅行、冷却、落下，再升起——像血液流经身体一样在行星上周而复始地循环（circulate）着。老水滴们喜欢说，大气（atmosphere）不过是一条流淌在我们头顶的河。

一个寒冷的夜晚，我落在高山草甸上——不是以雨的形式，而是化作露水（dew），给每一片草叶镀上一层银。到破晓时分，下面的山谷已经灌满了浓密（dense）的薄雾（mist），空气湿润（moist）而潮乎乎（damp）地悬在松林之间。后来向南漂移时，我又感到空气变得温暖而潮湿（humid）起来——那是热带（tropics）的呼吸。

然后，我变得太重、再也浮不住的那一天到了。云变暗了，我开始凝结降落（precipitate）——这是科学家使用的盛大字眼；你们只会说，我化作雨落了下来。雨倾泻（pour）了一个小时。我落在一片叶子上，在叶尖悬了片刻，然后滴落（drip）到下面的路上。

在城市里，我顺着排水沟滑动，直到被一个下水道口（drain）吞下。有一阵子，我在街道下面的黑暗中旅行。再见到天空时，我正从公园的喷泉（fountain）里飞出来；后来我又从一眼山泉（spring）里升起，那泉水正从岩缝间涌出（gush），冰凉而甘甜。

城市的空气并不总是友善。有些早晨，一层棕色的烟雾（smog）铺在屋顶上，饱含着上百万辆汽车排放的尾气（fume），我穿过它落下来，就成了灰色的雨，背上驮着它的尘垢。水会原谅，但水也记得。

在喷泉与河流、云朵与下水道之间辗转多次之后，我终于回到了海——我出生的那片温暖的海洋。在我头顶上方，太阳已经又伸手去够下一滴水了。我并不在意。我已经懂得：落下，不过是升起的开始。

quiz.q: In the story, the sun evaporated the water into vapour. To evaporate means to —
o: change from liquid into gas and rise into the air
flow along a river to the sea
quiz.ex: evaporate = 蒸发。物理义之外，它有个极生动的引申用法——"消失得无影无踪"：His confidence evaporated the moment the exam started. 考试一开始，他的信心烟消云散。名词 evaporation（蒸发作用，雅思水循环话题必会）。

quiz.q: As vapour, the raindrop floated above the waves. Vapour is —
o: the gas form of a liquid, such as steam
quiz.ex: vapour = 蒸气、汽（water vapour 水蒸气；美式拼写 vapor）。辨析一组：vapour 泛指蒸气；steam 专指沸水产生的蒸汽；mist 薄雾；smog 烟雾（smoke+fog 合成词）。水循环叙事的起点词。

quiz.q: The raindrop settled on the meadow as dew. Dew is —
o: tiny drops of water that form on cool surfaces at night
quiz.ex: dew = 露水、露珠（dew on the grass 草上的露水；形容词 dewy 带露水的）。与 frost（霜）的关键区别：dew 是液态小水珠，frost 是冻结的冰晶。日出前后草叶上的"晨露"是它的标准画面。

quiz.q: "I precipitated — that is the grand word scientists use." To precipitate means to —
o: rise from the sea into the sky
fall from clouds as rain, snow or hail
quiz.ex: precipitate 是降水（雨、雪、雹落下）的正式动词，名词 precipitation（降水量）是气象与气候类雅思阅读的核心术语：annual precipitation 年降水量。故事吐槽它是"科学家用的盛大字眼"——记住这个梗就忘不掉了。另两个义项：名词"沉淀物"，形容词"仓促的"。

quiz.q: The valley filled with dense mist. Mist is —
o: a thin fog made of tiny drops of water in the air
quiz.ex: mist = 薄雾。浓度排队：mist（薄雾）< fog（浓雾）< smog（烟雾）。搭配：a veil of mist 一层薄雾、misty morning 雾蒙蒙的早晨。苏格兰高地的 mist 与威士忌一样有名。

quiz.q: Water gushes cold and sweet from between the rocks. To gush means to —
o: drip slowly, one drop at a time
pour out suddenly and in large amounts
quiz.ex: gush = 涌出、喷涌（a gush of water 一股涌出的水）。口语引申义"过分热情地夸赞"：She gushed about her new job for ten minutes. 她滔滔不绝地夸了十分钟新工作。故事中与 drip（慢滴）形成速度对比。

quiz.q: A brown smog lay over the rooftops. Smog is —
o: dirty air caused by smoke and traffic fumes mixing with fog
quiz.ex: smog = 烟雾，构词一目了然：smoke + fog。城市环境话题标配：dense/heavy smog 浓重烟雾、traffic-induced smog 交通造成的烟雾、smog warnings 烟雾警报。故事里雨滴穿过 smog 变灰——湿沉降，正是雅思环境阅读的原理性描述。

quiz.q: A drain swallowed the raindrop. A drain is —
o: a natural spring in the mountains
a pipe or channel that carries water away
quiz.ex: drain 名词"排水沟、下水道"，动词"排走、耗尽"。必会引申义：brain drain 人才流失（雅思社会经济类高频表达！）；be drained of energy 精疲力竭。故事里雨滴"被下水道吞下"的隧道段落，就是城市排水的写实。

title: From Brook to Sea
text:
Last summer, my father and I spent a week paddling down the Clearwater River, from its {{source}} high in the mountains all the way to the sea. "A river is a story," Dad said as we pushed off. "It grows longer and louder as it goes, but it never forgets where it began."

On the first day the water was only a {{brook}}, so narrow that I could step across it. By the third day it had swollen into a proper {{stream}}, and then a river, fed by a hundred smaller ones. At one point we carried our kayak around a {{waterfall}}, where the whole river jumped off a cliff in a single white sheet.

Midweek we paddled across a man-made {{reservoir}}, flat and silent, where the water waits its turn to pass through the dam. Below the dam, the {{current}} ran fast and cold, and I had to grip the paddle with both hands.

On Friday we reached the lowlands. The river widened, slowed, and began to put down the mud it carried. Rivers are the planet's movers, Dad explained: they carry {{silt}} and {{clay}} down from the mountains, leave them along their {{muddy}} banks, and where they finally meet the sea, they build a {{delta}} out of their own dirt.

That night we camped in a {{swamp}} of reeds, where herons fished in the shallows and the mosquitoes played violins. The swamp smelled of rot and of life at the same time.

On the last morning we floated out into the {{gulf}}. We paddled along the {{shore}}, past the {{beach}} where children were building castles, following the {{coast}} eastward. The {{tide}} was coming in, pushing salt water back up against the river's flow. With a map and a compass, Dad taught me the basics of {{navigation}}: "On the sea, knowing exactly where you are is not a hobby. It is survival."

That afternoon we finally paddled past the last headland into the open {{ocean}}. A family of dolphins — {{marine}} mammals, Dad reminded me — crossed quietly in front of our bow. He dipped his hand into the salt water and waved goodbye to the river. "Every drop of this ocean came down a river like ours," he said. "And some of it, this very week, came down ours."
tr:
去年夏天，我和爸爸花了一个星期，沿清水河顺流划桨而下——从它高居山中的源头（source）一直划到大海。“河流是一个故事，”推船下水时爸爸说，“它越走越长、越走越响，但永远记得自己从哪里开始。”

第一天，河水还只是一条小溪（brook），窄得我一步就能跨过去。到第三天，它已经涨成一条像样的溪流（stream），再往下便是一条河了，一路上接纳了上百条更小的支流。有一处，我们抬着皮划艇绕过一道瀑布（waterfall）——整条河在那里化作一整幅白色的幕布，从崖壁上跳了下去。

星期三，我们划过一片人工水库（reservoir），水面平坦而安静，水在那里排队等候通过大坝。坝下的水流（current）又急又凉，我不得不用双手攥紧船桨。

星期五我们进入低地。河面变宽、流速变慢，开始把一路携带的泥沙卸下来。爸爸解释说，河流是这颗星球的搬运工：它们把山里的淤泥（silt）和黏土（clay）带下来，沉积在泥泞的（muddy）河岸沿线，而在最终入海的地方，它们用自己带来的泥土堆出一座三角洲（delta）。

那天晚上，我们宿营在一片芦苇沼泽（swamp）里，苍鹭在浅水中捕鱼，蚊子拉起了小提琴。沼泽的气味闻起来既像腐烂，又像新生。

最后一个早晨，我们漂进了海湾（gulf）。我们沿着岸（shore）划行，经过孩子们正在筑城堡的海滩（beach），顺着海岸（coast）向东。潮水（tide）正在上涨，把咸水顶回河流的去路。爸爸借着一张地图和一枚罗盘，教我航海导航（navigation）的基础：“在海上，确切知道自己在哪儿不是爱好，是生存。”

那天下午，我们终于划过最后一道海岬，进入开阔的海洋（ocean）。一群海豚——爸爸提醒我，它们是海洋（marine）哺乳动物——安静地从我们船头前游过。他把一只手伸进咸咸的海水里，向河流道别。“这片海洋里的每一滴水，都是从某条像我们这样的河里下来的，”他说，“而其中有一些，就是这个星期，从我们这条河里下来的。”

quiz.q: We paddled down the river from its source. The source of a river is —
o: the place where it meets the sea
the place where the river begins
the dam that holds back its water
quiz.ex: source = 源头；更常用的是"来源、出处"义：news source 消息来源、energy source 能源来源、source of income 收入来源、source of pride 骄傲的源泉。雅思写作万能表达：a major source of... ……的主要来源。反义词尾对照：source（源）↔ mouth（河口）。

quiz.q: The water was only a brook, so narrow I could step across it. A brook is —
o: a small, natural stream of water
quiz.ex: brook = 小河、小溪（比 stream 更小更窄）。冷知识：brook 还可作动词，意为"容忍、忍受"，且几乎只用于否定——He would brook no criticism. 他容不得半点批评。雅思阅读历史文献引用中出现过。

quiz.q: Below the dam, the current ran fast and cold. Here, a current is —
o: the steady flow of water in one direction
the rain that feeds the river
quiz.ex: current 名词义项一：（水、气、电）流——ocean currents 洋流（墨西哥湾流 Gulf Stream 是雅思阅读老朋友）、air currents 气流、an electric current 电流；义项二（形容词）：当前的——current affairs 时事、the current situation 当前局势。两个义项都是考点，别只记一个。

quiz.q: Where the river meets the sea, it builds a delta. A delta is —
o: a deep gorge high in the mountains
a triangle-shaped area of soil deposited at a river's mouth
quiz.ex: delta = 三角洲，因形状酷似希腊字母 Δ（delta）而得名，尼罗河三角洲（the Nile Delta）最经典。成因：河流入海口流速骤降，携带的 silt（淤泥）沉积成陆。雅思地理类题干常考 the Ganges delta（恒河三角洲）等。

quiz.q: We camped in a swamp of reeds. A swamp is —
o: soft, wet land where water covers the soil
quiz.ex: swamp = 沼泽（湿地），近义 marsh / wetland（wetland 湿地是环保类雅思高频词）。必会动词引申：be swamped with work 被工作淹没、忙得团团转（口语和写作都超好用）：I'd love to help, but I'm swamped this week. 本周我忙不过来了。

quiz.q: The tide was coming in, pushing salt water up the river. The tide is —
o: the regular rise and fall of the sea level
a storm blowing in from the ocean
quiz.ex: tide = 潮汐。the tide is coming in / going out 涨潮／退潮。两个习语顺手拿下：Time and tide wait for no man. 岁月不等人；swim with / against the tide 顺／逆潮流而行。雅思海洋能话题还考 tidal energy 潮汐能。

quiz.q: Dolphins are marine mammals. Marine means —
quiz.ex: marine = 海洋的、与海有关的：marine life 海洋生物、marine biologist 海洋生物学家、marine pollution 海洋污染、the Marine Corps 海军陆战队。拼写陷阱：marine（海洋的）≠ marital（婚姻的）——雅思听力听写翻车重灾区。

quiz.q: Dad taught me the basics of navigation. Navigation is —
o: the activity of planning and following a route
quiz.ex: navigation = 导航、航海术。搭配：satellite navigation 卫星导航、navigation system 导航系统、navigate the website 浏览网站（动词引申）。历史话题常考：Before GPS, sailors navigated by the stars. GPS 出现之前，水手靠星辰导航。

title: Climbing Blue Cloud Mountain
text:
Every autumn, our school's outdoor club spends a weekend climbing Blue Cloud {{Mountain}}, the highest {{peak}} of the whole {{range}}. Our leader, Mr. Okafor, likes to say that a mountain is a lesson you climb with your legs.

We set out at dawn from the {{valley}}, where a fast river ran between green fields. The first hour was easy — a gentle {{slope}} through pine forest, a cool {{breeze}}, the {{surrounding}} hills turning gold in the early light, and somewhere below us the steady roar of a {{waterfall}}.

Then the trail turned serious. The {{terrain}} grew rough: bare rock, loose stones, and one stretch where the path ran along the edge of a {{cliff}}, with a drop that made my stomach float. At noon we rested in a shallow {{cave}}, where centuries of wind had carved out a window.

Above the tree line, the {{landscape}} changed completely. We crossed a high {{plateau}}, flat as a table, where wild flowers grew low against the wind. Far to the east hung the {{glacier}} — a slow river of ice, blue-white and cracked — resting in its shaded bowl below the summit. Mr. Okafor pointed at the skyline: "Every {{ridge}} you see was carved by that ice, ten thousand years ago."

The final climb tested our legs. The air thinned with {{altitude}}, and some of us stopped every twenty steps to breathe. But at four o'clock we stood on the summit stone. Below us, the whole {{plain}} spread out like a green map, villages like grains of sugar. The {{hillside}} we had climbed that morning looked no bigger than a garden.

"So why do we do this?" asked Lily, red-faced and happy.

"Because the {{mountain}} teaches patience," said Mr. Okafor. "And by the way — the {{mount}} in 'Mount Fuji' is simply the older, shorter word for mountain. We keep it in names." Then he poured tea for everyone, and we watched the clouds pour themselves over the ridges below.
tr:
每年秋天，我们学校的户外社团都会用一个周末去攀登青云山（mountain）——整条山脉（range）中最高的山峰（peak）。领队奥卡福先生喜欢说：山是一堂用双腿去上的课。

黎明时分，我们从山谷（valley）出发，一条湍急的河在绿野间穿行。第一个小时很轻松——一道平缓的山坡（slope）穿过松林，凉风（breeze）习习，四周（surrounding）的山丘在晨光里泛着金色，我们下方某处还回荡着瀑布（waterfall）不变的轰鸣。

然后，山路变得严肃起来。地形（terrain）崎岖起来：裸露的岩石、松动的碎石，还有一段路贴着悬崖（cliff）的边缘，脚下的落差让我的胃都悬了起来。中午，我们在一个浅浅的洞穴（cave）里休息，千百年的风在那里凿出了一扇窗。

林线之上，风景（landscape）完全变了模样。我们穿过一片高原（plateau），平得像一张桌子，野花贴着地面迎风生长。远在东边悬着那条冰川（glacier）——一条缓慢的冰河，蓝白色，布满裂隙——安卧在峰顶背阴的冰斗里。奥卡福先生指着天际线：“你们看见的每一道山脊（ridge），都是一万年前那些冰雕刻出来的。”

最后的登顶考验了我们的双腿。随着海拔（altitude）升高，空气变得稀薄，有些人每走二十步就得停下来喘气。但下午四点，我们站上了峰顶的巨石。脚下，整片平原（plain）像一张绿色的地图铺展开去，村庄小得如同糖粒；清晨我们攀登过的那面山坡（hillside），看上去不过一座花园大小。

“所以我们为什么要做这件事？”莉莉红着脸、开开心心地问。

“因为山教会人耐心，”奥卡福先生说，“顺便说一句——‘Mount Fuji’（富士山）里的那个 mount（mount），就是 mountain 更古老、更简短的说法，我们把它保留在了地名里。”说完，他给每个人倒了茶，我们看着云把自己泼洒在下方的道道山脊上。

quiz.q: Blue Cloud Mountain is the highest peak of the range. A peak is —
o: the pointed top of a mountain
a deep cave in the rock
quiz.ex: peak = 山峰、顶峰；动词义"达到高峰"：Sales peaked in December. 十二月销售额登顶。高频搭配：off-peak hours 非高峰时段（雅思听力交通、电话账单场景必考）、peak season 旺季。近义词 summit（顶峰）常作同义替换。

quiz.q: We set out at dawn from the valley. A valley is —
o: the flat top of a mountain
the low land between hills or mountains, often with a river
quiz.ex: valley = 山谷、河谷；引申义"流域"：the Yangtze valley 长江流域。与 ridge（山脊）互为镜像：谷是凹，脊是凸。冰川削出的 U 形谷（U-shaped valley）是雅思地质阅读的常见考点。

quiz.q: The terrain grew rough: bare rock and loose stones. Terrain means —
o: the natural features of an area of land
quiz.ex: terrain = 地形、地势（法语借词，重音在后 /təˈreɪn/）。搭配：rough / mountainous / rugged terrain 崎岖、多山地形；all-terrain vehicle 全地形车。探险、军事、救援类雅思阅读的高频名词。

quiz.q: The path ran along the edge of a cliff. A cliff is —
o: a high, steep face of rock
quiz.ex: cliff = 悬崖、峭壁。搭配：cliff edge 悬崖边缘、sheer cliff 直上直下的峭壁；the White Cliffs of Dover 多佛白崖（雅思听力旅游景点场景出现过）。注意与 hill（小山）、ridge（山脊）的区分。

quiz.q: We crossed a high plateau, flat as a table. A plateau is —
o: a large area of flat high land
quiz.ex: plateau = 高原（如 the Tibetan plateau 青藏高原）。更妙的是引申义——雅思图表作文专用：reach a plateau 进入平台期、停滞不涨：House prices reached a plateau in August. 八月房价进入平台期。来自法语"平盘"。

quiz.q: The glacier was a slow river of ice. A glacier is —
o: a huge mass of ice moving slowly down a mountain
a field of flowers above the tree line
quiz.ex: glacier = 冰川（英音 /ˈɡlæsiə/）。环境话题高频搭配：melting glaciers 融化的冰川、glacial meltwater 冰川融水、retreating glaciers 后退中的冰川——全是全球变暖类雅思阅读的标准表述。故事里"river of ice"正是它的定义式比喻。

quiz.q: The air thinned with altitude. Altitude means —
o: distance north or south of the equator
quiz.ex: altitude = 海拔、高度：high / low altitude 高／低海拔、altitude sickness 高原反应。必辨形近词：altitude（海拔）vs latitude（纬度）vs attitude（态度）——雅思阅读选项偷换概念的老手法。故事中"air thinned with altitude"是高原反应的原理句。

quiz.q: "Every ridge you see was carved by that ice." A ridge is —
o: a long, narrow raised line of hills or rock
a deep cut in the earth
quiz.ex: ridge = 山脊（山的高凸长条），也可指屋脊（the ridge of a roof）。地质考点：冰川两侧削出 ridge、中间磨出 valley，两者常成对出题。作动词时表示"使成脊状"。

title: The View from Eagle Canyon
text:
Last month my cousin Ruby, who works as a canyon guide, took me to her favourite viewing platform. From there you can {{overlook}} the entire canyon — a {{dramatic}} gash of red rock, two kilometres wide, that the river below has spent ten million years cutting.

The {{cliff}}s are almost {{vertical}}, dropping hundreds of metres to a {{shallow}} green river. In some places the two rims come so close that only a {{narrow}} {{gap}} of sky remains between them. Far upstream, flat-topped {{plateau}}s stand above the gorge like tables left by giants. The layers of rock lie {{parallel}} to each other like the pages of an open book — Ruby calls this "the diary of the Earth".

The trail down to the river is {{steep}} and {{rough}}, switching back and forth; by the third bend my legs were shaking. Ruby kept up her commentary the whole way. "Careful — this stone is {{smooth}} from a million boots. And don't trust that ledge; the rock looks {{flat}}, but it isn't solid."

At the bottom we ate sandwiches beside the river. Above us, condors — enormous birds — rode the warm air without once flapping their wings. "They make it look easy," Ruby said, "but they have been practising for a million years." Then she pointed at the rock layers. "{{Interesting}} fact: every stripe is a different age. The canyon is a calendar written in stone."

On the way up, a tourist asked Ruby whether the view was "worth posting online". She laughed. "It is {{magnificent}}. It is {{grand}} and {{splendid}} and every other big word you like. But you will only see it if you put the phone down for five minutes."

In the evening, at the small {{flat}} she shares with two other guides, Ruby showed me photographs of the canyon in every kind of light. "That tourist today took two hundred pictures and never once looked up," she said. "{{Superficial}} people collect pictures. Curious people collect questions. The canyon rewards the second kind."

At sunset we stood on the platform one last time. The {{horizon}} burned gold, and the whole gorge filled with moving shadows. "This is {{super}}," I said — the least serious word I knew, for the most serious view of my life. Ruby pretended not to hear.
tr:
上个月，在峡谷当向导的表姐露比带我去了她最喜欢的观景台。从那里可以俯瞰（overlook）整座峡谷——一道气势逼人（dramatic）的红色岩缝，宽两公里，是脚下那条河用一千万年切出来的。

崖壁（cliff）近乎垂直（vertical），直落数百米，落到一条浅浅的（shallow）绿色河流里。有些地方，峡谷两侧的岩缘靠得极近，中间只剩下一线狭窄（narrow）的缝隙（gap）透着天空。再往上游，平顶的高原（plateau）像巨人留下的桌子一样立在峡谷之上。层层岩石彼此平行（parallel），像一本摊开的书的书页——露比管这叫“地球的日记”。

通往谷底的步道陡峭（steep）而崎岖（rough），来回折返；到第三个弯，我的腿就开始打颤。露比一路解说不停：“小心——这块石头被一百万双靴子磨得光滑（smooth）了。别信那块岩台；那岩石看着平坦（flat），其实并不结实。”

谷底，我们在河边吃了三明治。头顶上，几只秃鹫——巨大的鸟——乘着暖空气滑翔，一次也不扇动翅膀。“它们看起来毫不费力，”露比说，“可它们已经练了一百万年。”然后她指着岩层：“说个有趣（interesting）的事实：每一道条纹都是一个不同的年代。峡谷是一部用石头写成的日历。”

上山路上，一位游客问露比，这景色“值不值得发到网上”。她笑了。“它壮丽（magnificent）。它宏伟（grand）、辉煌（splendid），随你挑哪个大词。但你得先把手机放下五分钟，才看得见它。”

傍晚，在她和另外两名向导合住的小公寓（flat）里，露比给我看她拍下的各种光线里的峡谷。“今天那位游客，拍了两百张照片，一次也没抬头看，”她说，“肤浅（superficial）的人收集图片，好奇的人收集问题。峡谷奖赏的是第二种人。”

日落时分，我们最后一次站上观景台。地平线（horizon）燃烧成金色，整道峡谷充满了移动的暗影。“这真是太棒（super）了，”我说——用了我所知道的最不严肃的词，来形容我这辈子见过的最严肃的风景。露比假装没听见。

quiz.q: From the platform you can overlook the entire canyon. To overlook a place means to —
o: walk all the way around it
clean it from top to bottom
have a view of it from above
quiz.ex: overlook 两大高频义项：①俯瞰、俯视（本故事用法）；②忽略、没注意到：an important detail that is easily overlooked 一个容易被忽略的重要细节。做题时先判断方向：从高处看 = 俯视；看漏了 = 忽略。别与 overhaul（彻底检修）混淆。

quiz.q: The cliffs are almost vertical. Vertical means —
o: standing straight up and down, at ninety degrees to the ground
quiz.ex: vertical = 垂直的：a vertical cliff 垂直崖壁、vertical take-off 垂直起降、vertical farming 垂直农业（雅思城市农业新话题）。反义词 horizontal 水平的。辨析：vertical 强调 90°；steep 只说坡度大，不一定垂直。

quiz.q: Hundreds of metres above the shallow green river. Shallow means —
quiz.ex: shallow = 浅的：shallow water 浅水（海域安全旗话题）、a shallow dish 浅盘。高频引申义"肤浅的"：a shallow argument 肤浅的论证——与故事里的 superficial 恰好构成同义呼应（superficial 人 shallow 观点都是"只及表面"）。反义 deep。

quiz.q: The layers of rock lie parallel to each other. Parallel means —
o: side by side, the same distance apart everywhere, never meeting
quiz.ex: parallel = 平行的：parallel lines 平行线、run in parallel 并行进行。名词义"相似之处"超高频：draw parallels between A and B 在 A 与 B 之间做类比；a career without parallel 史无前例的职业生涯——雅思阅读推理题的信号词。

quiz.q: The trail down to the river is steep. Steep means —
o: rising gently over a long distance
rising or falling sharply, at a difficult angle
quiz.ex: steep = 陡峭的：a steep hill 陡坡。两个引申义都要会：①（价格）过高：$10 for a coffee is a bit steep. ②（变化）急剧的：a steep rise in prices 价格飙升——雅思图表作文的增长描述词。

quiz.q: "Superficial people collect pictures." A superficial person is one who —
o: cares only about the surface of things, never their depth
quiz.ex: superficial = 肤浅的、表面的（super- 上面 + -ficial 面 → 只碰表面）：superficial knowledge 浅薄的知识、a superficial analysis 流于表面的分析。近义 shallow；反义 thorough、profound。故事中"收集图片 vs 收集问题"是它最好的注脚。

quiz.q: The horizon burned gold at sunset. The horizon is —
o: the line far away where the earth seems to meet the sky
the top of the highest cliff
quiz.ex: horizon = 地平线。三个必会搭配：on the horizon 即将来临（New technology is on the horizon.）；broaden your horizons 开阔眼界（游学、留学话题金句）；horizontal 水平的（反义 vertical）。

quiz.q: "It is magnificent, grand and splendid." Magnificent means —
quiz.ex: magnificent = 壮丽的、宏伟的：a magnificent view 壮丽的景色、a magnificent palace 宏伟的宫殿。近义词族一并收入弹药库：grand 宏大的、splendid 辉煌的、spectacular 壮观的、breathtaking 惊艳的——雅思口语描述景点的五连发。

title: South to the Ice
text:
My sister Clara studies ice for a living, and every year she spends six months at a research station in the {{antarctic|Antarctic}}. In March, when autumn begins in the southern half of the world, she flies south until the cities disappear and only ice remains.

"Where exactly are you?" I asked her once on a video call. "Almost at the bottom of the {{globe}}," she said, turning her camera to the window. "Remember the model Earth at school? We live at the {{pole}} — the {{polar}} opposite of the {{arctic|Arctic}}, where the polar bears live. Cross the {{equator}} going south, and every kilometre grows colder."

During her winter — our summer — the thermometer turns shy. "Forty below zero," she reported happily. "The {{frigid}} air freezes your breath; my eyelashes {{freeze}} the moment I step outside. We {{shiver}} even indoors, and a {{chill}} creeps up your sleeve whenever the door opens. Our windows grow {{frost}} flowers on the inside."

She described the brief summer too: the edge of the ice {{thaw}}s a little, and meltwater carves blue rivers across the plain. Once they even had {{hail}} — ice falling out of the sky onto the ice. The sun hangs above the {{snowy}} plains for months without setting, and the {{ocean}} around the continent opens up so the whales can return.

"Which hemisphere you live in decides your season," she once explained. "The Earth leans slightly as it spins on its {{axis}}, so when the southern {{hemisphere}} tips towards the sun, we enjoy summer while you pull on your sweaters."

In September, Clara comes home tanned and quiet. Last year she sent me a photograph of penguins with one line written on the back: "Penguins live only in the southern hemisphere, and they will never meet a polar bear. The two poles are twins who have never seen each other."
tr:
我的姐姐克拉拉以研究冰为业，每年她都要在南极（antarctic）的一个科考站待上六个月。三月，当南半球的秋天开始时，她一路向南飞行，直到城市消失，只剩下冰。

“你到底在哪儿？”有一次视频通话时我问她。“差不多在地球仪（globe）的最底端，”她说着把镜头转向窗外，“还记得学校里的地球模型吗？我们就住在极点（pole）——北极（arctic）的极地（polar）反面，北极熊住在那一头。越过赤道（equator）一路向南，每一公里都更冷一点。”

在她的冬季——也就是我们的夏季——温度计变得羞怯。“零下四十度，”她开心地汇报，“严寒（frigid）的空气把呼吸都冻住；我一出门，睫毛就结冰（freeze）。我们在室内也发抖（shiver），门一开，一股寒气（chill）就顺着袖口爬进来。我们的窗户内侧开满了霜（frost）花。”

她也描述过短暂的夏季：冰缘会稍稍解冻（thaw），雪水在平原上冲出一道道蓝色的河。有一回他们甚至还下了场冰雹（hail）——冰从天上落下来，砸在冰上。太阳在雪白（snowy）的平原上空一挂就是几个月，不肯落山，环绕大陆的海洋（ocean）重新敞开，好让鲸鱼回来。

“你住在哪个半球（hemisphere），就过什么季节，”她有一次解释道，“地球绕着地轴（axis）自转时微微倾斜，所以当南半球朝向太阳倾斜时，我们享受夏天，而你们就得裹紧毛衣。”

九月，克拉拉晒得黝黑、话不多说地回到家。去年她寄给我一张企鹅的照片，背面只写了一行字：“企鹅只住在南半球（hemisphere），一辈子也遇不上一只北极熊。两个极点是从未见过面的双胞胎。”

quiz.q: In the story, penguins never meet polar bears because the two animals —
o: live at opposite poles of the Earth
are active at different times of day
live in the same place in different seasons
quiz.ex: the Arctic 北极地区，the Antarctic 南极地区（注意大写与定冠词）。构词溯源：arctic 来自希腊语"熊"（大熊座下方的区域）；antarctic = anti-（相反）+ arctic → 与北极相对。形容词用法：frigid antarctic waters 严寒的南极海域。记忆锚点就是故事结尾那句"从未见过面的双胞胎"。

quiz.q: "Cross the equator going south, and every kilometre grows colder." The equator is —
o: the imaginary line around the middle of the Earth
the line joining the two poles
the coldest circle on the globe
quiz.ex: equator = 赤道（zero latitude 零度纬线）。形容词 equatorial：an equatorial climate 赤道气候——正好衔接 S3 里"热带（tropics）几乎每天下午下雨"的知识点。地理题干常见表述：countries on the equator。

quiz.q: "Which hemisphere you live in decides your season." A hemisphere is —
o: a line around the middle of the globe
a layer of air around the Earth
quiz.ex: hemisphere = 半球：the northern / southern hemisphere 北／南半球。构词：hemi-（半）+ sphere（球体），同族词 atmosphere（atmo- 空气 + sphere）。故事核心考点：南北半球季节相反。

quiz.q: The Earth leans slightly as it spins on its axis. An axis is —
o: the line around the middle of an object
the coldest point of the globe
the imaginary line that an object turns around
quiz.ex: axis = 轴、轴线：the Earth's axis 地轴（倾斜约 23.5°，正是四季的成因）、the axis of symmetry 对称轴。复数形式是 axes（/ˈæksiːz/）。天文与物理类雅思阅读的通用词。

quiz.q: The frigid air freezes your breath. Frigid means —
quiz.ex: frigid = 极度寒冷的、严寒的，比 cold 语气重一档：frigid air 严寒的空气、frigid waters 冰冷的海水。寒意梯度：cool → cold → freezing → frigid。故事里"睫毛结冰"就是 frigid 的画面感。

quiz.q: In the brief summer, the edge of the ice thaws. To thaw means to —
o: change from frozen to soft or liquid
quiz.ex: thaw = 解冻、融化（动词、名词同形）：The river thaws in March. 三月河开。名词引申义"关系缓和"：a thaw in relations between the two countries 两国关系的解冻（外交类雅思阅读高频）。近义 melt，反义 freeze。

quiz.q: Once they even had hail — ice falling onto the ice. Hail is —
o: frozen rain that falls as small balls of ice
quiz.ex: hail 名词义"冰雹"。更要掌握的是它的两个动词义：①把…誉为（被动句型超高频）：The film was hailed as a masterpiece. 这部电影被誉为杰作。②hail from... 来自……：She hails from a small town in Yunnan. 她来自云南的一座小镇。一词三义，全是考点。

quiz.q: "We shiver even indoors." To shiver means to —
o: run in place to keep warm
shake slightly because of cold or fear
quiz.ex: shiver =（因寒冷或恐惧）哆嗦、发抖：shiver with cold 冷得发抖、send shivers down your spine 让人脊背发凉（恐怖惊悚话题金句）。近义辨析：shiver 专指冷颤；tremble 泛指发抖（S2 火山故事里"膝盖发颤"）；quake 剧烈颤动。

title: The Map Room
text:
My grandfather was a ship's navigator, and his study is still full of old maps. Last winter, when I reached the final of the school geography competition, he locked the door, spread a giant map across the table and said, "Six days. We begin with the world."

He taught me the grid first. "These lines running from north to south measure {{longitude}}," he said, drawing a finger down the map. "The lines crossing them, east to west, measure {{latitude}}. The line of zero latitude circles the {{equator}}, and north of it lies the northern {{hemisphere}}. Where longitude and latitude cross, you can point to any spot on Earth — even in the middle of the {{pacific|Pacific}}."

On the second day came the {{continent}}s and the {{ocean}}s. "Name the sea between Europe and Africa." "The {{mediterranean|Mediterranean}}!" "Good. And which ocean lies west of Europe, dividing the old world from the new?" "The {{atlantic|Atlantic}}!" "Now a trick question: which continent is mostly water?" "That's unfair — {{oceania|Oceania}}," I said, "thousands of islands scattered across the Pacific."

On the third day we studied coastlines. "Italy is a {{peninsula}} — a boot of land reaching into the sea. The {{mainland}} of China faces islands across a strait. Countries that touch, like France and Germany, are {{adjacent}}; countries far apart are {{distant}}. And every {{border}} on this map," he tapped the lines gently, "was drawn by war, marriage or ink. Remember that maps lie a little."

Some of his oldest maps had beautiful drawings in the {{margin}}s — waves, sailing ships, and sea monsters at the {{fringe}} of the known world. An {{oriental}} rug covered the table, a souvenir from his years in Hong Kong, and the study window faced east, so the morning sun always lit the eastern half of the map.

Grandfather drilled directions without mercy. "The compass has eight winds. North, south, east, west — and?" "{{Northeast}}, {{northwest}}, {{southeast}}, {{southwest}}," I recited, and he smiled like a lighthouse. "Then sail from the {{southern}} tip of Africa straight east — which coast do you strike?" "The {{eastern}} coast of Australia!"

At the competition, the final question was, of course, about longitude and latitude. When I came home with the silver medal, grandfather had already rolled the map up. At the exact point where our city sits — the crossing of two lines — he had drawn a small pencil circle. "You see?" he said. "Two lines meet, and a place is born."
tr:
我的祖父曾是船上的领航员，他的书房至今挂满了旧地图。去年冬天，当我闯入学校地理竞赛的决赛后，他锁上书房门，在桌上摊开一幅巨大的世界地图，说：“六天。我们从整个世界开始。”

他先教我经纬网。“这些南北走向的线测量的是经度（longitude），”他用手指顺着地图往下划，“与它们交叉、东西走向的那些测量的是纬度（latitude）。零度的纬线圈着赤道（equator），它的北边是北半球（hemisphere）。经度与纬度一交叉，你就能指出地球上的任何一点——哪怕是在太平洋（pacific）的正中央。”

第二天轮到大陆（continent）与海洋（ocean）。“说出欧洲与非洲之间那片海的名字。”“地中海（mediterranean）！”“好。那么哪片大洋在欧洲以西，把旧世界与新世界分开？”“大西洋（atlantic）！”“再来一道耍赖题：哪个大洲几乎全是水？”“这不公平——大洋洲（oceania），”我说，“上千座岛屿撒在太平洋上。”

第三天我们研究海岸线。“意大利是一个半岛（peninsula）——一只伸进海里的靴子。中国的大陆（mainland）隔着一道海峡与群岛相望。挨在一起的国家——比如法国和德国——是相邻的（adjacent）；相隔万里的国家是遥远的（distant）。而这张地图上的每一条边界（border），”他轻轻敲着那些线条，“都是由战争、联姻或者墨水画成的。记住：地图总会撒一点小谎。”

他那些最老的地图，页边的空白（margin）里画着漂亮的海浪和帆船，还有海怪趴在已知世界的边缘（fringe）。桌上铺着一块东方（oriental）图案的地毯，是他在香港那些年的纪念品；书房的窗子朝东，所以清晨的阳光总是先照亮地图的东半边。

祖父毫不留情地考我方向。“罗盘有八个风。北、南、东、西——然后呢？”“东北（northeast）、西北（northwest）、东南（southeast）、西南（southwest），”我背了出来，他笑得像一座灯塔。“那么，从非洲的南端（southern）笔直向东航行——你会撞上哪条海岸？”“澳大利亚的东部（eastern）海岸！”

竞赛那天，最后一题问的当然是经线与纬线。我拿回银牌回到家时，祖父已经把地图卷好了。在我们城市所在的那个点——两条线的交叉处——他用铅笔画了一个小圈。“看见了吗？”他说，“两条线相遇，一个地方就诞生了。”

quiz.q: In the story, lines running from north to south measure —
o: latitude — how far north or south a place is
longitude — how far east or west a place is
quiz.ex: longitude 经度 ↔ latitude 纬度，这对形近概念必须分清。记忆法：longitude 里有 long（长）——经线南北纵贯、看起来"长"；latitude 常被联想成 ladder（梯子）的横档——纬线是横向的圈。地图定位表述：The city lies at 40°N latitude, 116°E longitude. 雅思听力地图题与地理阅读的基础概念。

quiz.q: The line of zero latitude circles the equator. Latitude measures —
o: how far north or south of the equator a place is
how far east or west a place is
quiz.ex: latitude = 纬度；零度纬线即赤道（the equator）。搭配：high / low latitudes 高／低纬度地区；the tropics 位于低纬度（呼应 S3）。习语 give someone more latitude = 给某人更多自由余地（本义"纬度活动范围"的引申）。

quiz.q: Italy is a peninsula — a boot of land reaching into the sea. A peninsula is —
o: a small island far from any coast
a mountain range beside the sea
land almost surrounded by water, connected to the mainland by a narrow neck
quiz.ex: peninsula = 半岛：the Iberian Peninsula 伊比利亚半岛、the Korean Peninsula 朝鲜半岛。构词：pen(e)-（几乎）+ insula（岛）→"几乎是岛"。三者对比：island 岛（四面环水）、peninsula 半岛（三面环水）、cape 海角（深入海中的尖角）。

quiz.q: The mainland of China faces islands across a strait. The mainland is —
o: a small island near a coast
the main body of a country or continent, not counting its islands
quiz.ex: mainland = 大陆、本土（相对岛屿而言）：the Chinese mainland 中国大陆、the European mainland 欧洲大陆。雅思听力旅游场景高频对比：mainland tour vs island hop。形容词 mainland Chinese 等表述注意语境。

quiz.q: Countries that touch, like France and Germany, are adjacent. Adjacent means —
o: next to or very near something
quiz.ex: adjacent = 邻近的、毗连的（正式用词）：adjacent rooms 相邻的房间、the field adjacent to the school 学校旁边的田地。雅思阅读同义替换组：neighbouring / bordering / next to。故事中与 distant（遥远的）直接对举——一对反义一起记。

quiz.q: "Every border was drawn by war, marriage or ink." A border is —
o: the line that divides two countries or regions
quiz.ex: border = 边界、国界：cross the border 越境（雅思听力出入境场景）、border controls 边境检查。动词义"与…接壤"：France borders Germany. 引申义 on the border of 在……的边缘。祖父那句"战争、联姻或墨水"是对 border 历史最凝练的概括。

quiz.q: Some old maps had drawings in the margins. Here, margins are —
o: the blue colour of the sea
the empty space around the edge of the page
the wooden frame on the wall
quiz.ex: margin 三大高频义项：①页边空白（本故事）；②利润、差额：profit margin 利润率、win by a narrow margin 以微弱优势获胜（雅思商科、政治类阅读高频）；③余地：a safety margin 安全余量。一词贯穿"排版、经济、安全"三大场景。

quiz.q: An oriental rug covered the table. Oriental means —
o: coming from or related to East Asia
quiz.ex: oriental = 东方的（尤指中国、日本等东亚地区）：oriental rugs 东方地毯、oriental art 东方艺术。用法提示：现代英语中用来形容"人"已显过时且可能冒犯，雅思里基本只用于描述物品、艺术、风格；相关名词 the Orient 也已少用。故事中形容地毯是标准用法。

title: The River That Turned Grey
text:
The River Ash was the cleanest river in our county. Old photographs show children diving from the bridge and fishermen standing hip-deep below the mill. Then, last spring, the water slowly lost its colour and turned grey. Dead fish appeared along the banks like fallen leaves.

My mother, who teaches biology at the high school, went up the river with sample jars. The results were worse than anyone guessed: the water had been {{contaminate|contaminated}} by {{toxic}} waste from the chemical factory upstream. The {{pollutant|pollutants}} — heavy metals and dyes — had already reached the {{reservoir}} that supplies the town's drinking water. For one long week, we boiled everything.

The factory makes {{synthetic}} fabric out of {{petroleum}}, and it had been quietly discharging for months. Government inspections took place only {{irregularly}} — once in spring, never at night — and the outlet pipe had been hidden at an {{inappropriate}} spot, deep in the reeds where nobody walked.

At the town meeting, the hall was hot with anger. The factory manager spoke of jobs and costs; the fishermen said nothing at all — they simply stood there holding dead fish in plastic bags. As the summer went on, nobody's temper improved: the smell from the river {{aggravate|aggravated}} every conversation, and the situation continued to {{deteriorate}}. The banks, weakened by dead roots, began to {{erode}}; the river's whole living system had been so badly {{degrade|degraded}} that even the insects had left.

The town's answer was slow but firm. The factory was ordered to {{upgrade}} its treatment plant within a year, and an {{artificial}} wetland was planted downstream — reeds and rushes that filter water the way a kidney filters blood. My mother helped design it. "Nature cleans better than we do," she said, "if you give her the space."

We also had to look at ourselves. When it rained, every road in town washed oil and {{petrol}} into the river, and the farms upstream added fertiliser to the mix. My American cousin, visiting that summer, read the report and frowned. "So the {{pollution}} doesn't stop at the factory gate," he said. "Half of it is just the town — the {{gasoline}} on your streets, the soap from your sinks." It was an uncomfortable thought.

Two years on, the River Ash runs green again. The {{environment}} downstream has recovered faster than the scientists predicted — the birds returned first, then the fish, then the noisy children off the bridge. Only one thing never came back: a small brown mussel that lived nowhere else. Its loss, the report says, is {{irreversible}}. The river forgives a great deal, my mother likes to say. But it keeps a small museum of what it cannot forget.
tr:
灰河曾是我们郡最干净的河。老照片里，孩子们从桥上跳水，渔夫站在磨坊下游齐腰深的水里。然后，去年春天，河水慢慢失去了颜色，转成了灰色。死鱼像落叶一样出现在岸边。

我妈妈在高中教生物，她带着采样瓶逆流而上。结果比所有人猜的都糟：河水已被上游化工厂的有毒（toxic）废水污染（contaminate）。那些污染物（pollutant）——重金属和染料——已经抵达了为全镇供水的那个水库（reservoir）。整整一个星期，我们什么都得烧开了用。

这家工厂用石油（petroleum）制造合成（synthetic）纤维，已经悄悄排放了好几个月。政府的检查只是不定期地（irregularly）进行——春天来一次，夜里从不来——而排污口藏在一个不合适的（inappropriate）地方：芦苇深处，无人经过。

镇民大会上，礼堂里怒气蒸腾。工厂经理大谈就业与成本；渔夫们一言不发——只是举着装在塑料袋里的死鱼站在那里。夏天一天天过去，没有人的脾气变好：河里的气味让每一场对话都更加激化（aggravate），情况持续恶化（deteriorate）。岸边的泥土因草根枯死而酥软，开始被侵蚀（erode）；整条河的生命系统已被严重破坏、退化（degrade），连昆虫都走了。

小镇的回应缓慢而坚定。工厂被责令在一年内升级（upgrade）污水处理系统，下游还种出了一片人工（artificial）湿地——芦苇和灯心草，像肾脏过滤血液那样过滤河水。我妈妈参与了设计。“大自然比我们更会清洁，”她说，“只要你给她空间。”

我们也得审视自己。一下雨，镇上每条路的油污和汽油（petrol）就会被冲进河里，上游的农场还往这份混合物里添加肥料。那年夏天来做客的美国表哥读完了报告，皱起眉。“所以污染（pollution）并不止步于工厂大门，”他说，“其中一半就是小镇本身——你们街上的汽油（gasoline），你们水槽里的洗涤剂。”这是个让人不舒服的想法。

两年过去，灰河重新变绿了。下游的环境（environment）恢复得比科学家预测的更快——鸟最先回来，然后是鱼，然后是桥上吵闹的孩子。只有一样东西再没回来：一种只生活在这里的棕色小河蚌。报告说，它的消失是不可逆的（irreversible）。妈妈常说，河流原谅很多事情。但它保留着一座小小的博物馆，收藏它无法忘记的那些。

quiz.q: In the story, the water had been contaminated by toxic waste. To contaminate means to —
o: make something dirty, unsafe or poisonous
quiz.ex: contaminate = 污染、弄脏（强调"混入有害物质而不洁"）：contaminated water 受污染的水、contaminated food 受污染的食品。名词 contamination，形容词 contaminated。与 pollute 近义：pollute 偏"大规模污染环境"，contaminate 偏"使具体对象不再纯净安全"。

quiz.q: The waste from the factory was described as toxic. Toxic means —
o: poisonous and harmful to living things
quiz.ex: toxic = 有毒的：toxic waste 有毒废料、toxic chemicals 有毒化学物质、toxic gases 有毒气体。现代高频引申义："有毒的"人际关系或环境——a toxic relationship / a toxic work environment（雅思口语与写作社会话题加分表达）。

quiz.q: "The situation continued to deteriorate." To deteriorate means to —
quiz.ex: deteriorate = 恶化、变坏：His health deteriorated rapidly. 他的健康迅速恶化。现在分词 deteriorating 常作定语：the deteriorating situation 不断恶化的局势（雅思阅读高频形态）。反义 improve；名词 deterioration。

quiz.q: The weakened banks began to erode. To erode means to —
quiz.ex: erode = 侵蚀、腐蚀（本义风、水磨损岩石土壤）：soil erosion 水土流失（环保类雅思标配搭配）；coastal erosion 海岸侵蚀。引申义"逐渐削弱"：erode one's confidence 逐渐侵蚀信心、erode public trust 侵蚀公众信任。名词 erosion。

quiz.q: The factory was ordered to upgrade its treatment plant. To upgrade means to —
o: improve something and raise it to a higher standard
quiz.ex: upgrade = 升级、改进（up + grade）：upgrade the system 升级系统、an upgraded version 升级版、upgrade your skills 提升技能。反义 downgrade 降级、下调。注意它同时是名词：a major upgrade 一次重大升级。

quiz.q: An artificial wetland was planted downstream. Artificial means —
o: made or built by people rather than by nature
quiz.ex: artificial = 人造的、人工的：artificial wetlands 人工湿地（雅思环保解决方案类文章常客）、artificial intelligence 人工智能（AI 的全称！）、artificial light 人造光。辨析：artificial 泛指"非天然"；synthetic 特指"化学合成的"；fake 是"假冒的"。

quiz.q: The factory makes synthetic fabric from petroleum. Synthetic means —
o: produced by chemical processes rather than nature
quiz.ex: synthetic = 合成的、人工合成的：synthetic fabric 合成纤维、synthetic materials 合成材料、synthetic rubber 合成橡胶。词源：syn-（一起）+ -thetic（放置）→"组合制造出来的"。雅思常考对比：natural fibres（cotton, wool）vs synthetic fibres（polyester）。

quiz.q: The loss of the mussel is irreversible. Irreversible means —
o: impossible to change back or repair
quiz.ex: irreversible = 不可逆转的：irreversible damage 不可逆的破坏、irreversible climate change 不可逆转的气候变化——环境类雅思阅读的最高频搭配之一。构词：ir-（不）+ reverse（逆转）+ -ible（可…的）；反义 reversible。

title: A Week on Green Island
text:
Our family lives in a quiet {{suburb}} of the capital, on a street where the houses all look like cousins. But every August we escape for one week to Green Island, where my grandmother was born — a place so {{rural}} that its {{outskirts}} are marked by three cows and an oak tree.

The roof of grandmother's house now wears {{solar}} panels, which hum quietly and heat the water. She keeps two calendars on the kitchen wall, though: the printed one, and the round wooden {{lunar}} one her father carved. "One for the sea, one for the moon," she says. "The potatoes follow the moon."

The days pass slowly and well. My father, an accountant who never rises before eight, is up at five to watch the {{sunrise}} with the fishermen. At noon we hide from the {{sunshine}} in the {{shade}} of the fig tree, where my {{shadow}} is as short as a cat's. In the evening we walk to the western rocks for the {{sunset}} — the sky like a struck match — and at {{dusk}} the first bats go out, punctual as buses. On the third day, swimming in the warm green cove, my little brother announced that this was {{paradise}}; even our father, who calls everything "fine", admitted it was close to {{heaven}}.

On Thursday afternoon came the event of the year: a partial {{solar}} {{eclipse}}. The whole island climbed the hill with pieces of smoked glass. The light turned thin and silver, the birds stopped singing mid-note, and the temperature dropped as if a door to winter had been opened. Through the glass, the sun had a bite taken out of it. "The moon is eating the sun," said my brother, and for once nobody corrected him. A warm {{breeze}} ran along the {{coast}} road, and the {{humid}} air went very still.

On our last evening, grandmother took me to her vegetable garden. She stood between the rows with her basket and said: "The island needs nothing. Everything here is {{natural}} — the water, the wind, the quiet. When you go back to the city, keep something natural in your life."

On the ferry home, I watched the island grow small. I marked next August in my {{calendar}}, and then thought of the wooden one on the kitchen wall. Some calendars follow the moon, some follow the sun — and August follows grandmother.
tr:
我们家住在首都一个安静的郊区（suburb），街上的房子长得都像表亲。但每年八月，我们都会逃去绿岛住一个星期——我祖母出生的地方。那是个乡下（rural）得不能再乡下的小地方，村子外围（outskirts）的界标是三头牛和一棵橡树。

祖母家的屋顶如今装着太阳能（solar）电池板，安静地嗡嗡作响，把水烧热。不过她厨房的墙上仍挂着两本日历（calendar）：一本是印刷的，另一本是圆形的木制阴历（lunar）盘，她父亲亲手雕的。“一本给海，一本给月亮，”她说，“土豆跟着月亮走。”

日子过得又慢又好。我那位从来八点前不起床的会计师父亲，五点就爬起来和渔民一起看日出（sunrise）。正午，我们躲开阳光（sunshine），藏进无花果树的树荫（shade）里，我的影子（shadow）短得像一只猫。傍晚，我们走去西边的礁石看日落（sunset）——天空像一根划着的火柴——黄昏（dusk）时分，第一批蝙蝠准时出门，像公交车一样守时。第三天，在温暖翠绿的小海湾里游泳时，我弟弟宣布这里就是天堂（paradise）；连我们家那位把一切都称作“还行”的父亲也承认，这里离天国（heaven）不远了。

星期四下午迎来了全年大事：日偏食（eclipse）。全岛人带着熏黑的玻璃片爬上山。光线变得稀薄而银白，鸟儿唱到一半突然噤声，气温骤降，仿佛有人朝冬天开了一扇门。透过玻璃，太阳缺了一口。“月亮在吃太阳，”弟弟说，这一次没有人纠正他。一阵温暖的微风（breeze）掠过海岸（coast）公路，潮湿（humid）的空气安静下来。

最后一个傍晚，祖母带我去她的菜园。她挎着篮子站在垄间，说：“这岛上什么都不缺。这里的一切都是自然的（natural）——水、风、安静。你们回到城里，也要在生活里留一点自然的东西。”

回家的渡轮上，我看着小岛慢慢变小。我在日历（calendar）上标出明年八月，然后想起厨房墙上的那只木盘。有些历法跟着月亮走，有些跟着太阳走——而八月，跟着祖母走。

quiz.q: The roof wears solar panels that heat the water. Solar means —
quiz.ex: solar = 太阳的：solar panels 太阳能板、solar energy 太阳能、the solar system 太阳系。必考反义对：solar（太阳的）↔ lunar（月亮的）——a solar eclipse 日食 / a lunar eclipse 月食。雅思能源类话题第一词，本故事中与 lunar calendar（农历）同框出现，正好对照记忆。

quiz.q: Grandmother's round wooden calendar is lunar. Lunar means —
quiz.ex: lunar = 月亮的、与月亮有关的：the lunar calendar 阴历／农历、a lunar eclipse 月食、Lunar New Year 农历新年（雅思听力多元文化场景）。"土豆跟着月亮走"正是农耕文明用农历指导播种的写实。

quiz.q: The islanders watched a partial eclipse of the sun. An eclipse is —
o: an event in which one body in space hides another from view
quiz.ex: eclipse =（日、月）食：a solar eclipse 日食、a lunar eclipse 月食、a partial/total eclipse 偏食／全食。动词引申义"使黯然失色"：Her performance eclipsed all others. 她的表演令其他所有节目黯然失色（比较类阅读高频）。故事里"月亮在吃太阳"是各文明对 eclipse 共通的古老想象。

quiz.q: At dusk, the first bats went out. Dusk is —
o: the still period before a storm
the moment the sun first appears
the hottest hour of the day
the time just after sunset, when the light is fading
quiz.ex: dusk = 黄昏、暮色（不可数名词）：at dusk 在黄昏、from dawn to dusk 从早到晚（超高频短语，雅思工作时长话题直接可用）。辨析时间线：sunset（日落那一刻）→ dusk（日落后天色渐暗的时段）→ night；反义 dawn / daybreak 破晓。

quiz.q: We hid from the sunshine in the shade of the fig tree. Shade is —
o: the dark shape your body casts on the ground
an area sheltered from the sun's light
quiz.ex: shade（不可数）= 荫、阴凉处：sit in the shade 坐在树荫下、keep it in the shade 放在阴凉处。另一个义项"色调"：a shade of blue 一种蓝。经典辨析：shade 是"遮阳带来的凉爽区域"，shadow 是"物体挡光投下的具体影子"——荫是 shade，影是 shadow。

quiz.q: My shadow was as short as a cat's. A shadow is —
o: a cool sheltered spot under a tree
the dark shape made when your body blocks the light
quiz.ex: shadow = 影子：cast a shadow 投下影子、long evening shadows 拉长的暮色影子。引申义"阴影、坏影响"：the shadow of war 战争的阴影、live in someone's shadow 活在某人的光环之下。正午影子最短——故事里"short as a cat's"即正午时分的写照。

quiz.q: Green Island is so rural that its outskirts are marked by three cows and an oak tree. Rural means —
o: connected with the countryside rather than the city
quiz.ex: rural = 乡村的、农村的：rural areas 乡村地区、rural life 乡村生活、the rural population 农村人口。标准反义对（雅思城乡话题标配）：rural ↔ urban；相关概念 rural-urban migration 城乡人口迁移、rural depopulation 农村人口流失。

quiz.q: The village is so small that its outskirts are marked by three cows. Outskirts are —
o: the tallest buildings in a place
the outer parts of a town or village, away from the centre
quiz.ex: outskirts（恒用复数）= 外围地区、市郊：on the outskirts of the city 在市郊（固定搭配 on！）。近义辨析：suburb 指城市边缘的居住区（有住宅、通勤），outskirts 更泛指外围地带（常略显荒凉）。雅思听力租房场景：a cheaper flat on the outskirts。

title: The Geography Magazine
text:
On the last Friday of the school year, Ms. Lin gave the geography club its final assignment: a magazine. "Twelve pages," she said, dropping a stack of blank paper on the table. "About everything this planet has shown us this year. Next year's club will read it and think we are exaggerating. Good — let them come and see for themselves."

Leo wrote the cover story about his aunt's night on a {{volcano}} in Sicily: the trembling ground, the {{crust}} like a pot lid, the orange river of magma behind it. His headline was simply, "The Earth Has a Lid."

My own page was about water. I described how the sea {{evaporate|evaporates}} into {{vapour}}, how the vapour travels and falls, and how rivers {{erode}} valleys in the mountains and then, growing tired, drop their mud and build {{delta}}s at the sea. To illustrate it, I borrowed a drawing of the water cycle from Mr. Rossi at the weather station, and added his record at the bottom: "{{Forecast|Forecasts}} made: 20. Forecasts correct: 16. Attitude: proud anyway."

Anna interviewed her sister Clara by satellite phone from the {{antarctic|Antarctic}} — from the very bottom of the {{globe}}, where the windows grow {{frost}} flowers on the inside and the summer sun refuses to set.

Wei sent photographs from his {{remote}} village: the green {{oasis}} after three years of {{drought}}, the melon fields the farmers {{fertilise|fertilised}} with such care, and the sharp line where the desert simply stops.

The club's autumn climb filled two pages: the {{glacier}} like a frozen river beneath the summit, the {{pebble}}s we gathered from the stream, and the small {{magnet}} Ms. Lin carried to test which rocks held iron. My cousin Ruby sent a panorama of the canyon where she works — the layered rock so {{magnificent}} that the editor, which is to say me, printed it across two full pages.

The darkest page belonged to a guest writer from the town with the grey river, who described the year the {{pollution}} arrived and what it cost — and warned that some damage is {{irreversible}}, so prevention is always the cheaper choice. The bravest page came from a boy on the Chilean coast, whose town walked up the hill ahead of a {{tsunami}} and watched, from safety, while the sea took the streets.

On the back cover we printed my photograph of the partial {{eclipse}} from grandmother's island — the sun with a bite taken out of it — above a single line from Ms. Lin: "The {{atmosphere}} you are breathing, the {{breeze}} turning this page, the paper made from trees that drank the rain that fell from the sea — it is all one subject. That is why we call it Earth studies."
tr:
学年最后一个星期五，林老师给地理社团布置了最后一项任务：做一本杂志。“十二页，”她说，把一摞白纸拍在桌上，“写这颗星球今年让我们看到的一切。明年的社团读到它会以为我们在夸张。很好——让他们自己来看看。”

利奥写了封面故事，讲他阿姨在西西里一座火山（volcano）上过夜的经历：颤抖的大地、像锅盖一样的地壳（crust）、锅盖后面橙色的岩浆之河。他的标题只有一句：“地球有一口锅盖。”

我负责的版面写水。我描写海水如何蒸发（evaporate）成水汽（vapour），水汽如何旅行、落下；河流如何在山间侵蚀（erode）出峡谷，又如何像走累了似的卸下泥沙，在入海口堆出三角洲（delta）。配图是从气象站罗西先生那里借来的水循环示意图，我在图下加了他一年的战绩：“预报（forecast）次数：20。预报正确：16。态度：依然自豪。”

安娜通过卫星电话，采访了远在南极（antarctic）——地球仪（globe）最底端——的姐姐克拉拉：那里的窗子内侧开满霜（frost）花，夏季的太阳拒绝落山。

韦从他偏僻（remote）的村庄寄来了照片：三年干旱（drought）之后重新变绿的绿洲（oasis），农民们精心施肥（fertilise）的瓜田，还有沙漠戛然而止的那条界线。

社团秋天的登山占了两个版面：山顶下像冻结河流的冰川（glacier），我们从溪水里捡回的鹅卵石（pebble），还有林老师随身携带、用来检验岩石是否含铁的小磁铁（magnet）。我的表姐露比寄来一张她工作的峡谷的全景照——层层岩石壮观（magnificent）得让主编（也就是我）直接把它铺满了两个版面。

最沉重的一页来自一位客座作者，来自那条灰河边的小镇。他写污染（pollution）降临的那一年和它夺走的一切，并警告说：有些破坏是不可逆（irreversible）的，所以预防永远是最便宜的选择。最勇敢的一页来自智利海岸的一个男孩，他的小镇赶在海啸（tsunami）之前走上了山，在安全处看着大海收走了街道。
