quiz.ex: brake = 刹车。hit the brakes 踩刹车。brake lights 刹车灯。对比 break（打破）——同音不同义。

quiz.q: Sixty horsepower — the old unit of engine power, literally the pulling of sixty horses. Horsepower is —
quiz.ex: horsepower = 马力（功率单位）。缩写 hp。瓦特为对比蒸汽机与马而发明。

quiz.q: The intersection — the place where two roads cross and negotiate — is where you will have your first religious experience. An intersection is —
o: the building where cars are mended
the slow emperor of country lanes
the channel beside a country road
where two or more roads cross
quiz.ex: intersection = 交叉路口（美式）；交集（数学）。intersect 相交。英式常说 crossroads/junction。

quiz.q: The lorry — the British word for the great goods vehicle the Americans call a truck. A lorry is —
o: a large goods vehicle, in British English
a passenger carriage pedalled by a cyclist
quiz.ex: lorry = 卡车（英式）。美式用 truck。a lorry driver 卡车司机。

quiz.q: The curb — the stone edge where road meets pavement, which the tyre must never meet. A curb is —
o: the stone edge between road and pavement
the payment demanded for a ride
the urgent vehicle with a siren
quiz.ex: curb = 路缘（美式，英式 kerb）；动词"抑制"（curb inflation 抑制通胀）。

quiz.q: The hazard — any danger on the road, and also the orange lights you flash to warn of one. A hazard is —
o: the meter that ticks like a heart
the quiet channel beside a road
a danger or source of risk
quiz.ex: hazard = 危险、隐患。hazard lights 双闪警示灯。hazardous 危险的（hazardous waste 有害废物）。

quiz.q: An ambulance — the vehicle that carries the sick and injured, urgently — went past with its siren on. An ambulance is —
o: an emergency vehicle for the sick and injured
a vehicle for carrying goods in bulk
the electric carriage of the city
quiz.ex: ambulance = 救护车。call an ambulance 叫救护车。词根 ambul = 走（ambulant 能走动的）。

title: The Postmistress Explains a Parcel
text:
The parcel began, as most things do, with string. Mrs Mwangi, postmistress of the valley for twenty years, took the box of seeds, wrapped it in brown paper, and {{bind}}ed it — tied it fast with knots — because, she said, a {{parcel}} — the wrapped, addressed, posted thing itself — has one duty, which is to stay shut.

"The {{package}}," she told the customer, "is the general word for any wrapped thing, and the American word for this one; a {{packet}}, with its small ending, is the small flat kind — a packet of seeds, of biscuits, of photographs — and an {{envelope}} is the flat paper sleeve that carries a letter and no more." She weighed it. "The {{mail}} — the postal system, and everything it carries, considered as one great slow river — will take it; the {{postage}} — the charge for carrying it — is four dollars; the {{stamp}}" — the small gummed square that proves payment, the collecting of which has ruined better people than us — "goes here, in the corner, like a small flag."

"Words of the service," she said, stamping. "{{Express}} — the fast one, which arrives tomorrow and costs treble; or the ordinary, which arrives when it arrives. The {{carrier}} — the company, or the man, or the lorry, or the airline, that carries — is written here. And the grand verb is to {{convey}} — to carry something from one place to another, the word used in contracts and in court."

The parcel would {{travel}} — go from place to place, the verb wearing the broadest shoes — nearly twelve thousand kilometres. It would be {{load}}ed — lifted aboard as cargo — among the {{freight}} — the technical word for goods carried in bulk, cargo that is not passengers — onto a plane; it would sit in {{transit}} — the condition of being carried, neither here nor there, the parcel's purgatory — for two days; it would {{cross}} the equator and make its {{passage}} — the journey, and the old word for the right to make one — south; and at the far end another postman would {{deliver}} — bring it to the very door of the address — it into a sister's hands.

"Along the way it will learn the words for waiting," said Mrs Mwangi. "To {{postpone}} — to move an event to a later time — and to {{defer}} — the same, but wearing a suit, said of decisions and payments. Weather postpones; committees defer. It may rest a night in a {{rack}} — the frame built to hold things — among the {{luggage}} — the bags and cases of travellers, the word for what people carry when they themselves are the parcel — and it will find its {{way}} — its route, its means of getting — because that is what an address is: a way for everything that has one."

"Is a parcel a traveller?" asked the customer. "It makes a {{journey}}," said the postmistress, dropping it into the sack — "the act of travelling, the noun a parcel deserves as much as a person. But it cannot ask directions, or complain, or come home. That is the whole difference between freight and passengers, and why freight is better behaved."
tr:
包裹和大多数事物一样，从一根绳子开始。在山谷里当了二十年邮政所长的姆万吉夫人接过那盒种子，用牛皮纸包好，捆（bind，bind 指用绳结把它扎紧；过去式 bound）住——因为她说，一件包裹（parcel，parcel 指包好、写好地址、交了寄的这件东西本身）只有一个义务：一路不散。

“package（package，package 是任何包装之物的通称，也是美式英语里对 parcel 的说法），”她对顾客说，“是通称；packet（packet，packet 是小型扁平的那类——一包种子、一包饼干、一包照片）；而信封（envelope，envelope 是只装一封信的扁平纸套）。”她称了称。“邮政（mail，mail 指邮政系统，以及它所运送的一切，被看作一条缓慢的大河）会把它带走；邮资（postage，postage 指运送它收取的费用）是四块；邮票（stamp，stamp 是证明已付款的小小方纸片，集邮这件事毁掉过的正派人不比我们少）贴在这儿，角上，像一面小旗。”

“业务的词，”她盖章时说。“快件（express，express 是快的那种，明天到，价格三倍）；或者平邮，它什么时候到就什么时候到。承运人（carrier，carrier 指承运的公司，或者那个人、那辆卡车、那家航空公司）写在这儿。而那个气派的动词是 convey（convey，convey 指把某物从一处运往另一处，合同和法庭上用的词）。”

这件包裹将要旅行（travel，travel 指从一个地方到另一个地方，穿鞋最宽的那个动词）将近一万两千公里。它将被装载（load，load 指作为货物装上）在货运（freight，freight 是大宗货物运输的技术用词，不是乘客的那种货）之中、装上一架飞机；它将在转运（transit，transit 指“正在被运送”的状态，既不在此地也不在彼处，包裹的炼狱）里待两天；它将越过（cross，cross 指横穿、穿过）赤道，完成它的通路（passage，passage 指旅程，也是“通行权利”的老说法）向南；而在另一头，另一个邮递员会把它投递（deliver，deliver 指送到地址的那扇门前）到一位姐妹手里。

“一路上它还会学到等待的词，”姆万吉夫人说。“推迟（postpone，postpone 指把一件事挪到更晚的时间）和 defer（defer，defer 也是推迟，但穿着西装，用于决定和付款）。天气 postpone，委员会 defer。它也许会在行李架（rack，rack 指为放置东西而造的架子）上过一夜，混在行李（luggage，luggage 指旅客的箱包——人自己成了包裹时随身带的那些东西）中间；它会找到它的路（way，way 指路线、到达的办法），因为地址就是干这个的：给每件有地址的东西一条 way。”

“包裹算是旅行者吗？”顾客问。“它进行一场旅程（journey，journey 指旅行的行为，这个名词包裹和人都配得上），”女所长说着，把它投进邮袋——“可它不能问路，不能抱怨，不能回家。这就是货运与乘客的全部区别，也是货运更守规矩的原因。”

quiz.q: A parcel — the wrapped, addressed, posted thing itself — has one duty, which is to stay shut. A parcel is —
o: a wrapped thing sent by post
the flat sleeve carrying a letter
the small gummed proof of payment
quiz.ex: parcel = 包裹；一小块地（a parcel of land）。part and parcel of 固定搭配：……的主要部分。

quiz.q: A packet, with its small ending, is the small flat kind — a packet of seeds, of biscuits, of photographs. A packet is —
o: the slow river of the postal system
the right to make a journey
quiz.ex: packet = 小包；一盒（a packet of cigarettes 一包烟）。英国也指"班轮"（a packet boat）。

quiz.q: The grand verb is to convey — to carry something from one place to another, the word used in contracts and in court. To convey means —
o: to carry from one place to another
to move an event to a later time
quiz.ex: convey = 运送；传达（convey information 传递信息）。名词 conveyance 运输；运输工具。

quiz.q: Among the freight — the technical word for goods carried in bulk, cargo that is not passengers. Freight is —
o: the bags and cases of travellers
the frame built to hold things
the company that does the carrying
quiz.ex: freight = 货运；货物。freight train 货运列车。air freight 空运。对比 cargo（船/飞机上的货）。

quiz.q: It would sit in transit — the condition of being carried, neither here nor there, the parcel's purgatory. Transit is —
o: the act of tying with string
the state of being carried between places
quiz.ex: transit = 运输、转运；过境。in transit 在途。the London Transit 伦敦公交系统。transit visa 过境签证。

quiz.q: To defer — the same as postpone, but wearing a suit, said of decisions and payments. To defer means —
o: to deliver to the very door
quiz.ex: defer = 推迟；服从（defer to sb 尊重某人意见）。名词 deferral 延期。对比 postpone（日常用词）。

quiz.q: Among the luggage — the bags and cases of travellers, what people carry when they themselves are the parcel. Luggage is —
o: the postal system as a river
quiz.ex: luggage = 行李（英式，不可数）。luggage rack 行李架。美式多说 baggage。hand luggage 随身行李。

quiz.q: It would cross the equator and make its passage — the journey, and the old word for the right to make one. A passage is —
o: the payment demanded for a ride
a small flat package of seeds
a journey, or the right of travel
quiz.ex: passage = 通道；航程；（文章）段落。bird of passage 候鸟；过客。passenger 由它而来。

title: The Suitcase of a Traveller
text:
Every object in Mrs Whitcombe's spare room had been somewhere, and on her grandson's twelfth birthday she opened the old suitcase and let each one speak.

First came the {{atlas}} — the book of maps, named for the titan made to hold up the sky, which is what every map does — worn soft at the page for Africa. "You make an {{itinerary}} — the planned route of a journey, the list of days and places — and then life amends it. You {{navigate}} — find and steer your way, a word born on ships that now lives in every phone — by it, and you learn that the {{path}} — the narrow track made by walking, the way animals and then people agreed on — is older than every {{avenue}} — the broad, tree-lined city street, and by extension any means towards a goal — and both are older than the {{rail}}." The {{rail}} — the steel bar on which the wheels run, and the line of them together — had carried her across Siberia in a {{carriage}} — the railway's passenger compartment, and before the railway, the horse-drawn equivalent — hauled by a {{locomotive}} — the engine of a train, a machine that loves only one direction. "The British call the system the {{railway}}," she said, "the Americans the {{railroad}}, and it is the only word the two nations have ever agreed to disagree about politely."

"In New York I rode the {{subway}} — the American word for the underground city railway — and in London the {{underground}}, which is the British one; both go through the {{tunnel}} — the passage bored under ground or water, the earth's own corridor — at a {{velocity}} — the physicist's word for speed in a given direction — that felt, to the body, like standing still. The trains were {{swift}} — fast, quick, an old word for a fast bird — but the cities above them were swifter."

She held up a small tin camel. "The {{safari}} — the overland expedition, the word Swahili gave the world — in Kenya, when the {{attraction}}s — the things that attract, that draw the traveller — were animals, and not wifi. We stood in a {{lull}} — a quiet interval, a temporary stillness — between the dawn {{parade}} — the ordered marching procession, of soldiers here, of wildebeest there — and the noon heat. The best {{signpost}} — the post at a roadside carrying directions — I ever met was in Wales: it pointed at two villages and a waterfall and gave no distances at all."

A postcard of Egypt: "the {{pyramid}}s — the oldest architecture on earth that still keeps its shape — and the {{memorial}} at El Alamein — the monument built for remembering, for the dead who cannot attend — which I visited with your grandfather. A boy asked me to {{parachute}} — to fall slowly from the sky under a canopy — over the desert once, and I said no, and I have regretted it for fifty years."

"In Cairo the crowd would {{crush}} — press and crowd together, unbearably — at the station at six; by seven it would {{vanish}} — disappear entirely, as if switched off — like water finding its level. People {{disappear}} — cease to be seen — into their evenings; cities vanish into theirs."

"And this," she said, holding up nothing at all, "is the smell of the sea at Wreck Point. A {{wreck}} — the remains of a destroyed thing, most often a ship — gave the bay its name, and the old house is one of my {{haunt}}s — a place one frequents; also a place ghosts frequent, and both are true of it. A traveller's {{burden}} — the load she carries, physical or otherwise — is never the suitcase. It is the list of places she has promised to return to."
tr:
惠特科姆太太 spare room——备用间——里的每一样东西都去过什么地方；孙子十二岁生日那天，她打开那只旧手提箱，让每一件东西开口。

先来的是地图册（atlas，atlas 是地图的书，得名于被迫扛着天的大力神阿特拉斯——每张地图干的就是这个），非洲那一页已经磨软了。“你做行程（itinerary，itinerary 指旅程的计划路线，日子和地点的清单）——然后生活来修改它。你靠它导航（navigate，navigate 指寻找并掌控路线，一个生在船上、如今住在每部手机里的词），然后你发现小径（path，path 是走出来的窄路，动物先同意、人类后同意的那条）比每一条大道（avenue，avenue 是宽阔的林荫城市大街，引申为通往目标的任何途径）都古老，而它们都比铁轨老。”铁路（rail，rail 是车轮在其上滚动的钢轨，也是钢轨连成的那条线）曾载着她坐着一节车厢（carriage，carriage 指铁路的载客车厢；在铁路出现之前是马拉的同类物）横穿西伯利亚，牵引它的是一台机车（locomotive，locomotive 是火车头，一台只爱一个方向的机器）。“英国人管这套系统叫 railway（railway，英式‘铁路’），”她说，“美国人叫 railroad（railroad，美式‘铁路’），这是两个民族唯一礼貌地各执一词的词。”

“在纽约我坐地铁（subway，subway 是美式英语的地下城市铁路），在伦敦我坐 underground（underground，英式的同一样东西）；两者都穿过隧道（tunnel，tunnel 是在地下或水下凿出的通道，大地自己的走廊），以一种速度（velocity，velocity 是物理学家说的、带方向的速度）——身体却感觉像站着不动。列车迅捷（swift，swift 指快、敏捷，一个原本形容飞鸟的老词），可列车上面的城市更迅捷。”

她举起一只小小的锡骆驼。“那次东非猎游（safari，safari 指陆路远征，斯瓦希里语送给世界的词）——在肯尼亚，那时吸引物（attraction，attraction 指吸引人、招徕旅行者的东西）还是动物，而不是无线网络。我们站在一段间歇（lull，lull 指安静的间歇、暂时的平静）里——在黎明的列队行进（parade，parade 指有序的行进队列：这儿是士兵，那儿是角马）与正午的酷热之间。我见过最好的路标（signpost，signpost 是路边指示方向立柱）在威尔士：它指着两个村子和一道瀑布，一个距离也不给。”

一张埃及的明信片：“金字塔（pyramid，pyramid 是地球上至今还保持形状的最老建筑）；阿拉曼的纪念碑（memorial，memorial 指为纪念而建、为无法出席的死者而立的碑）——我是和你祖父一起去的。有个男孩曾约我在沙漠上空跳伞（parachute，parachute 指撑着一顶伞盖从天上缓缓落下），我说不去，为此我后悔了五十年。”

“在开罗，六点钟的人群会在车站挤（crush，crush 指挤压、拥挤到难以忍受）；到七点就会消失（vanish，vanish 指彻底不见，像被关了开关）——像水找到自己的平面。人消失（disappear，disappear 指从视野里不见）进各自的夜晚；城市消失进它们的夜晚。”

“还有这个，”她什么也没拿出来地举起手，“是沉船角的海的味道。一艘沉船（wreck，wreck 指被毁之物的残骸，最常是船）给了海湾这个名字，而那座老房子是我的常去之地（haunt，haunt 指常去的地方；也指鬼魂常出没的地方——对它来说两样都真）。旅行家的负担（burden，burden 指她背负的担子，身体的或别的）从来不是手提箱，而是她答应过要回去的那些地方的清单。”

quiz.q: First came the atlas — the book of maps, named for the titan made to hold up the sky. An atlas is —
o: a planned list of days and places
the steel bar the wheels run on
quiz.ex: atlas = 地图册。得名于希腊神话擎天神 Atlas。road atlas 公路地图册。

quiz.q: You make an itinerary — the planned route of a journey, the list of days and places — and then life amends it. An itinerary is —
o: the act of steering a ship
a planned travel route and schedule
quiz.ex: itinerary = 行程表、路线。travel itinerary 旅行日程。词根 iter（路，拉丁语）。

quiz.q: You navigate — find and steer your way, a word born on ships that now lives in every phone. To navigate means —
o: to find and direct one's way
to hold up the sky like a titan
to fall slowly under a canopy
quiz.ex: navigate = 导航；驾驶（船/飞机）。navigation 航海术；navigator 领航员。词根 navis（船）。

quiz.q: Hauled by a locomotive — the engine of a train, a machine that loves only one direction. A locomotive is —
o: the passage bored under a river
the remains of a destroyed ship
quiz.ex: locomotive = 火车头、机车。loco（地方）+ motive（动的）：从一个地方挪到另一个地方的。

quiz.q: In New York I rode the subway — the American word for the underground city railway; in London, the underground. A subway is —
quiz.ex: subway = 地铁（美式）；地下通道（英式）。英式地铁叫 the underground 或 the tube。注意英美差异。

quiz.q: The safari — the overland expedition, the word Swahili gave the world — in Kenya. A safari is —
o: an overland expedition, especially in Africa
the quiet between parade and noon
quiz.ex: safari = （东非）游猎、陆上远征。来自斯瓦希里语（旅程）。go on safari 去游猎。

quiz.q: A wreck — the remains of a destroyed thing, most often a ship — gave the bay its name. A wreck is —
o: a fast bird or swift train
quiz.ex: wreck = 残骸；（船只）失事。shipwreck 海难。nervous wreck 精神崩溃的人。动词：使失事。

quiz.q: A traveller's burden — the load she carries, physical or otherwise — is never the suitcase. A burden is —
o: the pressing crowd at a station
the list of planned days and places
a heavy load, physical or emotional
the canopy that slows a fall
quiz.ex: burden = 负担、重担。burden of proof 举证责任。动词 burden sb with sth 使背负。

title: The Model United Nations
text:
Every March St Brendan's School held its Model United Nations, and this year the smallest delegate was Nadia of Year 11, who had drawn the card that said NEW ZEALAND and had spent a fortnight learning to say "we agree with Canada" in three tones of voice.

The hall was hung with the paper flags of sixty {{nation}}s — a nation being a people and its country considered as one political family — and each row of desks was a {{delegation}} — the group sent to represent a country, its interests, and its patience. Nadia, alone, was the entire delegation of {{new zealand}}, a country famous for sheep, rugby, and being awake before everyone else.

Around her the world rehearsed itself. The {{britain}} delegate spoke with borrowed authority; {{france}} apologised for nothing; {{germany}} arrived with statistics; the {{italian}} delegate's charm won three laughs and one abstention; {{canada}} apologised to everyone, including the chairs; {{australia}} voted early and often; the {{swiss}} delegate remained neutral even in the lunch queue; the {{russian}} delegate, dressed as though the {{soviet}} union — the adjective of the USSR, the union that no longer exists — were still taking the minutes, argued grandly and lost beautifully; and the {{portuguese}} delegate, for a small country with an oceanic past, reminded the room that empires are weather, not architecture.

Older words came from older delegations. The {{greek}} delegate, for the country that invented voting, kept order in the assembly; the {{roman}} delegate answered her in {{latin}} — the language of the {{roman}} Empire, dead these fifteen centuries and still voting; the {{indian}} delegate spoke for the largest democracy on earth; the {{jewish}} delegate spoke for a country younger than her grandmother; the {{arabian}} delegate spoke for the peninsula of the same name; and the {{african}} delegates sat together, forty nations in one bloc, waiting, with the patience of continents, for the room to notice that most of the {{global}} problems under discussion — global meaning of the whole globe, worldwide — had been drawn on their map first.

The crisis, this year, was a famine in the Horn of Africa. Money was wanted from {{overseas}} — from beyond the seas — and from home; the {{foreign}} ministries — foreign meaning of, from, or concerning other countries — would have to be persuaded; the {{worldwide}} response would be coordinated, or not. Nadia's brother, who was studying {{abroad}} — in another country, the word that lives in every parent's worry — had told her on the phone: when people are hungry, do not ask whose flag feeds them.

In the last hour the great delegations locked themselves into rival resolutions. A {{bilateral}} agreement — bilateral meaning between exactly two countries, the easiest kind to sign and the hardest to widen — was proposed between the American and Russian blocs, and the room divided along the old lines. Nadia, who had not spoken all day, stood up. "New Zealand proposes one small amendment. Honourable delegates are arguing about who leads the convoy. In the South Pacific we say: the canoe that argues about the mast arrives after the storm. Let the food go first, and the flags follow."

The hall was quiet, and then it was not. The amendment passed, forty-one nations to nine, and the Secretary-General brought down his mallet. Afterwards the {{european}} bloc — european meaning of Europe, the adjective that believes itself a continent — invited Nadia to draft the final communiqué, and the {{league}} — the old, idealistic word for an association of nations, attempted after the last war and lost — was, for one afternoon, in one school hall, briefly and imperfectly, real.
tr:
每年三月，圣布伦丹学校都会举办模拟联合国，而今年最小的代表是十一年级的纳迪娅——她抽到写着“新西兰”的牌子，花了两星期学会用三种语气说“我们同意加拿大”。

礼堂里挂着六十个国家的纸旗（nation，nation 指一个民族及其国家，被视为一个政治大家庭）；每排课桌是一支代表团（delegation，delegation 指被派去代表一个国家的那群人，连同它的利益和耐心）。纳迪娅一个人，就是整个新西兰（new zealand，以羊、橄榄球和比谁都醒得早闻名的国家）代表团。

她周围，世界在预演。英国（britain）代表带着借来的权威发言；法国（france）不为任何事道歉；德国（germany）带着统计数据到场；意大利（italian，italian 指“意大利的”）代表的魅力赢得三声笑和一次弃权；加拿大（canada）向所有人道歉，包括向主席；澳大利亚（australia）早投票、多投票；瑞士（swiss）代表连排队吃午饭都保持中立；俄罗斯（russian）代表——穿得好像苏联（soviet，soviet 是 USSR 的形容词，那个已不复存在的联盟）还在做会议记录似的——大张旗鼓地争辩、体面地输掉；葡萄牙（portuguese）代表——为一个有着海洋史的袖珍国家代言——提醒全场：帝国是天气，不是建筑。

更老的词来自更老的代表团。希腊（greek）代表来自发明投票的那个国家，维持着会场秩序；罗马（roman）代表用拉丁语（latin，latin 是罗马帝国的语言，死了十五个世纪却还在投票）回答她；印度（indian）代表为地球上最大的民主国家发言；犹太（jewish）代表为一个比她祖母还年轻的国家发言；阿拉伯（arabian）代表为同名半岛发言；而非洲（african）代表们坐在一起，四十个国家组成一个集团，以大陆的耐心等着全场注意到：正在讨论的大部分全球（global，global 指全世界的、整个地球的）问题，最先画在他们的地图上。

今年的危机是非洲之角的饥荒。要钱，从海外（overseas，overseas 指大海之外的地方）要，也从国内要；各国外交（foreign，foreign 指其他国家的、与外国相关的）部门必须被说服；遍及全球（worldwide，worldwide 指遍布全世界的）的响应将得到协调——或者得不到。纳迪娅的哥哥在国外（abroad，abroad 指在另一个国家，住在每个家长担忧里的那个词）读书，他在电话里对她说过：人饿肚子的时候，别问粮食打着谁的旗。

最后一小时，大国代表团把自己锁进了相互对立的决议里。有人提出一份双边（bilateral，bilateral 指恰好在两国之间的——最好签、最难扩大的那种）协议——美俄两个集团之间——会场沿着旧的界线分裂。全天没发过言的纳迪娅站了起来。“新西兰提出一个小小的修正案。各位尊敬的代表在为谁带队争执。在南太平洋我们说：争吵桅杆的独木舟，风暴过后才到。让粮食先走，旗子跟在后面。”

会场先是安静，然后不再安静。修正案以四十一票对九票通过，秘书长落下了木槌。会后，欧洲（european，european 指“欧洲的”，一个相信自己是大洲的形容词）集团邀请纳迪娅起草最后公报——而国际联盟（league，league 指国家间的联合，那个在上次大战后尝试过又失败了的理想主义的词），在一个下午、一间学校礼堂里，短暂地、不完美地，真实了一次。

quiz.q: Each row of desks was a delegation — the group sent to represent a country, its interests, and its patience. A delegation is —
o: the language of a dead empire
the cloth emblem flown from a pole
an agreement between exactly two countries
a group sent to represent a country or body
quiz.ex: delegation = 代表团；授权（delegate 委派；代表）。delegate duties 分派任务。

quiz.q: A bilateral agreement — between exactly two countries, the easiest kind to sign and the hardest to widen. Bilateral means —
o: of a country beyond the seas
carried out by the UN alone
quiz.ex: bilateral = 双边的。bi-（二）+ lateral（边的）。bilateral talks 双边会谈。对比 multilateral 多边的、unilateral 单边的。

quiz.q: The foreign ministries — foreign meaning of, from, or concerning other countries — would have to be persuaded. Foreign means —
o: taking no side in a dispute
quiz.ex: foreign = 外国的；陌生的（a foreign concept 陌生概念）。foreign affairs 外交事务；foreign currency 外币。

quiz.q: Money was wanted from overseas — from beyond the seas — and from home. Overseas means —
o: of the whole globe at once
in or to a foreign land across the sea
quiz.ex: overseas = 海外的。overseas students 留学生。overseas market 海外市场。对比 abroad（在国外）。

quiz.q: The worldwide response would be coordinated, or not — worldwide meaning everywhere in the world. Worldwide means —
quiz.ex: worldwide = 全世界的。worldwide web 环球网（WWW）。对比 global（全球的，常指全局性影响）。

quiz.q: The league — the old, idealistic word for an association of nations, attempted after the last war and lost. A league is —
o: an association of nations or groups for common action
a group sent to represent one country
quiz.ex: league = 联盟；联赛（the Premier League 英超）。the League of Nations 国际联盟（联合国前身）。in league with 与……勾结。

quiz.q: Her brother was studying abroad — in another country, the word that lives in every parent's worry. Abroad means —
o: in or to a foreign country
quiz.ex: abroad = 在国外。go abroad 出国。at home and abroad 国内外。注意：不加 to/in（study abroad 不说 study in abroad）。

quiz.q: Dressed as though the Soviet union — the adjective of the USSR, the union that no longer exists — were still taking the minutes. Soviet refers to —
o: the peninsula of the Arabian desert
the former USSR and its system
quiz.ex: soviet = 苏维埃的；苏联的。the Soviet Union 苏联（1991 年解体）。俄语本义"委员会"。

title: A Morning at the Town Hall
text:
Mrs Osei, newly arrived, went to the town hall to register, and the clerk, who had been born in the building and would retire in it, gave her the tour with the vocabulary attached.

"You are now a {{resident}} — one who lives in a place, with rights and duties there — and, when the paperwork succeeds, a {{citizen}} — a full member of the state, entitled to its protection and liable for its taxes. The {{state}} — the political organisation of a country, or, in America, one of its provinces — runs in layers, like weather.

"The {{government}} — the group that governs, the ministers and their machinery — sits at the top. The {{parliament}} — the elected assembly that makes the laws — meets in the capital; the {{administration}} — the managing of public affairs, and the people who manage them — carries out what it decides. In a {{republic}} — a state whose head is elected, not inherited — the {{president}} is that head; in other systems the {{premier}} — the first minister, the head of the government's business — leads, while the monarch merely opens flower shows. Beneath them sit the {{minister}}s — the heads of the great offices of state.

"Around the ministers, the machinery: the {{department}}s — the divisions of a government, each with its territory, health or transport or war; the {{bureau}}s — the smaller official offices, the word the French gave us for desk, and the desk's descendants; the {{bureaucracy}} — the whole system of officials, forms and waiting rooms, the word people pronounce with a sigh; the {{federal}} level — the word for a system in which power is shared between a central government and its regions; and closest to your door, the {{municipal}} one — of the town, the city, its own elected layer — where the {{mayor}} — the elected head of a city — argues about parking. The {{senate}} — the upper chamber, where bills go to grow older — reviews what the lower chamber sends up. And an {{office}}, mind you, is both a position of authority and the room it lives in.

"Your part in all this is small and enormous. Your {{vote}} — your formal choice, expressed in an election — is one among thousands. You {{elect}} the council — choose it by voting; you may one day be {{nominate}}d — formally proposed as a candidate — yourself. A {{poll}} — the counting of votes, or the sampling of opinions before them — will tell you what your neighbours think. {{Democracy}} — rule by the people — is the worst system ever devised, except for the others, and it is kept alive by exactly this: the {{authority}} — the right to decide, and the body that holds it — answering to the people who filed past this desk.

"What the state does for you are the {{service}}s — water, fire, libraries, the sweeping of streets; how anything official happens is the {{process}} — the sequence of steps, forms, and queues by which a decision becomes a stamp; and where it all is organised from is the {{headquarters}} — the main office of an organisation, the building that loses the letters."

"And this," said the clerk, stamping her form, "is the {{process}} by which you become registered: twenty minutes and one stamp. We call that efficiency. The capital calls it a miracle."
tr:
刚搬来的奥塞夫人去市政厅登记；那位生在这栋楼、也将退休在这栋楼里的办事员，把带着词汇的导览送给了她。

“您现在是一位居民（resident，resident 指住在某地、在当地享有权利并承担义务的人）；手续成功之后，您还是一位公民（citizen，citizen 指国家的正式成员，受国家保护、也向国家纳税）。国家（state，state 指一个国家的政治组织；在美国也指它的一个州）像天气一样分层运行。

“政府（government，government 指执政的集团、各位部长及其机器）在顶层。议会（parliament，parliament 指制定法律的民选大会）在首都开会；行政（administration，administration 指公共事务的管理，也指做管理的人）执行它的决定。在共和国（republic，republic 指元首由选举而非继承产生的国家），总统（president，president 指那位元首）是首脑；在另一些体制里，总理（premier，premier 指首席部长、政府事务的首脑）主事，君主只负责为花展开幕。他们之下是各位部长（minister，minister 指国家各大臣/部长的首长）。

“部长周围是机器：部（department，department 指政府的各 division，各管一方——卫生、交通、战争）；局（bureau，bureau 指较小的官署，法语送给我们的“写字台”一词和它的后裔）；官僚体系（bureaucracy，bureaucracy 指官员、表格和候审室构成的整套系统，人们叹着气念出来的那个词）；联邦（federal，federal 指中央政府与地方分享权力的那套体制）这一层；而离您的门最近的，是市政（municipal，municipal 指城市自己的、自治市镇的那层）——市长（mayor，mayor 指城市的民选首脑）在那儿为停车位吵架。参议院（senate，senate 指议会上院，法案去那儿变老）复审下院送上来的东西。而 office（office，office 既指权力的职位，也指职位所在的房间），请您注意，一身兼二职。

“您在这一切里的份额很小，也大得吓人。您的选票（vote，vote 指选举中正式表达的选择）是千万张中的一张。您选举（elect，elect 指用投票选出）市议会；也许有一天您自己会被提名（nominate，nominate 指作为候选人被正式提出）。民调（poll，poll 指计票，也指投票前的民意抽样）会告诉您邻居们想什么。民主（democracy，democracy 指人民统治）是迄今设计出的最糟的制度——除了其他所有制度之外——而维持它生命的正是这件事：权力机关（authority，authority 指决定之权，也指掌握它的机构）向从这个桌子前走过的人们负责。

“国家为您做的事叫服务（service，service 指水、消防、图书馆、扫街）；任何官方事务得以发生的方式叫程序（process，process 指决定变成一枚图章所经过的步骤、表格和队伍）；而这一切从中组织起来的地方叫总部（headquarters，headquarters 指一个组织的主办公室，专门丢信的那栋楼）。

“而这，”办事员在她的表格上盖章，“就是您完成登记的程序：二十分钟，一枚图章。我们管这叫效率。首府管这叫奇迹。”

quiz.q: You are now a resident, and, when the paperwork succeeds, a citizen — a full member of the state, entitled to its protection and liable for its taxes. A citizen is —
o: a full member of a state, with rights and duties
one who merely lives in a place
the elected head of a city
the upper chamber of a parliament
quiz.ex: citizen = 公民；市民。citizenship 公民身份。senior citizen 老年人。对比 resident（居民）。

o: the elected assembly that makes laws
the counting of votes on election day
the sharing of power with regions

quiz.q: The bureaucracy — the whole system of officials, forms and waiting rooms, the word people pronounce with a sigh. Bureaucracy is —
o: the main office of an organisation
the system of official rules and administrators
the sequence of steps to a stamp
quiz.ex: bureaucracy = 官僚体系。bureau（局）+ cracy（统治）。反讽用法常见。 bureaucrat 官僚。

quiz.q: The federal level — the word for a system in which power is shared between a central government and its regions. Federal means —
o: of a system sharing power between centre and regions
of the town and its parking disputes
of the head of state's household
of the counting of public votes

quiz.q: Closest to your door, the municipal one — of the town, the city, its own elected layer. Municipal means —
o: of a town or city and its government
of a country beyond the seas
quiz.ex: municipal = 市政的。municipal services 市政服务。the municipality 市政当局。对比 federal（联邦的）。

quiz.q: In other systems the premier — the first minister, the head of the government's business — leads, while the monarch opens flower shows. A premier is —
o: the elected head of a city
a position and the room it sits in
the head of a government's business
quiz.ex: premier = 总理、首相。法语 premier（第一）。the British premier 英国首相。

quiz.q: A poll — the counting of votes, or the sampling of opinions before them — will tell you what your neighbours think. A poll is —
o: a formal proposal of a candidate
a count of votes, or an opinion survey
the protection owed by the state
quiz.ex: poll = 民意调查；投票。opinion poll 民调。go to the polls 去投票。pollster 民调机构。

quiz.q: Where it all is organised from is the headquarters — the main office of an organisation, the building that loses the letters. Headquarters is —
o: the main office of an organisation
the elected assembly of a country
the division in charge of health
the sequence of steps and queues
quiz.ex: headquarters = 总部（缩写 HQ）。army headquarters 军队司令部。单复数同形。

title: The Last Lesson
text:
Mr Almeida's last history lesson was about their own country, which he drew on the board as one long line.

"We began," he said, "with a {{crown}} — the monarch's headpiece, and by extension the monarchy itself — and a {{throne}} — the seat of the king, and the power that sits in it. The {{reign}} of the last king — reign being the period during which a monarch rules — was thirty-one years, and the {{hierarchy}} beneath him — the ranked pyramid of power, duke above earl above peasant — was believed to be the will of God.

"Then the ships came, and the country became a {{colony}} — a territory ruled and settled by a foreign power, for that power's benefit. The flag on the fort changed; the {{regime}} — the ruling system, the word that quietly implies it may be temporary — changed with it. For a century the people farmed for another country's table.

"The {{revolution}} — the overthrow of a government; the word comes from astronomy, and means a full turn — came in the spring. They {{declare}}d — announced formally, with documents — {{independence}} — the condition of governing oneself — in the square, and a man stood on the fort wall to {{proclaim}} — to declare publicly and officially — the new republic. The monarchy's supporters {{claim}}ed — asserted, maintained to be true — that the king would return; history has outvoted them.

"The first republic was an {{egalitarian}} experiment — egalitarian meaning founded on the belief that all people are equal — and it did not survive its first winter. A general {{dominate}}d — ruled over absolutely, overshadowed everything — for a decade, and he was a {{puppet}} — a ruler controlled from elsewhere, a hand inside a glove — of interests he never met. The economy's {{meltdown}} — total collapse, the word borrowed from nuclear reactors — brought him down: when money dies, dictators follow it.

"The second republic tried {{socialism}} — the system of shared or state ownership — and read {{marxism}} — the theory that history is the story of class struggle, written by a man in the British Museum — aloud in its parliament. The neighbour went further, into {{communism}} — the system of common ownership, classless by intention, ruthless in practice. At home the trade {{union}}s — the associations of workers, bargain by bargain — grew strong; the regions {{unite}}d — joined together as one — behind a new constitution; and a genuine {{statesman}} — a person of political wisdom and long view, a word rare enough to be precious — steered the {{reform}}s — the changes that improve without destroying — of the 1990s: land, schools, the {{liberty}} of the press — liberty being freedom, the right to act and speak unafraid.

"The {{power}} — the capacity to rule, and the word for those who hold it — passed peacefully twice, which is all a republic can be asked to prove. The old king died in exile; his grandson {{succeed}}ed — inherited, followed into the position — to nothing at all, and the {{succession}} — the sequence by which a title or office is inherited — ended in a rented flat. The line on the board," said Mr Almeida, putting down the chalk, "is not straight, and it is not finished. That is the whole lesson. Go home and continue it."
tr:
阿尔梅达先生的最后一节历史课讲他们自己的国家，他在黑板上画了一条长线。

“我们从王冠（crown，crown 指君主的头冠，引申为君主制本身）和御座（throne，throne 指国王的座位，也指坐在上面的权力）开始。末代国王的统治期（reign，reign 指一位君主在位的那段时间）是三十一年，他脚下那个等级制（hierarchy，hierarchy 指权力的金字塔，公爵压着伯爵压着农民）被认为是神的旨意。

“然后船来了，这个国家成了殖民地（colony，colony 指被外国强权统治和移民定居、为该强权利益经营的领土）。堡垒上的旗换了；政权（regime，regime 指统治体制，这个词悄悄暗示它可能是暂时的）随之而变。一个世纪里，人民为另一个国家的餐桌耕种。

“革命（revolution，revolution 指推翻政府；这个词来自天文学，意思是转满一整圈）在春天到来。他们在广场上宣布（declare，declare 指以文件正式宣布）了独立（independence，independence 指自己治理自己的状态）；一个人站上堡垒的墙，宣告（proclaim，proclaim 指公开地、正式地昭告）新共和国成立。君主制的支持者声称（claim，claim 指断言、坚称）国王会回来；历史投了反对票。

“第一共和国是一场平等主义（egalitarian，egalitarian 指建立在人人平等信念之上的）实验，没熬过第一个冬天。一位将军支配（dominate，dominate 指绝对地统治、让一切黯然失色）了十年，而他是傀儡（puppet，puppet 指被别处操控的统治者，手套里的那只手）——被他从没见过的利益操纵着。经济的大崩溃（meltdown，meltdown 指彻底崩塌，从核反应堆借来的词）把他拉下了台：钱一死，独裁者跟着死。

“第二共和国试了社会主义（socialism，socialism 指共有或国有的体制），在议会里大声朗读马克思主义（marxism，marxism 指把历史看作阶级斗争史的学说，由一个大英博物馆里的人写成）。邻国走得更远，进入了共产主义（communism，communism 指意图上无阶级、实践中无情的公有制）。在国内，各工会（union，union 指工人的联合组织，一寸一寸地讨价还价）壮大起来；各地区在新宪法背后团结（unite，unite 指结成一体）起来；一位真正的政治家（statesman，statesman 指有政治智慧和长远眼光的人，一个稀有到珍贵的词）驾驭了九十年代的改革（reform，reform 指改良——不毁掉一切的改变）：土地、学校、出版自由（liberty，liberty 指自由，无所畏惧地行动和言论的权利）。

“权力（power，power 指统治的能力，也指掌握它的人）两次和平交接，这是一场共和制能被要求证明的全部。老国王死在流亡中；他的孙子继承（succeed，succeed 指继承、接任那个位置）了个空，而那场继承序列（succession，succession 指头衔或职位接替的顺序）终结在一套租来的公寓里。黑板上这条线，”阿尔梅达先生放下粉笔，“不直，也还没画完。这就是这节课的全部。回家去，把它接着画。”

quiz.q: The country became a colony — a territory ruled and settled by a foreign power, for that power's benefit. A colony is —
o: a territory ruled by a foreign power
the seat of the king and its power
a full turn of the astronomers
quiz.ex: colony = 殖民地；聚居区（artists' colony 艺术家聚居区）。colonise 殖民化。the colonies（英史）殖民地。

quiz.q: The regime — the ruling system, the word that quietly implies it may be temporary — changed with the flag. A regime is —
o: the sequence of inheriting a title
quiz.ex: regime = 政权、统治体制。the old regime 旧政权。也指"养生法"（fitness regime 健身计划）。

quiz.q: The revolution — the overthrow of a government; the word comes from astronomy, and means a full turn. A revolution is —
o: the belief that all people are equal
the total collapse of an economy
quiz.ex: revolution = 革命；旋转（天文学义）。the Industrial Revolution 工业革命。revolt 叛乱；revolve 旋转。

quiz.q: A man stood on the fort wall to proclaim — to declare publicly and officially — the new republic. To proclaim means —
o: to assert quietly to be true
to inherit a throne in exile
quiz.ex: proclaim = 宣告、声明。proclaim independence 宣布独立。名词 proclamation 宣言。对比 claim（声称）。

quiz.q: The first republic was an egalitarian experiment — founded on the belief that all people are equal. Egalitarian means —
o: believing in rule by one general
believing in the will of God
quiz.ex: egalitarian = 平等主义的。来自法语 égal（平等）。an egalitarian society 平等社会。

quiz.q: He was a puppet — a ruler controlled from elsewhere, a hand inside a glove. A puppet is —
o: the head of state who is elected
quiz.ex: puppet = 傀儡；木偶。puppet government 傀儡政府。puppet regime 傀儡政权。

quiz.q: A genuine statesman — a person of political wisdom and long view, a word rare enough to be precious. A statesman is —
o: the head of a workers' union
quiz.ex: statesman = 政治家（褒义）。对比 politician（政客，常含贬义）。elder statesman 元老。

quiz.q: The succession — the sequence by which a title or office is inherited — ended in a rented flat. Succession is —
o: the sequence of inheriting a position
quiz.ex: succession = 继承（顺序）；连续。in succession 连续地。a succession of failures 一连串失败。动词 succeed（继承；成功）。

title: The Field Officer's Report
text:
Amara's monthly report was due on Friday, and like every field officer of the {{aid}} agency — aid meaning help, especially help from one country or organisation to another that cannot manage alone — she wrote it twice: once for the donors, and once for herself.

She had been born in the {{slum}} she now served — the overcrowded, run-down district of a city, packed and unequal — and this fact did more for her work than her degree had. Her parents had {{emigrate}}d — left their own country to settle in another — when she was two; she had {{immigrate}}d — arrived to settle in a country not originally hers — back at twenty-five, with a degree and a debt of memory. Outside the district office — a shipping container with a fire extinguisher and a notice about {{safety}} — the condition of being safe from danger — the queue at the tap was already long.

Her mornings were for the water project. Her job was to {{monitor}} — to watch and check regularly, over time, the way a nurse takes a pulse; to {{implement}} — to carry out, to put into effect — the plan; to follow the {{guideline}}s — the written advice on how to act — and the {{checklist}} — the list of things to be verified, ticked one at a time — that the head office sent with them. The {{community}} — the people of the place, considered together — had built the tap-stands themselves; her role was to {{assist}} — to help, to support — and never, in public, to lead. "The {{proposal}} — the formal written plan, the document that asks for money — promised twenty taps," she wrote. "The district has nineteen. The twentieth is a question of pipe, not of will."

Afternoons were for the shelter. Two families had applied for {{asylum}} — protection granted by a country to people fleeing danger in their own — and were waiting on the paperwork; the old {{refuge}} — shelter, protection from danger, the word for the place and the state both — at the church was full. The {{welfare}} officer — welfare meaning the health, comfort and fortunes of people, especially as the state's care for them — came on Thursdays. The {{well-being}} of the district — the state of being comfortable, healthy and happy — could not be measured, Amara wrote in the margin, but it could be counted in washing lines.

Evenings were meetings. The elders' {{perspective}} — the way of seeing things, determined by where one stands — was that the project belonged to them; the engineer's {{standpoint}} — position, point of view, the place one argues from — was that pipes came before people; the teacher's {{viewpoint}} — opinion, the angle of looking — fell somewhere in between; and Amara's own {{outlook}} — the general attitude towards the future, the prospects as seen from here — was the only word for hope she had ever trusted. What she could not do was {{affect}} — influence, have an effect upon — the price of pipe; what she could do was use her {{influence}} — the power to change things without force — on the engineer, who had a mother in the district.

Nights were for the report. Under SIGNIFICANCE she wrote: "The {{significance}} — the meaning, what a thing signifies — of this project is not the water. It is the {{importance}} — the quality of mattering — of the district learning that it can build." Under AMBITION: "My {{ambition}} — the strong desire to achieve something — for this district is a library." Under RECOMMENDATIONS she wrote that the donors should {{encourage}} — give courage and hope to — rather than instruct; that the new cards {{entitle}} — give a formal right to — every family to free clinic visits; and that the district lived in {{harmony}} — the state of fitting together, of agreement — with itself, which is not the same as peace, and is rarer.
tr:
阿玛拉的月度报告星期五截止。像援助（aid，aid 指帮助，尤其指一国或一组织给予独力难支者的帮助）机构的每一位现场员一样，她写两遍：一遍给捐助人，一遍给自己。

她出生在她如今服务的贫民窟（slum，slum 指城市里过度拥挤、破败失修、挤迫而不平等的区域）——这件事对她工作的助益，比她的学位更大。她两岁时父母移民出境（emigrate，emigrate 指离开自己的国家去别处定居）；二十五岁时她自己移民入境（immigrate，immigrate 指来到一个原本不是自己的国家定居）回来，带着一个学位和一笔记忆的债。地区办公室——一只海运集装箱，一支灭火器，一张关于安全（safety，safety 指免于危险的状态）的告示——门外，水龙头前的队伍已经很长。

上午属于供水工程。她的工作是监测（monitor，monitor 指长期地、定期地查看核查，像护士号脉那样）；是执行（implement，implement 指把计划付诸实施）；是遵守指导方针（guideline，guideline 指关于如何行事的书面建议）和核对清单（checklist，checklist 指逐一勾选核对的清单）——总部随文件一起寄来的那些。社区（community，community 指一个地方的人们，作为整体来考虑）自己建起了水台；她的角色是协助（assist，assist 指帮助、支持）——而且绝不当众领导。“项目建议书（proposal，proposal 指正式的书面计划，那份开口要钱的文件）里承诺了二十个水龙头，”她写道，“本区已有十九个。第二十个是管子的问题，不是决心的问题。”

下午属于收容所。两户人家正在申请庇护（asylum，asylum 指一国给予逃离本国危险者的保护），材料还在途中；教堂的老避难所（refuge，refuge 指庇护、躲避危险之处，这个词兼指地方和状态）已经满员。福利（welfare，welfare 指人们的健康、舒适与境遇，尤指国家对他们的照管）官员星期四来。本区的幸福（well-being，well-being 指舒适、健康、快乐的状态）无法测量，阿玛拉在页边写，但可以按晾衣绳清点。

晚上是会议。长老们的视角（perspective，perspective 指由站立之处决定的看事物的方式）是：工程属于他们；工程师的立场（standpoint，standpoint 指立场、观点，据以争辩的位置）是：管道先于人群；老师的看法（viewpoint，viewpoint 指意见、观看的角度）在两者之间；而阿玛拉自己的展望（outlook，outlook 指对未来的总体态度、从这里望见的前景）是她唯一信得过的希望之词。她做不到的，是影响（affect，affect 指对……产生影响）管子的价格；她做得到的，是运用她的影响力（influence，influence 指不用强力而改变事情的力量）去打动那位母亲住在本区的工程师。

夜里写报告。在“意义”一栏她写：“本工程的意义（significance，significance 指含义、一个事物所表示的东西）不在水，而在本区学会‘我们能自己建设’这件事的重要性（importance，importance 指要紧的品质）。”在“雄心”一栏：“我对本区的雄心（ambition，ambition 指成就某事的强烈愿望）是一座图书馆。”在“建议”一栏她写道：捐助人应当鼓励（encourage，encourage 指给人勇气和希望），而不是发号施令；新卡让（entitle，entitle 指给予正式的权利）每户人家免费就诊；而本区与自己和谐相处（harmony，harmony 指彼此相合、协调一致的状态）——这与和平不是一回事，而且更稀有。

quiz.q: Every field officer of the aid agency — aid meaning help, especially from one country or organisation to another. Aid is —
o: help given to those who need it
quiz.ex: aid = 援助；辅助物。first aid 急救。foreign aid 对外援助。hearing aid 助听器。

quiz.q: She had been born in the slum she now served — the overcrowded, run-down district of a city. A slum is —
o: the shelter at the old church
the queue at the water tap
quiz.ex: slum = 贫民窟。slum clearance 贫民区拆迁。slumlord 收租恶房东。

quiz.q: Two families had applied for asylum — protection granted by a country to people fleeing danger in their own. Asylum is —
o: the formal right to clinic visits
a formal written plan for money
quiz.ex: asylum = 庇护（权）；精神病院（旧义）。political asylum 政治庇护。seek asylum 寻求庇护。

quiz.q: Her job was to monitor — to watch and check regularly, over time, the way a nurse takes a pulse. To monitor means —
o: to carry a plan into effect
to watch and check over time
quiz.ex: monitor = 监测；显示器（名词）。monitoring system 监控系统。来自拉丁语 monere（警告）。

quiz.q: To implement — to carry out, to put into effect — the plan. To implement means —
o: to have an effect upon prices
to put a plan into effect
quiz.ex: implement = 实施、执行。implement a policy 执行政策。名词 implement（工具，农具）——同形异义。

quiz.q: The elders' perspective — the way of seeing things, determined by where one stands. A perspective is —
o: a written plan asking for money
a way of seeing, from where one stands
the general attitude to the future
the power to change without force
quiz.ex: perspective = 视角；远景（绘画透视法）。from my perspective 在我看来。keep perspective 保持全局观。

quiz.q: The new cards entitle — give a formal right to — every family to free clinic visits. To entitle means —
o: to give a formal right to
to flee danger in one's own country
quiz.ex: entitle = 使有权；给……题名。be entitled to sth 有权享有。The book is entitled... 书名为……。

quiz.q: The well-being of the district — the state of being comfortable, healthy and happy — could be counted in washing lines. Well-being is —
o: the state of health and happiness
quiz.ex: well-being = 福祉、安康。physical well-being 身体安康。national well-being 国民幸福。

title: The Annual General Meeting
text:
The Annual General {{Meeting}} of the Millbrook Residents' {{association}} — an association being a group of people organised for a shared purpose — was held, as always, in the drill hall it existed to save. It was not a {{conference}} — a conference being the grander thing, the large formal meeting to which people travel, wear badges, and sit in numbered rows—; nobody had travelled further than the church, the only badge in the hall was the secretary's pencil, and it began, as always, with an argument about the minutes.

The {{secretary}} — the officer who keeps the records, writes the letters and remembers everything — read them aloud. "I {{clarify}} one point," she said — clarify meaning to make clear, to remove confusion — "that the figure was two thousand, not two hundred." The chair, whose whole art was to remain {{neutral}} — taking no side, favouring no faction — said "Thank you," which was his entire vocabulary.

The business was the roof. The old drill hall, a genuine local {{institution}} — an established organisation so long part of local life that it has become a custom — needed rebuilding. A property {{consortium}} — a group of companies joined together for a single project — had offered to buy it and convert it into flats; a heritage {{organisation}} — the general word for any organised body, from a charity to a company — had offered a grant towards repairs; and the meeting had to choose.

The lawyer {{advise}}d — gave formal professional advice — caution. "I {{announce}}," said the treasurer — announce meaning to make a public, formal declaration — "that we have four hundred and twelve pounds in the bank." A voice from the back {{hint}}ed — hinted, suggested indirectly, without saying the thing outright — that certain councillors might prefer the flats, and was invited by the chair either to say the thing or to withdraw it. "On {{behalf}} of the older residents" — on behalf of meaning in the name of, representing — "I {{suggest}} — put forward for consideration — that we accept the grant and the debt together," said Mrs Petherbridge.

The survey was then read out. Every {{respondent}} — a person who answers a questionnaire or survey — under forty preferred the flats; every respondent over sixty, the hall; and the {{demographic}} analysis — demographic meaning relating to the structure of a population, its ages and numbers — said the tide ran one way. The {{population}} of Millbrook — all the people living there, as counted — stood at three thousand one hundred, and falling.

"We must be {{political}}," said one member — political meaning of party politics, and, more gently, of the art of the possible — "or we shall be nothing." "We must be {{conservative}}," said another — conservative meaning cautious, inclined to keep what exists, and also the name of a party — "with the only asset we have." The members stated their {{preference}} — the thing preferred, chosen before the others — by show of hands, and the hands came out almost even.

Then the chair, breaking thirty years of neutrality, stood up. "I {{admit}}," he said — admit meaning to confess, to acknowledge a thing as true and unwelcome — "that I signed the grant application last Tuesday." Cries of order. "And I would {{affirm}} — state positively, as a conviction — that this hall is worth a debt, because a village that sells its roof has sold its memory." The vote went fifty-eight to forty-one for the grant; the consortium's letter was filed under "Awaiting Events"; and the secretary, closing the minutes, recorded that the association had chosen, for one more year, to be the kind of {{organisation}} that meets in the building it is trying to save.
tr:
磨坊溪居民会（association，association 指为共同目的组织起来的一群人）的年度大会（meeting，meeting 指会议、集会）照例在它存在下来就是为了拯救的那座操练厅里举行。它算不上会议（conference，conference 指更气派的那种、人们要专程赶来、别着名牌、按编号入座的大型正式会议）；没人赶得比教堂更远，厅里唯一的名牌是秘书的铅笔，而它也照例以一场关于会议记录的争论开场。

秘书（secretary，secretary 指保管记录、撰写信函、什么都记得的干事）大声宣读记录。“我澄清（clarify，clarify 指讲清楚、消除混淆）一点，”她说，“那个数字是两千，不是两百。”主席的全部艺术在于保持中立（neutral，neutral 指不偏袒任何一方、不照顾任何派系），他说“谢谢”，这是他的全部词汇。

议题是屋顶。老操练厅——一个真正的地方机构（institution，institution 指早已融入本地生活、已经变成风俗的既有组织）——需要翻修。一家地产财团（consortium，consortium 指为单个项目联合起来的一组公司）出价收购并改建成公寓；一家遗产保护组织（organisation，organisation 指一切有组织机构的通称，从慈善会到公司）提供了一笔修缮补助；会议必须选择。

律师劝告（advise，advise 指提供正式的专业意见）谨慎。“我宣布（announce，announce 指公开地、正式地宣告），”司库说，“我们账上有四百一十二镑。”后排有个声音暗示（hint，hint 指不明说地、间接地提示）某些议员可能更喜欢公寓方案，主席请他要公把话说完、要么收回。“我代表（behalf，behalf 用于 on behalf of，指以……的名义、代表……）年长的居民，”佩瑟布里奇夫人说，“建议（suggest，suggest 指提出供考虑）我们同时接受补助和债务。”

接着宣读调查。四十岁以下的每位受访者（respondent，respondent 指问卷或调查的回答者）更想要公寓；六十岁以上的每位想要礼堂；而人口结构（demographic，demographic 指与人口结构相关的，关于年龄与数量）分析说，潮水朝一个方向流。磨坊溪的人口（population，population 指住在那里的全部人口，数出来的那个数）是三千一百，还在减少。

“我们必须讲政治（political，political 指政党政治的；也温和地指可能性的艺术）”，一位会员说，“否则我们什么都不是。”“我们必须保守（conservative，conservative 指谨慎的、倾向于保全现状的；也是一个政党的名字）”，另一位说，“对我们唯一的资产。”会员举手表达偏好（preference，preference 指优先选择之物），举出来的手几乎打平。

这时，打破了三十年中立的主席站了起来。“我承认（admit，admit 指承认一件真实而不受欢迎的事），”他说，“上星期二我在补助申请上签了字。”秩序之声四起。“我并且要申明（affirm，affirm 指作为信念加以肯定地陈述）：这座礼堂值得一笔债，因为卖掉屋顶的村子就是卖掉了记忆。”表决五十八票对四十一票，通过了补助方案；财团的信被归档在“等待事件”之下；秘书合上会议记录，写道：本会决定，再当一年那种在自己拼命拯救的房子里开会的组织。

quiz.q: The secretary — the officer who keeps the records, writes the letters and remembers everything — read them aloud. A secretary is —
o: the person who answers a survey
the group of companies joined for a project
the officer who keeps an organisation's records
the elected head of the city
quiz.ex: secretary = 秘书；干事；部长（英国内阁，the Home Secretary 内政大臣）。secretariat 秘书处。

quiz.q: The chair, whose whole art was to remain neutral — taking no side, favouring no faction. Neutral means —
o: taking no side in a dispute
quiz.ex: neutral = 中立的；（化学）中性的。a neutral country 中立国。neutrality 中立（状态）。

quiz.q: A property consortium — a group of companies joined together for a single project — had offered to buy it. A consortium is —
o: a group of organisations joined for one project
quiz.ex: consortium = 财团、联合体。a banking consortium 银行财团。复数 consortia。

quiz.q: The lawyer advised — gave formal professional advice — caution. To advise means —
o: to give formal advice or counsel
to state positively as a conviction
quiz.ex: advise = 劝告、建议。advise sb to do sth 建议某人做某事。advice 名词。advise against 劝阻。

quiz.q: On behalf of the older residents — in the name of, representing. On behalf of means —
o: in favour of selling the roof
against the tide of the survey
in the name of, representing others
quiz.ex: behalf = 利益、方面。on behalf of 代表……；in behalf of（美式，为……利益）。固定搭配。

quiz.q: Every respondent — a person who answers a questionnaire or survey — under forty preferred the flats. A respondent is —
o: one who hints without saying it
the officer who keeps the minutes
one who answers a survey or question
quiz.ex: respondent = 受访者；（法律）被告。respond 回答、响应。correspondent 通讯员。

quiz.q: The demographic analysis — relating to the structure of a population, its ages and numbers — said the tide ran one way. Demographic means —

title: The Second Sunday of November
tcn: 十一月的第二个星期日
text:
On the second Sunday of November the town put on its memory and walked it to the war memorial.

The {{police}} — the civil force that keeps public order, and the officers of it — closed the road with politeness. The {{flag}} of the country — the cloth emblem of a nation, flown from poles and carried into battle — hung at half-mast. Behind the band came the {{banner}}s — the long strips of cloth carried on poles: the regiment's, the fire brigade's, the trade union's, each heavy with its own dust. At the memorial the old men laid their {{wreath}}s — the circles of leaves and flowers laid on graves and monuments, a shape with no beginning and no end.

Mrs Kowalska, the history teacher, had walked in this parade for sixty years, first as a girl holding her mother's hand, and had taught the vocabulary of the morning to three generations.

"This town," she would say, "was built by {{clan}}s" — the old extended family groups, name and loyalty and quarrel bundled into one — "who came for the coal. There were {{civil}} quarrels" — civil meaning between citizens of the same community, as in the civil war — "and {{racial}} ones" — racial meaning to do with race, with the hierarchies of skin that people invent and enforce — "and the mines taught an {{ethnic}} decency" — ethnic meaning of a people's shared origin and culture — "that the surface never managed: a man who has shared the dark with you has no politics you care about. In 1937 forty men from this valley went to fight in the {{spanish}} civil war, on the side of a republic, and eleven came back, and none of them ever spoke of it lightly."

Her own grandmother had marched for the {{franchise}} — the right to vote; the word began as a word for freedom and ended as a piece of paper — and had been arrested on this same street in 1913. "An {{ethic}}," Mrs Kowalska told her pupils — the moral code, the rules a person or a profession actually lives by, as distinct from the ones it claims — "is what you do when the street is watching, and what you do when it is not."

After the two minutes, the crowd folded back into its Sunday. The town was not rich. It had been told for thirty years that its {{prospect}} — the view forward, the likely future as seen from here — was decline, and had quietly declined to agree. It had learned to {{harness}} — to control and put to use, as one harnesses a horse to a cart — what it actually had: water, stubbornness, and memory. In small ways it had begun to {{flourish}} — to thrive, to grow vigorously — again. Not with money: the {{materialism}} of the age — the doctrine that possessions and money are the measures of a life — had missed the place entirely. But {{steady}}ly — steadily, with a firm, unshaken constancy — insisting on its own worth.

"This town is not {{unique}}," Mrs Kowalska told her last class — unique meaning the only one of its kind — "every town has this morning, and every town is unique, because every town has its particular dead. And most of history," she said, nodding towards the memorial, "is not decided in the {{arena}} — the place of contest, the Roman sand, the word for any field of battle or debate. It is decided in rooms like this one, by tired people who choose, steadily, not to hate."
tr:
十一月的第二个星期日，小镇穿上它的记忆，把它一路走到战争纪念碑。

警察（police，police 指维持公共秩序的治安力量及其人员）客气地封了路。国旗（flag，flag 指一个国家的布质徽记，升上旗杆、也扛进战场）降半旗。乐队后面是各色横幅（banner，banner 指扛在杆子上的长条布——军团的、消防队的、工会的——每一条都压着自己的尘土）。在纪念碑前，老人们献上花圈（wreath，wreath 指安放在墓碑和纪念碑上的环形花叶，一个没有起点也没有终点的形状）。

历史教师科瓦尔斯卡夫人在这支游行队伍里走了六十年，起初是牵着母亲手的小女孩；她已把这个上午的词汇教给了三代人。

“这座镇子，”她会说，“是各个宗族（clan，clan 指旧时的家族集团——姓氏、忠诚和世仇捆成一捆）建起来的，他们为煤而来。有过内部的（civil，civil 指同一社群公民之间的，如 civil war 内战）纷争，也有过种族（racial，racial 指关于种族的，人们发明并强制推行的那些肤色等级）的冲突；而矿井教会了一种族裔（ethnic，ethnic 指一个民族共享的出身与文化）之间的体面，地面上一辈子也没学会：和你分过黑暗的人，没有你在乎的政治。一九三七年，山谷里四十个人去西班牙（spanish，spanish 指“西班牙的”）内战中为一个共和国作战，十一个回来了，没有一个轻飘飘地提起过它。”

她自己的祖母曾为选举权（franchise，franchise 指投票的权利；这个词从一个意为“自由”的词开始，最后变成一张纸）游行，一九一三年在这条街上被捕。“伦理（ethic，ethic 指道德准则——一个人或一个行当实际奉行的规矩，而不是它宣称的那套），”科瓦尔斯卡夫人告诉学生，“就是街上有人看时你做的事，和没人看时你做的事。”

两分钟静默之后，人群折回它的星期日。镇子不富裕。三十年来它一直被告知它的前景（prospect，prospect 指向前望的景、从这里看去大概率的事）是衰落，而它悄悄地拒绝了同意。它学会了驾驭（harness，harness 指像给马上挽具一样控制并加以使用）它真正拥有的东西：水、倔强和记忆。它已经开始以各种小小的方式重新繁荣（flourish，flourish 指兴旺、蓬勃生长）。不靠钱：这个时代的物质主义（materialism，materialism 指财产和金钱是人生尺度的学说）完全错过了这个地方。而是稳定地（steady，steady 指坚定的、不动摇的、持续的）坚持自己配得上的东西。

“这座镇子并不独特（unique，unique 指独一无二的）”，科瓦尔斯卡夫人对她最后一届学生说，“每个镇子都有这样的早晨，而每个镇子又都独特，因为每个镇子都有它特定的死者。而历史的大部分，”她朝纪念碑点点头，“不是在竞技场（arena，arena 指角逐之地——罗马的沙地，泛指一切战场或辩论场）上决定的。它是在这样的房间里、由疲惫的人们决定的——他们稳定地选择了不去恨。”

the march for the right to vote

title: The Millbrook Savings Bank
text:
The Millbrook Savings Bank opened at nine o'clock, and by four minutes past nine Mrs Tregenna was at the counter with a biscuit tin.

"{{Coin}}s," she announced — a coin being a flat piece of metal used as money, as distinct from a paper note — "forty years of them."

The tin held {{shilling}}s — the shilling being the silver coin, worth twelve old pence, that Britain used before its money went decimal — and Hazel the cashier counted them while the queue listened to every one land. "And what will you have for them?" she asked. "The current {{currency}}" — the currency being the money a country actually uses, pounds here, yen in Japan — "or a receipt and my sympathy?"

"The {{cash}}, of course," said Mrs Tregenna — cash meaning money in notes and coins, money you can hold, as opposed to money in an account. "That is why I brought the tin."

"Then you shall have a {{receipt}}" — a receipt being the written proof that money has been paid or received — "and the sum will stand as a {{deposit}}" — a deposit being money placed into a bank account, where it may earn interest — "in your {{account}}, which is our record of your money, every sum in and every sum out. Your balance will then be four thousand one hundred and six pounds."

"And I may take it out whenever I like?"

"Whenever the bank is open."

"That," said Mrs Tregenna, leaving the tin on the counter as a gift, "is what my husband said about the biscuit tin, and look how that turned out."

Behind her stood Mr Chubb the photographer, bound for France. "I should like to {{exchange}} some money," he said — to exchange being to give one thing and receive another in return, here pounds for euros — "while the rate is what it is." "While the rate is what it is," agreed Hazel, "it is kindest to do it quickly and think about it never."

In his office Mr Chipman, the manager, had spent the morning with the {{financial}} pages — financial meaning concerned with money, income and investment — and now received Mr Bell the farmer, hat in his hands.

"I want to {{invest}}," said Mr Bell — to invest being to put money into land, machines or shares in the hope that more money comes back — "in a new milking parlour. But I should have to borrow to do it, and borrowing frightens me."

"A loan is a {{debt}}" — a debt being money owed to another — "and a debt is only frightening when it grows faster than the thing you bought with it. While you carry it you will pay {{interest}}" — interest being the lender's charge for lending, so much in the hundred each year — "and we will hold {{security}}" — security being something pledged behind a loan, land usually, which the lender may take if the loan is not repaid. "And you should {{insure}} the parlour" — to insure being to pay a company a yearly sum so that the company, and not you, carries the loss if it burns or floods — "which is the one thing in farming cheaper than the fire."

"If I would rather not borrow," said Mr Bell, "what are the quiet ways?"

"A {{bond}}" — a bond being a written promise by a government or a company to repay a sum at a fixed date, with interest — "is the quietest. Units in our Beacon {{fund}}" — a fund being a pool of money gathered from many investors and managed as one — "are quieter still. Or you could buy shares in the Lampford creamery and take the {{dividend}}" — a dividend being the share of the profits paid out to the shareholders each year — "which is not quiet at all, but has bought Mrs Petherbridge two greenhouses."

"And which would you have yourself?"

"Under {{inflation}}" — inflation being the general rise in prices, by which each pound buys a little less every year — "a savings account quietly loses; under {{deflation}}" — deflation being the general fall in prices — "a farmer loses loudly, because his milk brings less while his debts stay the same size. Between the two, I like land, a parlour and cows."

"The {{tax}} will take its fifth of the interest," said Mr Chipman — a tax being the charge the state lays upon income, goods and property — "and the county has announced a fresh {{levy}}" — a levy being a charge imposed and collected by official authority — "on unmown verges, which your cows are technically equipped to solve."

At lunchtime Poppy Tregenna arrived with business of her own. She had a {{coupon}} — a coupon being a small printed paper giving money off a product — for shampoo, and a {{voucher}} — a voucher being a paper worth a stated sum, exchangeable for goods — from her aunt for the bookshop, and a plan to make both work on a single bottle. Hazel ruled that the {{discount}} — a discount being a reduction from the ordinary price — could not be doubled; Poppy then proposed to {{swap}} — to swap being to exchange one thing for another — the coupon to any customer with a book to buy; and three customers in the queue, immediately, had.

At two o'clock a man returned a milk-frother that had never frothed, and asked for a {{refund}} — a refund being the return of money paid — with the gravity of a man closing a treaty. Hazel offered a replacement; the man pointed at the frother; Hazel counted out the money. Beside him a young couple arranged to pay for a cooker by monthly {{installment}}s — an installment being one of the successive payments into which a debt is divided — and left discussing hobs.

At half past four the day's {{transaction}}s — a transaction being one completed piece of business, a deposit, a withdrawal, a payment — were added up, and the drawer showed a {{deficit}} of two pence — a deficit being the amount by which what goes out exceeds what comes in — which the whole staff hunted for three-quarters of an hour before Hazel found it under the biscuit tin.

"Under the tin," she said. "It has been there since nine o'clock."

"Then it has earned nothing all day," said Mr Chipman, and dropped it in. "Which is still better than the bond market managed."
tr:
磨坊溪储蓄银行九点开门。九点过四分，特雷真纳太太已经拿着一只饼干罐站到了柜台前。

“硬币（coin，coin 指作为货币使用的扁平金属块，与纸币相对），”她宣布，“四十年攒下的。”

罐子里装的是先令（shilling，shilling 指英国货币十进制化之前流通的银币，值十二旧便士），收银员黑兹尔一枚一枚地数，队伍里的人听着每一枚落下的声音。“这些您要换成什么呢？”她问，“现行的货币（currency，currency 指一个国家实际使用的货币，这里是英镑，在日本是日元）？还是一张收据外加我的同情？”

“当然是现金（cash，cash 指纸币和硬币形式的钱、拿在手里的钱，与账户里的钱相对），”特雷真纳太太说，“所以我才把罐子带来了。”

“那您会得到一张收据（receipt，receipt 指款项已付或已收的书面凭证），这笔钱将作为一笔存款（deposit，deposit 指存入银行账户、可以生息的钱）记入您的账户（account，account 指银行保存的客户资金记录，每一笔进出都有记载）。届时您的余额是四千一百零六英镑。”

“我想取就随时能取？”

“只要银行开门，随时可以。”

“这句话，”特雷真纳太太说着，把罐子留在柜台上当作礼物，“我丈夫当年讲到饼干罐时也是这么说的，结果如何您都看见了。”

她身后站着准备去法国的摄影师丘布先生。“我想兑换（exchange，exchange 指以一物换回另一物，这里是英镑换欧元）一点钱，”他说，“趁汇率还是现在这个样子。”“既然汇率是现在这个样子，”黑兹尔表示同意，“最仁慈的做法是赶紧换完，从此不再想起它。”

经理奇普曼先生的整个上午都花在金融（financial，financial 指与货币、收入和投资有关的）版上，此刻他接待了把帽子捧在手里的农场主贝尔先生。

“我想投资（invest，invest 指把钱投入土地、机器或股份，指望收回更多的钱），”贝尔先生说，“买一间新挤奶厅。但那样就得借钱，而借钱让我害怕。”

“贷款就是一笔债务（debt，debt 指欠别人的钱），而债务只有当它涨得比你用它买到的东西还快时才可怕。背着债的期间，你要付利息（interest，interest 指贷方出借资金的收费，每年按百分之几计算），我们则要留担保物（security，security 指押在贷款后面的抵押品，通常是土地，贷款不还时贷方可将其收走）。另外你应该给挤奶厅投保（insure，insure 指每年付给保险公司一笔钱，万一失火或被淹，损失由公司而不是你承担）——这是农事里唯一比火灾本身便宜的东西。”

“要是不想借钱呢，”贝尔先生说，“有什么安静的法子？”

“债券（bond，bond 指政府或公司出具的书面承诺，承诺在固定日期还本付息）最安静。我们'灯塔基金'（fund，fund 指从众多投资人汇集起来、作为整体统一管理的一笔资金）的份额还要更安静些。或者买兰普福德奶厂的股票，拿股息（dividend，dividend 指每年分派给股东的那一份利润）——那可一点也不安静，不过已经给佩瑟布里奇太太赚来了两座温室。”

“要是您自己，会选哪个？”

“在通货膨胀（inflation，inflation 指物价普遍上涨、英镑一年比一年买得少）之下，储蓄账户在悄悄缩水；在通货紧缩（deflation，deflation 指物价普遍下跌）之下，农民亏得震天响，因为牛奶卖得越来越少，债却一分不小。两者之间，我喜欢土地、挤奶厅和奶牛。”

“税（tax，tax 指国家对收入、货物和财产征收的费用）会拿走利息的五分之一，”奇普曼先生说，“而且郡里刚宣布了一项新的征收（levy，levy 指凭借官方权力强制加征并收取的费用）——针对未修剪的路边草带，而您的奶牛在技术上完全有能力解决这个问题。”

午餐时分，波比·特雷真纳带着她自己的事务来了。她有一张洗发水的优惠券（coupon，coupon 指印在商品上、可抵扣部分价款的小纸片），还有一张姨妈送的、书店用的代金券（voucher，voucher 指票面标明金额、可换取商品的票据），并且计划让两者在同一瓶洗发水上同时生效。黑兹尔裁定折扣（discount，discount 指在原价基础上减收的部分）不能叠加；波比随即提议把优惠券交换（swap，swap 指以一物换另一物）给任何要买书的顾客——队伍里立刻有三个人说他们正要买书。

两点钟，一位先生退回了一台从未打出过奶泡的打奶泡机，要求退款（refund，refund 指退还已付的钱款），神情庄重得像在缔结一项条约。黑兹尔提出换一台新的；那人指了指打奶泡机；黑兹尔便把钱数了出来。他旁边，一对年轻夫妻安排好按月分期（installment，installment 指一笔欠款分成的一期期偿付款）支付一台灶具，然后一边讨论着灶台式样一边走了。

四点半，当天的全部交易（transaction，transaction 指一笔完成的业务，如一次存款、一次取款、一次付款）被加总起来，钱柜里出现了两便士的亏空（deficit，deficit 指支出超过收入的那部分金额），全体员工为此找了三刻钟，最后黑兹尔在饼干罐底下找到了它。

“罐子底下，”她说，“从九点起它就一直在那儿。”

“那它一整天连一点利息都没挣到，”奇普曼先生说着，把它投了进去，“这仍然比债券市场当天的表现强。”

the lender's charge for lending money

quiz.q: A young couple arranged to pay for a cooker by monthly installments — one of the successive payments into which a debt is divided. An installment is —
o: a sum kept in a biscuit tin
one of the successive payments of a debt

quiz.q: The county has announced a fresh levy on unmown verges — a charge imposed and collected by official authority. A levy is —

quiz.q: The man returned a milk-frother that had never frothed and asked for a refund — the return of money paid. A refund is —
