这张谱是为亲族（kin，kin 指家族、血亲）和族人（folk，folk 指自己的一族人，取其最古老最宽泛之义）而画的，而且它把他们都找了出来：珀斯有一位亲戚（relative，relative 指有血缘或姻亲关系的人），每年寄一张卡片；家里有一位至交（intimate，intimate 指亲密可信的朋友），出现在三张照片和零份文件里，因此用铅笔登记。谱上最年轻的青年（youth，youth 指年轻男子）在啤酒厂当学徒；最年幼的孩子（youngster，youngster 指小孩、年少者）四岁；而最新的那根细枝预计在秋天到来，最初是一个胚胎（embryo，embryo 指新生命诞生之前的第一阶段；就这一例而言，是在布里斯托一家诊所的培养皿里）——学会沉默片刻记下了这个事实，然后，以学会的做派，办了个小小的仪式，喝了茶。学会一致认为，怀夫人本人是个可爱的人（dear，dear 指可亲可爱的人）；纸商说，这墨水保用一百年——大概也就够了。

quiz.q: The first pioneer of her line was a Huguenot weaver who reached Millbrook in 1685 — one who goes first and opens the way for those behind. A pioneer is —
o: the family name, carried after the Christian one
one who claims to foretell the end
one who inherits like a watch
one who goes first, opening the way
quiz.ex: pioneer = 先驱；开拓者。a pioneer of aviation 航空先驱；pioneering research 开创性研究。

quiz.q: An uncle who was the town herald, and cried the fair and the bread prices — of old, an officer of arms; by extension, one who makes announcements. A herald is —
o: a child whose parents are dead
one who inherits the mill sideways
an officer of arms; one who announces
a young man apprenticed at the brewery
quiz.ex: herald = 传令官；预兆。the town crier as herald 充当传令官的镇上喊话人；dark clouds heralding rain 预示下雨的乌云。

quiz.q: The honest word for each holder is not heir but successor — one who follows another in a place or office, by inheritance or otherwise. A successor is —
o: the father of one's husband or wife
one who goes first and opens the way
two children born of one birth
one who follows another in an office
quiz.ex: successor = 接任者；继任者。his successor at the bank 他在银行的继任者；succeed v. 继任。

quiz.q: There is the orphan of the famine year, whom the family took in and kept — a child whose parents are dead. An orphan is —
o: a close, trusted friend of the family
a baby who did not see its second birthday
a young person fined sixpence for apples
a child whose parents are dead
quiz.ex: orphan = 孤儿。orphaned by the epidemic 因瘟疫成为孤儿；an orphanage 孤儿院。

quiz.q: The Society voted to add a column for gender — the social state of being male or female. Gender is —
o: the family name carried after the first name
the biological classification into male and female
the span of about thirty years
the social state of being male or female
quiz.ex: gender = 社会性别；（语法）性。gender equality 性别平等；gender roles 性别角色。

quiz.q: Mrs. Vye entered Graham in the column headed spouse — a married partner, husband or wife. A spouse is —
o: a married partner, husband or wife
a child born of the same birth
quiz.ex: spouse = 配偶。surviving spouse 未亡配偶；spousal support 配偶赡养。

quiz.q: The newest twig of all began as an embryo — the first stage of a new creature, before it is born. An embryo is —
o: one's people in the widest sense
a child in its first years
a young man of the family
the first stage of a new creature
quiz.ex: embryo = 胚胎；（事物的）萌芽期。an embryo in a dish 培养皿中的胚胎；in embryo 在萌芽中。

quiz.q: An intimate of the family who appears in three photographs and no document — a close, trusted friend. An intimate is —
o: a relative by blood in Perth
a person marked in red ink
quiz.ex: intimate = 至交；亲密的。an intimate friend 至交；intimate details 隐私细节。

title: The Landlady of the Bull
text:
Mrs. Tizzard has kept the Bull for fifty-one years, which the Guinness people confirmed, by letter, is a record for a woman; and she has been the {{landlady}} — a landlady being a woman who runs an inn or lets rooms — of it for thirty-seven, her husband Alf having been the {{landlord}} — a landlord being a man who owns or lets property; the keeper of an inn — for the first fourteen. They divided the work in the old way: Alf was the {{host}} — a host being the man who receives and entertains guests — of the public bar, and she was the {{hostess}} — a hostess being the woman who does the same — of everything else, which was more.

She came to the house at nineteen, as the {{maid}} — a maid being a female servant, indoors — from the fen country, under her {{maiden}} — maiden meaning unmarried; a maiden name being a woman's family name before marriage — name of Pratt; and the registers of the county record her marriage, her widowhood and her licences, all in the same round hand, since she learned to fill the forms herself. Alf died in 1984, on a Tuesday, between the lunch and the darts; and the town held its breath to see whether the {{widow}} — a widow being a woman whose husband is dead — would sell. She did not sell. She put on the black for the year of it, took both bars, and ran the house as its {{mistress}} — a mistress being the woman at the head of a household; in the old books, simply the female master — which she had been doing since 1971 anyway, as the licensing magistrate observed when he renewed her.

The Bull keeps its shape around her. There are six letting rooms and one permanent {{tenant}} — a tenant being one who occupies and pays rent for another's property — a retired schoolmaster up under the eaves who has been there twenty years and pays, by arrangement, in book reviews. The regular {{customer}}s — a customer being one who buys, regularly or not, from a tradesman — occupy the settle by the fire; the commercial travellers take the middle table; and in the coffee room, on Thursdays, Mr. Quayle the solicitor meets his {{client}}s — a client being one who employs a professional person — because, he says, his own office smells of his own filing. The {{guest}}s — a guest being one who is received at another's table or roof — at the front come mostly for the walking now; the walkers, she has found, are the same people who were hippies in the seventies, wearing better boots.

Her days have a tide to them. The {{chore}}s — a chore being a small, recurring piece of household work — come twice daily, the rooms at eight and the bars at four; the {{housewife}} — a housewife being a woman who keeps her own house — from across the road calls in each morning for a fresh loaf and the news, in that order; and her own {{household}} — a household being all the people living under one roof and under one management — gathers at nine for supper, by which is meant the tenant, the bar staff, whichever of the grandchildren is staying, and the dog. {{Madam}} — madam being a respectful, and in the old use simply the word for, a married woman; in the new use, what a well-brought-up child calls any grown woman — is what the village children call her, without irony, because it has never occurred to them that there is anything to be ironic about.

The stories are mostly chases. She has {{chase}}d — to chase meaning to run after, to pursue — three non-payers down the high street in her overall, and caught two; the third was a racing man who came back next season to pay, out of respect. She once {{encounter}}ed — to encounter meaning to meet, unexpectedly and face to face — the Bishop of Lampford in the cellar at midnight, both of them pretending to be checking the gas, and neither ever mentioning it since. She {{miss}}ed — to miss meaning to fail to catch, to be too late for — the coronation on the television in 1953 to {{accompany}} — to accompany meaning to go with, to be companion on a journey — the district nurse on a snowbound call, and has never once said she regretted it, though she has asked everybody else's opinion of the programme for seventy years. Her {{appointment}} — an appointment being an arrangement to meet at a set time — book, kept since 1961, is a social history of the valley in pencil.

She has also, in her time, been a mother. Her son left at eighteen for the north; her daughter stayed, and her daughter's boys are the despair and the pride of the house. The elder is in his {{adolescence}} — adolescence being the years between childhood and adulthood, in which a person is no child and no grown man — and goes about in headphones, answering all questions in the future tense; the younger leads a {{gang}} — a gang being a band of companions; in the disapproving use, a band of young ruffians — of six small boys who have declared the car park a jungle, and whom she pays in lemonade to fetch coal. When the boys were {{teenage}} — teenage meaning of the years from thirteen to nineteen — she took in washing for the hippies, and has the bead curtains still, in the loft, against the day they come back into fashion.

She is, at eighty-three, the last of a kind, and she knows it. Her {{dependent}} — a dependent being one who relies on another for support — list has shortened over the years from a household to a dog; the brewery sends representatives with leaflets about the future; and the walkers' guides give the Bull two stars for comfort and none for the landlord, because there isn't one, and the form has no space for what there is. When the Mercury sent a young man to interview her on the anniversary, he asked what she attributed her long tenancy to. "Well," she said, "I never learned to drive, so I was always here."
tr:
蒂泽德太太经营“公牛”客栈已经五十一年——吉尼斯方面来函确认，这是女性的纪录；而她当它的老板娘（landlady，landlady 指经营客栈或出租房间的女主人）已有三十七年，她的丈夫阿尔夫当房东（landlord，landlord 指拥有或出租物业的人，客栈的男主人）则占了头十四年。两口子按老法子分工：阿尔夫是大众酒吧的东道（host，host 指接待、款待客人的人），她是其余一切的东道主妇（hostess，hostess 指做同样事情的女人）——而“其余一切”要多得多。

她十九岁来到这座房子，当女仆（maid，maid 指做室内活计的女佣），从沼泽地区来，用的是她婚前的（maiden，maiden 指未婚的；maiden name 指女子婚前娘家的姓氏）姓氏普拉特；郡里的登记册记下了她的婚姻、她的孀居和她的营业执照，全是同一笔圆润的字——因为表格是她自己学着填的。阿尔夫死于一九八四年某个星期二，午饭和飞镖之间；全镇屏住呼吸，看这位寡妇（widow，widow 指死了丈夫的女人）会不会把店卖掉。她没有卖。她为这一年披了黑，接手了两间酒吧，以宅子女主人（mistress，mistress 指一家之主妇；在旧书里就是“女性主人”）的身份执掌这座房子——反正自一九七一年起她也是一直在这么干的，换发执照的治安官在续期时如此评论。

“公牛”围着她的形状运转。楼上有六间客房和一位常住的房客（tenant，tenant 指占用并付租金使用他人房产的人）——一位住在屋檐下的退休教师，住了二十年，按约定用书评付租。常客（customer，customer 指向商家买东西的人，常来不常来都算）占着炉边的长椅；行商们坐中间的桌子；每逢星期四，事务律师奎尔先生在咖啡厅里见他的委托人（client，client 指雇用专业人士的人），因为，他说，他自己的办公室一股他自己的档案味。前门的住客（guest，guest 指在他人餐桌或屋檐下受接待的人）如今大多是来徒步的；她发现，这些徒步者就是七十年代那批嬉皮士，换了双好点的靴子。

她的日子自有潮汐。家务杂活（chore，chore 指每日重复的小件家务）一天两次，八点收拾房间，四点收拾酒吧；对面那位家庭主妇（housewife，housewife 指操持自家家务的妇人）每天上午来买一个新出炉的面包和一耳朵新闻——顺序如此；她自己的一户人（household，household 指同一个屋顶、同一套管理之下的所有人）九点钟聚齐吃晚饭，所谓一户人，指的是房客、酒吧伙计、碰巧住着的哪个外孙，和那条狗。夫人（madam，madam 是尊称，旧义就是“已婚妇女”这个称呼；新义是有教养的孩子对任何成年妇女的称呼）——村里的孩子们就这么叫她，不带讥诮，因为他们压根没想到这里面有什么可讥诮的。

关于她的故事多半是追赶。她穿着罩衫沿大街追赶（chase，chase 指追着跑、追捕）过三个没付账的，逮住了两个；第三个是赛马场上的人，下一季出于敬意回来补了钱。她曾在半夜的地窖里撞见（encounter，encounter 指不期而遇、当面碰上）兰普福德的主教，两人都假装在查煤气，此后谁也没再提过。一九五三年她错过（miss，miss 指没赶上、迟了一步）了电视转播的加冕礼，为的是陪同（accompany，accompany 指随行、结伴前往）地段护士出一趟大雪封路的诊；她从没说过后悔，尽管七十年来她一直在征集别人对那场节目的看法。她那本从一九六一年记到现在的预约（appointment，appointment 指约定时刻的会面）簿，就是一部用铅笔写成的河谷社会史。

她这辈子当然也当过母亲。儿子十八岁去了北方；女儿留下，女儿的两个男孩是这座房子的绝望与骄傲。大的正处青春期（adolescence，adolescence 指童年与成年之间的岁月，人在其中既非孩童亦非大人），整天戴着耳机，对一切问题都用将来时回答；小的领着一帮（gang，gang 指一伙同伴；贬义指一伙小流氓）六个小男孩，已宣布停车场为丛林，她用柠檬水雇他们运煤。当年孩子们十几岁（teenage，teenage 指十三到十九岁之间的年纪）时，她为嬉皮士们洗过衣服，阁楼里至今留着那些珠帘，等着它们重新流行的那一天。

八十三岁的她是同类中的最后一个，这一点她清楚。她的受赡养人（dependent，dependent 指仰赖他人供养的人）名单，这些年从一户人家缩减成了一条狗；啤酒厂派代表带着关于未来的宣传册来；徒步指南给“公牛”的舒适度打了两颗星，房东一栏一颗也没有——因为没有房东，而表格上没有格子留给实际存在的这一位。《信使报》派了个年轻人来采访周年纪念，问她把这么长的任期归功于什么。“唔，”她说，“我从来没学会开车，所以我一直都在。”

quiz.q: She has been the landlady of the Bull for thirty-seven years — a woman who runs an inn or lets rooms. A landlady is —
o: a woman who runs an inn or lets rooms
a woman whose husband is dead
one who occupies and pays rent
quiz.ex: landlady = 女房东；客栈老板娘。the landlady of the pub 酒馆老板娘。

quiz.q: One permanent tenant, a retired schoolmaster under the eaves — one who occupies and pays rent for another's property. A tenant is —
o: one who is received at another's roof
one who occupies and pays rent
a woman who keeps her own house
quiz.ex: tenant = 租户；房客。sitting tenants 现有租户；tenant farmer 佃农。

quiz.q: Mr. Quayle the solicitor meets his clients in the coffee room — one who employs a professional person. A client is —
o: a female servant of the house
one who buys from a tradesman
one who employs a professional person
a respectful word for any grown woman
quiz.ex: client = 委托人；客户。a solicitor's clients 律师的委托人；client base 客户群。

quiz.q: She once encountered the Bishop of Lampford in the cellar at midnight — to meet, unexpectedly and face to face. To encounter is to —
quiz.ex: encounter = 遭遇；邂逅。encounter a problem 遇到问题；a chance encounter 偶遇。

quiz.q: She missed the coronation to accompany the district nurse on a snowbound call — to go with, to be companion on a journey. To accompany is to —
o: go with, be companion on a journey
quiz.ex: accompany = 陪同；伴随。accompany a guest to the door 送客到门口；piano accompanying 钢琴伴奏。

quiz.q: She came at nineteen, under her maiden name of Pratt — unmarried; a maiden name being a woman's family name before marriage. Maiden means —
quiz.ex: maiden = 未婚的；初次的。maiden name 娘家姓；maiden voyage 处女航。

quiz.q: The younger boy leads a gang of six small boys — a band of companions; in the disapproving use, young ruffians. A gang is —
o: the years between child and man
a band of companions or ruffians
a small recurring piece of work
a respectful address to a lady
quiz.ex: gang = 一帮；一伙（贬义指团伙）。a gang of youths 一伙年轻人；gang crime 团伙犯罪。

quiz.q: Her dependent list has shortened from a household to a dog — one who relies on another for support. A dependent is —
o: one who receives guests at a table
one who relies on another for support
a woman at the head of a household
a man who owns the property
quiz.ex: dependent = 受赡养者；家属。dependants on the tax form 税单上的受抚养人；be dependent on 依赖于。

title: The Slowest Proposal in the Valley
text:
The {{neighbourhood}} — a neighbourhood being the people among whom one lives; a place taken, in the word, as its people — waited eleven years for Dan Locke to {{propose}} — to propose meaning to offer marriage; and, in the plainer sense, to put a thing forward for acceptance — to Miss Warde, the {{veterinary}} — veterinary meaning of the healing of animals; a veterinary surgeon being, in the valley's shorthand, the animals' doctor — surgeon; and it gave up hoping aloud somewhere around the millennium, settling for the raising of eyebrows, which is the valley's way of keeping faith.

They had met as {{stranger}}s — a stranger being one not known, not of one's household or one's place — in the autumn of 1998, over a cat with its head wedged in a sweet jar, and had got through the introduction, the extraction and the bill without either of them raising a voice. What began as {{acquaintance}} — acquaintance being slight knowledge of a person, social and short of friendship — had reached first names by the second visit, and ripened by honest degrees into {{friendship}} — friendship being the state of friends; the liking that has stopped keeping accounts — which is where, the valley agrees, the delay began. It is one thing to be a {{lover}} — a lover being one who loves, in the romantic sense — and another thing entirely to say the sentence out loud, with the door open, wearing your own face.

The Mercury, writing the engagement up years later, called Dan the most patient man in the valley, which was politeness; the darts team at the Bull called him a {{coward}} — a coward being one who shrinks from danger, pain or difficulty — which was not, quite. The charge is hard to sustain against a {{fireman}} — a fireman being a man whose trade is the fighting of fires — who has twice been up the mill ladder in smoke the Mercury photographed from a safe distance; Dan is the {{hero}} — a hero being a man admired for brave deeds; in the oldest sense, a man of half-divine parentage, a sense the valley stretches to cover the Locke family generally — of the flood of 2007, having taken two children and a spaniel off the wool warehouse roof in a borrowed dinghy while the whole town shouted advice from the bridge; and Miss Warde has been the valley's {{heroine}} — a heroine being a female hero — since the snowbound calving of 2010, the last mile of which she walked, in January, carrying what she carried. The plain truth, as she told Mrs. Tizzard at the time, is that both of them had seen enough of other people's emergencies to be unhurried about their own.

He proposed at last on the anniversary of the flood, in March, at the ford, in waders, with the ring in a tobacco tin against the wet; and she had said yes before the tin was open, which she has never let him forget and he has never once tried to. The {{engagement}} — an engagement being a promise to marry, and the state of being promised — ran eighteen months, the wedding having to wait for the hall, the ewes and the school holidays, in that order; the Mercury announced it under MARRIAGES INTENDED, a heading it invented for the occasion and has used four times since.

The night before, his {{comrade}}s — a comrade being a companion in arms, or in a shared trade — from the station held him {{hostage}} — a hostage being a person seized and held until terms are met — in the old manner of the valley, from eight until midnight, at the Bull; the terms being three songs sung standing on the mounting stone and a round for the engine crew; and his best {{mate}} — a mate being a companion, a fellow; in the trades, one of a pair who work together — the station officer, paid the ransom on Dan's behalf and entered it in the day book as training.

The {{wedding}} — a wedding being the marriage rite together with its feast — was at St. Cuthbert's on the longest Saturday in June. The {{groom}} — a groom being a bridegroom; in the older and wider sense, one who tends horses, which the Locke family did for two hundred years before the engines — wore his number-one uniform and the expression of a man at a chimney fire; {{each}} — each meaning every one of a number, taken one by one — family of the valley had given what it had: the Tizzards the beer, the Women's Institute the marquee, the rugby club the crockery, three pieces short by the end and nobody asking. The {{respective}} — respective meaning of or belonging to each; separate and particular to each — mothers sat in the front pew and wept in perfect formation, having drilled by telephone for a fortnight; Miss Warde's mother, a retired {{nurse}} — a nurse being one trained to tend the sick — had the seat of honour and the first speech; the {{individual}} — individual meaning of or for one single person or thing, taken separately — portions of trifle were Mrs. Tizzard's answer to the whole question of ices; and the {{separate}} — separate meaning apart, one from the other; not shared — rooms both of them had kept for eleven years, hers over the surgery, his over the station, were given up in the same week; the {{single}} — single meaning one only; unmarried — state of both being thereby ended, which the valley found more eloquent than the banns. Cyril Vye and Graham came down from London for it, and were seated, by Mrs. Vye's arrangement, beside the longest branch of the tree they belonged to.

Inside the church it went as these things go. Dan looked at his {{beloved}} — the beloved being the greatly loved one; beloved also being simply the adjective, greatly loved — the way he looks at a fire that has stopped surprising him; the vicar, who has married the valley for thirty years, kept to {{marry}} — to marry meaning to take as husband or wife — the short form; {{divorce}} — a divorce being the legal ending of a marriage — was mentioned once, from the pulpit, as a thing neither of them had behind them, the vicar calling it a professional courtesy to himself; the {{kiss}} — a kiss being the touching of lips, in love or in greeting — at the porch was held for the photographer and then repeated, unpaid, at the gate; the {{affection}} — affection being fondness; warm and settled liking — of the neighbourhood was such that the bells were late starting, the ringers all being at the gate as well. The {{honeymoon}} — a honeymoon being the holiday of the newly married; the word keeping, in its honey and its moon, the old idea that the sweetness lasts a month — was twelve days in the Outer Hebrides, out of season, at Miss Warde's choosing, the weather having the grace to be terrible, so that they came back rested; her {{partner}} — a partner being one who shares with another in a business, or in a life — from the practice held the rings, and has told the story of the tobacco tin, with improvements, at every Christmas party since. The {{sole}} — sole meaning one and only; the word also naming the flatfish and the bottom of the boot, all three being honest trades — mishap of the day was the best man's speech, which ran eleven minutes and has never once been forgiven.

Mrs. Vye had the two of them onto the family-tree paper before they reached the lychgate; the red ink, the paper merchant said, is guaranteed for a hundred years.
tr:
磨坊溪的街坊邻里（neighbourhood，neighbourhood 指与自己同住一地的人们；这个词把一个地方当作它的人来讲）等了丹·洛克十一年，等他向沃德小姐——那位兽医（veterinary，veterinary 指医治动物的；veterinary surgeon 即兽医，河谷里简称“兽大夫”）——求婚（propose，propose 指求婚；平常用义是把一件事提出来请人接受）；到了千禧年前后，大家连出声盼望都放弃了，改用扬眉毛来维持信念——扬眉毛是河谷保持信念的方式。

两人是一九九八年秋天作为陌生人（stranger，stranger 指不相识的人，非自家、非本地之人）认识的，起因是一只猫把头卡在糖果罐里；介绍、拔罐、结账三道工序下来，谁也没抬高过嗓门。起初的相识（acquaintance，acquaintance 指对一个人的浅识，属社交层面，还够不上友谊）到第二次上门就改叫名字了；又按着老实的进度酿成了友谊（friendship，friendship 指朋友之间的状态；那种不再记账的喜欢）——河谷公认，耽搁正是从这里开始的。做一个恋人（lover，lover 指相爱之人，取恋爱之义）是一回事，敞着门、用自己的脸把那句话说出口，是完完全全另一回事。

《信使报》多年后写订婚报道时，称丹为河谷最有耐心的人，这是客气话；“公牛”的飞镖队管他叫懦夫（coward，coward 指在危险、痛苦或困难面前退缩的人），这就不太客气了。可这罪名安在一个消防员（fireman，fireman 指以救火为业的人）头上很难站得住：他两次顶着浓烟爬上磨坊的梯子，《信使报》还从安全距离拍过照；丹是二〇〇七年洪水中的英雄（hero，hero 指因勇敢事迹而受敬仰的人；最古老的义项指半神血统之人——河谷把这个义项放宽，大致囊括了整个洛克家族），当时他划着借来的小艇，从羊毛仓库的屋顶上救下两个孩子和一条西班牙猎犬，全镇在桥上七嘴八舌地出主意；而沃德小姐自二〇一〇年雪夜接生牛犊那件事起，就是河谷的女英雄（heroine，heroine 指女性的英雄），最后一英里是她在一月里走着去的，背着她的那些家伙什。实情正如她当时对蒂泽德太太说的：两人见过的别人的急难已经够多，轮到自己的，反倒不着急了。

他终于在一周年纪念日那天、三月里、浅滩上、穿着连靴水裤求了婚，戒指装在防潮的烟丝铁盒里；铁盒还没打开她就答应了——这件事她从没让他忘掉，他也一次没试过。订婚（engagement，engagement 指婚约，也指订婚的状态）持续了十八个月，婚期要等礼堂、等母羊、等学校放假，顺序如此；《信使报》在自创的“拟婚”栏下登了启事，这个栏目专为这桩事发明，此后一共用过四次。

婚礼前夜，他在消防站的战友们（comrade，comrade 指并肩作战或同行共事之人）按河谷的老规矩把他扣作人质（hostage，hostage 指被扣押至条件满足之人），从八点到半夜，地点在“公牛”，条件是站上磨石唱三支歌、给机车班组请一轮酒；他的好伙计（mate，mate 指同伴、伙伴；行业里指搭手干活的一对之一）——站长——替他付了赎金，记在勤务簿上，事由写的是“训练”。

婚礼（wedding，wedding 指婚礼及其喜宴）定在六月最长的那个星期六，圣卡斯伯特教堂。新郎（groom，groom 指新郎；更古老的宽义指照管马匹之人——洛克家在有机车之前干这行干了两百年）穿着一号礼服，脸上是烟囱失火时才有的表情。河谷的每户人家（each，each 指若干中的每一个，逐个而论）都拿出了自家的东西：蒂泽德家出啤酒，妇女协会出帐篷，橄榄球俱乐部出瓷器——散场少了三只，没人追问。两位各自的母亲（respective，respective 指属于各人的、各别而论及的）在前排长椅上按队形垂泪，事先用电话排练了两个星期；沃德小姐的母亲是退休护士（nurse，nurse 指受过训练、看护病人的人），坐了首席、致了第一段辞；一人一份（individual，individual 指单个的、逐个的）的甜冻是蒂泽德太太对“要不要冰品”这一整个问题的回答；而两人分居两处的（separate，separate 指分开的、各不共享的）房间——她那间在诊室楼上，他那间在消防站楼上——守了十一年，同一个星期先后退掉；两人的单身（single，single 指仅只一个的；未婚的）状态就此一并结束，河谷认为这比结婚公告更有说服力。西里尔·怀和格雷厄姆专程从伦敦赶来，按怀夫人的安排，坐在他们所属的那根最长分枝旁边。

教堂里的事照常进行。丹望着他的心上人（beloved，beloved 指深爱的人；作形容词即“深爱的”），用的是他看一场不再让他吃惊的火情时的眼神；主持了河谷三十年婚礼的牧师用的是娶嫁（marry，marry 指娶、嫁，结为夫妻）的短式；离婚（divorce，divorce 指婚姻的法律解除）被从讲道台上提过一次，作为两人身后都没有的东西——牧师称之为对他个人的职业性礼遇；门廊处的吻（kiss，kiss 指唇与唇的相触，示爱或致意）为摄影师保留了一帧，随后在大门口免费重演了一次；街坊的深情（affection，affection 指喜爱、温暖而安定的好感）浓到钟声都迟了才开始——敲钟人也都挤在大门口。蜜月（honeymoon，honeymoon 指新婚夫妇的假期；这个词的“蜜”和“月”里存着甜头只保一个月的旧观念）是外赫布里底十二天，淡季，沃德小姐选的，天气也识趣地坏透了，于是两人休整充分地回来了；她的合伙人（partner，partner 指在生意或人生里与人分担共享的另一方）——诊所那位——负责捧戒指，此后每年圣诞晚会上都要讲烟丝铁盒的故事，越讲越精彩。全天唯一（sole，sole 指唯一的；这个词也指比目鱼和鞋底，三者皆为正经营生）的灾祸是伴郎致辞，十一分钟，至今没有被原谅过。

怀夫人在两位新人走到教堂墓地大门之前就把他们登上了家谱纸；红墨水，纸商说，保用一百年。

quiz.q: Miss Warde, the veterinary surgeon, is the animals' doctor of the valley — veterinary meaning of the healing of animals. Veterinary means —
o: of the buying and selling of meat
quiz.ex: veterinary = 兽医的。a veterinary surgeon 兽医；veterinary medicine 兽医学。

quiz.q: What began as acquaintance had reached first names by the second visit — slight knowledge of a person, social and short of friendship. An acquaintance is —
o: slight social knowledge of a person
the liking that has stopped keeping accounts
a person seized and held until terms are met
a companion in arms or in a trade
quiz.ex: acquaintance = 相识；熟人。a passing acquaintance 泛泛之交；make sb's acquaintance 结识某人。

quiz.q: The darts team called him a coward for waiting eleven years — one who shrinks from danger, pain or difficulty. A coward is —
o: one who shrinks from danger or difficulty
a man whose trade is fighting fires
a man admired for brave deeds
one who travels daily by train
quiz.ex: coward = 懦夫。cowardly adj. 胆怯的；cowardice n. 懦弱。

quiz.q: His comrades from the station held him hostage from eight until midnight — a person seized and held until terms are met. A hostage is —
o: a companion at the darts team
a person seized and held until terms are met
the holiday of the newly married
the legal ending of a marriage
quiz.ex: hostage = 人质。hold sb hostage 扣押某人为人质；hostage crisis 人质危机。

quiz.q: The respective mothers sat in the front pew and wept in formation — of or belonging to each; separate and particular to each. Respective means —
quiz.ex: respective = 各自的。their respective homes 他们各自的家；respectively adv. 分别地。

quiz.q: The honeymoon was twelve days in the Outer Hebrides, out of season — the holiday of the newly married. A honeymoon is —
o: the holiday of the newly married
the marriage rite with its feast
the rings held at the church door
quiz.ex: honeymoon = 蜜月。honeymoon period 蜜月期；go on one's honeymoon 去度蜜月。

quiz.q: Her partner from the practice held the rings — one who shares with another in a business, or in a life. A partner is —
o: a woman who acts for a living
one bound to learn a trade
one under the orders of another
one who shares in a business or a life
quiz.ex: partner = 合伙人；伴侣。a business partner 生意合伙人；life partner 人生伴侣。

quiz.q: The sole mishap of the day was the best man's speech — one and only. Sole means —
quiz.ex: sole = 唯一的。the sole survivor 唯一的幸存者；sole responsibility 全部责任。

title: The Meeting of the Valley
text:
The annual meeting of the parish {{council}} — a council being a body of persons chosen to deliberate and govern on behalf of the rest — is held in the corn exchange on the first Monday of April, between the whist drive and the judo, the hall bookings enforcing this with perfect impartiality. The {{member}}s — a member being one who belongs to a body, one of its number — sit behind the trestle table; the footbridge {{committee}} — a committee being a smaller body to which a larger one hands its business — which has sat since February without once standing, reports; the {{delegate}} — a delegate being one sent out with power to act for those who send him — to the county association gives his account of the county association, which is brief; and in the chair this year, standing in as {{deputy}} — a deputy being one appointed to act in another's place — for the chairman, who is at his daughter's in Perth, sat Mr. Wadsworth the cricket {{umpire}} — an umpire being the judge appointed to keep a game fair; by extension, any arbiter between two sides — on the grounds, as the Mercury put it, that he has watched the valley attempt to cheat at sport for thirty years without once being taken in.

The trade of the valley was present in person. The {{barber}} — a barber being one who cuts hair and shaves for his living — shut the shop for the hour, the first such closing in living memory, on a card reading BACK AT TWO; the {{haircut}} — a haircut being the cutting of the hair; by extension, the barber's whole trade and its price — could wait, he said, the dead being in no hurry and the living mostly done already. The {{butcher}} — a butcher being one who kills and sells meat — arrived with sawdust still on his apron and seconded everything, once each, on principle; the {{gardener}} — a gardener being one whose trade is the keeping of gardens — from the Hall brought his {{apprentice}} — an apprentice being one bound to serve a master and learn his trade, for years and small wages — to see, he said, how the governing classes behaved, the boy being at the doubting age; the {{fisherman}} — a fisherman being one who catches fish, for the market or for the pot — came up from the weir with a view of the footbridge that ran to forty minutes and finished nowhere; and the {{cashier}} — a cashier being one who has charge of money, receiving and paying — came up from the bank, the branch's future being the second item, and sat where he could see the door.

The professions had sent their full weight. Mr. Quayle, the {{solicitor}} — a solicitor being a lawyer who advises, drafts and prepares — had with him for the occasion a visiting cousin from Boston, a retired {{attorney}} — attorney being the American name for much the same officer — who compared the meeting, aloud and favourably, to a town meeting in Vermont, and was forgiven, the tea having been poured for him. The hospital {{consultant}} — a consultant being a senior physician to whom the difficult cases are sent — and the ear, nose and throat {{specialist}} — a specialist being one who gives himself wholly to one branch of a science or trade — shared the second row and a settled opinion of the hall's acoustics; the brewery's {{manager}} — a manager being one who runs a concern on behalf of its owners — spoke for the marquee licence; the quarry's {{boss}} — a boss being the master, the one who gives the orders; a word borrowed from America and worn smooth by use — took no sides, the bridge being bad for custom either way; the water board's {{director}} — a director being one who directs; a member of the governing board of a company — read a statement about levels; the road {{supervisor}} — a supervisor being one set over work and workers to see it done — stood at the back with his {{subordinate}}s — a subordinate being one under the orders of another — like a fence with its posts; and the {{colleague}}s — a colleague being a fellow of one's office or profession — of them all filled the settles, having come, as one said, to watch their betters argue for free.

The {{commuter}}s — a commuter being one who travels daily between home and work, most often by train — were the largest single party, the footbridge being the way to the station and the seven o'clock being the way to everything else; they sat with folded timetables and the stillness of men who have already stood for two hours that day.

The minute book, brought out for its tercentenary, put the company in its place. Under 1720 it records the baptism, the manumission and the hiring of one January Vye, born a {{slave}} — a slave being one who is the property of another, owned, bought and sold — in Barbados, brought home by a sea captain of the family, freed at the font of St. Cuthbert's, and kept on afterwards at wages as the parish's first paid gardener, the wage entered, at his own insistence, above his name; under 1802, the burial and the bequest of the parish {{beggar}} — a beggar being one who lives by asking alms — who had kept a pitch by the corn exchange for thirty years, saved fourteen pounds, and left the lot to the poor of the parish, the vestry having first weighed the coins for bad money; and against both entries, in a later hand, stands the word the valley has always used for itself: {{toil}} — toil meaning hard, wearying work, the honest kind being understood — honest toil, which the meeting took, unanimously, to be the whole of the record and the better part of the speech.

The item itself ran two hours. Old Lord Lampford, the retired {{chancellor}} — a chancellor being, among other things, the elected head of a university; in the state, one of the great officers — of his university, who has held the Hall and the chairman's opinions since 1979, opened for the bridge in Latin, briefly, and then in English, at length; the {{commander}} — a commander being one in command; an officer set over officers — of the fire brigade gave the safety case, being the only speaker of the evening to be heard without a single cough, on the grounds of practice; the {{proponent}} — a proponent being one who puts a scheme forward and stands behind it — of the cheaper option, the engineer, had brought drawings; the school {{counsellor}} — a counsellor being one who gives counsel, especially of the listening kind — spoke for the children who cross the ford in term time; and the summer theatre's leading {{actress}} — an actress being a woman who acts — read the objections as a set piece, dying beautifully on each, which settled the vote if the speeches had not.

The bridge was carried, forty-one to nine, the nine being the trout, by the fisherman's account. The meeting rose at ten; the judo had the hall by half past; and the minute book was carried back to the safe by the deputy and the umpire together, the one holding the lamp, the other the past, and both walking, the Mercury noted, as if the book were the heavier.
tr:
教区议会（council，council 指受众人推选、代为议事与治理的一班人）的年会在四月的第一个星期一于谷物交易所召开，排在惠斯特牌局和柔道课之间——场地预订表在这件事上铁面无私。议员们（member，member 指团体中的一员）坐在长条桌后；人行桥委员会（committee，committee 指大团体把事务托付给的小团体）自二月起一直“坐着”开会、一次也没“站”过，此刻前来汇报；派驻郡联合会的代表（delegate，delegate 指奉派出、有权代众人行事之人）汇报郡联合会的情况，内容简短；而今年坐在主席位上、替正在珀斯女儿家的主席代行职务的副手（deputy，deputy 指受命代他人之职者），是板球裁判（umpire，umpire 指受委以保证比赛公平的裁判；引申为争执双方的公断人）沃兹沃思先生——用《信使报》的话说，理由是他看了三十年河谷在体育运动上耍花招，一次也没上过当。

河谷的各行当都亲身到场。理发师（barber，barber 指以剃头剪发为生的人）停业一小时，门上挂牌“两点回来”，记忆所及头一回；理发（haircut，haircut 指剪发这件事；引申指理发师的全套营生和价钱）不急，他说，死人赶时间，活人多半已经理完了。屠夫（butcher，butcher 指宰杀并售卖肉类的人）到场时围裙上还带着锯末，对每项动议都附议一次，这是原则；庄园的园丁（gardener，gardener 指以照料花园为业者）把他的学徒（apprentice，apprentice 指立契跟师学艺数年、领取微薄津贴之人）带来了，说是让他见识见识统治阶层的行为举止——这孩子正处在怀疑一切的年纪；渔夫（fisherman，fisherman 指捕鱼的人，为市集或为口腹）从堰坝上来，关于人行桥的看法讲了四十分钟，没有结论；银行出纳（cashier，cashier 指经手钱款、负责收付之人）从分行上来——分行的前途是第二项议程——坐在看得见门的位置。

专业阶层也倾巢出动。事务律师（solicitor，solicitor 指提供法律意见、起草文书的律师）奎尔先生带了位从波士顿来的表亲撑场面，一位退休的律师（attorney，attorney 指律师，是美国人对大致同一职位的叫法），他大声且善意地把这场会比作佛蒙特镇的镇民大会，并且被原谅了——茶是给他斟的。医院的会诊医生（consultant，consultant 指疑难病例被送到他那里的高级医师）和耳鼻喉专家（specialist，specialist 指潜心一门学科或行业的人）共用第二排座位，同时对礼堂的音效持保留意见；啤酒厂的经理（manager，manager 指替业主经营企业之人）为帐篷售酒执照发言；采石场的老板（boss，boss 指工头、发号施令者；这个词是从美国借来的，已经用得溜光）不表态——桥修与不修对生意都不妙；水务局的董事（director，director 指主持其事者；公司管理委员会的成员）宣读了一份关于水位的声明；道路监工（supervisor，supervisor 指督视工程与工人之人）带着他的下属（subordinate，subordinate 指受他人指挥之人）站在后排，像一排带桩的栅栏；他们的诸位同行（colleague，colleague 指同一机构或行业的同僚）坐满了长椅，用其中一人的话说，是来看上等人免费吵架的。

通勤者（commuter，commuter 指每日往返于住所与工作地之间的人，多半乘火车）是最大的一党——人行桥是去车站的路，七点钟那班车是去其余一切的路；他们带着折好的时刻表，带着今天已经站过两小时的人才有的那种安静。

为纪念三百周年搬出来的会议记录簿，让在场诸公各安其分。一七二〇年那页记着一位雅努埃里·怀的受洗、释奴与受雇：他生为巴巴多斯的奴隶（slave，slave 指作为他人财产、可被拥有买卖之人），被家族里一位船长带回家，在圣卡斯伯特教堂的洗礼盆前获得自由，此后领工钱留用，成了教区第一位领薪的园丁——工钱那一笔按他本人的坚持记在名字上方。一八〇二年那页记着教区乞丐（beggar，beggar 指靠求人施舍为生者）的下葬与遗赠：他在谷物交易所旁的固定摊位守了三十年，攒下十四镑，全数遗赠教区贫民——教务会先把硬币验了一遍成色。两条记录的页边，有一只后来的手写着河谷一贯用来自称的那个词：辛劳（toil，toil 指艰苦、累人的活计；“诚实的”是不言自明的）——“honest toil”，全会一致认为，这四个字就是整部记录，也是当晚演说里最好的部分。

议程本身进行了两个小时。老兰普福德勋爵——他大学荣休的名誉校长（chancellor，chancellor 义项之一指大学推举的首脑；国家层面指国之重臣），自一九七九年起执掌庄园和主席的意见——先用拉丁语简短地为人行桥开了场，然后用英语，详尽地；消防队的指挥官（commander，commander 指指挥之人；管辖军官的军官）讲了安全方面的问题，是整晚唯一发言时没人咳嗽压过的讲者，理由是训练有素；便宜方案的倡议者（proponent，proponent 指提出方案并站在方案后面的人）、那位工程师，带了图纸来；学校的辅导老师（counsellor，counsellor 指给人以劝导之人，尤指善听的那种劝导）替学期里蹚水过滩的孩子们说了话；夏季剧社的当家女演员（actress，actress 指演戏的女子）把反对意见念成了折子戏，每念一条便美丽地死去一次——就算前面的演讲没定局，这一出也把票定了。

桥以四十一票对九票通过，那九票按渔夫的说法是鳟鱼投的。十点散会，柔道课十点半进场；记录簿由副手和裁判一并护送回保险柜，一个举灯，一个捧着过去——《信使报》注意到，两人走路的架势，都仿佛捧的是更沉的那位。

quiz.q: The annual meeting of the parish council is held in the corn exchange — a body of persons chosen to deliberate and govern on behalf of the rest. A council is —
o: the judge who keeps a game fair
a body chosen to deliberate and govern
a smaller body handed the business
one sent out with power to act
quiz.ex: council = 议会；委员会。parish council 教区议会；city council 市议会。

quiz.q: Mr. Wadsworth the cricket umpire sat in the chair — the judge appointed to keep a game fair; any arbiter between two sides. An umpire is —
o: one who has charge of money
one appointed to act in another's place
one who kills and sells meat
the judge appointed to keep a game fair
quiz.ex: umpire = 裁判。a cricket umpire 板球裁判；umpire a match 担任比赛裁判。

quiz.q: The gardener brought his apprentice to see how the governing classes behaved — one bound to serve a master and learn his trade. An apprentice is —
o: one set over work and workers
one who cuts hair for a living
one given wholly to one branch
one bound to learn a trade from a master
quiz.ex: apprentice = 学徒。an apprentice to a gardener 园丁的学徒；serve as an apprentice 当学徒。

quiz.q: A visiting cousin from Boston, a retired attorney — the American name for much the same officer as the solicitor. An attorney is —
o: one who runs a concern for owners
a senior physician of hard cases
a member of a company's board
the American name for a lawyer
quiz.ex: attorney = 律师（美）。power of attorney 委托书；attorney general 总检察长。

quiz.q: The commuters were the largest party, the footbridge being the way to the station — one who travels daily between home and work. A commuter is —
o: one who lives by asking alms
one who travels daily between home and work
one who catches fish for the market
one freed at the font of a church
quiz.ex: commuter = 通勤者。commuter belt 通勤带；commute v. 通勤。

quiz.q: One January Vye, born a slave in Barbados, freed at the font — one who is the property of another. A slave is —
o: one bound to serve for small wages
one who is the property of another
one whose work is hard and wearying
one kept on afterwards at wages
quiz.ex: slave = 奴隶。born a slave 生而为奴；the slave trade 奴隶贸易。

quiz.q: The proponent of the cheaper option had brought drawings — one who puts a scheme forward and stands behind it. A proponent is —
o: one who puts a scheme forward
the elected head of a university
one who gives counsel that listens
quiz.ex: proponent = 倡议者；拥护者。a proponent of reform 改革的倡议者。

quiz.q: The school counsellor spoke for the children who cross the ford — one who gives counsel, especially of the listening kind. A counsellor is —
o: one who receives and pays money
a woman who acts for a living
quiz.ex: counsellor = 辅导员；顾问。a school counsellor 学校心理辅导老师；marriage guidance counsellor 婚姻辅导师。

title: The Great Sheep Escape
text:
The meadow behind the mill was {{mow}}n — to mow meaning to cut grass, with scythe or with machine — at last on the second Saturday of June, three weeks late and all the better for it; and the forty-two ewes in the next field watched the operation with the interest of critics. When Mr. Sprague's nephew went up to the house for his dinner, he left the top gate resting on its post instead of latched; and it is the settled view of the valley that the sheep had been waiting all morning for exactly this. At the first shout they {{panic}}ked — to panic meaning to be seized by a sudden terror that spreads — and {{flee}}d — to flee meaning to run away, from danger or from duty — through the gap and down the hill toward the town, at the pace of a small grey flood.

What followed took eleven minutes and is retold at the Bull in versions that agree only on the number of sheep. The flock {{scatter}}ed — to scatter meaning to fling apart, to spread in all directions — at the war memorial; one ewe {{collide}}d — to collide meaning to strike together, one body against another — with the baker's bicycle, which {{upset}} — to upset meaning to knock over; and by extension, to distress — the rack of seed trays outside the Stores; and the milk churns at the dairy door went over together, so that the milk {{spill}}ed — to spill meaning to run over and out of what was holding it — across the pavement in a white tide the Mercury later measured in column inches. A ladder against the George and Dragon {{tilt}}ed — to tilt meaning to lean, to tip toward one side — and was saved; the sacks on Hosken's lorry {{sway}}ed — to sway meaning to swing, to lean this way and that — and were not, two of them choosing the moment to {{drop}} — to drop meaning to fall, to let fall — into the road and burst.

The town, to do it justice, did not stand and watch. Mrs. Tizzard came off her step with a speed the Guinness people would want in writing, and {{grab}}bed — to grab meaning to seize roughly and at once — the leader by the fleece; the butcher {{snatch}}ed — to snatch meaning to seize hastily, in passing — at a second and got the neck wool; the schoolmistress, marshalling her infants behind the bus shelter, was close enough to {{catch}} — to catch meaning to take hold of a thing in motion — a third as it went by, and did; and the gardener from the Hall intercepted the last of them at the lychgate and {{grasp}}ed — to grasp meaning to seize and hold fast — a double armful of it. The whole street {{lean}}ed — to lean meaning to incline the body, to bend for a better view — out of its windows. Nell the dog — who had watched the entire escape from the hill with the expression of a professional on holiday — arrived at last, took the flock on her eye, and {{propel}}led — to propel meaning to drive forward, to push on — them up the lane; the school did not need telling twice to {{hurry}} — to hurry meaning to move with haste — to the railings; and Mr. Sprague {{hasten}}ed — to hasten meaning to make haste, to come at speed — down from the meadow in the tractor, {{steer}}ing — to steer meaning to guide the course of, as of a vehicle — it between the memorial and the postbox with an inch to spare on either side. The sheep, finding themselves between dog, tractor and the entire population of Millbrook, chose the one door left open — the mill yard, where the race was running — and {{launch}}ed — to launch meaning to set moving with force; to send off — themselves into the water in a body.

The wheel, which has not {{rotate}}d — to rotate meaning to turn on an axis, as a wheel turns — to any purpose since 1911, turned half a revolution out of habit. The flock gathered on the island below the hatch, forty-two wet sheep — the number was verified twice, once by count and once by reputation — standing like a committee that has lost its chairman. Dan Locke brought the tender and {{tow}}ed — to tow meaning to pull along by a rope or a chain — the worst swimmers out two at a time; Mr. Sprague, wading, {{twist}}ed — to twist meaning to turn sharply; to wrench — his ankle in a rabbit hole and was towed out himself, to the enjoyment of everybody but two. The last ewe stopped on the bank to {{shake}} — to shake meaning to be moved quickly to and fro; to tremble — the water from her fleece, and looked back at the race with something like satisfaction.

Afterwards there was the accounting. The {{trail}} — a trail being the line left behind by what has passed — of evidence ran from the top gate to the church porch, and was swept up by the verger with dignity. The lorry, in all the excitement, had {{touch}}ed — to touch meaning to come into light contact with — the bridge wall, which Hosken reported to himself and to nobody else. The baker {{react}}ed — to react meaning to act in answer, to respond from feeling — by laughing; the butcher by ordering a new bicycle bell; and the vicar {{respond}}ed — to respond meaning to answer, in word or in act — with tea for everybody in the schoolroom, on the grounds that the town had earned it. The motorcyclist whose backfire had started it all was {{scold}}ed — to scold meaning to rebuke with words, at length and in public — by Mrs. Tizzard to the exact degree the town felt appropriate; {{excuse}}s — an excuse being the apology offered in place of the deed — were offered by, and accepted from, the nephew, whose face had by then done three days of penance in one afternoon. Asked whether he could {{forgive}} — to forgive meaning to pardon, to give up resentment — the contractor, Mr. Sprague said he could, by supper, and did. The mutton jokes {{annoy}}ed — to annoy meaning to vex, to trouble with small persistent provocations — him for a week; and the ewes themselves, back in the pen, {{behave}}d — to behave meaning to conduct oneself; to act as one should — with an air of perfect propriety, as though the afternoon had been arranged for their instruction. Only Nell was unappeased: she {{tap}}ped — to tap meaning to strike lightly — the gatepost twice with her paw, in the way she has, and went to sleep facing the hill. The children at the railings needed {{reassure|reassuring}} — to reassure meaning to restore confidence to, to make safe again — on one point only, that the sheep had enjoyed it; and on this the valley, the vicar and the schoolmistress were happily agreed.
tr:
磨坊后面的草场终于在六月第二个星期六开了镰（mow，mow 指用镰刀或机器割草）——晚了三个星期，反倒因祸得福；隔壁田里的四十二只母羊全程围观，神情如评委。斯普拉格先生的侄子上屋吃午饭时，把顶门搭在门柱上而没有扣上；河谷的一致看法是：羊群等这一刻等了一整个上午。第一声吆喝响起，它们便惊慌失措（panic，panic 指被突然而蔓延的恐惧攫住）起来，从缺口逃窜（flee，flee 指逃跑，逃离危险或逃离职责）而出，顺坡冲向镇子，速度堪比一场灰色的小洪水。

接下来的十一分钟，“公牛”里流传的各个版本只在羊的数目上一致。羊群在战争纪念碑前四散（scatter，scatter 指散开、向各处飞溅）开来；一只母羊撞上（collide，collide 指相撞、一个身体撞上另一个）面包师的自行车，车又掀翻（upset，upset 指打翻；引申为使人心烦意乱）了杂货铺门外的育苗架；奶站门口的奶桶一齐倒下，牛奶泼洒（spill，spill 指漫出、从盛着它的容器里流出来）过人行道，成了一道白色潮水——后来《信使报》用栏寸来计量它。“乔治与龙”门口的梯子倾侧（tilt，tilt 指倾斜、歪向一边）了一下，被扶住了；霍斯肯货车上的麻袋摇晃（sway，sway 指摇摆、晃来晃去）起来，却没人管——其中两袋瞅准时机摔落（drop，drop 指落下、掉下）到路上，破了。

必须说句公道话：镇子没有袖手旁观。蒂泽德太太从台阶上冲下来的速度，吉尼斯方面都想请她出具书面证明；她一把攥住（grab，grab 指粗鲁地、立刻抓住）领头羊的羊毛；屠夫顺手一捞（snatch，snatch 指匆忙间抓住、掠过时抓取）第二只，攥了一把颈毛；正在公交候车亭后集合孩子们的女校长离得近，赶上一只跑过的便顺势捉住（catch，catch 指抓住运动中的东西）了第三只；霍尔庄园的园丁在教堂墓地门口截住最后一只，满满一怀地牢牢抓住（grasp，grasp 指抓住并握紧）。整条街的人都从窗口探身（lean，lean 指俯身、倚出去）出来。内尔——那条从山上全程围观、表情像休假中的专业人士的牧羊犬——终于赶到，一眼定住羊群，把它们沿着小巷一路驱赶（propel，propel 指推动、驱策向前）；学校的孩子根本不用吩咐第二遍就急忙（hurry，hurry 指带着急切移动、赶紧行动）奔向栏杆；斯普拉格先生驾着拖拉机从草场上疾驰（hasten，hasten 指赶紧行动、加速赶来）而下，在纪念碑和邮筒之间掌舵（steer，steer 指引导方向，如驾驶车辆）穿行，两边各余一寸。羊群发现自己夹在狗、拖拉机和磨坊溪全体居民之间，便选中了仅剩的那扇敞开的门——磨坊院子，那里的水渠正奔流，于是它们成群发力、纵身（launch，launch 指用力发动、投掷出去）跳进了水里。

那只自一九一一年起就没正经转过（rotate，rotate 指绕轴旋转，如车轮转动）的水轮，出于习惯转了半圈。羊群聚在水闸下面的河心洲上，四十二只湿羊——数目核对了两遍，一遍靠清点，一遍靠口碑——站在那儿，活像一个丢了主席的委员会。丹·洛克开来消防艇，把水性最差的几只两只两只地拖曳（tow，tow 指用绳索或铁链拖拽）出来；斯普拉格先生蹚水时在兔窝里崴了（twist，twist 指扭伤、猛地拧转）脚踝，结果自己也被拖了一只来回——除了两个人，人人都觉得好看。最后一只上岸的母羊停在岸边，抖掉（shake，shake 指快速摇动、抖动）毛里的水，回头望了一眼水渠，神情近乎满意。

事后自然要算账。从顶门到教堂门廊，一路留着羊群经过的踪迹（trail，trail 指经过之物留下的一线痕迹），教堂司事庄重地扫净了。慌乱之中，货车蹭到（touch，touch 指轻轻碰上）了桥墙，霍斯肯向他自己汇报了此事，再无他人知晓。面包师的反应（react，react 指作出反应、出于情绪而回应）是大笑；屠夫的反应是订了一只新车铃；牧师的回应（respond，respond 指以言语或行动作答）是在教室里给所有人上茶，理由是全镇都挣得了这顿。那辆回火引发一切的摩托车手，被蒂泽德太太数落（scold，scold 指责骂、当众训斥）了恰好全镇认为合适的长度；侄子赔了不是（excuse，excuse 指以辩解代替行为的托词），也被接受了——到那时，他的脸已经在一下午里做完了三天的苦修。有人问斯普拉格先生能否原谅（forgive，forgive 指宽恕、放下怨气）包工头，他说到晚饭时就能，而且做到了。屠夫的羊肉笑话让他恼火（annoy，annoy 指因细小而持续的撩拨而恼怒）了一个星期；而回到栏里的母羊们举止（behave，behave 指行为举止、守规矩）无可挑剔，一副整个下午都是为它们受教育而安排的神气。只有内尔意难平：她用爪子在门柱上轻敲（tap，tap 指轻叩）了两下，以她惯有的方式，然后面朝小山睡着了。从头到尾扒在学校栏杆上的孩子们只需要被宽慰（reassure，reassure 指使人重获安心）一件事：羊玩得很开心——在这一点上，河谷、牧师和女校长欣然一致。

quiz.q: The flock scattered at the war memorial — to fling apart, to spread in all directions. To scatter is to —
o: turn on an axis like a wheel
quiz.ex: scatter = 散开；撒播。The crowd scattered 人群散开；scatter seeds 播种。

quiz.q: One ewe collided with the baker's bicycle — to strike together, one body against another. To collide is to —
o: run over out of the churn
drop into the road and burst
quiz.ex: collide = 碰撞。collide with a lorry 与货车相撞；collision n. 碰撞。

quiz.q: Nell took the flock on her eye and propelled them up the lane — to drive forward, to push on. To propel is to —
quiz.ex: propel = 推进；驱策。a boat propelled by oars 由桨推动的船；propeller 螺旋桨。

quiz.q: The sheep chose the mill yard and launched themselves into the water — to set moving with force; to send off. To launch is to —
quiz.ex: launch = 发射；使下水；发起。launch a ship 使船下水；launch an attack 发动进攻。

quiz.q: Dan Locke towed the worst swimmers out two at a time — to pull along by a rope or chain. To tow is to —
o: pull along by a rope or chain
quiz.ex: tow = 拖；牵引。tow a car away 把车拖走；a tow rope 拖缆。

quiz.q: Mr. Sprague twisted his ankle in a rabbit hole — to turn sharply; to wrench. To twist is to —
quiz.ex: twist = 扭；拧；扭伤。twist one's ankle 扭伤脚踝；twist the cap 拧开盖子。

quiz.q: Excuses were offered by, and accepted from, the nephew — the apology offered in place of the deed. An excuse is —
o: the apology offered in place of the deed
the line left by what has passed
quiz.ex: excuse = 借口；辩解。make an excuse 找借口；excuse me 对不起（客套语）。

quiz.q: The children needed reassuring on one point only — to restore confidence to, to make safe again. To reassure is to —
quiz.ex: reassure = 使安心；打消疑虑。reassure the passengers 安抚乘客；reassuring news 令人宽心的消息。

title: The Night of the Gale
text:
The gale came in from the southwest on the third of February, in the dark, without an introduction. By nine the church tower {{loom}}ed — to loom meaning to rise vast and dim against the sky, with an air of threat — over streets that usually pretend not to notice it; by ten the rain had given up falling and was travelling {{sideways}} — sideways meaning to or toward the side, and not downward — in ropes and in handfuls; and by eleven the Mercury's correspondent, filing from the Bull by candle, the power having failed at half past, had used the word unprecedented twice. The loose shutter that had rattled since dusk was {{muffle}}d — to muffle meaning to wrap or pad so as to deaden sound — with a rolled blanket, and the house settled.

Slate {{plummet}}ed — to plummet meaning to fall straight and fast, like the plumb line — from the George and Dragon into the yard; the poplar at the ford {{reel}}ed — to reel meaning to sway and stagger, as a man does when struck — like a man remembering an old wound; rubbish {{whirl}}ed — to whirl meaning to spin and circle rapidly — down the high street in shapes nobody could name; the school windows {{vibrate}}d — to vibrate meaning to tremble with rapid motion — in their frames; and the river, which had been rising all day, {{saturate}}d — to saturate meaning to soak utterly, to fill to capacity — the water meadows in the dark, so that by morning the valley floor was a second river with the first one's opinions about roads.

After midnight the water began to {{seep}} — to seep meaning to pass slowly through, as through small openings — under Widow Tregenna's back door; the cellar at Rose Cottage began to {{ooze}} — to ooze meaning to flow or leak out slowly, thickly — at the joints of the old floor; and the school roof, patched twice and promised oftener, began to {{leak}} — to leak meaning to let in what should be kept out — in four places, which the schoolmistress located by the arithmetic of the buckets. The causes were established next day: a gutter given over to {{neglect}} — neglect meaning the leaving of what ought to be attended to — for want of a ladder, and a report from the surveyor that {{cause}}d — to cause meaning to bring about, to be the origin of — the promising to be promised again.

The town {{cope}}d — to cope meaning to manage, to deal successfully with what is thrown at one — in its own fashion. Mrs. Tizzard {{fasten}}ed — to fasten meaning to fix firmly, to make fast — the shutters; the boatman rowed out at the worst of it to {{loosen}} — to loosen meaning to unfasten, to slacken — the mooring ropes; the plumber {{wrap}}ped — to wrap meaning to wind round, to cover by winding — the standpipe in sacking; the fire crew {{fold}}ed — to fold meaning to double over upon itself — the great tarpaulin over the haystack; a wedge was {{insert}}ed — to insert meaning to put in, to drive between — under the schoolhouse door; the cat {{scratch}}ed — to scratch meaning to claw at, to mark with the claws — at the shutter until somebody took pity; a branch of the copper beech {{scrape}}d — to scrape meaning to rub against, with friction — the vestry roof all night, like a beggar with a grievance; and the fete poster, left up since July by an optimist, {{peel}}ed — to peel meaning to come away in strips, as skin from a fruit — off the hoarding and went into the dark, promoting nothing.

Morning came grey and quiet, the gale blown out to sea and taking no responsibility with it. The poplar had {{split}} — to split meaning to crack apart along the grain — from crown to shoulder; the road by the ford was {{clear}}ed — to clear meaning to remove what blocks or fills — of branches by Dan Locke's crew before the milk van needed it; and the village turned out to {{sort}} — to sort meaning to separate into kinds, to put in order — the wreckage into the burnable, the mendable and the ceremonially retellable. The {{mess}} — a mess being a state of disorder, of things out of their places — was general but not tragic: nobody hurt, nothing lost that could not be mended except the poplar's dignity. The burglar alarm at the Stores, {{trigger}}ed — to trigger meaning to set off, to spring — by the power's return at three in the morning, summoned the brigade a second time; the cistern at the Manse, which could not {{contain}} — to contain meaning to hold within, to have room for — another hour of it, gave up at dawn; the moon, {{conceal}}ed — to conceal meaning to hide, to keep from sight — since Tuesday, came out at midnight like an auditor; and the old punt at the boathouse chose the night to {{sink}} — to sink meaning to go down below the water — properly at last.

The vicar {{kneel}}ed — to kneel meaning to rest upon the knees — in the flooded vestry to save the parish registers, wet to the elbows and reconciled to it; the shepherd's wet wool {{itch}}ed — to itch meaning to prick and irritate the skin — all day, which he took as evidence of being alive; everybody with a beam to shore up had {{exert}}ed — to exert meaning to put forth strength, to apply force — themselves nobly; and the main beam of the hay barn, which had {{bear}}... borne — to bear meaning to carry, to support weight — gales since Victoria, bore this one too. The Bull itself, which has {{survive}}d — to survive meaning to outlast, to live through — storms, floods, two fires and the 1970s, took two feet of water in the cellar and lost a chimney pot; and by noon the bar was {{wipe}}d — to wipe meaning to rub over with a cloth, to clean or to dry — down, the fire was lit, and the whole affair was being converted into anecdote at the usual speed.
tr:
大风是二月三日从西南方向来的，在黑暗里，无人引荐。九点，教堂尖塔已隐隐浮现（loom，loom 指庞然朦胧地逼现、带着威胁的气势压上）在街道上空——而这条街平日里假装注意不到它；十点，雨已放弃下落，改为一股一股、一捧一捧地横着（sideways，sideways 指向侧面、不朝下）飞行；十一点，《信使报》的通讯员在“公牛”借烛光发稿——电在半点钟就断了——已经两次用上“史无前例”这个词。那扇入夜起就哐当作响的活百叶窗，被一床卷起的毯子裹住捂住了声（muffle，muffle 指裹住或填塞以消音），屋子这才安定下来。

石板从“乔治与龙”笔直坠落（plummet，plummet 指垂直急坠，如铅垂线），掉进后院；浅滩边那棵杨树像想起旧伤的人一样踉跄摇晃（reel，reel 指摇晃蹒跚，如受击之人）；垃圾瓦砾顺着大街打着旋（whirl，whirl 指快速旋转回旋）飞过，形状没人叫得出名字；学校的窗子在框里震颤（vibrate，vibrate 指快速颤动）；而涨了一整天的河在黑暗里把水草地彻底浸透（saturate，saturate 指浸透、饱和），到早晨，谷底已成第二条河，并且继承了第一条河对道路的全部意见。

半夜过后，水开始从特雷根纳寡妇的后门底下渗进（seep，seep 指从缝隙缓慢渗过）来；玫瑰小屋的地窖从旧地板的接缝里慢慢洇出（ooze，ooze 指缓慢而黏稠地渗流）水来；学校的屋顶——补过两次、许诺过更多次——从四处漏（leak，leak 指本该挡在外面的东西漏了进来）起雨，女校长靠水桶的算术定位了这四处。缘由第二天查明：一条因够不着梯子而失修（neglect，neglect 指该照管的事被搁置不管）的檐沟，外加测量员的一份言辞妥帖的报告，这份报告促成（cause，cause 指引起、成为……的起因）了“许诺过更多次”变成“再次许诺”。

镇子以自己的方式应对（cope，cope 指应付、成功地处理扔到面前的局面）了过去。蒂泽德太太钉牢（fasten，fasten 指固定、系牢）了窗板；船工在风最大的时候摇出去，解开（loosen，loosen 指松开、放松）系船的缆绳；水暖工用麻布把立管缠裹（wrap，wrap 指缠绕包裹）起来；消防队把大块油布对折（fold，fold 指对折、翻叠）后蒙住干草垛；校舍门下楔进（insert，insert 指插入、塞进）一块楔子；家里的猫对着窗板抓挠（scratch，scratch 指用爪子挠、抓刮）个不停，直到有人发了善心；铜毛榉的一根枝条整夜蹭着（scrape，scrape 指摩擦刮蹭）法衣室的屋顶，像个含冤的告状人；而那张自七月就被乐观者挂着的游园会海报，四角一一投降，成条剥落（peel，peel 指剥落、成片脱下），飞进黑暗里，从此什么也不推销了。

清晨灰白而安静，大风出海去了，责任一概不带。杨树从树冠到肩部劈裂（split，split 指顺着纹理裂开）；丹·洛克的班组赶在送奶车需要之前，把浅滩旁路上的树枝清除（clear，clear 指清除堵塞、占位之物）干净；全村出动，把废墟分拣（sort，sort 指分类归置）成可烧的、可修的和可供郑重讲古的。满目狼藉（mess，mess 指混乱、东西不成样子的状态）是普遍的，悲剧却不是：无人受伤，除了杨树的体面，没有失去任何修不回来的东西。杂货铺的防盗警报在凌晨三点被恢复的电力触发（trigger，trigger 指触发、引发），把消防队招来了第二趟；牧师宅的储水槽再也容纳（contain，contain 指盛得下、装得住）不下多一个小时的大雨，黎明时分彻底放弃了；自星期二起就被云遮蔽（conceal，conceal 指隐藏、藏匿不见）的月亮半夜露了面，神情如查账的；船屋里那条旧平底船选在这一夜正式沉没（sink，sink 指下沉、没入水下）了，总算沉得其所。

牧师跪（kneel，kneel 指跪下）在被淹的法衣室里抢救教区登记册，湿到臂肘，内心已与此事和解；牧羊人湿透的羊毛外套扎痒（itch，itch 指皮肤刺痒难耐）了一整天，他视之为活着的证据；凡是需要顶梁的人都奋力争了一把力（exert，exert 指使力、出力）；干草棚的主梁自维多利亚时代起就一直在承载（bear，bear 指承受重量、支撑），这一晚也扛了下来。“公牛”自身经历过风暴、洪水、两场大火和整个二十世纪七十年代，都熬了过来（survive，survive 指幸存、熬过、比……活得久），这回地窖进了两英尺水，丢了一只烟囱帽；到中午，吧台已擦拭（wipe，wipe 指用布擦净、揩干）干净，炉火生起，整场灾难正以惯常的速度被加工成轶闻。

quiz.q: Slate plummeted from the George and Dragon into the yard — to fall straight and fast, like the plumb line. To plummet is to —
quiz.ex: plummet = 骤降；垂直坠落。Prices plummeted 物价暴跌。

quiz.q: The poplar at the ford reeled like a man remembering an old wound — to sway and stagger, as one struck. To reel is to —
quiz.ex: reel = 蹒跚；摇晃。reel under the blow 被打得踉跄；reel off 一口气说出。

quiz.q: The water began to seep under the back door at midnight — to pass slowly through, as through small openings. To seep is to —
quiz.ex: seep = 渗漏；渗出。rain seeping through the roof 渗过屋顶的雨。

quiz.q: The cellar began to ooze at the joints of the old floor — to flow or leak out slowly, thickly. To ooze is to —
quiz.ex: ooze = 渗出；缓缓流出。mud oozing between the toes 从脚趾间冒出的泥。

quiz.q: The river saturated the water meadows in the dark — to soak utterly, to fill to capacity. To saturate is to —
quiz.ex: saturate = 使饱和；浸透。a saturated sponge 吸饱水的海绵；saturated fat 饱和脂肪。

quiz.q: The burglar alarm, triggered by the power's return at three, summoned the brigade again — to set off, to spring. To trigger is to —
quiz.ex: trigger = 触发；引爆。trigger an alarm 触发警报；the trigger of a gun 扳机。

quiz.q: The fête poster peeled off the hoarding and went into the dark — to come away in strips, as skin from a fruit. To peel is to —
quiz.ex: peel = 剥落；去皮。peel an apple 削苹果；paint peeling 油漆剥落。

quiz.q: Everybody with a beam to shore up exerted themselves nobly — to put forth strength, to apply force. To exert is to —
quiz.ex: exert = 施加；尽力。exert oneself 尽力；exert influence 施加影响。

title: The Fête
text:
The fete is held on the vicarage lawn on the last Saturday of July, to {{celebrate}} — to celebrate meaning to keep a day with festivity — the patronal festival, the harvest being still a rumour and the school holidays a fact. The committee {{invite}}s — to invite meaning to ask, to bid to come — the whole valley by poster; the valley arrives and is {{welcome}} — to welcome meaning to receive with gladness, to greet warmly on arrival — at the gate from eleven; and the greetings there are the valley's own liturgy, neighbours who have {{greet}}ed — to greet meaning to meet with words of welcome — one another at the same gate for forty years performing it again with undiminished ceremony. At noon Lord Lampford opens the proceedings; the Legion under Bill Skidmore {{salute}}s — to salute meaning to greet with formal honour, as soldiers do — the flag with a precision the church clock then copies; and the vicar {{bless}}es — to bless meaning to ask God's favour upon — the produce tent, the personnel and the weather, in that order.

The fortune teller's tent does the steadiest trade, its {{allure}} — allure meaning the power of attraction, of drawing by charm — being the one force in the valley that has never needed a poster. Madame Zora, who is Mrs. Hosken in a headscarf and a changed voice, {{gaze}}s — to gaze meaning to look long and steadily — into her crystal ball with total commitment, {{glance}}s — to glance meaning to look quickly, and away again — at her watch between customers, and has predicted the same wedding for the same girl three years running, on the sound principle that she will be right eventually. The coconut shy {{attract}}s — to attract meaning to draw toward itself — the optimists; the tombola {{arouse}}s — to arouse meaning to stir up, to waken, as interest or feeling — the cupidity of the sober; the infants {{peep}} — to peep meaning to look through a small opening, slyly and briefly — into the bran tub before plunging an arm; and those who decline the shilling entrance {{peer}} — to peer meaning to look closely and with effort, as over or through something — over the churchyard wall all afternoon, in the numbers of a fire drill. Nobody saw the bishop arrive; several {{glimpse}}d — to glimpse meaning to catch a brief, partial sight of — him leaving, by the hedge, with a toffee apple.

In the marquee the whist drive proceeds under the schoolmistress, who {{shuffle}}s — to shuffle meaning to mix by repeated passes, as cards — with the solemnity of surgery; and the gardener, known to the valley simply as the {{whistler}} — a whistler being one who whistles, which he does continuously and through the nose, so that the whist drive is accompanied — deals his own hand to a tune nobody can name. The marrow classes are where the honour lies. Mr. Sprague {{boast}}s — to boast meaning to praise oneself, one's beasts or one's vegetables, in loud terms — of his runner beans on the walk from the gate; the judge, drafted from the county show on the grounds of impartiality, {{flatter}}s — to flatter meaning to praise beyond the truth, to please with praise — nobody; the losers' wives {{tease}} — to tease meaning to mock playfully, without malice — the winners' husbands; the sceptics from the quarry {{mock}} — to mock meaning to ridicule, to laugh at with contempt — the whole institution of vegetable competition, from inside the beer tent, annually, and without the least effect; and in 1979 two sisters {{quarrel}}ed — to quarrel meaning to dispute angrily and at length — over the identity of a marrow, an {{argument}} — an argument being a dispute; the reasons offered on either side — that ran to forty minutes and cost two Christmases of silence, during which the sisters, meeting at the gate, could only {{glare}} — to glare meaning to look fiercely, with fixed anger — until the elder, bending for a better view of the scales, {{curse}}d — to curse meaning to swear; to call down evil upon — the pumpkin's ancestry in the hearing of the judge, who gave her second prize for honesty of fruit, if not of language.

The afternoon acts belong to the visitors. The magician from Lampford {{mesmerize}}s — to mesmerize meaning to hold spellbound, as the first mesmerists were said to hold their patients — the front three rows; his dove, released for the finale, {{astonish}}ed — to astonish meaning to strike with sudden wonder — everybody by roosting in the church tower and staying the week; the maypole {{bewilder}}s — to bewilder meaning to confuse utterly, to lose in a maze — nobody but its dancers; the trombonist of the town band, whose top note carries to the ford, {{amaze}}s — to amaze meaning to fill with astonishment — the sceptics from the quarry into silence, which no marrow ever managed; and the field {{clap}}ped — to clap meaning to strike the palms together in praise — and {{applaud}}ed — to applaud meaning to express approval, as by clapping — the whole of it, as it does every year, the memory of last year having been worn smooth by the winter; and the children, brought up to the front, {{stare}} — to stare meaning to look fixedly, with wide eyes — at the magician's moustache in a way he has mentioned to his wife.

The day closes as it opened, by ceremony. A shilling may be {{bet}} — to bet meaning to stake money on an opinion — on the wheelbarrow race, the smart money following the district nurse's sons, who have won it nine times and are beginning to be resented; the infants drop their pennies in the wishing well and {{wish}} — to wish meaning to want; to express a hope — briefly, practically, and mostly for confectionery; the prize-giving {{congratulate}}s — to congratulate meaning to praise for good fortune achieved — the winners and, more warmly, the runners-up, who will try again; the {{hug}}s — a hug being the embrace of friends, arms and all — are exchanged by the gate; the vicar's closing speech, which has {{impress}}ed — to impress meaning to fix in the mind; to strike with weight — nobody since 1962, is treasured for exactly that; and the {{farewell}} — a farewell being the parting word, the leave-taking taken — is said by seven o'clock, leaving the field to the marquee, the moon and Madame Zora, counting the takings with her glasses on and her headscarf off, which is how the valley knows her best.
tr:
游园会在七月最后一个星期六于牧师宅的草坪上举行，为的是庆祝（celebrate，celebrate 指以 festivity 纪念、欢度）主保瞻礼——此时丰收还是个传闻，学校放假已是事实。委员会用海报邀请（invite，invite 指请、邀约前来）全河谷；河谷的人到了，从十一点起在门口受到欢迎（welcome，welcome 指满怀欣喜地接待、热忱迎候）；门口的寒暄是河谷自己的礼拜仪轨——在同一扇门口互致问候（greet，greet 指相见时以言语迎候）了四十年的邻里们，再演一遍，仪式感丝毫不减。正午，兰普福德勋爵宣布开幕；比尔·斯基德摩率领的退伍军人分会向旗帜敬礼（salute，salute 指以正式的礼节致意，如军礼），其精准程度随后被教堂大钟效仿；牧师则为果蔬帐篷、工作人员和天气依次祝福（bless，bless 指祈求神的恩惠降临于）——顺序如此。

算命帐篷的生意最稳，它的魅力（allure，allure 指吸引力、以魅力诱人靠近的力量）是河谷里唯一从不需要海报的力量。佐拉夫人——其实是换上头巾、改了嗓音的霍斯肯太太——全情投入地凝视（gaze，gaze 指长久而专注地注视）她的水晶球，趁客人换手的间隙瞥一眼（glance，glance 指快速一看随即移开）手表；她连续三年为同一位姑娘预言同一场婚礼，依据的是一条可靠的原则：总有一天她会说对。掷椰子摊吸引（attract，attract 指把人或物引向自己）来乐观主义者；摸彩摊唤醒（arouse，arouse 指唤起、激发，如兴趣或情绪）了清醒者的贪心；小孩子们把手臂伸进 Bran 斗之前，先从小孔里偷看（peep，peep 指从小缝里偷偷地、匆匆地窥看）一眼；而不肯花一先令门票的那些人，整个下午都趴在教堂墓地的墙上费力地看（peer，peer 指吃力地、凑近了细看，如越过或透过某物张望），人数多得像消防演习。没人看见主教来；倒有几位瞥见（glimpse，glimpse 指匆匆一瞥、看见局部）他离开——抄树篱那边，手里拿着一只太妃苹果。

帐篷里，惠斯特牌局在女校长主持下进行，她洗牌（shuffle，shuffle 指反复交叠洗牌）时的庄重堪比外科手术；那位被河谷径直称作“吹口哨的”（whistler，whistler 指吹口哨的人——他不停地用鼻子吹，于是牌局自带伴奏）的园丁，一边给自己的牌发牌，一边吹着一支没人叫得出名字的曲子。南瓜大赛才是荣誉所在。斯普拉格先生从大门口一路夸耀（boast，boast 指大声地自夸，夸自己、夸牲口或夸自家蔬菜）他的红花菜豆；因公正立场从郡展会上借调来的裁判不奉承（flatter，flatter 指言过其实地恭维、以赞美讨好）任何人；输家的太太们打趣（tease，tease 指善意而不带恶意地取笑）赢家的丈夫们；采石场来的怀疑论者们年年坐在啤酒帐篷里嘲弄（mock，mock 指讥讽、轻蔑地取笑）蔬菜竞赛的整个建制，年年毫无效果；一九七九年，两姐妹为一只南瓜的归属争吵（quarrel，quarrel 指生气地、长篇大论地争执）起来，那场争论（argument，argument 指争执、双方各自摆出的理由）持续了四十分钟，代价是两个圣诞节互不搭理——其间两姐妹在门口相遇，只能怒目相视（glare，glare 指凶狠地、含怒地瞪视）；直到姐姐弯腰细看秤盘时，当着裁判的面低声咒骂（curse，curse 指咒骂、祈降祸于）了那只南瓜的祖宗十八代——裁判因其果蔬诚实、言语不诚，给了她二等奖。

下午的节目属于外来的客人。兰普福德来的魔术师令前三排观众着迷（mesmerize，mesmerize 指施催眠术般迷住、使入神）；他终场时放出的那只鸽子令所有人惊愕（astonish，astonish 指以突发的奇事击中人心）——它飞进教堂塔楼，住了一个星期；五月柱舞只把跳它的人绕糊涂（bewilder，bewilder 指彻底弄糊涂、如坠迷宫）了；镇乐队的长号手——他的最高音能传到浅滩——令采石场的怀疑论者们惊服（amaze，amaze 指使人大为惊奇）到鸦雀无声，这是任何南瓜都做不到的；整片草坪鼓掌（clap，clap 指拍击双掌以示赞许）、喝彩（applaud，applaud 指以鼓掌等方式表达赞许），年复一年如此——去年这事的记忆已被冬天磨平了；被领到前排的孩子们直勾勾地盯着（stare，stare 指睁大眼睛死死盯着看）魔术师的胡子，那样子他后来向太太提起过。

一天以仪式开场，也以仪式收场。一先令可以押（bet，bet 指就某个看法下注）独轮车赛——内行的钱都押在地段护士的儿子们身上，他们已经赢了九届，开始招人记恨；小孩子们往许愿井里丢便士，许愿（wish，wish 指希望、表达心愿）简短而务实，多半与糖果有关；颁奖环节向获奖者致贺（congratulate，congratulate 指为获得的好运道而道贺），更热忱地向亚军致贺——他们来年还会再战；门口彼此拥抱（hug，hug 指朋友间的搂抱，连胳膊带人）；牧师的闭幕致辞自一九六二年起就没给任何人留下印象（impress，impress 指在头脑中刻下印记、以分量打动），而正因如此被珍视；到七点钟，道别（farewell，farewell 指告别的言语、临行之礼）已毕，田野留给帐篷、月亮和佐拉夫人——她戴上眼镜、摘下头巾清点收入，河谷最熟悉的就是她这副模样。

quiz.q: The Legion under Bill Skidmore salutes the flag — to greet with formal honour, as soldiers do. To salute is to —
quiz.ex: salute = 敬礼；致敬。salute the flag 向国旗敬礼；salute with a nod 点头致意。

quiz.q: The fortune teller's tent does the steadiest trade, its allure never needing a poster — the power of attraction, of drawing by charm. Allure is —
o: the power of drawing by charm
the parting word at the gate
quiz.ex: allure = 魅力；诱惑力。the allure of the stage 舞台的魅力；alluring adj. 诱人的。

quiz.q: Those who decline the shilling entrance peer over the churchyard wall — to look closely and with effort, as over or through something. To peer is to —
o: look slyly through a small opening
quiz.ex: peer = 凝视；费力地看。peer over one's glasses 从眼镜上方端详；peer into the dark 向黑暗中张望。

quiz.q: Several glimpsed the bishop leaving by the hedge, with a toffee apple — to catch a brief, partial sight of. To glimpse is to —
o: catch a brief, partial sight of
quiz.ex: glimpse = 瞥见。catch a glimpse of sb 一瞥之间看见某人；a fleeting glimpse 匆匆一瞥。

quiz.q: The judge, drafted for impartiality, flatters nobody — to praise beyond the truth, to please with praise. To flatter is to —
quiz.ex: flatter = 奉承；恭维。flatter oneself 自以为；flattering remarks 奉承话。

quiz.q: Two sisters quarrelled over the identity of a marrow — to dispute angrily and at length. To quarrel is to —
quiz.ex: quarrel = 争吵。quarrel with one's neighbour 与邻居争吵；a lovers' quarrel 情侣间的拌嘴。

quiz.q: The magician from Lampford mesmerizes the front three rows — to hold spellbound, as the first mesmerists were said to hold their patients. To mesmerize is to —
quiz.ex: mesmerize = 使入迷；催眠。a mesmerizing performance 令人入迷的表演。

quiz.q: The farewell is said by seven o'clock, leaving the field to the moon — the parting word, the leave-taking taken. A farewell is —
quiz.ex: farewell = 告别。bid sb farewell 向某人道别；a farewell speech 告别演说。

title: The Case of the Missing Deed
text:
Of the mill's deeds the Society possesses everything but the original: copies, references, an inventory of 1822 — everything except the parchment itself, which left the valley in 1809 in the trunk of a bride. The project of the winter was to {{seek}} — to seek meaning to look for, to go in search of — it; and the Society, being the Society, opened proceedings with tea. Mrs. Vye could {{recall}} — to recall meaning to call back to mind — the family story at first hand, having had it from her grandmother: the niece who married out in 1809 and took the deeds with her, out of Halifax spite, to a wool merchant whose firm outlived the mill by a century. Nobody now living could {{recollect}} — to recollect meaning to gather again into the mind — the niece herself; the younger members could only collect fragments heard at funerals, which the Society stitched together and called evidence.

The trail was taken up in earnest. The Society {{correspond}}ed — to correspond meaning to exchange letters — with the record office at Northallerton; {{contact}}ed — to contact meaning to get in touch with — the auction house in Leeds, whose ledger of 1937 held a lot described, in a hand that had given up, as 'box, old papers, unsold' — an entry that did not {{specify}} — to specify meaning to name in detail, to particularise — what the box held, or how old, or whose; and {{explore}}d — to explore meaning to travel through in search of what is there — the bank's old strongroom, where the family papers had lain from 1854 to 1912 and where the mice had done their own filing. The archivist at Northallerton, {{notify}}ing — to notify meaning to give formal notice to — the Society of a deposit made in 1919 by a Halifax solicitor's executors, added one sentence that kept the committee awake until spring: 'Deeds and other parchments, condition various.'

There was a rival in the matter. Mr. Prynne, the professional genealogist of Lampford, had published a monograph in 1974 in which he {{assert}}ed — to assert meaning to state positively, as of right — that the 1809 deed burned with the mill office in the fire of 1868, a fire the histories {{attribute}} — to attribute meaning to assign as a cause or an author — to a carelessly banked stove; and he {{regard}}ed — to regard meaning to look upon, to consider — the Society's enquiries with the {{contempt}} — contempt meaning the feeling that a thing is beneath one — that a professional keeps in reserve for an afternoon a month. He {{disregard}}ed — to disregard meaning to pay no attention to — their first letter for five weeks. The Society {{dispute}}d — to dispute meaning to argue against, to contest — him in the Mercury's letters page for the length of that; and his monograph, the Society observed without being asked, was {{bias}}ed — bias meaning a leaning of the mind, a weight on one side of it — toward documents he had himself catalogued.

The box, when it came up from Northallerton under Mr. Quayle's escort, held eleven parchments, of which three were the mill and eight were other people's barns. The Halifax descendants, in their {{ignorance}} — ignorance meaning the state of not knowing — of what the box held, had for thirty years used the top parchment to line a larder shelf. The fortnight's work was to {{distinguish}} — to distinguish meaning to tell apart, to mark the difference between — the 1809 original from the 1832 copy made for the bank; and to {{differentiate}} — to differentiate meaning to make or to mark a difference between — them, the sheets were held against the vestry window, where the watermark showed the crown, the initials, and, in the copy, a restorer's stitch that told the whole story. Mr. Quayle {{explain}}ed — to explain meaning to make plain, to give the reasons of — conveyancing to the meeting for the ninth year running, and was thanked as for the first; the auctioneer's ledger was fetched, where lot 441 bore an annotation half {{erase}}d — to erase meaning to rub out, as writing from paper — by a dealer's thumb, and the clerk of 1937 had {{delete}}d — to delete meaning to strike out, to remove from a record — the word 'unsold' altogether, being unable to countenance it. The archivist {{assure}}d — to assure meaning to tell confidently, to remove doubt — them that watermarks do not lie and stitches rarely do; the College of Arms, written to with photographs, {{verify}}... verified — to verify meaning to establish the truth of, to confirm — the seal; and the stitch, more than the crown, {{convince}}d — to convince meaning to satisfy by proof, to win the belief of — the last of the sceptics.

The conditions of deposit, {{stipulate}}d — to stipulate meaning to demand as a condition, to specify formally — by the Society in a single sentence, were that the deed should remain at Northallerton, be photographed for the Society's wall, and never again travel in a trunk. The parchment itself, {{retrieve}}d — to retrieve meaning to get back, to recover what was lost or far away — after two hundred years and ninety miles, was carried back through the valley in a police escort's worth of ceremony for one afternoon, and seen by everybody. The {{irony}} — irony meaning the fitness of things running the other way — of the affair, on which the vicar preached to general satisfaction, is that the niece, carrying the deeds out of spite, carried them out of the fire of 1868; her motive was malice, her achievement preservation. Mrs. Vye, who has {{retell}}ed — to retell meaning to tell again, as a story is told again — the affair at every meeting since and will again, calls it the family's one undisputed kindness to itself; Mr. Prynne, {{remind}}ed — to remind meaning to put in mind again — of his monograph by the Mercury, {{reply}}... replied — to reply meaning to answer — with a letter of two sentences conceding the watermark and withdrawing the fire, which the Society framed. The Mercury {{mention}}ed the whole business in a paragraph it headed 'Millbrook's Parchment Comes Home'; the project, which had {{obsess}}ed — to obsess meaning to occupy the mind beyond reason — the Society for two winters, ended in a spring evening and tea; and in {{retrospect}} — retrospect meaning the view of a thing afterward, the looking back upon it — even Mr. Quayle, who {{reflect}}ed — to reflect meaning to think carefully, to turn a matter over in the mind — that conveyancing was mostly waiting, allowed that it had been the pleasantest case of his career. The 1811 chancery papers, found in the same box, record a millwright who {{testify}}... testified — to testify meaning to give evidence, as on oath — that the wheel was older than the church clock and twice as honest; the Society {{contemplate}}s — to contemplate meaning to consider with continued attention — making that next winter's project, and has already ordered the tea. The whole affair, the chairman said over that tea, had proved a {{bond}} — a bond being the thing that binds: of paper, the sealed obligation; of people, the tie that holds them — between the living valley and every man who had ever milled in it, and the Society had merely tightened it.
tr:
关于磨坊的地契，学会什么都齐，唯独没有原件：抄本、引证、一八二二年的清单——什么都齐，只差那张羊皮纸本身，它在一八〇九年随着一位新娘的嫁妆箱离开了河谷。这个冬天的课题就是去寻找（seek，seek 指寻找、前去搜寻）它；而学会，以学会的做派，先用茶开了场。怀夫人能凭第一手材料回忆（recall，recall 指回想、召回脑海）起家族的故事——那是从她祖母那儿听来的：一八〇九年嫁出门的侄女带着地契出走，出于哈利法克斯式的怨气，嫁给了呢绒商，那家商号比磨坊多活了一个世纪。如今活着的人谁也回忆不起（recollect，recollect 指把旧事重新收拢回脑海）侄女本人；年轻会员们只能收集葬礼上听来的碎片，学会把它们缝缀起来，称为证据。

追寻是认真的。学会与诺思阿勒顿的档案局通信（correspond，correspond 指互通信件）往来；联络（contact，contact 指取得联系）了利兹的拍卖行——它一九三七年的账簿上有一个条目，出自一只已然放弃的笔迹：“一箱，旧纸，未售出”——这条目没有具体说明（specify，specify 指详列、逐一指明）箱里是什么、多旧、谁的；学会还探查（explore，explore 指为查明其中所有而遍历探勘）了银行旧金库——那批家族文件一八五四到一九一二年一直存放在那里，老鼠们做过自己的归档。诺思阿勒顿的档案员正式通知（notify，notify 指正式告知）学会，有一批文件系哈利法克斯某律师的遗产执行人于一九一九年存入，并加了一句让委员会彻夜难眠到开春的话：“地契及其他羊皮纸若干，品相不一。”

这件事上有个对头。兰普福德的职业谱系学家普林先生一九七四年出过一本专著，其中断言（assert，assert 指肯定地宣称、以权威口吻陈述）：一八〇九年的地契已随磨坊办公室毁于一八六八年的大火——那场火，几部地方史把它归因（attribute，attribute 指把原因或作者归属给）于一次没封好的炉子；而他把学会的查询视为（regard，regard 指看待、视为）不值一顾，怀着职业人士为“每月一个下午”级别的对手所保留的轻蔑（contempt，contempt 指认为某事卑不足道的 feeling）。他们的第一封信被他置之不理（disregard，disregard 指不加理会）了五个星期。学会在《信使报》读者来信版上与他论战（dispute，dispute 指辩驳、争议）了同样久；而且学会没人问也自己指出：他的专著带有偏见（bias，bias 指心思的倾斜、压在某一侧的分量），偏向他自己编目过的那批文件。

箱子由奎尔先生护送从诺思阿勒顿送下来时，里面装着十一张羊皮纸：三张是磨坊的，八张是别人家谷仓的。哈利法克斯的后人们全然不知（ignorance，ignorance 指不知情的状态）箱中所藏，三十年来一直拿最上面那张垫食品柜的搁板。两个星期的工夫，是要分辨（distinguish，distinguish 指区分开来、辨明两者之别）一八〇九年的原件与银行为自己誊的一八三二年抄本；为了区分（differentiate，differentiate 指使有别、标出差异）两者，纸页被举在法衣室的窗前对光看——水印现出王冠、姓名缩写，而在抄本上，还有一道修复针脚，道破了全部真相。奎尔先生连续第九年向全会讲解（explain，explain 指讲明白、说明缘由）产权转让的流程，大家像第一年那样谢了他；拍卖行账簿调来了——第441号拍品上有一条被商人拇指蹭得半掉的批注，另外一九三七年的书记员把“未售出”三个字整个划掉（delete，delete 指勾销、从记录中除去）了，因为他无法面对它；旁边还有半行字被擦去（erase，erase 指擦除、把字迹从纸上抹去）。档案员使大家确信（assure，assure 指有把握地告知、打消疑虑）水印不会说谎、针脚也很少说谎；纹章院收到了照片，验证（verify，verify 指查证属实、加以确认）了那枚火漆印；而那道针脚，比王冠更有说服力，说服（convince，convince 指以证明使人信服）了最后几个怀疑的人。

学会用一句话规定的（stipulate，stipulate 指作为条件提出、正式约定）存档条件是：地契留在诺思阿勒顿，为学会的墙面拍照留存，永不再装进嫁妆箱旅行。那张羊皮纸本身，在两百年和九十英里之后被找回（retrieve，retrieve 指取回、寻回失散或遥远之物），被以一个下午的、相当于警车开道的仪仗接回了河谷，人人得见。这件事的反讽（irony，irony 指事理偏偏反向而行的巧合）——牧师就此讲了一篇皆大欢喜的道——在于：侄女出于怨气带走地契，却把它们带出了那场一八六八年的大火；她的动机是恶意，她的功绩是保全。怀夫人从此每逢聚会都要把这个故事重讲（retell，retell 指把故事再讲一遍）一遍，以后也会，她称之为这个家族对自己唯一一次无可争议的善意；普林先生被《信使报》提醒（remind，remind 指使重新想起）了他的专著，回复（reply，reply 指作答、回信）了一封两句话的信，承认了水印，撤回了大火——学会把它装了框。《信使报》用一段题为“磨坊溪的羊皮纸回家了”的报道提过（mention，mention 指提及、说到）整件事；这个把学会迷住（obsess，obsess 指在脑中盘踞到超出常理）了两个冬天的课题，在一个春夜和一壶茶里结束；而回顾（retrospect，retrospect 指事后回望、回头看）起来，连奎尔先生——他思忖（reflect，reflect 指沉思、在心里反复掂量）过产权转让这一行大半是等待——也承认这是他职业生涯里最愉快的一桩案子。同一箱子里找到的一八一一年大法官法庭卷宗记着一位磨坊匠的证言（testify，testify 指作证、宣誓陈述），说水轮比教堂大钟还老，且比它诚实一倍；学会正在考虑（contemplate，contemplate 指持续而专注地思量）把它立为下一个冬天的课题，并且已经订好了茶。主席就着那场茶说道：这整桩事情证明了一条纽带（bond，bond 指起连结作用之物：在纸上，是盖印封缄的债券义务；在人之间，是维系彼此的联结）——一边是活着的河谷，一边是每一个曾在这里磨过面的人——而学会所做的，不过是把它收紧了一点。

quiz.q: The project of the winter was to seek the original deed — to look for, to go in search of. To seek is to —
o: look for, go in search of
establish the truth of a seal
tell the original from the copy
quiz.ex: seek = 寻找；寻求。seek employment 找工作；seek the truth 寻求真相（sought 为过去式）。

quiz.q: He regarded the Society's enquiries with contempt — the feeling that a thing is beneath one. Contempt is —
o: a leaning of the mind to one side
the feeling that a thing is beneath one
the view of a thing afterward
quiz.ex: contempt = 轻蔑；鄙视。hold sb in contempt 鄙视某人；contemptuous adj. 轻蔑的。

quiz.q: The fortnight's work was to distinguish the original from the copy — to tell apart, to mark the difference between. To distinguish is to —
quiz.ex: distinguish = 区分；辨别。distinguish right from wrong 明辨是非；distinguished adj. 卓越的。

quiz.q: An annotation half erased by a dealer's thumb — to rub out, as writing from paper. To erase is to —
o: rub out, as writing from paper
quiz.ex: erase = 擦除；抹掉。erase a blackboard 擦黑板；erase the memory 抹去记忆。

quiz.q: The parchment, retrieved after two hundred years and ninety miles — to get back, to recover what was lost or far away. To retrieve is to —
o: demand as a condition of deposit
get back what was lost or far away
line a larder shelf for years
quiz.ex: retrieve = 寻回；取回。retrieve the ball 把球捡回来；retrieve data 恢复数据。

quiz.q: The irony is that the niece, carrying the deeds out of spite, carried them out of the fire — the fitness of things running the other way. Irony is —
o: the pleasantest case of a career
the fitness of things running the other way
quiz.ex: irony = 反讽；讽刺。the irony of fate 命运的嘲弄；ironic adj. 讽刺的。

quiz.q: The College of Arms verified the seal from photographs — to establish the truth of, to confirm. To verify is to —
o: argue against in the letters page
put in mind again of a monograph
quiz.ex: verify = 核实；查证。verify the figures 核实数字；verification n. 验证。

quiz.q: The Halifax descendants, in their ignorance of what the box held, lined a larder shelf with it — the state of not knowing. Ignorance is —
o: a weight on one side of the mind
the formal notice of a deposit
the looking back upon a thing
quiz.ex: ignorance = 无知；不知。keep sb in ignorance 使某人蒙在鼓里；ignorant adj. 无知的。

title: The Bell Fund
text:
The tenor bell, cast in 1710 and silent twice in three hundred years — once for the fire, once for the war — cracked on New Year's Eve, at the twelfth stroke, in front of witnesses. The foundry's letter, which the vicar read to the meeting twice, once for the content and once for the price, put the matter plainly: recast or retire, and either way, fourteen thousand pounds.
