The vicar {{preach}}ed — to preach meaning to deliver a sermon; and beyond the pulpit, to urge a cause earnestly and at length — on it the following Sunday, {{invoke}}d — to invoke meaning to call upon, as a witness or a power — Saint Cuthbert, the bell-founders of 1710, and the example of the parish's grandmothers, in ascending order of generosity, and {{urge}}d — to urge meaning to press a request, to push it earnestly — the fund from every angle the pulpit offered.

The fund opened the same afternoon. The ringers {{pledge}}d — to pledge meaning to promise solemnly, to bind oneself by a promise — a month's ringing money apiece, which in the valley is a vow with figures attached; the youngest of them {{vow}}ed — to vow meaning to swear to a thing, solemnly and before witnesses — his first quarter's wages; and an {{oath}} — an oath being a solemn calling on heaven to witness what one says — was taken, on the tower steps, that the cracked bell would not be rung again but mended or buried. Bill Skidmore, asked at the Legion whether the old bell might not simply be left cracked, as the veterans had been, {{swear|swore}} — to swear meaning to affirm with an oath; and by extension, to use oath-strong language — that it could not, in terms the Mercury printed with a long dash and the village repeated without one. The chairman of the trustees {{promise}}d the foundry's discount in writing; and the meeting, thus {{induce}}d — to induce meaning to lead on, to persuade by something put forward — closed early for once, everybody hurrying home to be first at the collecting tin.

The campaign ran the winter and took every shape persuasion wears in a valley. The raffle {{tempt}}ed — to tempt meaning to attract with a prize, as the devil is said to attract with better ones — even the chapel, which does not hold with bells on principle; the farmers were {{incline}}d — to incline meaning to lean, in the mind as in the body; to tend toward — to give in hay, lambs and leaning rather than in coin; the sceptic at the quarry, {{provoke}}d — to provoke meaning to goad into speech or action — past endurance by the third appeal, gave twenty pounds on the strict condition of never being thanked; the February floods {{impede}}d — to impede meaning to hinder, to stand in the way of — the house-to-house round to the extent of a tractor; the school {{participate|participated}} — to participate meaning to take part, to have a share in the doing — with a concert of recorders, which raised eleven pounds and cost the fund a portion of its composure; and when the total stood at nine thousand and stuck there for a month, the bishop himself {{intervene|intervened}} — to intervene meaning to come between, to step in where others stand — with a letter the Mercury printed whole, whereupon the fund doubled in a fortnight, the bishop being the one authority the valley has tried arguing with and given up.

Not everybody was moved, and the unmoved had reasons, which the vicar wrote down faithfully in the minute book, so that they should at least be beautiful. Three households {{refuse}}d — to refuse meaning to decline, to say no to — outright, on the principle that the roof had come first in their own houses for two hundred years; the Mercury was accused of having {{exaggerate}}d — to exaggerate meaning to carry beyond the truth, in statement or in figure — the price, and answered by printing the foundry's letter again, in facsimile, with the figure ringed in red; and the quarrel about whether ringing a figure in red was editorialising kept the letters page warm until March, the Mercury having decided at last to {{uphold}} — to uphold meaning to maintain, to stand by — its own judgement, as newspapers will.

The works were {{tackle|tackled}} — to tackle meaning to set about a task with intent and grip, as a player tackles — in April, while the scaffolding was up and the tower could be mended at the same time; and the mason offered, unprompted, to {{render}} — to render meaning, in the builder's trade, to plaster a wall with its first coat; and in the pulpit's, to give what is due — the ringing chamber at cost, an offer the committee {{adopt}}ed — to adopt meaning to take up formally, as a scheme is taken up — by acclaim. The valley, having heard the cracked note for six months, had grown {{accustom}}ed — to accustom meaning to make used to, as to weather or to silence — to it as to a limp, and found the mended note, when it came, almost too true; the appeal was {{repeat}}ed — to repeat meaning to say or to do again — exactly once, at the harvest, for the clock, and was answered before it finished; the committee, having declared it would never {{resort}} — to resort meaning to have recourse to, to turn to as a last expedient — to a second raffle, held a second raffle, with stoicism; and at the rededication, the vicar, {{impart}}ing — to impart meaning to give, as one gives knowledge or a gift — the final figures from the pulpit, {{enlighten}}ed — to enlighten meaning to instruct, to take the darkness of ignorance from — the parish on the subject of bell-foundries, which it had not known it wished to be enlightened upon. The parish had {{support}}ed — to support meaning to bear the weight of; to stand behind, as a wall supports a roof — the whole affair so thoroughly that the surplus, when counted, came to eleven pounds and a henhouse; and it was resolved, without a vote, that the henhouse should go to the recorder players, by way of apology.
tr:
低音钟铸于一七一〇年，三百年里只哑过两次——一次为大火，一次为战争——却在除夕第十二响上，当着众人的面裂了。铸造厂的来信，牧师在会上读了两遍，一遍读内容，一遍读价钱，把事情说得明白：重铸或者退役，无论哪条路，一万四千英镑。第二个星期日，牧师为此布道（preach，preach 指讲道；讲坛之外指恳切而长篇地鼓吹一项事业），祈请（invoke，invoke 指吁请、召唤，如唤证人或唤力量）圣卡斯伯特、一七一〇年的铸钟匠，以及本教区祖母们的榜样——慷慨程度依次递增——并从讲坛所能提供的每一个角度敦促（urge，urge 指力劝、恳切地推动一项请求）这项基金。

当天下午基金就开了张。敲钟人每人认捐（pledge，pledge 指郑重承诺、以誓约束己）一个月的敲钟报酬——在河谷，这就等于一份带数字的誓言；其中最年轻的一位立誓（vow，vow 指郑重其事、当众立誓）要捐出第一季工资；钟塔台阶上还起了一道誓（oath，oath 指吁请上天见证所言的郑重誓言）：裂钟不再敲响，要么修好，要么安葬。军团那儿有人问比尔·斯基德摩，老钟能不能就让它裂着——反正老兵们也都这样——他发誓（swear，swear 指起誓确证；引申指说出带咒语的强硬语言）说不能，措辞之烈，《信使报》刊登时打了一个长破折号，村里转述时连破折号也省了。托管会主席书面承诺（promise，promise 指许诺、担保将来之事）争取到铸造厂的折扣；全会就这样被诱导（induce，induce 指以摆到面前的某种好处劝动、引着走）得破天荒提前散会——人人都赶着回家，抢着第一个到募捐罐前。

募捐跑了一整个冬天，把劝说在一个河谷里能穿的所有衣裳都穿了一遍。抽奖让（tempt，tempt 指以奖品吸引，如魔鬼被说成以更好的奖品吸引）连原则上不赞成敲钟的礼拜堂都动了心；农户们倾向于（incline，incline 指如身体般倾斜、心思偏向；倾向于）捐干草、羊羔和农具而不是现钱；采石场那位怀疑论者被第三次呼吁激得（provoke，provoke 指激怒到开口或行动）忍无可忍，捐了二十镑，条件是永不致谢；二月的洪水把挨家挨户的劝捐妨碍（impede，impede 指阻碍、挡道）到需要动用拖拉机的程度；学校以一场竖笛音乐会参与（participate，participate 指参加、在做事中占一份）其中，筹得十一镑，基金折损了三分仪态；而当总数停在九千镑上一个月不动时，主教亲自出面调停（intervene，intervene 指介入其间、插身于他人僵持之处），来了一封信，《信使报》全文照登——此后两周基金翻了一番：主教是河谷唯一试着与之争辩又终于放弃的权威。

并非人人都被打动，而不为所动者自有理由——牧师把这些理由一字不落地记进会议簿，好歹让它们漂亮。三户人家断然拒绝（refuse，refuse 指谢绝、说不），理由是两百年来自家屋顶从来排在第一位；《信使报》被指夸大（exaggerate，exaggerate 指在陈述或数字上超出实情）了价钱，它的回应是把铸造厂的来信影印再登一遍，数字上圈了红圈；至于给数字圈红圈算不算社论立场，这场争执让读者来信版一直暖到三月，最终《信使报》决定维护（uphold，uphold 指维持、坚守）自己的判断——报纸向来如此。

工程在四月动手（tackle，tackle 指带着意图和抓握扑向一项任务，如球员擒抱），趁着脚手架还架着，钟塔可以一并修缮；石匠主动提出，把敲钟室抹灰（render，render 建筑行当指给墙面打底抹灰；讲坛上指交付应尽之责），只收成本——委员会一致鼓掌通过，正式采纳（adopt，adopt 指正式采纳、照单收下一项方案）了这项提议。河谷听了六个月裂音，已经习惯（accustom，accustom 指使习惯于，如习惯天气或习惯寂静）得像习惯一条瘸腿，修好的钟声传来时，反而觉得真得过分；为修大钟的呼吁只在收获节照原样重复（repeat，repeat 指再说一遍、再做一次）了一次，是为钟表的，话音未落就已筹足；委员会曾声明绝不诉诸（resort，resort 指求助于、作为最后的权宜之计转向）第二次抽奖，随后以斯多噶的坚忍办了第二次抽奖；落成祝圣礼上，牧师从讲坛上授予（impart，impart 指给予、如授予知识或礼物）最终账目时，把本教区在铸钟这件事上启蒙（enlighten，enlighten 指开导、驱除无知的黑暗）了一番——教区此前并不知道自己是愿意受此启蒙的。本教区对整件事支持（support，support 指承受重量；如墙支撑屋顶般撑持）得如此彻底，以至于结余清点出来是十一镑加一间鸡舍；未经表决，全场一致同意：鸡舍归竖笛队，权当赔罪。

quiz.q: The ringers pledged a month's ringing money apiece — to promise solemnly, to bind oneself by a promise. To pledge is to —
quiz.ex: pledge = 承诺；保证。pledge allegiance 宣誓效忠；make a pledge 作出保证。

quiz.q: An oath was taken on the tower steps that the cracked bell would not be rung — a solemn calling on heaven to witness what one says. An oath is —
o: a solemn calling on heaven to witness
an urgent request from the pulpit
quiz.ex: oath = 誓言；宣誓。take an oath 宣誓；on oath 发誓说实话。

quiz.q: The raffle tempted even the chapel, which does not hold with bells — to attract with a prize, as the devil is said to attract. To tempt is to —
o: hinder to the extent of a tractor
quiz.ex: tempt = 诱惑；吸引。tempt sb with chocolate 用巧克力诱惑某人；temptation n. 诱惑。

quiz.q: The sceptic at the quarry, provoked past endurance by the third appeal, gave twenty pounds — to goad into speech or action. To provoke is to —
o: call on a bishop to step in
quiz.ex: provoke = 激怒；激起。provoke a quarrel 挑起争吵；provocative adj. 挑衅的。

quiz.q: Three households refused outright, on the principle that the roof came first — to decline, to say no to. To refuse is to —
o: give on condition of no thanks
quiz.ex: refuse = 拒绝。refuse an offer 拒绝提议；refusal n. 拒绝。

quiz.q: The mason offered to render the ringing chamber at cost — in the builder's trade, to plaster a wall; in the pulpit's, to give what is due. To render is to —
o: plaster a wall; give what is due
make used to a cracked note
quiz.ex: render = 抹灰；给予；使成为。render a service 提供服务；render thanks 致谢。

quiz.q: The committee, having said it would never resort to a second raffle, held one — to have recourse to, to turn to as a last expedient. To resort is to —
o: set about with intent and grip
have recourse to, turn to at the last
quiz.ex: resort to = 诉诸；求助于。resort to force 诉诸武力；as a last resort 作为最后一招。

quiz.q: The school participated with a concert of recorders — to take part, to have a share in the doing. To participate is to —
o: bear the weight of a roof
urge the fund from every angle
take part, share in the doing
quiz.ex: participate = 参与。participate in a discussion 参与讨论；participant n. 参与者。

title: The New Hands at the Stores
text:
The Stores passed in March from the Treloars, who had kept it for forty years and could price a shelf by closing their eyes, to a young couple from town called Blake, who had a plan of three pages and a van of their own. The new owners {{commence}}d — to commence meaning to begin, formally and with intent — with a coat of paint and a meeting; and the plan, laid before the village in the corn exchange, proposed to {{enlarge}} — to enlarge meaning to make larger, to add to — the shop into the old stable; to {{combine}} — to combine meaning to join into one what was separate — the post counter with the till; to {{connect}} — to connect meaning to join, as points once apart — the whole to the internet, a word the Treloars had respected from a distance; to {{integrate}} — to integrate meaning to make into a whole, to bring the parts together — a bakery corner and a coffee machine; and to admit the National Lottery, which the vicar was consulted upon and pronounced himself powerless to prevent. Nobody was {{exclude}}d — to exclude meaning to shut out, to bar from entering — from the consultation, including several who had moved to Perth and wrote in with opinions; and the plan, being thus {{involve}}d — to involve meaning to draw in, to have as a necessary part — with the whole village, was passed by the whole village, which reserved the right to be surprised by it afterward.

The works were {{conduct}}ed — to conduct meaning to carry on, to direct the course of — over six weeks, and watched. The spectators {{follow}}ed — to follow meaning to come after; to keep track of the course of — the works from the bench by the memorial in shifts, in the manner of test cricket; the old stable, {{designate}}d — to designate meaning to mark out and appoint to a purpose — as the bakery corner, was knocked through; the ceiling was {{raise}}d — to raise meaning to lift, to set higher — two courses of brick; the tasks were {{assign}}ed — to assign meaning to allot, to give out as a task — in a rota the couple had printed and the village ignored; the stock was {{assort}}ed — to assort meaning to sort into kinds, to arrange in varieties — into kinds the trade had never heard of; the shelves were {{range}}d — to range meaning to set out in rows; and by extension, to stretch between limits — from the floor to the new ceiling; the window was {{arrange}}d — to arrange meaning to set in order, to dispose pleasingly — with a skill the Treloars would have been the first to own; the new glass, {{magnify}}ing — to magnify meaning to make appear greater, as a lens does — the pies to the size of cartwheels; the coffee machine's hiss {{amplify|amplified}} — to amplify meaning to increase, as sound is increased by an instrument — the general sense of occasion; the range of goods was {{augment}}ed — to augment meaning to add to, to make greater by additions — by olives, coffee beans and two kinds of bread the valley had previously sent to Lampford for; and the Tuesday tea break was {{prolong}}ed — to prolong meaning to lengthen, to make longer — into a whole institution, by popular demand.

Then the systems arrived, and with them the education of the valley. The brass till, which had rung out the decade of the corvette, was {{replace}}d — to replace meaning to put in the place of, to succeed — by a machine that beeped; the machine was {{manipulate}}d — to manipulate meaning to handle with skill; in the worse use, to manage persons to one's own ends — with ease by the couple and with heroism by everybody else; its {{backup}} — a backup being a second copy kept against the loss of the first — failed on the third day and took Thursday's accounts into the dark with it, which settled the valley's opinion of progress; the price list, once chalk, was {{update}}d — to update meaning to bring up to date — weekly, still in chalk, by common insistence; the new ledger, complete and beautiful, was found to have {{omit}}ted — to omit meaning to leave out, to pass over in silence — the Treloars' system of chalk marks, which had governed credit in the valley for forty years, and was amended; the losses on bread were {{offset}} — to offset meaning to balance against, to set one thing against another — by the takings on coffee, which the couple explained in a graph and the valley understood perfectly, having run the same system on bees for a century; the shelves were {{replenish}}ed — to replenish meaning to fill again, as a thing run empty — twice weekly by van, a van that in a year never once {{deviate}}d — to deviate meaning to turn aside, to leave the appointed line — from its route except for the gala; parcels were {{despatch}}ed — to despatch meaning to send off, toward a destination — daily instead of Tuesdays; the Mercury was {{distribute}}d — to distribute meaning to deal out, to give out in shares — with the milk round by an arrangement nobody could afterwards remember making; the post office, {{detach}}ed — to detach meaning to unfasten, to separate from what it was fixed to — from the counter, was given a window of its own; and the cream round, {{cancel}}led — to cancel meaning to call off, to annul what had been arranged — in April on the grounds that nobody drank cream, was reinstated in May on the discovery that everybody did.

By June the Blakes had quietly {{undo}}... undone — to undo meaning to reverse, to unmake what had been done — the great shelf rearrangement, restoring the sugar to the shelf the valley knew it to live on; they had been accused by nobody of anything except a scheme to {{exploit}} — to exploit meaning to turn to full account; in the worse use, to use unfairly — the valley's loyalty, an accusation withdrawn after the first Friday pies; the old counter, {{dispose}}d — to dispose meaning to get rid of, to put out of the way — of by raffle, fetched forty pounds for the bell fund; and when September came, the school's new {{intake}} — an intake being that which is taken in; the year's new scholars — was introduced to the shop on its first morning, as by rite, and sold a quarter-pound of aniseed balls by lunchtime. The Treloars, invited back for the anniversary, said the shop had never looked better; and Mrs. Treloar, who had priced a shelf blindfold for forty years, was asked to demonstrate for the camera and got it right to the penny, in the general delight of all present.
tr:
三月，杂货铺从特雷洛夫妇手里交了出去——他们经营了四十年，闭着眼睛就能给一整架货定价——接手的是一对从城里来的姓布莱克的年轻人，带着一份三页的计划和一辆自己的货车。新店主以刷漆和一场会议开了张（commence，commence 指正式地、带着意图开始）；那份摆在谷物交易所全村面前的计划提出：把店铺扩建（enlarge，enlarge 指扩大、增补）进旧马厩；把邮政柜台与收银台合并（combine，combine 指把分开的东西合而为一）；把整个铺子连接（connect，connect 指把原本分开的点接通）到互联网上——这个词特雷洛夫妇一向敬而远之；把面包角和咖啡机整合（integrate，integrate 指使成一体、把各部分拢到一处）进来；并接纳国家彩票——牧师被征询意见，宣布自己无力阻止。协商无人被排除（exclude，exclude 指把人关在门外、拒之入内）在外，连几位搬去珀斯的人都来信发表了意见；计划就这样把全村卷入（involve，involve 指把……牵连进来、作为必要部分包含）其中，由全村通过，并保留事后为之惊讶的权利。

工程由小两口主持进行（conduct，conduct 指开展、主持……的进程）了六个星期，全程有人围观。观众们轮班坐在纪念碑旁的长椅上跟踪（follow，follow 指跟在后面；持续关注……的进展）工程进展，作风如看板球联赛；被指定（designate，designate 指标出并派定用途）为面包角的旧马厩被打穿了；天花板升高（raise，raise 指抬升、垫高）了两皮砖；各项任务按一对小两口印好的值日表分派（assign，assign 指分派、作为任务下发），全村对这个表不予理会；货物被分门别类（assort，assort 指分成各类、按品种归置）成这个行业从未听说过的类别；货架从地面排（range，range 指排成行列；也指两点之间的范围）到新天花板；橱窗被布置（arrange，arrange 指安排妥帖、陈设悦目）得颇有章法，特雷洛夫妇第一个承认这点；新玻璃把馅饼放大（magnify，magnify 指使显得更大，如透镜）到车轮那么大；咖啡机的嘶嘶声把整个场面的隆重感放大（amplify，amplify 指增大、如器械扩音）了一圈；货品的品类被橄榄、咖啡豆和两种河谷从前要跑兰普福德去买的面包扩充（augment，augment 指增添、以追加变得更大）了；星期二的茶歇应众人要求延长（prolong，prolong 指拉长、使更久）成了一项制度。

然后系统到货，河谷的教育也随之而来。那台敲响过护航舰年代的黄铜收银机，被一台会哔哔叫的机器取代（replace，replace 指放进……的位置、接替）；机器被小两口轻松驾驭（manipulate，manipulate 指熟练地操作；贬义指耍弄人以遂己愿），其他人操作起来则堪称壮烈；它的备份（backup，backup 指为防第一份丢失而留存的第二份）第三天就坏了，把星期四的账目一并带进黑暗——河谷对进步的看法就此定型；价目牌，从前是粉笔写的，如今每周更新（update，update 指更新到最新），经众人坚持，仍用粉笔；新账簿完备而漂亮，却被发现漏掉（omit，omit 指遗漏、略过不载）了特雷洛家的粉笔记号制——那套记号管了河谷四十年的赊账——于是获准修订；面包上的亏空由咖啡的进项抵偿（offset，offset 指以彼抵此、拿一样东西平衡另一样），小两口用一张图解释，全村秒懂——他们在一个世纪里对蜜蜂用的正是同一套；货架每周两次由货车补货（replenish，replenish 指重新填满、补给空虚之物），那辆货车一年里从未偏离（deviate，deviate 指偏离、离开既定路线）路线一次，除了游园会那天；包裹每日发运（despatch，despatch 指发送出去、发往目的地），不再是每星期二一次；《信使报》随送奶线分发（distribute，distribute 指分发、按份散给），这个安排事后谁也想不起是怎么定下的；邮局从柜台拆分（detach，detach 指解开、从固定处分离）出去，有了自己的窗口；奶油配送线四月以“没人喝奶油”为由取消（cancel，cancel 指取消、废止既定之事），五月发现人人都喝，又恢复了。

到六月，布莱克夫妇悄悄撤销（undo，undo 指逆转、把做过的事拆掉）了那场货架大重排，把糖放回河谷知道它住在哪儿的那一格；他们没有受到任何指控，除了一项“企图榨取（exploit，exploit 指充分利用、发挥到极致；贬义指不公平地利用）河谷感情”的嫌疑——此项嫌疑在第一批星期五馅饼出炉后即告撤销；旧柜台以抽奖的方式处理（dispose，dispose 指处理掉、清除出屋子）掉，为修钟基金筹得四十镑；九月开学，学校新招收（intake，intake 指纳入之物；指学校该年度的新生）的一届按古礼在第一个早晨被领进店里，午饭前便买掉了四分之一磅茴香糖。特雷洛夫妇受邀回来参加周年庆，说铺子从没这么体面过；特雷洛太太——那位闭眼定价四十年的人——应摄影机之邀表演了一次，分毫不差，满堂欢喜。

quiz.q: The new owners commenced with a coat of paint and a meeting — to begin, formally and with intent. To commence is to —
o: shut out the objections of Perth
quiz.ex: commence = 开始；着手。commence operations 开始运作；commencement n. 开始；毕业典礼。

quiz.q: To integrate a bakery corner and a coffee machine — to make into a whole, to bring the parts together. To integrate is to —
o: send off toward a destination daily
make appear greater, as a lens
turn aside from the appointed line
make into a whole, bring parts together
quiz.ex: integrate = 整合；融合。integrate new members 使新成员融入；integrated transport 一体化交通。

quiz.q: The new ledger was found to have omitted the Treloars' chalk marks — to leave out, to pass over in silence. To omit is to —
o: put in the place of the old
bring up to date in chalk
quiz.ex: omit = 遗漏；省略。omit a word 漏掉一个词；omission n. 省略；疏漏。

quiz.q: The losses on bread were offset by the takings on coffee — to balance against, to set one thing against another. To offset is to —
quiz.ex: offset = 抵消；补偿。offset the cost 抵消费用；carbon offset 碳补偿。

quiz.q: The shelves were replenished twice weekly by van — to fill again, as a thing run empty. To replenish is to —
quiz.ex: replenish = 补充；重新装满。replenish supplies 补给物资；replenish one's glass 续杯。

quiz.q: The machine's backup failed on the third day, taking Thursday's accounts into the dark — a second copy kept against the loss of the first. A backup is —
o: the till that beeped for coffee
a van that never leaves its route
a second copy kept against loss
quiz.ex: backup = 备份；后援。keep a backup of files 备份文件；backup plan 备用方案。

quiz.q: The old counter, disposed of by raffle, fetched forty pounds — to get rid of, to put out of the way. To dispose is to —
o: get rid of, put out of the way
quiz.ex: dispose of = 处理掉；解决。dispose of old furniture 处理旧家具；disposal n. 处理；支配。

quiz.q: The van in a year never once deviated from its route except for the gala — to turn aside, to leave the appointed line. To deviate is to —
quiz.ex: deviate = 偏离；越轨。deviate from the plan 偏离计划；deviation n. 偏差。

title: The Smuggler's Dusk
text:
When the floor of the old stable at the Bull was taken up in March — the same month, as it happened, that the Stores changed hands, the valley being incapable of attending two events at once — the carpenter found beneath forty boards and a century of mice a tin box sealed with pitch; and in the box, tied with ribbon gone to iron, the confession of Zebediah Vye, smuggler, written out fair in 1834 and addressed "To whoever has paid for this floor." The Mercury called it the valley's strangest {{deed}} — a deed being a thing done, an act performed; and, on paper, a sealed writing by which a thing is owned — and the only one in the records that nobody has tried to own.

Zebediah had been a tide-waiter at Lampford quay, of all employments, before the long wars made honest gin expensive and dishonest gin an industry; and his account of the twenty years after is the fullest the county possesses. The gang {{smuggle}}d — to smuggle meaning to carry goods into or out of a country against the law, and past the officers set to stop it — brandy in wool-sacks, lace in Bibles, and once, on a wager, a whole anvil under a funeral wreath; the wreath being the {{disguise}} — a disguise meaning the dress or the paint by which one is made to seem other than one is — and the sexton, who walked before it with a face of canonical grief, the finest actor in the county. The kegs were landed at Holt Ness and sunk in the shingle in {{trench}}es — a trench being a long narrow ditch, dug for drainage, for war, or for hiding things in — two feet down and marked by a stone the tide moved every winter, so that a full third of each season was spent hunting for the other two.

The great {{effort}} — an effort being the exertion of strength or mind toward an end — of his career was the run of October 1811: forty kegs, a new lugger, and, as he tells it, the entire revenue establishment of the coast at evening service. He describes the {{attempt}} — an attempt meaning a trying; an essay toward a thing, succeeded or not — as the purest {{gamble}} — to gamble meaning to play a game for money staked on the issue; and beyond the tables, to risk anything upon chance — the valley ever saw, the {{stake}} — a stake being that which is set up and risked on the throw; the money, or the neck, laid upon the issue — being the lugger, the cargo and eleven men's necks, and the odds being the weather, the moon, and one informer.

The informer was the ruin of it, as informers are; he had sold the tide and the place for thirty guineas and the Crown's uneasy gratitude. The fog that night {{penetrate}}d — to penetrate meaning to enter into and pass through, as damp passes a coat — everything on the marsh, riders included; but the revenue had brought a lantern of the new sort, whose light {{pierce}}d — to pierce meaning to thrust through, as a point passes what it enters — a quarter-mile of it, and the riders {{overtake|overtook}} — to overtake meaning to come up with, as pursuit comes up with flight — the cart at two in the morning. Zebediah felt the first rider's {{grip}} — a grip being the seizing and holding fast, as a hand grips an arm — on his shoulder, and performed the one {{act}} — an act being a thing done; and in Parliament's language, a law so called — that no Parliament had thought to provide for: he whipped the horses into the creek, where the tide took the cart, the kegs, the lantern, and very nearly the rider.

There is one page the valley reads with its fingers flat. In the affray at Holt Marsh a young officer went down — whether by keg, by hoof or by the creek itself, the confession does not say — and the Mercury's great-grandmother called it a {{massacre}} — a massacre being the slaughter of the defenceless without mercy; in newspaper use, any affray that exceeds a paragraph — in a headline two columns wide, being short of facts and fond of type. The affair ended in what the chaplain called, with more precision than comfort, the {{decimation}} — decimation being, strictly, the destruction of one in ten, as armies were punished of old; loosely, any heavy thinning of a company — of the gang: three taken, two transported, one drowned, and the trade itself moved twenty miles east. The three who were taken were {{convict}}ed — to convict meaning to prove or to declare guilty, as a jury declares — at the assizes; the gaoler {{bully}}ed — to bully meaning to use strength or office to oppress the smaller; to cow by menace — them in the ordinary course of his trade, and was rebuked for it by the judge, who held that his prisoners should be frightened by nothing but the sentence. The eldest suffered the {{indignity}} — an indignity being an affront offered to dignity, a humiliation — of the pillory at Lampford, and bore it, the Mercury records, "with a bearing that drew applause from persons the Crown is unable to name," which {{mortify|mortified}} — to mortify meaning to subdue the flesh, as the cloister subdues it; and beyond the cloister, to humble the pride — the Crown considerably more than the sentence had. The gang {{evacuate}}d — to evacuate meaning to withdraw from a place, as a garrison or a population withdraws — the coast inside the week; Zebediah was {{expel}}led — to expel meaning to drive out, to put forth by force — from the roll of Lampford freemen "with all his name and kin, in one sentence of magnificent length."

What saved his neck, and his standing in the valley ever since, was the affair of the following spring. The supervisor of excise — the same — was taken by the tide at Holt Ness while supervising rather further out than the tide approved of; and it was Zebediah, of all men on the coast, who went in after him and brought him back, a service the confession passes over in eleven words and the supervisor's own diary gives four pages, the last of which records that the smuggler had {{rescue}}d — to rescue meaning to save out of danger, to deliver from peril — him "with a contempt for the water which I have tried, since, without success, to cultivate." The Crown's case against Zebediah was not proceeded with. The informer, kept on by the revenue as {{bait}} — bait meaning the food set upon the hook to lure the fish; and by extension, anything offered to draw a victim in — for the remainder of the gang, was {{terrify|terrified}} — to terrify meaning to fill with terror — into Portsmouth by the next carrier, though no hand had been raised; the confession records, with the distaste of a craftsman, that a rival crew had proposed to {{strangle}} — to strangle meaning to stop the breath of, by compression of the throat — him, and that his own gang had declined, "having no stomach for knots while rope could be spent on cargo." The {{revenge}} — revenge meaning the repayment of an injury; the satisfaction taken for a wrong — of the county was never formally taken; but the Mercury noted that the informer's mother's best bonnet was seen, that harvest, on a head it had no business being on, and let the county draw its own conclusions.

The two exploits the valley actually remembers are, characteristically, the two the confession spends least ink upon. In 1813 the gang stopped the revenue cart on the turnpike and carried it off entire with its season of confiscated brandy — {{hijack}} — to hijack meaning to seize a thing in transit and take it, with its cargo, where one pleases; a word the century had not yet coined, though not for want of the practice — a feat the Crown's own ledger describes, in a hand shaking with arithmetic, as "a loss of eleven pounds fourteen shillings, and of face." And in 1816 they {{kidnap}}ped — to kidnap meaning to steal a person away by force and hold him to terms — no less a person than the supervisor himself, on the eve of the assizes, and kept him three days at the Bull, at cards and roast mutton, returning him rested, four shillings to the good, and — as the same diary admits — "unable to swear to the face of any man who had beaten me so handsomely at picquet."

Zebediah died at eighty-six, in his bed, in the smell of the sea. The {{nightmare}}s — a nightmare being a fearful dream; and by extension, any dread that returns by night — he records were never of the gallows but of the tide, "which keeps no ledger, and never once mistook me for a customer." When the tin box was opened at the Bull, the smell of pitch and old brandy {{pervade}}d — to pervade meaning to pass through and through, to spread into every part of — the tap-room for a week; and the carpenter {{marvel|marvelled}} — to marvel meaning to wonder, to be struck with astonishment — for a month that the mice had eaten the string and left the ribbon. The papers are with the county archivist now; the boards were {{restore}}d — to restore meaning to give back, as a thing taken is returned; and to mend, as a thing worn or broken is brought back toward its first state — by the carpenter on the Friday; and the legend, which had grown fat on two sentences of the Mercury, found itself {{overshadow|overshadowed}} — to overshadow meaning to cast a shadow over; to dwarf by superior presence — for good by eleven pages of the man himself, the man being the better writer. The Mercury, asked why it had never said so much, replied that it had had a headline to fill; and the valley, which has read both, has drawn its own conclusions, as it does.
tr:
三月，公牛客栈的旧马厩地板被撬开——恰好是杂货铺易手的同一个月，河谷向来没法一次只顾一件事——木匠在四十块地板和一百年的老鼠窝底下，发现了一只用沥青封口的铁盒；盒子里，用一根早已锈成铁条的缎带捆着，是走私客泽比迪亚·维的忏悔书，一八三四年誊写得工工整整，抬头写着“给付钱铺这块地板的人”。《信使报》称之为河谷有史以来最奇特的一份契据（deed，deed 指做成的事、行为；落在纸上指加盖印信、以之拥有某物的文书）——也是档案里唯一一份没人想据为己有的。

泽比迪亚本在兰普福德码头当潮汐看守员——偏偏是这么个营生——直到漫长的战争让正经金酒变得昂贵、不正经的金酒成了个行当；此后二十年的记述，是全县现存最完整的一份。那伙人把白兰地藏进羊毛袋走私（smuggle，smuggle 指违法运货进出国境、从缉私官眼皮底下运过），花边塞进《圣经》，还有一回打着赌，把一整块铁砧装在葬礼花圈底下运了进来；花圈便是伪装（disguise，disguise 指让人显得不像自己的衣装或涂饰），走在前面的教堂司事摆着一脸教规级的哀恸，是全县最好的演员。酒桶在霍尔特角上岸，沉进卵石滩挖出的壕沟（trench，trench 指狭长的沟，为排水、为战事、也为藏东西而挖）里，两英尺深，上面压块石头做记号——潮水每年冬天都要挪动它，于是每一季都有整整三分之一的工夫，花在寻找另外三分之二上。

他生涯里最费力气（effort，effort 指为达目的而使出的身心之力）的一仗，是一八一一年十月那一趟：四十桶酒，一条新单桅帆船，而且照他的说法，全海岸的税务人员都在晚祷。他把这次尝试（attempt，attempt 指一试、对成败尚在两可的进取）形容为河谷见过的最纯粹的豪赌（gamble，gamble 指押上赌注博输赢；牌桌之外泛指把任何东西押在运气上），押上的赌注（stake，stake 指立起来押在输赢上的东西；押在那一掷上的钱，或者脖子）是船、货，外加十一条人命的脖子；而赔率是天气、月亮，和一个告密者。

坏事坏在告密者身上——告密者向来如此；他把潮水和地点卖了三十几尼，换来王室一份心怀不安的感激。那夜的雾穿透（penetrate，penetrate 指穿入并透过，如潮气浸透外套）了沼泽上的一切，骑马的缉私队也不例外；可税务方面带来了一盏新式灯笼，光柱刺透（pierce，pierce 指扎穿、如尖物穿透所入之物）四分之一英里的雾，凌晨两点，骑队追上（overtake，overtake 指追及，如追逐赶上逃亡）了马车。泽比迪亚感到第一个骑手攥紧（grip，grip 指抓住不放、如手攥住手臂）了他的肩膀，便做出了一件任何议会都不曾想过要立法防范的行为（act，act 指做成的事；议会的语言里指一部法律）：他扬鞭把马赶进小河湾，潮水随即吞了马车、酒桶、灯笼，差点连那个骑手也一并收下。

有一页，河谷是摊平了手指读的。霍尔特沼泽那场混战里，一个年轻官员倒下了——是酒桶、马蹄还是河湾本身干的，忏悔书没有说——而《信使报》的曾祖母用两栏宽的大标题称之为一场屠杀（massacre，massacre 指对手无寸铁者无情杀戮；报纸用语里泛指任何超出一段篇幅的混战），因为事实不够、铅字来凑。这件事的结局，用牧师的话说，比安慰更精确，是那伙人的十中损一（decimation，decimation 严格指罗马军中十人惩一的刑罚；泛指任何惨重的折损）：三人被抓，两人流放，一人溺亡，买卖本身东迁二十英里。被抓的三人在巡回法庭上被定罪（convict，convict 指证明或宣告有罪，如陪审团之所为）；狱卒按他的行规欺压（bully，bully 指仗着力气或职权压迫弱者、以威吓使人屈服）他们，为此挨了法官一顿申斥——法官认为，他的犯人只该被判决书吓着。年长的那位受了兰普福德颈手枷的羞辱（indignity，indignity 指对尊严的冒犯、折辱），《信使报》记载，他扛得“让一些王室叫不出名字的人鼓了掌”——这比判决本身更让王室挫败（mortify，mortify 指如修道院般苦修克己；修道院之外指挫折骄傲）。不出一星期，那伙人撤出（evacuate，evacuate 指从一地撤出，如守军或居民之撤退）了海岸；泽比迪亚被逐出（expel，expel 指驱逐、以强力逐出）兰普福德自由民名册，“连名带姓带全部亲眷，一句话写完，句子长得气象堂皇”。

救了他的脖子、也救了他此后在河谷的名声的，是第二年春天的一桩事。税务总监——就是那位——在霍尔特角督察，督得比潮水许可的更远，被潮水收了去；而全海岸偏偏是泽比迪亚下海去把他捞了回来。这件事忏悔书十一个字打发，总监自己的日记却写了四页，最后一页记着：这位走私客营救（rescue，rescue 指救出险境、从危难中解救）他时“对水的那份蔑视，我后来一直想学，没有学成”。王室对泽比迪亚的案子就此没有再追究。那个告密者被税务方面留作钓饵（bait，bait 指钩上引鱼上钩的食；泛指引人上钩的任何东西），钓这伙人的余党，结果被吓得（terrify，terrify 指使充满恐惧）搭下一班脚夫车去了朴次茅斯——其实谁也没碰他一根指头；忏悔书记着一句行家的嫌弃：有一伙对头曾提议勒死（strangle，strangle 指扼住喉咙、使其断气）他，他们自己这伙没答应，“绳子能花在货上，谁还有胃口去打结”。县里的报复（revenge，revenge 指对伤害的偿还、为冤屈讨回的满足）始终没有正式执行；只是《信使报》注意到，那年收获节，告密者母亲最好的那顶软帽出现在了一颗它绝不该出现的脑袋上，然后让全县自己下结论。

河谷真正记得的两桩壮举，偏偏是忏悔书着墨最少的两桩。一八一三年，那伙人在收费大道上截下税务的货车，连车带货整个掳走——劫夺（hijack，hijack 指劫夺运送中的东西、连货带去自己想去的地方；这个词那个世纪还没造出来，可这门手艺一点不缺）了王室整整一季的充公白兰地——王室自己的账簿用一只被算术气得发抖的手记为“损失十一镑十四先令，外加脸面”。一八一六年，他们绑架（kidnap，kidnap 指以强力掳走一个人、扣着他讲条件）的不是别人，正是税务总监本人，在巡回法庭开庭前夜，把他留在公牛客栈三天，打牌，吃烤羊腿；还回去的时候，他休整一新，口袋里还多出四先令，而且——同一本日记承认——“任何在皮克牌上赢得我这样体面的人，我都无法出庭指认他的脸”。

泽比迪亚八十六岁死在自家床上，屋里一股海的气味。他记下的那些噩梦（nightmare，nightmare 指可怖的梦；泛指夜里回访的恐惧）从来不是绞架，而是潮水——“它不记账，也从不把我错当成主顾。”铁盒在公牛客栈开启时，沥青和陈年白兰地的气味弥漫（pervade，pervade 指穿透过透、渗进每一处）了酒馆一个星期；发现盒子的木匠称奇（marvel，marvel 指惊奇、被惊得叹服）了一个月——老鼠吃掉了麻绳，却留下了缎带。文件如今在县档案馆；地板由木匠在星期五修复（restore，restore 指归还，如取走之物送回；也指修葺，如破旧之物恢复旧观）归位；而那个靠《信使报》两句话养肥了的传说，从此被当事人亲笔的十一页彻底盖过（overshadow，overshadow 指投下阴影罩住；以更强的存在使之失色）——毕竟当事人是更好的作者。《信使报》被问起当年为何没写这么多，答曰版面要填标题；读了两样的河谷，照例自己下了结论。

quiz.q: The gang smuggled brandy in wool-sacks and lace in Bibles — to carry goods into or out of a country against the law. To smuggle is to —
o: sink a stone as a mark
sell the tide for thirty guineas
walk before a wreath with grief
quiz.ex: smuggle = 走私。smuggle goods into a country 向某国走私货物；smuggler n. 走私者。

quiz.q: The wreath was the disguise, and the sexton the finest actor in the county — the dress or paint by which one seems other than one is. A disguise is —
o: the tide that keeps no ledger
the kegs sunk in the shingle
the lantern of the new sort
what makes one seem other than one is
quiz.ex: disguise = 伪装；假扮。in disguise 乔装打扮；a blessing in disguise 因祸得福。

quiz.q: He describes the attempt as the purest gamble the valley ever saw — to play a game for money staked on the issue; to risk anything upon chance. To gamble is to —
o: come up with a fleeing cart
quiz.ex: gamble = 赌博；冒险。gamble on the stock market 在股市投机；take a gamble 冒险一试。

quiz.q: The stake was the lugger, the cargo and eleven men's necks — that which is set up and risked on the throw. A stake is —
o: a fear that returns by night
what is risked on the throw
quiz.ex: stake = 赌注；利害关系。at stake 濒于险境；stake one's reputation 拿名誉打赌。

quiz.q: The three who were taken were convicted at the assizes — to prove or declare guilty, as a jury declares. To convict is to —
o: drive out of the freemen's roll
quiz.ex: convict = 定罪。convict sb of theft 判某人盗窃罪；convict n. 囚犯。

quiz.q: The affair ended in what the chaplain called the decimation of the gang — strictly, the destruction of one in ten; loosely, any heavy thinning. Decimation is —
o: a heavy thinning of a company
quiz.ex: decimation = 大量毁减；十中损一。源自罗马军团的"什一惩"。

quiz.q: Zebediah went in after the supervisor and rescued him — to save out of danger, to deliver from peril. To rescue is to —
o: spread into every part of a room
quiz.ex: rescue = 营救。rescue a drowning man 救起溺水者；come to the rescue 前来救援。

quiz.q: In 1816 they kidnapped no less a person than the supervisor himself — to steal a person away by force and hold him to terms. To kidnap is to —
o: steal a person away by force
quiz.ex: kidnap = 绑架。kidnap a child 绑架儿童；kidnapper n. 绑匪。

title: The Tug-of-War at the Harvest
text:
The tug-of-war between the mill and the quarry has closed the harvest festival since 1953, when the vicar instituted it in the first flush of the Coronation as a {{substitute}} — a substitute being one who, or that which, stands in the place of another — for the boxing, which had closed the festival since 1901 and had been retired, with relief on every side, after the matter of the second Bevan. It is held across the ford at six o'clock, when the light is going and the water at its kindest; the rope is manila, a hundred feet, and older than the average age of both teams; and the prize is a ram's horn, silver-mounted, {{obtain}}ed — to obtain meaning to get, to come by, as a thing sought is come by — from a farm at Bodmin in 1954 by persons now dead and much missed at committee.

The {{objective}} — an objective being the thing aimed at, the end held in view — is the obvious one: to put the other side into the ford. The {{purpose}} — purpose meaning the reason for which a thing is done or made; the end intended — of the institution is less often stated, but the vicar set it out at the founding in a sentence the Mercury keeps in standing type: "to let the valley be rivals for one afternoon, and neighbours for the other three hundred and sixty-four." The rules have never been written down; they subsist in an {{accord}} — accord meaning agreement; and, beyond a single agreement, harmony of minds — between the two captains that has held unbroken since 1958, when they fell out over boots, carried the quarrel to the ford, settled it in the water, and shook hands dripping.

This year the quarry suffered a succession. Ron Pethick, who had anchored the quarry side for thirty-one years and was called, without a smile anywhere in it, the Rock, retired in the spring at sixty-eight, on medical advice and his wife's, in that order of authority; and the quarry, {{strive|striving}} — to strive meaning to labour toward an end, to exert the whole of the strength — as it had always striven, was suddenly obliged to {{undertake}} — to undertake meaning to take upon oneself, as a task or a trust is taken on — the education of an anchor inside a single summer. The Rock {{offer}}ed — to offer meaning to present a thing for acceptance, to hold it out — to come out of retirement for one pull; the quarry declined him, with tears at both ends of the committee table, and gave the rope's end to young Tregose, nineteen, who {{worship}}ped — to worship meaning to pay divine honours to; and beyond the church, to regard with a devotion exceeding sense — the Rock with the whole of his heart and knew his instructions by heart. The new rope, bought against the retirement, was {{baptise|baptised}} — to baptise meaning to christen, to name with water at the font; and loosely, to initiate with any liquid whatever — in cider at the Bull on the Thursday, the old rope attending as godparent.

The mill, for its part, had not won since 1989, and its captain did not pretend otherwise. His men {{polish}}ed — to polish meaning to rub to brightness; and by extension, to finish and perfect, as a performance is finished — their boots and their footwork in the old coach-house all August, to the despair of the pianist who shared it; the Stores laid in a special {{supply}} — a supply being that which is supplied; a stock laid in against use — of linseed oil for the rope's last dressing, and refused, on a principle older than the rope, to take payment for it; the landlady of the Bull {{nourish}}ed — to nourish meaning to feed, to sustain with food, as the soil feeds what grows in it — both sides impartially through the training, against her own interest, the quarry drinking twice what the mill did; and the mill's single {{desire}} — desire meaning the longing of the mind toward a thing — was, in the captain's phrase, to {{reverse}} — to reverse meaning to turn the other way about; to undo, as a verdict is undone — the verdict of thirty-five years, a thing the mill had {{yearn}}ed — to yearn meaning to long with tenderness, as one longs for what stands at the far side of a room — after openly, as only the defeated may.

On the day, the whistle went at six exactly; both sides {{exhale}}d — to exhale meaning to breathe forth, to send the breath out — together, in the manner taught them by a man neither team can now name, and the first heat went to the quarry by a yard. The second the mill {{gain}}ed — to gain meaning to get, to win, as ground is won — by two; the third was, in the Mercury's phrase, "a {{smash}} — a smash meaning the act of dashing to pieces; and in the newspapers, a conspicuous success — from the first heave," the mill {{surmount}}ing — to surmount meaning to climb over, to get the better of, as a wall or a difficulty is got over — its own astonishment in time to put it to use; and in the deciding pull the quarry went half a length down and {{recover}}ed — to recover meaning to get back what was lost; to regain, as ground, health or composure is regained — six inches of it, and no more. The mill's drought ended at thirty-five years and one afternoon; the quarry took the water; the horn changed mantelpieces for the first time in living memory; and the referee, having {{rectify|rectified}} — to rectify meaning to make straight and right, as an error or an account is made right — his own mistake about the centre mark in the second heat, to the mill's advantage and the match's, was carried shoulder-high to the Bull by both teams together, by common consent, being right twice and merciful once.

The Rock presented the horn to the mill's captain with a speech of nine words: "You were due it; we shall want it back." Tregose, who had feared all summer that he was the reason and now learned that he was the making of it, had {{fulfil|fulfilled}} — to fulfil meaning to fill full; to perform wholly, as a promise or a duty is performed — the Rock's instruction to the letter and the larger part of the Rock's prophecy besides; and being asked, in the general noise, what he now {{aspire}}d — to aspire meaning to climb toward, as flame climbs the chimney; to seek a height — to, said: "Next year." The singing after the pull, lapsed since the year of the flood, was {{revive}}d — to revive meaning to bring or come back to life, as fainting strength or a lapsed custom returns — by the veterans on the mutual condition that nobody led; the mill's honour stood {{redeem}}ed — to redeem meaning to buy back; to make good, as a pledge or a name is made good — at last, and cheap at the price of one ford apiece; the quarry consoled itself with the thought, printed by the Mercury next morning, that the horn would look well in either window; and the whole valley agreed, over cider, that both teams had {{deserve}}d — to deserve meaning to merit, to have earned by conduct — to win, that the ford alone had lost, and that they had every one of them pulled, in the end, for the {{sake}} — sake meaning cause, account, consideration, as a thing is done for honour's sake — of the thing itself, which is the only stake that never asks to be cashed.
tr:
磨坊对采石场的拔河，自一九五三年起便是收获节的收场戏——那一年牧师趁着加冕礼的头一股热乎劲儿设立了它，作为拳击的替代（substitute，substitute 指站在他人位置上顶替的人或物）；拳击从一九〇一年起便是收场戏，却在“第二个贝文事件”之后各方都松了口气地退了休。比赛六点整在浅滩上举行，那时天光将尽，水也最和气；绳子是马尼拉麻的，一百英尺，比两队人的平均年龄都老；奖品是一只羊角，镶着银座，一九五四年由如今已故、且为委员会深深怀念的几位，从博德明一家农场购得（obtain，obtain 指获得、如所寻之物被弄到手）。

目标（objective，objective 指瞄准的东西、心中看着的那个终点）是明摆着的：把对面那一侧拽进浅滩。这桩制度的目的（purpose，purpose 指做一件事的理由、打算达成的效果）却不常有人讲，但牧师在成立时用一句话说透了，《信使报》至今存成现成的铅字：“让河谷当一下午的对头，当其余三百六十四天的邻居。”规则从未落在纸上；它们活在一任任两位队长之间的默契（accord，accord 指一致同意；也指超出单次同意的心意相通）里，自一九五八年不曾破过——那年他们为靴子闹翻，把争端带到浅滩，在水里解决了它，然后滴着水握了手。

今年采石场遭了接班之变。罗恩·佩西克——给采石场压了三十一年阵脚、被大家不带一点笑意地称作“磐石”的人——春天退了役，六十八岁，遵医嘱，遵太太嘱，权威顺序如此；于是向来只知道苦干（strive，strive 指向着目标尽全力苦干）的采石场，突然不得不在一个夏天里承担（undertake，undertake 指把任务或信托揽到自己身上）起培养一名压阵手的工程。“磐石”主动提出（offer，offer 指把东西呈上供人接受）为最后一拔复出一场；采石场谢绝了——委员会桌子两头都有眼泪——把绳头交给了十九岁的特雷戈斯。这孩子崇敬（worship，worship 指对之行敬神之礼；教堂之外指超出常理的顶礼膜拜）“磐石”崇敬得五体投地，把他的口诀背得一字不差。为这场退役新买的绳子，星期四在公牛客栈受了苹果酒的洗礼（baptise，baptise 指以水行洗礼命名；泛指以任何液体为入行礼）——旧绳子到场做了教父。

磨坊这边，自一九八九年就没赢过，队长也不装作不是。他的人整个八月在旧马车房里打磨（polish，polish 指擦到发亮；泛指把一场表演修得圆熟）靴子和步法，把同屋的钢琴师折磨得够呛；杂货铺为绳子最后一道上油备下一批特供（supply，supply 指被供应之物、为备用而囤的存货）亚麻籽油，并本着比绳子还老的原则拒收货款；公牛客栈的老板娘在训练期间不分彼此地供养（nourish，nourish 指喂养、如土壤滋养所长之物）着两队——有违她自己的利益，采石场的酒量是磨坊的两倍；而磨坊唯一的愿望（desire，desire 指心思对一物的渴望），用队长的话说，就是扭转（reverse，reverse 指掉过头来；如判决被推翻）三十五年前的裁决——为这个他们已经公开渴念（yearn，yearn 指带着柔情渴想，如渴想摆在房间另一头之物）了很多年，唯有败者可以如此。

比赛当天，哨音六点整准时响起；两队一同呼出（exhale，exhale 指呼出、把气送出体外）一口气——教这口气的人，两队如今都叫不出名字——第一局采石场赢了一码。第二局磨坊夺回（gain，gain 指获得、赢得，如夺回地面）两码；第三局，用《信使报》的话说，“从第一把起就是一场完胜（smash，smash 指砸得粉碎；报章用语指一鸣惊人的大捷）”，磨坊翻越（surmount，surmount 指翻过、如翻过一堵墙或一道难关）了自己的震惊，及时把它用上了；决胜局里，采石场被拉下去半个人身，又夺回（recover，recover 指收回所失；如地面、健康或镇定之失而复得）六英寸——只有六英寸。磨坊的旱季在三十五年零一个下午之后结束了；采石场下了水；羊角有生以来头一次换了壁炉架；裁判在第二局里纠正（rectify，rectify 指把错误或账目改直改对）了自己对中心记号的误判——判给了磨坊便宜，也判给了比赛公道——随后被两队一齐扛在肩上送到公牛客栈，出于一致同意：他判对过两回，慈悲过一回。

“磐石”把羊角授给磨坊队长，致辞共九个字：“该你们了；我们会来讨还。”特雷戈斯一夏天都怕自己是个缺口，此刻才知道自己是块成料；他履行（fulfil，fulfil 指填满做足；如承诺或职责之全然履行）了“磐石”的口诀一字不落，顺带也应验了那更大的预言；在满场喧闹里有人问他，如今他向往（aspire，aspire 指向上攀，如火苗爬烟囱；追求一个高度）什么。“明年。”他说。拔河之后的合唱——发大水那年起就断了——由老兵们复活（revive，revive 指使之或使之重获生气，如昏厥的力气或中断的老例）了，条件是互相不许领唱；磨坊的名誉终于赎回（redeem，redeem 指赎回；如典当之物或名声之挽回），代价不过是每人一条浅滩，便宜得很；采石场用《信使报》次日的说法安慰自己：这羊角摆在哪个窗口都好看；而全村就着苹果酒达成一致：两队都配得上赢（deserve，deserve 指值得、以行为挣得），输的只有浅滩；他们所有人到头来，为的都是这件事本身的缘故（sake，sake 指缘由、缘故，如“为了荣誉的缘故”）——那是唯一一枚从不要求兑付的赌注。

quiz.q: The vicar instituted the tug-of-war as a substitute for the boxing — one who, or that which, stands in the place of another. A substitute is —
o: the act of dashing to pieces
a stock laid in against use
one who stands in another's place
quiz.ex: substitute = 替代者；替代品。substitute A for B 用 A 代替 B；substitute teacher 代课教师。

quiz.q: The rules subsist in an accord between the two captains — agreement; and beyond a single agreement, harmony of minds. An accord is —
o: the reason a thing is done
quiz.ex: accord = 一致；协议。in accord with 与……一致；peace accord 和平协议。

quiz.q: Being asked what he now aspired to, Tregose said: 'Next year.' — to climb toward, as flame climbs the chimney; to seek a height. To aspire is to —
o: long for what stands across a room
quiz.ex: aspire = 渴望；追求。aspire to greatness 追求卓越；aspiration n. 抱负。

quiz.q: The mill's single desire was to reverse the verdict of thirty-five years — to turn the other way about; to undo, as a verdict is undone. To reverse is to —
quiz.ex: reverse = 逆转；颠倒。reverse a decision 推翻决定；in reverse order 按相反顺序。

quiz.q: The mill, surmounting its own astonishment in time to use it — to climb over, to get the better of, as a wall or a difficulty is got over. To surmount is to —
o: decline with tears at both ends
get the better of a difficulty
quiz.ex: surmount = 克服；越过。surmount obstacles 克服障碍；insurmountable adj. 不可逾越的。

quiz.q: The referee rectified his own mistake about the centre mark — to make straight and right, as an error or an account is made right. To rectify is to —
o: settle a quarrel in the water
quiz.ex: rectify = 纠正；矫正。rectify a mistake 纠正错误；rectify an account 核正账目。

quiz.q: The mill's honour stood redeemed at last — to buy back; to make good, as a pledge or a name is made good. To redeem is to —
o: bring a custom back to life
quiz.ex: redeem = 赎回；弥补。redeem a promise 兑现诺言；redeem oneself 挽回名誉。

quiz.q: They had pulled, in the end, for the sake of the thing itself — cause, account, consideration, as a thing is done for honour's sake. Sake is —
o: a rope of manila, a hundred feet
the end intended by the vicar
quiz.ex: sake = 缘故。for the sake of 为了……起见；for safety's sake 为安全起见。

title: The New Doctor
text:
Dr. Chubb retired in April, at seventy-nine, halfway through a consultation, having practised in the valley for fifty-three years with a black bag, three questions and one bottle. His successor arrived the same week: Dr. Anand, from the county hospital, thirty-one years old, with the {{physician}} — a physician being a doctor of medicine; one who treats the sick as a profession and, at the best of it, as a calling — 's coat still new enough to creak, a wife who played the cello, and opinions that ran to four pages where Dr. Chubb's had run to three words. He turned the front parlour of Ivy Cottage into a {{clinic}} — a clinic being a place where patients are received and treated; and where, in the old use, teaching goes on beside the curing — and opened it on a Monday, with the Mercury in attendance and the whole valley pointedly not ill.

The valley withheld its custom for a month, out of loyalty to a memory and mistrust of a handwriting. Dr. Chubb had asked three questions and poured from one bottle; the new man asked forty and wrote instead of pouring, sending every order to the {{pharmacy}} — a pharmacy being the place where medicines are kept, compounded and dispensed — at Lampford, by name, on paper, each order a {{prescription}} — a prescription being the physician's written direction, by which the medicine is prepared and given — naming the drug, the form and the {{dose}} — a dose being the quantity of a medicine to be taken at one time — with a precision the valley read, for a fortnight, as showing off. He gave {{pill}}s — a pill being a small tablet of medicine, made to be swallowed — where Dr. Chubb had given reassurance, and {{injection}}s — an injection being the driving of a medicine into the body by needle — where Dr. Chubb had given the bottle; and when he asked, at the desk, whether there was an {{allergy}} — an allergy being the body's quarrel with a substance that leaves other bodies in peace — to {{penicillin}} — penicillin being the mould-made medicine that fights the bacterial invader and leaves the rest of the body standing — in the family, the question was taken, briefly, as a personal remark.

He had come with plans, which he laid before the parish meeting in November like a man laying out tools. He proposed to {{vaccinate}} — to vaccinate meaning to inoculate; to give the body its lesson against a sickness, in a small and harmless schooling of the same — every child in the valley against measles, the valley having lost four to it in living memory; the {{infection}}s — an infection being the entering and multiplying of disease-carrying things within the body — of the bad winters would be met with {{antibiotic}}s — an antibiotic being a medicine, made mostly of moulds, that kills the invading things and leaves the patient standing — where the old bottle had been met with the old bottle; the {{immune}} — immune meaning exempt, protected against a disease, as the recovered are protected against its return — would be counted, and the rest brought up to strength; there would be a yearly {{check}} — a check being an examination, a looking-over to see that all is as it should be — for the well, beginning with a {{physical}} — a physical being a bodily examination in full, the word the army made common — that took an hour and offended nobody who survived it; and the machine arrived at Christmas: the {{x-ray}} — an x-ray being the picture made by rays that pass through flesh and stop at bone — a cabinet the size of a wardrobe that could see through a hand as through a window pane, at which the Sunday congregation forgave it everything, having voted it, the week before, the second most suspicious thing to enter the valley that year, after the phrase he used for the whole enterprise: {{health care}} — health care meaning the whole trade of keeping the well well and the ill less so.

His first winter supplied the cases the winter demanded. The quarry foreman came in with a {{chronic}} — chronic meaning long-continuing, of a sickness that settles in and stays, as against one that comes and goes — cough of twenty years, and left with a diagnosis, a plan and the first hope of a quiet night since the Coronation; the {{arthritis}} — arthritis being the inflammation of the joints, the stiffness that age and weather put into them — in Mrs. Tizzard's knuckles was not cured but {{alleviate|alleviated}} — to alleviate meaning to lighten, to make less, as a burden or a pain is made less — by exercises taught at the kitchen table; and he went at the quiet killers in order: the {{hypertension}} — hypertension being the state of blood driven at too high a pressure — of half the men over fifty, taken at the {{pulse}} — a pulse being the beat of the arteries, felt at the wrist, by which the heart's work is counted — and written down; the {{diabetes}} — diabetes being the sugar sickness, in which the body loses its government of sweet things — of the sweet-toothed; the {{obesity}} — obesity being the state of being fat past the line of health — of the two, and the mere {{overweight}} — overweight meaning heavy past the standard, but not yet past hope — of the rest; all of it to be met, he said, not with medicine but with {{lifestyle}} — lifestyle meaning the manner of a life; the sum of its habits — which word caused more offence than any diagnosis, the valley having considered its manner of life the one field in which it led the county. The first blood tests came back from Lampford: {{normal}} — normal meaning according to the rule, of the usual sort, as the healthy are usual — in eleven cases, {{positive}} — positive meaning, of a test, showing the thing tested for to be present — in two, {{negative}} — negative meaning, of a test, showing it absent — in the rest; and the valley learned the new arithmetic of good news, in which negative is what you pray for and positive what you dread. The {{medical}} — medical meaning of the healing art; belonging to the physician and his science — journals arrived weekly and were read, within a month, by the barbers; the {{medicine}} — medicine meaning the art and science of healing; and, by extension, the stuff by which it is practised — of the county hospital, he said, was ten years ahead of the valley and thirty behind the journals, a sentence he was wise enough to keep for the bishop.

The rest of the practice was the old practice, which he respected. He kept the midwifery, as Dr. Chubb had kept it, and delivered the spring's babies on the same kitchen table; the {{pregnancy}} — a pregnancy being the state of carrying a child unborn — book was a ledger of the valley's futures, and he was the first to read it. A drawer of the desk was given over to the {{condom}}s — a condom being the sheath worn to prevent both conception and disease — to be asked for in whatever roundabout sentence the asker preferred; the drawer was known, without a word ever passing, as the quiet drawer. He pulled teeth on Fridays, the {{dental}} — dental meaning of the teeth — chair set by the window where the light was; the word he used of the complaints men brought him quietly, {{dysfunction}} — dysfunction meaning the failure of a part to do its appointed work; in the surgery's language, most often of the kind not discussed at the Legion — he said was commoner than the silence around it suggested, and treatable, a sentence the Legion received in the spirit of a border raid. His {{private}} — private meaning one's own, apart from the public — patients were the same as his public ones, seen in the same order; a {{familiar}} — familiar meaning well known, of the family of one's knowledge — face turned up at every surgery hour, the Mercury noted, before the snow was off the cross; and the parish's {{concern}} — concern meaning the matter that touches one; the anxiety felt for a person or a thing — for his health, after the winter he had had, took the form of leaving rabbits on the step, which he accepted as the valley's handwriting and never once failed to {{relieve}} — to relieve meaning to ease, to lift a weight or a pain from — with thanks in kind.

What settled the matter was the night of the twelfth of January. The miller's boy, at midnight, with an {{acute}} — acute meaning of sudden onset and sharp course, as the chronic is of slow — appendix; the county ambulance an hour away and the snow four feet deep. Dr. Anand took him to Lampford on the quarry's snow-plough, holding the boy's hand the whole way and the boy holding the diagnosis the whole way; the county hospital, which had expected to be introducing the case to the coroner, removed the appendix at two and had him drinking tea at six. The valley, which had been patient in the old sense all winter — bearing, enduring, waiting — became his {{patient}}s — a patient being one who is under medical care — by Friday; and when the Mercury asked him, at his anniversary, what had changed, he said: "Nothing. They got ill."
tr:
丘布医生四月退休了，七十九岁，问诊问到一半退的休——他在河谷行医五十三年，凭一只黑包、三个问题和一个瓶子。接班人同一星期到任：阿南德医生，来自县医院，三十一岁，那件内科医生（physician，physician 指医师、以内科行医为业者；说到最好处，视之为天职）的白大褂新得咔咔作响，太太会拉大提琴，而他的见解能写满四页纸，丘布医生的见解则历来不超过三个词。他把常春藤小屋的前客厅改成了诊所（clinic，clinic 指接诊治病之处；旧义中兼作临床教学之地），星期一开诊，《信使报》到场，而全村出奇地齐整——没一个人生病。

全村把生意扣了一个月，一半出于对亡人的忠诚，一半出于对那笔新字迹的不信任。丘布医生问三个问题、从一只瓶子里倒药；新医生问四十个问题，并且只写不倒——每一张处方都送往兰普福德的药房（pharmacy，pharmacy 指储存、配制并发售药品之所），指名道姓，落在纸上，每一单都是处方（prescription，prescription 指医生据以配药发药的书面指示），写明药名、剂型与剂量（dose，dose 指一次服下的药量），精确得让全村当成足足两个星期的卖弄。丘布医生给安慰的地方，他给药片（pill，pill 指制成便于吞服的小药丸）；丘布医生给瓶子的地方，他给注射（injection，injection 指以针剂将药液注入体内）；他在登记处问每户人家对青霉素（penicillin，penicillin 指以霉菌制成、杀灭细菌而保全病人的药）有无过敏（allergy，allergy 指身体与某种旁人无事之物的龃龉）时，这个问题一度被当成了人身攻击。

他是带着计划来的，十一月拿到教区会议上，像工匠摆开工具。他提议给全谷的孩子接种疫苗（vaccinate，vaccinate 指接种；以一次小而无害的同源操练，教会身体认识一场疫病）以防麻疹——活人记忆里，河谷为此失去过四个孩子；坏年冬天的感染（infection，infection 指致病之物侵入体内并滋长）将改用抗生素（antibiotic，antibiotic 指多由霉菌制成、杀灭来犯之物而令病人站稳的药）应对，不再像旧瓶子对旧瓶子那样硬扛；有免疫力（immune，immune 指豁免的、对疫病有保护的，如康复者之于复发）的要清点入册，其余的补齐元气；还要给健康人一年一次检查（check，check 指查验、看一眼是否一切如常），从全面体检（physical，physical 指从头到脚的身体检查，这个词是军队叫响的）开始——一次一小时，挺过来的人无一觉得受了冒犯；机器是圣诞到的：X光（x-ray，x-ray 指以能穿透皮肉、止于骨骼的射线拍成的影像），一台衣柜大小的柜子，隔着它看一只手如隔一层窗玻璃——星期日的会众原谅了它的一切，因为前一星期刚把它选为本年度进入河谷的第二可疑之物，仅次于他给整个事业起的名字：保健（health care，health care 指让健康人保持健康、让病人少受病痛的整个行当）。

他的第一个冬天立刻送来了冬天该有的病例。采石场工头带着二十年的慢性（chronic，chronic 指迁延不愈、一病安营扎寨长住不走，与来去匆匆者相对）咳嗽进门，走时带着诊断、方案，以及加冕礼以来第一次对安睡一夜的指望；蒂泽德太太指节里的关节炎（arthritis，arthritis 指关节的炎症、年岁与天气塞进关节的僵硬）没有治愈，却被厨房餐桌上传授的操练缓解（alleviate，alleviate 指减轻，如负担或疼痛被减轻）了；然后他按次序对付那些无声的杀手：五十岁以上的男人一半有高血压（hypertension，hypertension 指血液被驱动得过猛的状态），他把脉（pulse，pulse 指动脉的搏动、在腕上摸到的心跳，据以计数心脏的工作）记录在案；嗜甜的有糖尿病（diabetes，diabetes 指糖分之病、身体失去对甜物的管辖）；两位到了肥胖（obesity，obesity 指胖过了健康之线），其余的只是超重（overweight，overweight 指超过标准体重、但还没超到没救）；而这一切，他说，要对付靠的不是药，是生活方式（lifestyle，lifestyle 指生活的方式、诸般习惯的总和）——这个词引起的公愤比任何诊断都大，河谷一向认为自己的活法是全县唯一领先的领域。第一批血检从兰普福德回来了：十一例正常（normal，normal 指合乎常规、如健康人之平常），两例阳性（positive，positive 指检验中显示所查之物确实存在），其余阴性（negative，negative 指检验中显示所查之物并不存在）；河谷于是学会了好消息的新算术——阴性是求之不得，阳性避之不及。医学（medical，medical 指医术的、属于医师及其科学的）期刊每周寄到，不出一个月，理发师们也读上了；他说县医院的医术（medicine，medicine 指救疗之艺与科学；也指行医所用的药物）比河谷超前十年、比期刊落后三十年——这句话他很明智地留给了主教听。

其余的营业还是旧的营业，他对之保持了敬意。他照丘布医生的老例接生，春天的新生儿仍降生在同一张厨房餐桌上；孕册（pregnancy，pregnancy 指身怀未出生之子的状态）是一本河谷未来的账簿，而他是第一个读者。书桌的一只抽屉专放安全套（condom，condom 指避孕且防病的套状物），供人用各自迂回的句子来讨要；那只抽屉人尽皆知，却从来没有一个字说破，都叫它“安静的抽屉”。他星期五拔牙，牙科（dental，dental 指牙齿的）椅摆在窗边光线最好的地方；至于男人们悄悄带来的那种毛病——功能障碍（dysfunction，dysfunction 指某一部位不能履行其职；诊所用语里多指军团里不便讨论的那一类）——他说这毛病比围绕它的沉默所暗示的普遍得多，而且治得好，这句话军团以边境突袭的精神予以接收。他的私家（private，private 指自己的、与公家分开的）病人和公家病人是同一批人，按同一顺序就诊；雪还没化过十字路口，《信使报》就注意到，每门诊时段都有一张熟面孔（familiar，familiar 指熟识的、在认识范围内的）准时出现；教区对他整个冬天操劳的关切（concern，concern 指牵挂在心之事、对人或事的挂念）表现为往台阶上放兔子，他把这当作河谷的笔迹，每次都投桃报李地致谢，从无一次疏漏（relieve，relieve 指纾解、把重量或疼痛从身上卸下）。

真正定局的是一月十二日的夜里。磨坊主的儿子半夜得了急性（acute，acute 指骤起而凶险的，与慢性之迟缓相对）阑尾炎；县里的救护车在一小时之外，雪有四英尺深。阿南德医生用采石场的铲雪车把他送去兰普福德，一路握着孩子的手，孩子一路握着诊断书；县医院本以为要见的是验尸官，结果凌晨两点切掉阑尾，六点孩子就喝上了茶。全村一冬天都在旧意义上忍耐——承受、坚持、等待——到星期五，都成了他的病人（patient，patient 指受医疗照护之人）；周年纪念日上《信使报》问他，是什么改变了河谷，他说：“什么都没变。他们病了。”

quiz.q: Dr. Anand arrived with the physician's coat still new enough to creak — a doctor of medicine; one who treats the sick as a profession. A physician is —
o: a place where patients are received
the quantity of medicine taken at once
quiz.ex: physician = 内科医生；医师。physician and surgeon 内科与外科医生；family physician 家庭医生。

quiz.q: He sent every order to the pharmacy, each a prescription naming the drug, the form and the dose — the physician's written direction, by which the medicine is prepared. A prescription is —
o: the body's quarrel with a substance
the beat of the arteries at the wrist
quiz.ex: prescription = 处方。write out a prescription 开处方；on prescription 凭处方。

quiz.q: Each prescription named the drug, the form and the dose — the quantity of a medicine to be taken at one time. A dose is —
o: the state of blood at high pressure
a small tablet to be swallowed
the quantity taken at one time
quiz.ex: dose = 剂量；一剂。take a dose of medicine 服一剂药；overdose n. 过量。

quiz.q: He asked whether there was an allergy to penicillin in the family — the body's quarrel with a substance that leaves other bodies in peace. An allergy is —
o: the entering of disease into the body
the body's quarrel with a substance
the failure of a part to work
quiz.ex: allergy = 过敏。have an allergy to pollen 对花粉过敏；allergic adj. 过敏的。

quiz.q: He proposed to vaccinate every child against measles — to inoculate; to give the body its lesson against a sickness in a harmless schooling of it. To vaccinate is to —
o: count the immune and log them
quiz.ex: vaccinate = 给……接种疫苗。vaccinate children against measles 给儿童接种麻疹疫苗；vaccine n. 疫苗。

quiz.q: The foreman came in with a chronic cough of twenty years — long-continuing, of a sickness that settles in and stays. Chronic means —
o: heavy past the standard of hope
of sudden onset and sharp course
quiz.ex: chronic = 慢性的；长期的。chronic bronchitis 慢性支气管炎；a chronic problem 长期问题。

quiz.q: The miller's boy, at midnight, with an acute appendix — of sudden onset and sharp course, as the chronic is of slow. Acute means —
o: of sudden onset and sharp course
able to be seen through flesh
quiz.ex: acute = 急性的；剧烈的。acute appendicitis 急性阑尾炎；acute pain 剧痛。

quiz.q: The arthritis in Mrs. Tizzard's knuckles was not cured but alleviated by exercises — to lighten, to make less, as a burden or a pain is made less. To alleviate is to —
o: make a burden or pain less
quiz.ex: alleviate = 减轻；缓解。alleviate pain 缓解疼痛；alleviation n. 减轻。

title: Osbert
text:
Dr. Chubb's will, opened in April, left the school his skeleton, with a letter in the shaky upright hand of his last year: "To Millbrook School, my oldest colleague. He taught me all I know of anatomy and none of what I know of kindness, which I got elsewhere. Treat him accordingly." The {{skeleton}} — a skeleton being the frame of bones on which the rest of us is carried — arrived in a crate of straw, was unpacked by the science teacher on the football field for reasons of ventilation, and stood, by the following Monday, at the back of the science room on a wheeled stand, wearing the school tie.

He had come with a name. The {{corpus}} — corpus being the Latin for body; and in English, a body of writings or of stuff entire, as the corpus of a law or of a language — of him was genuine, and so was the name: Osbert, given by the medical students of Dr. Chubb's year, os being the Latin for bone, and the joke having outlived everyone who first laughed at it. The {{skull}} — the skull being the bony box that houses the brain, hinged at the jaw for teaching — was his best feature; the {{bone}}s — a bone being one of the hard members of the frame, three hundred and six of them by the school's count — were wired at the joints in the approved manner; and the {{backbone}} — the backbone being the spine's stack of bones, thirty-three of them; and beyond anatomy, the seat of resolution in a person — stood so straight that the first inspection committee pronounced him the most upright figure the school had produced in a decade.

The first lesson was given to the top form, who filed in sideways. The science teacher, who had rehearsed, began at the top: the {{brain}} — the brain being the organ of thought and government, housed in the skull, and the only organ that studies itself — was absent, being a lesson for the diagrams; the {{chamber}}s — a chamber being a room, a compartment; in anatomy, one of the heart's four receiving rooms — of the heart were demonstrated on the model that worked, the {{organ}} — an organ being any part of the body that does a work of its own, as the heart pumps and the eye sees — of the class having been the bladder of the football outside; and the {{muscle}}s — a muscle being the flesh that pulls on bone to move it, Osbert's being painted on in red, as on a map — were named in the Latin the valley's farmers had been using for their cattle all along, to their manifest satisfaction.

The second lesson went inside. The {{abdomen}} — the abdomen being the cavity of the body below the chest, the belly — was opened with the dignity of a county occasion; the {{chest}} — the chest being the cavity above it, the box of the heart and lungs — had already been the occasion of two faintings, both among the parents at open day; the {{rib}}s — a rib being one of the curved bones that fence the chest, twelve a side — were counted aloud, the school having voted this the finest thing it had ever done in company; the {{lung}}s — a lung being one of the two organs of breath, the bellows of the blood — were demonstrated with the football bladder and a bicycle pump, the {{liver}} — the liver being the great organ of the abdomen, the body's chemical works — with a diagram and a warning about the Legion at darts night; the {{kidney}}s — a kidney being one of the two organs that filter the blood and keep its water honest — with the same diagram and the same warning, delivered in both directions; the {{intestine}}s — the intestines being the folded tube of the belly, along which the meal makes its long way — with a length of drainpipe that had seen service at the gala; and the {{gland}}s — a gland being an organ that makes and pours out a substance of its own, as the tears and the sweat are poured — were explained as the body's taps, an image that has outlived every other in the valley's memory.

The parents were invited to the third lesson, and came in the spirit of an inspection. The {{neck}} — the neck being the column that carries the head, and the word for it in every family's tone — and the {{jaw}} — the jaw being the hinged bone of the mouth, by which the teeth do their work and arguments their harm — were demonstrated as one system; the {{brow}} — the brow being the forehead; and, by extension, the arch of hair above it — was shown to be the only part that never moves on its own and yet says the most; and the {{womb}} — the womb being the organ in which the child is carried before birth, drawn for the girls on the blackboard and left, by the boys' own request, undrawn — was treated by the teacher with a plainness that ended, in a single afternoon, a century of the valley's folklore on the subject.

The last lesson was the valley's own idea. The science teacher had meant to end with the senses, but the top form had questions: whether Osbert had been tall; what a man's {{stature}} — stature being the height of a standing person; and by extension, the height of a reputation — had to do with his temper; whether the boys of the top form, standing beside the frame, {{resemble|resembled}} — to resemble meaning to be like, to bear the likeness of — him or he them, the class being, on the whole, long in the bone; whether the frame of a man from the last century was {{similar}} — similar meaning like, of the same sort, not identical — to the frames of this one, and how you could tell; and whether any of it — the wiring, the painting, the Latin — would have been {{visible}} — visible meaning able to be seen — to Osbert himself, who had, after all, never once been consulted. The teacher gave the questions the hour they deserved; and the new boiler, installed that autumn in the corner of the science room, {{dwarf}}s — to dwarf meaning to make small by standing large beside; to put a thing out of scale — the whole arrangement, Osbert included, so that the frame of him, between the boiler and the window, looks less like the school's proudest possession than like a thin gentleman waiting modestly for the bus.
tr:
丘布医生的遗嘱四月启封，把他的骨架留给了学校，附一封他最后一年里抖而端正的手写的信：“赠米尔布鲁克学校，我最老的同事。我所懂的解剖学全是它教的，我所懂的仁慈它一点没教——那是我从别处学的。请照此相待。”骨架（skeleton，skeleton 指驮着我们其余部分的骨骼架子）装在一板条箱刨花里运到，科学老师出于通风的考虑在足球场上拆的箱；到下星期一，他已站在科学教室后部一台带轮的架子上，系着学校的领带。

他是带着名字来的。他的躯体（corpus，corpus 为拉丁语“身体”；英语中指文集或某一整体之全帙，如法律或语言之全典）是真的，名字也是真的：奥斯伯特，丘布医生那届医学生起的——os 是拉丁语的“骨头”，而这个玩笑活得比最初笑它的所有人都长。颅骨（skull，skull 指容脑之骨匣，下颌带铰链以便教学）是他最体面的部分；骨头（bone，bone 指骨架中坚硬的一员，按学校的数法共二百零六块）按规范在关节处缚了铜丝；而那根脊梁（backbone，backbone 指脊柱三十三节骨的叠柱；解剖之外，也指人的骨气）挺得笔直，以致初次视察的委员会宣称他是本校十年来培养出的最端正的人物。

第一课讲给高年级，学生们侧着身鱼贯而入。科学老师排练过，从头讲起：大脑（brain，brain 指思想与统辖之官，居颅骨之中，是唯一研究它自己的器官）缺席——那是挂图上的课；心的四个腔（chamber，chamber 指房间、隔间；解剖学上指心脏四个受血之室）用会动的那台模型演示，全班最当用的器官（organ，organ 指身体中自成一职的部件，如心之泵血、目之视物）当时是外头那只足球的球胆；肌肉（muscle，muscle 指牵动骨头的肉，奥斯伯特的以红漆描出，如地图着色）用了拉丁名——河谷的农户给牛用的正是这一套，皆大满意。

第二课进了内脏。腹腔（abdomen，abdomen 指胸以下、肚子的体腔）以郡级典礼的郑重打开了；胸腔（chest，chest 指其上的体腔、心肺之匣）此前已在开放日诱发过两起晕厥，都出在家长中间；肋骨（rib，rib 指圈护胸腔的弯骨，每侧十二根）被齐声数过——学校公认这是它有史以来集体做过的最美的事；肺（lung，lung 指两个司呼吸的器官、血的风箱）用足球胆和打气筒演示；肝（liver，liver 指腹腔最大的器官、身体的化工厂）用一张挂图外加一句针对军团飞镖之夜的警告；肾（kidney，kidney 指滤血、掌管水之诚实的两个器官之一）用同一张图、同一句警告，双向发送；肠（intestine，intestine 指腹腔里折叠的长管、食糜漫长旅途所经之道）用一节在游园会服役过的排水管；腺（gland，gland 指自产自销某种分泌物的器官，如泪与汗之涌出）被讲成身体的龙头——这个比喻活得比河谷记忆里其他一切比喻都长。

家长受邀听第三课，来时都带着视察的心情。颈（neck，neck 指扛着脑袋的柱子，也是各家语气里指代它的那个词）与下颌（jaw，jaw 指口部带铰链的骨头，牙齿的作为与吵架的祸害都由它承当）被作为一个系统演示；眉（brow，brow 指前额；引申指其上的眉弓）被指出是唯一自己不动、却说得最多的部位；子宫（womb，womb 指孕养未出生之子的器官）给女生画在黑板上，应男生自己请求，没有画——老师处理这个题目的那份直白，一个下午就终结了河谷在这个题目上一个世纪的民间传说。

最后一课是河谷自己的主意。科学老师本想以感官收尾，高年级却自有问题：奥斯伯特生前高不高；一个人的身量（stature，stature 指站立之人的高度；引申指名声的高度）与脾气有无关系；高年级这些站在骨架旁边的男孩像不像（resemble，resemble 指相似、具有……的样貌）他，或他像不像他们——这个班普遍骨头偏长；上个世纪的骨架与这一个世纪的是否同类（similar，similar 指相像、同属一类而不相同），又如何分辨；以及这一切——铜丝、红漆、拉丁文——有没有一样是奥斯伯特本人看得见（visible，visible 指可见的）的，毕竟从头到尾没人问过他的意见。老师给了这些问题应有的一小时；那年秋天在科学教室角落新装的锅炉，把整套陈设都衬小了（dwarf，dwarf 指以高大立于其侧而使之显小、使之失了比例）——奥斯伯特也在内，于是他那副骨架，夹在锅炉与窗户之间，看上去不像学校最引以为豪的珍藏，倒像一位瘦绅士在谦逊地等公交。

quiz.q: Dr. Chubb's will left the school his skeleton — the frame of bones on which the rest of us is carried. A skeleton is —
o: the organ that makes and pours out
the hinged bone of the mouth
the frame of bones that carries us
quiz.ex: skeleton = 骨骼；骨架。a skeleton in the cupboard 家丑；skeleton staff 基干人员。

quiz.q: The chambers of the heart were demonstrated on the model that worked — a room, a compartment; in anatomy, one of the heart's four receiving rooms. A chamber is —
o: a curved bone fencing the chest
the folded tube of the belly
the column that carries the head
quiz.ex: chamber = 房间；腔。the four chambers of the heart 心脏四腔；chamber of commerce 商会。

quiz.q: The abdomen was opened with the dignity of a county occasion — the cavity of the body below the chest, the belly. The abdomen is —
o: the arch of hair above the eye
the box of the heart and lungs
the organ of thought and government
quiz.ex: abdomen = 腹部。pain in the abdomen 腹痛；abdominal adj. 腹部的。

quiz.q: The glands were explained as the body's taps — an organ that makes and pours out a substance of its own, as the tears and sweat are poured. A gland is —
o: the great chemical works of the belly
one of the two organs of breath
the painted red that pulls on bone
quiz.ex: gland = 腺。sweat glands 汗腺；the glands swell 腺体肿大。

quiz.q: The womb was drawn for the girls on the blackboard — the organ in which the child is carried before birth. The womb is —
o: the organ that carries the unborn child
the cavity of the belly entire
one of the body's receiving rooms
quiz.ex: womb = 子宫。in the womb 在子宫内；同义词 uterus。

quiz.q: They asked what a man's stature had to do with his temper — the height of a standing person; and by extension, the height of a reputation. Stature is —
quiz.ex: stature = 身高；声望。a man of short stature 身材矮小的人；a writer of towering stature 巨匠。

quiz.q: Whether the boys standing beside the frame resembled him or he them — to be like, to bear the likeness of. To resemble is to —
o: be of the same sort only
put a thing out of scale
quiz.ex: resemble = 像；类似于。She resembles her mother. 她长得像母亲。

quiz.q: The backbone stood so straight the committee pronounced him the most upright figure of the decade — the spine's stack of bones; and beyond anatomy, the seat of resolution. A backbone is —
o: the flesh that pulls on bone
the bony box that houses the brain
the spine; and the seat of resolve
the column that carries the head
quiz.ex: backbone = 脊柱；骨气。show some backbone 拿出点骨气；the backbone of the team 队伍的中坚。

title: The Winter of the Flu
text:
The {{flu}} — the flu being influenza; the winter sickness that travels as readily by bus as by breath — came up the valley in the third week of January, on the school bus, which had collected it at Lampford along with the groceries. The first cases were the Tregose boys, who reported it as an excuse for arithmetic and were believed for a day and a half; by Friday their mother had it, the bus driver had it, and what the valley had called a cold since October was revealed, by the doctor's thermometer, to be an {{illness}} — an illness being a state of being unwell; a sickness's residence in a person — of the {{disease}} — a disease being a sickness with a cause and a course of its own, that travels — kind that keeps its own calendar. It was, the doctor said, the {{common}} — common meaning general, of the shared lot; ordinary — lot of every valley that winter, which consoled the valley not at all, its opinions on originality being settled.

The second week took the mill, the third the school; by February half the valley was flat. The {{fever}} — a fever being the body's fire, raised to burn out what ails it — ran two days and broke at dawn, punctual as the milking; the {{headache}} — a headache being a pain in the head, of the kind that makes the skull its house — was the universal report, and the only thing the whole valley ever agreed upon in February; the {{sore}} — sore meaning tender, hurting to the touch or to the use — throat made speech a tax and gossip an economy; the strong were {{dizzy}} — dizzy meaning feeling the world turn, as after a long spin — on the stairs and {{faint}} — to faint meaning to fall into brief unconsciousness, the blood leaving the head — in the passages; and the {{pain}} — pain being the body's alarm, rung at the site of the harm — in the back and the limbs was described by the Mercury, which had it twice, as "a thoroughness".

The doctor met it with the regulations he had brought from the county hospital, and the valley met the regulations as it meets all written things, with respect and exceptions. Every infected house had its card in the window — the {{precaution}} — a precaution being a measure taken beforehand, against a harm that may come — of the cross of chalk, which the grocer honoured by leaving the bread on the step and the children honoured by nothing at all; the {{quarantine}} — quarantine meaning the keeping apart of the exposed, for the term of the disease's showing — of the school ran three weeks and would have run a fourth had the school not burned through its supply of patience before its supply of chalk; the {{isolate}}d — to isolate meaning to set apart, to cut off from the company of others — were visited through windows, a courting custom the valley found it had missed; the {{hygiene}} — hygiene meaning the art of health; the cleanliness that keeps disease from its openings — lectures at the well were attended by every woman in the valley and no man, on the grounds that the men were too ill; and the {{sanitary}} — sanitary meaning of health; clean, as drains and habits are clean — arrangements at the chapel, which became the hospital for the worst, were inspected by the doctor twice a day and by everybody else once, from the gate.

The chapel held eleven beds and the valley's whole stock of fortitude. The {{suffering}} — suffering meaning the bearing of pain or loss — was borne, on the whole, in the valley's usual dialect of understatement; the {{severe}} — severe meaning grave, of a heavy hand; harsh in degree — cases were the old, as the doctor had warned and the valley had overruled; the {{seriously}} — seriously meaning in earnest; in gravest degree — ill were turned twice an hour through the night by a rota that filled itself; the {{agony}} — agony being pain at its uttermost, the struggle of it — of the worst nights was met with what the doctor had and what the chapel had, which between them proved enough; the {{distress}} — distress being the strain of mind or body under hardship — of the families was eased by the Mercury's daily list of the improving, read aloud at the gate like shipping news; and the ward's whole population learned to {{moan}} — to moan meaning to give voice, low and continuous, to pain — in the same key, which the doctor said was not in any textbook and the vicar said was the closest thing to plainsong the valley had ever managed.

The cost fell where the doctor had said it would, and first of all on the doctor. His {{overwork}} — overwork meaning labour beyond the strength — was the talk of the parish: ninety calls in the worst week, the snow-plough requisitioned twice, the cello unheard from Christmas to Lent; his {{fatigue}} — fatigue being tiredness become a state, the strength's own winter — showed only in his handwriting, which sank by degrees into Dr. Chubb's; the {{exhaust}}ion — to exhaust meaning to draw the strength out wholly, as a well is drawn — was complete by March, and he slept one entire Sunday in the vestry, waking to find the congregation had tiptoed round him and left, in the collection, eggs; and the valley, watching him {{tire}} — to tire meaning to grow tired; to have the strength spent — and {{weaken}} — to weaken meaning to grow weak, to lose strength — on its behalf, felt the strange pride of a village that has worn out its own defender and fed him on rabbits.

The ice of February brought the other trade, and the surgery filled with it. The {{wound}}s — a wound being a break in the flesh, by cut or by tear — of the slide at Holt pond were sewn on the kitchen table by lamplight; the {{injury|injuries}} — an injury being harm done to the body, of the kind the law also counts — ran to a page of the minute book; the {{bleed}}ing — to bleed meaning to lose blood — lip of the youngest Bevan took four stitches and grew him a moustache of thread; the {{bruise}}s — a bruise being a hurt beneath unbroken skin, where blood has gathered — came up in rainbow order and were compared like medals; the {{swell}}ed — to swell meaning to grow large, as injured flesh does — ankles filled their boots and were photographed for the school's nature table; a {{lump}} — a lump being a swelling, a raised bit of flesh — rose on every third head and was named; the {{choke}}d — to choke meaning to stop the breath of, by throat or by water — boy of the second dive was revived by the fire brigade's training and the third dive of the fire brigade; the {{broken}} — broken meaning snapped, of bone — collarbones arrived two a week and left in slings; and the {{rash}} — a rash being an outbreak on the skin, of spots or of redness — that followed one batch of the medicine was the subject of the doctor's only published paper, which the Mercury ran whole, above a headline about the valley's own contribution to science.

By April it was over, and the valley audited it as it audits everything. The {{scar}}s — a scar being the mark a healed wound leaves, in skin and in memory — were the only records kept where the valley could see them; the chapel was scrubbed, returned to the choir, and found to have better acoustics than before, a mercy nobody pursued; the convalescents, let out on the first warm day, {{gorge}}d — to gorge meaning to eat greedily, to fill the throat past hunger — on the spring's first strawberries at the Stores and paid for it in the way of convalescents; the {{ease}}d — to ease meaning to loosen, to make less tight or less hard — restrictions went the way of all restrictions, remembered as tyranny at the time and as wisdom afterward; the school {{resume}}d — to resume meaning to take up again what was laid down — with a holiday granted for the mathematics of the mortality, which came to none, the valley having decided in committee that a winter with no funerals and one wedding owed more to luck than the books could carry; and the last of the {{heal}}ed — to heal meaning to grow whole, as flesh closes and strength returns—, which was the doctor himself, was stood a drink at the Bull that he was too wise to finish, and a toast that he was too honest to accept: "To the man who caught it last."
tr:
流感（flu，flu 指流行性感冒、随季节更迭而来的时疫）是二月的第三个星期随校车进河谷的——车在兰普福德捎上了杂货，也捎上了它。头一拨病人是特雷戈斯家的兄弟俩，报病时只当是逃避算术的借口，被信了一天半；到星期五，他们的母亲倒了，校车司机倒了，而从十月起就被河谷叫作“着凉”的东西，经医生的体温表一验，原来是一场病（illness，illness 指不适的状态、疾病在某人身上的驻留），属于会自己排日程、还会旅行的那种疫病（disease，disease 指自有病因与病程、能传染的疾病）。医生说，那年冬天这是每个河谷共有的（common，common 指普遍的、人人有份的、寻常的）份——这话一点没让河谷宽心，它对自己“不落俗套”的看法早已定型。
