第二个星期攻下磨坊，第三个星期攻下学校；到二月，半个河谷都躺平了。发烧（fever，fever 指身体为烧尽病邪而升起的火）一烧两天，黎明准时退去，准得像挤奶；头痛（headache，headache 指头上之痛、以颅骨为宅的那种）是全民共报的症状，也是二月里全谷唯一达成一致的事项；嗓子发疼（sore，sore 指一碰一用就疼的、酸痛的）让说话成了纳税，八卦成了节约用粮；壮实的在楼梯上发晕（dizzy，dizzy 指天旋地转之感，如久转之后），在过道里晕倒（faint，faint 指一时昏厥、血离开头顶而人倒下）；背上的、四肢的疼痛（pain，pain 指身体在受伤处敲响的警钟），《信使报》——它自己也病了两回——形容为“无微不至”。

医生以他从县医院带来的条例迎战，河谷以它对待一切成文之物的方式迎战条例：心怀敬意，各留后门。每家有病人的窗户上贴了卡片——那是一项预防（precaution，precaution 指事先采取的措施、以备可能之害）：一个粉笔记号，杂货商敬重它，面包留在台阶上；孩子们对它毫无敬意。学校的隔离（quarantine，quarantine 指将接触者隔开、以病之显现期为限）执行了三个星期，若不是学校耐心的储备先于粉笔耗尽，本可执行第四个星期；被隔离（isolate，isolate 指另行安置、切断与他人的往来）的人隔窗探视——这门旧式的谈情手艺，河谷发现自己竟还怪想念的；水井边的卫生（hygiene，hygiene 指保健之术、把疾病挡在入口处的清洁之道）讲座，全谷的女人都到了，一个男人也没到，理由是男人们病得太重；充当重症病房的小教堂，其卫生（sanitary，sanitary 指关乎健康的、如排水与习惯之洁净）设施由医生一天查验两次，其余人等在门口各望一眼。

小教堂摆了十一张床，和河谷全部的坚忍。苦难（suffering，suffering 指对痛苦或损失的承受）总体上是以河谷惯用的轻描淡写方言承受的；重症（severe，severe 指沉重的、来势凶的、程度严酷的）都是老人，正如医生警告过、而河谷否决过的那样；病危（seriously，seriously 指当真地、以最重的程度）者夜里每两小时翻一次身，值班表自己填满了自己；最重的夜里那种苦痛（agony，agony 指痛到极处、痛的挣扎）靠医生所有的和教堂所有的合力对付，结果证明够了；家属的悲苦（distress，distress 指身心在困厄之下的紧绷）由《信使报》每日的好转名单抚平——名单在大门口宣读，如同宣读航讯；而全病房的人学会了一个调门的呻吟（moan，moan 指低而不断地出声诉痛），医生说任何教科书里都没有这一条，牧师则说这是河谷有史以来最接近素歌的成就。

代价落在医生预告的地方，首先落在医生身上。他的操劳过度（overwork，overwork 指超出体力的劳作）成了本教区的谈资：最重的一周出诊九十次，铲雪车征用两回，大提琴从圣诞沉默到大斋期；他的疲乏（fatigue，fatigue 指疲倦成了常态、力气自己的冬天）只显在笔迹上——那笔迹一步步沉下去，沉成了丘布医生的字；到三月他衰竭（exhaust，exhaust 指把力气抽干、如井水被抽尽）已尽，在法衣室睡了整整一个星期天，醒来发现会众踮着脚绕他而行，奉献盘里留下的是鸡蛋；河谷看着自己这位守护人为它劳乏（tire，tire 指渐生倦意、力气耗去）、衰弱（weaken，weaken 指变弱、失去力气），心中涌起一种奇特的骄傲——一座把自己的卫士累垮、又拿兔子把他喂起来的村庄。

二月的冰送来了另一路生意，诊所里摆满了它。霍尔特池塘滑冰场的伤口（wound，wound 指皮肉的破口，由割或撕而来）在厨房餐桌上就着灯光缝合；伤情（injury，injury 指对身体造成的损害、也是法律要计数的那类损害）记满了会议簿一整页；最小的贝万那张流血（bleed，bleed 指失血）的嘴唇缝了四针，给他下巴养出了一圈线的髭；淤伤（bruise，bruise 指皮未破而血已聚于其下的伤）按彩虹的次序发出来，被当勋章攀比；肿起（swell，swell 指胀大、如受伤的皮肉那样）的脚踝塞满了靴子，还上了学校自然课的展台；每三颗脑袋上鼓起一个肿块（lump，lump 指鼓包、皮肉上隆起的一块），且各有其名；第二次跳水那个呛水（choke，choke 指堵住呼吸，或因喉咙或因水）的孩子由消防队的训练救活——消防队则由第三次跳水救活；骨折（broken，broken 指断了的、骨头的）锁骨每周两副地来，吊着绷带走；一批药跟出来的皮疹（rash，rash 指皮肤上斑点或发红的一阵爆发）成了医生唯一发表的论文，《信使报》全文刊出，标题说这是河谷对科学的自有贡献。

到四月，一切结束了，河谷照例逐项盘点。伤疤（scar，scar 指愈合的伤口留在皮上和记忆里的记号）是唯一摆在明处的档案；小教堂擦洗一新、还给唱诗班，音响效果反比从前更好——这份恩典没人细究；将养的人放出来头一个暖天，就在杂货铺对着春天的头茬草莓大快朵颐（gorge，gorge 指贪吃、把喉咙填到超过饥饿），随即以将养者的方式付了账；松开的（ease，ease 指放松、把紧的和难的变松）种种限制照一切限制的下场收场——当时记得是暴政，事后记得是明智；学校复课（resume，resume 指把放下的重新拾起），还因“死亡率数学”放了一天假——算下来一个也没死，河谷在会上认定：一个没有葬礼只有一场婚礼的冬天，欠下的与其说是账本，不如说是运气；最后痊愈（heal，heal 指长好、如皮肉合拢气力回头）的那位——医生本人——在公牛客栈被敬了一杯他聪明得不喝干的酒，和一句他诚实得不受用的祝词：“敬那个最后病倒的人。”

quiz.q: The fever ran two days and broke at dawn, punctual as the milking — the body's fire, raised to burn out what ails it. A fever is —
o: the body's alarm at the site of harm
a break in the flesh by cut
quiz.ex: fever = 发烧；热度。run a fever 发烧；feverish adj. 发热的。

quiz.q: The quarantine of the school ran three weeks — the keeping apart of the exposed, for the term of the disease's showing. Quarantine is —
o: the daily list of the improving
the keeping apart of the exposed
quiz.ex: quarantine = 隔离；检疫。be put in quarantine 被隔离；quarantine period 隔离期。

quiz.q: The hygiene lectures at the well were attended by every woman and no man — the art of health; the cleanliness that keeps disease from its openings. Hygiene is —
o: the art of health and cleanliness
the chalk cross on the door
quiz.ex: hygiene = 卫生。personal hygiene 个人卫生；dental hygiene 口腔卫生。

quiz.q: The agony of the worst nights was met with what the doctor had and the chapel had — pain at its uttermost, the struggle of it. Agony is —
o: a pain in the head, its house
the strain of mind under hardship
the bearing of loss in dialect
quiz.ex: agony = 极度痛苦。in agony 极度痛苦之中；agonizing adj. 折磨人的。

quiz.q: The bruises came up in rainbow order and were compared like medals — a hurt beneath unbroken skin, where blood has gathered. A bruise is —
o: an outbreak of spots or redness
a break in the flesh by tear
a swelling raised on the head
quiz.ex: bruise = 淤伤；青肿。bruise easily 容易淤青；bruised adj. 青肿的。

quiz.q: The wounds of the slide at Holt pond were sewn on the kitchen table — a break in the flesh, by cut or by tear. A wound is —
quiz.ex: wound = 伤口；创伤。dress a wound 包扎伤口；wounded adj. 受伤的。

quiz.q: The choked boy of the second dive was revived by the fire brigade's training — to stop the breath of, by throat or by water. To choke is to —
quiz.ex: choke = 使窒息；呛。choke on a fishbone 被鱼刺卡住；choking adj. 令人窒息的。

quiz.q: His exhaustion was complete by March, and he slept one entire Sunday in the vestry — to draw the strength out wholly, as a well is drawn. To exhaust is to —
quiz.ex: exhaust = 使耗尽；使精疲力竭。exhaust one's patience 耗尽耐心；exhausted adj. 筋疲力尽的。

title: The Long Leave-taking
text:
Mrs. Hancock was a hundred and one, and had been dying, the valley agreed, for thirty years, with the same unhurried thoroughness she brought to jam-making. She had outlived a husband, two wars, three doctors and the habit of dying; she was the last of the valley's Victorians, and she kept its opinions the way the museum keeps its clocks, wound and running whether or not anyone came to see. The doctor called Tuesdays. She received him upright in the chair by the fire, {{feeble}} — feeble meaning weak, lacking strength — as a wren and about as impressible, and gave him her symptoms with the detachment of a woman reading a shipping list; she had been an {{invalid}} — an invalid being one laid aside by broken health; a person whose sickness has moved in for good — since the year of the coronation of the elder George, she said, and had never once let it get above the ankle of her.

The winter thinned her. The {{mortal}} — mortal meaning subject to death, as all of us are; and, of the body, ending in it — arithmetic was plain to the doctor and to her, and the two of them, being professionals, discussed it over the fire like weather; her {{fate}} — fate meaning the course of a life as it is appointed; what falls to one — she called "the last appointment I shall be early for"; the {{fatal}} — fatal meaning dealing death or meeting it; of issues, deadly — delicacy of the heart was, in her account, "the family clock, running down punctually, and no shame to the maker"; and when the doctor spoke of the hospital she declined it in a sentence the valley has since carved into its own memory: "I have made every arrangement with this valley that a body can make, and I mean to keep the last one at home." She was not {{wretched}} — wretched meaning miserable, in a pitiable state — about any of it, and would not {{endure}} — to endure meaning to bear, to last through, as she had lasted through two wars — a syllable of pity, which she classed with gossip as a waste of breath.

She declined, through February, the way the light declines through an afternoon: by being, each time you looked, a little less there, and still entirely herself. The {{doom}} — doom meaning the end appointed; the fate that cannot be put off — she had expected all her life did not frighten her, she said, having read its file; she had seen {{mankind}} — mankind meaning the human race entire, taken as one body — through worse and would see it, she trusted, out of this too; and she took to receiving, in the last weeks, the whole valley in the order of its nerves, a {{sound}} — sound meaning whole and healthy, as judgment and timber are sound — mind arranging her last effects while the others were still arranging their faces.

{{death|Death}} — death being the end of life; the closing of the account — came for her on the ninth of March, between the snowdrop and the crocus, as if choosing flowers, and with the {{mercy}} — mercy meaning compassion shown to the suffering; the clemency that spares — of the painless kind the doctor had promised and she had priced in advance. The {{demise}} — demise meaning a death; and in the law's language, the passing of an estate from its holder — was announced at church by the vicar, who managed the sentence and then lost the room; the flags, of which the valley owned two, went to half; and the Mercury came out bordered in black for the first time since the war.

The valley did its mourning in the old grammar. It {{grieve}}d — to grieve meaning to feel the loss as pain; to mourn within — sincerely and in private; the {{grief}} — grief being sorrow's full weight, the pain of a loss that stays — came out at the funeral in the front pews and in the coffin's six bearers, four of them her tenants and two her scholars; it {{mourn}}ed — to mourn meaning to sorrow outwardly, in the shapes the customs give — with shutters and hush and the bells at half-muffle; it {{lament}}ed — to lament meaning to mourn aloud, in words or in song — chiefly in the public house, where her sayings were repeated until they wore smooth as coins; and the youngest of the valley, to whom a hundred and one was a country they would never visit, {{weep|wept}} — to weep meaning to let grief out in tears — for the first of their dead who had been a person rather than a relation, which is the death that teaches the rest.

Her life was read out entire, and read out well. She had been {{born}} — born being brought into life, of a mother — in the cottage above the ford in the first year of the last century's second quarter; she was the {{first}} — first meaning before all others in time or order — girl in the valley to sit the scholarship, the {{first}} to drive a car into it (a Singer, at eleven miles an hour, preceded by a boy with a flag), and the last to remember the flood of the 'eighties; her {{regret}}s — regret being the sorrow of wishing undone; the ache of the thing not done — were itemised in her own hand and proved, the valley was pained to learn, to number three, none of them crimes; and her will, which distributed the estate in the proportions of a poem, left the interest of the greater part to the district nurse, on a condition the lawyers called unusual and the valley called her all over: that it be spent, in her words, "on the people I have outlived, who have need of it longer than I shall." The churchyard took her on the south side, in the plot she had chosen for the view; and the vicar, who had lost the room once already, kept it this time, and gave her the one line of hers she had left for the stone: "I was the {{first}} to arrive in this valley of any of you, and I am not, you will find, the last to leave."
tr:
汉考克太太一百零一岁，而照河谷的说法，她已经垂危三十年了——那份从容不迫的彻底劲儿，跟她做果酱时一模一样。她送走了丈夫、两场战争、三位医生，以及“垂危”这个习惯本身；她是河谷最后一位维多利亚时代的人，那些见解她保存得像博物馆保存钟表——上着弦，走着，不管有没有人来看。医生每逢星期二上门。她直挺挺坐在炉边的椅子上接见他，虚弱（feeble，feeble 指弱的、缺乏力气的）得像一只鹪鹩，也像鹪鹩一样不肯示弱，报起自己的症状来，带着一位女士念航讯清单的冷静；她说自己自老乔治加冕那年起就是个病人（invalid，invalid 指健康已垮、被病挪到一旁的人，是病已长住不走的那种），而从未有一次让它漫过自己的脚踝。

冬天削薄了她。凡人皆有死（mortal，mortal 指终有一死的、血肉之躯终将终结的）这道算术，医生明白，她也明白，两个专业人士隔着炉火讨论它，如讨论天气。她管自己的命数（fate，fate 指被指定的那条人生轨迹、落在头上的那份）叫“我此生唯一会提前赴的约”；她心脏那处致命（fatal，fatal 指致死的、结局是死亡的）的旧患，在她嘴里是“家里的钟，走得规规矩矩地停摆，不丢制钟人的脸”；医生提到医院，她一句话回绝了，这句话河谷后来刻进了自己的记忆：“我能跟这个河谷办妥的 arrangement 都办妥了，最后这一桩，我要在家里履约。”这一切她没有一处可怜兮兮（wretched，wretched 指凄惨的、境况堪怜的），也不肯承受（endure，endure 指经受、撑过，如她撑过两场战争那样）一句怜悯——怜悯在她的分类里和闲话同档，都是浪费气息。

她在二月里衰退下去，像午后的天光那样：每次看去，都少了一点，却仍然完完全全是她自己。她等了一辈子的那个大限（doom，doom 指被指定的结局、推不掉的那个命），她说吓不着她——案卷她都读过了；她见过人类（mankind，mankind 指人类的整体、合为一族的人）挺过更坏的，也信得过会看着它挺过这一回；最后几个星期，她开始按各人神经的承受力依次接待全谷，那颗健全（sound，sound 指完好的、如判断或木料之无伤）的头脑从容料理着最后的身后事，而其余人还在料理自己的脸色。

死亡（death，death 指生命的终结、账目的收结）在三月九日来接她，赶在雪花莲与番红花之间，仿佛专挑着花来；带着医生许诺过、她也预先谈好了价的那种免于疼痛的仁慈（mercy，mercy 指对受苦者的怜恤、予以宽免的慈悲）。讣闻（demise，demise 指亡故；法律用语指产业的移转）由牧师在教堂宣布，句子他说完了，教室却失控了；全谷仅有的两面旗降了半旗；《信使报》自战争以来第一次出了黑框版。

河谷用旧的文法守丧。全谷由衷地、私下地哀恸（grieve，grieve 指把失去当作疼痛来感受、在心里服丧）；悲恸（grief，grief 指哀伤的全重、留下不走的那份失亲之痛）在葬礼上显在前排座席里、显在抬棺的六个人身上——其中四位是她的佃户，两位是她的学生；全谷戴孝志哀（mourn，mourn 指以外在的形式致哀、循旧俗之形），关窗，息声，钟裹了半消音的皮；哀唱（lament，lament 指出声地悲悼，以言辞或以歌）主要在酒馆进行，她的名言在那里被反复念诵，念得像硬币一样磨得溜光；而谷中最小的孩子们——对他们来说，一百零一岁是一个永远不会去旅行的国度——为他们的死者里头一位“是人而不仅是亲戚”的哭了（weep，weep 指让哀伤化作眼泪流出来），教人认识死亡的就是这一场。

她的一生被完整宣读，而且读得好。她出生（born，born 指由母亲生下、来到人世）在上个世纪第二季度的头一年，浅滩上方那座小屋里；她是全谷第一个（first，first 指在时间或次序上先于一切）考得奖学金的女孩，第一个把汽车开进河谷的人（一辆辛格牌，时速十一英里，前头有个男孩举旗开道），也是最后一个记得八十年代大洪水的人；她的遗憾（regret，regret 指但愿未曾如此的哀伤、未做之事之痛）由她亲笔逐条列出，河谷痛心地得知，一共三条，没有一条算得上罪。她的遗嘱以一首诗的比例分配产业，大头的利息给了地区护士，条件是律师们称为罕见、河谷称为“整个她”的那一条：照她的话说，“花在我送走的人身上——他们需要它的日子，比我长。”墓园把她安置在南侧，那一角是她自己选的，为了景色；牧师已经失控过一回，这次稳住了，把她留给石碑的那句话给了她：“在你们各位当中，我是第一个到这河谷来的——而你们会发现，我不是最后一个离开的。”

quiz.q: She received him upright in the chair, feeble as a wren and about as impressible — weak, lacking strength. Feeble means —
o: subject to death as all are
quiz.ex: feeble = 虚弱的；微弱的。a feeble old man 虚弱的老人；a feeble excuse 站不住脚的借口。

quiz.q: She had been an invalid since the year of the elder George's coronation — one laid aside by broken health; a person whose sickness has moved in for good. An invalid is —
o: a wound that will not close
quiz.ex: invalid = 病人；久病衰弱者。wait on an invalid 服侍病人；注意重音在第一音节。

quiz.q: The mortal arithmetic was plain to the doctor and to her — subject to death, as all of us are. Mortal means —
quiz.ex: mortal = 终有一死的；致命的。mortal beings 凡人；mortal danger 致命危险。

quiz.q: Her demise was announced at church by the vicar — a death; and in the law's language, the passing of an estate. Demise is —
o: a death, and a passing of estate
quiz.ex: demise = 逝世；（财产的）转让。upon his demise 在他去世后；demise and transfer 移交。

quiz.q: Death came with the mercy of the painless kind the doctor had promised — compassion shown to the suffering; the clemency that spares. Mercy is —
o: the ache of the thing not done
quiz.ex: mercy = 仁慈；宽恕。show mercy to the defeated 对败者施以仁慈；at the mercy of 任由……摆布。

quiz.q: The grief came out at the funeral in the front pews and in the six bearers — sorrow's full weight, the pain of a loss that stays. Grief is —
o: a saying worn smooth as coins
quiz.ex: grief = 悲痛。come to grief 遭难；be overcome with grief 悲痛欲绝。

quiz.q: The valley lamented chiefly in the public house, where her sayings were repeated like coins — to mourn aloud, in words or in song. To lament is to —
o: mourn aloud in words or song
quiz.ex: lament = 哀悼；悲叹。lament the loss of a friend 哀悼亡友；lamentation n. 悲叹。

quiz.q: The doom she had expected all her life did not frighten her, having read its file — the end appointed; the fate that cannot be put off. Doom is —
o: the south side of the churchyard
quiz.ex: doom = 厄运；末日。meet one's doom 遭遇厄运；doomed adj. 注定失败的。

title: The Blacksmith's Temper
text:
Harry Curnow, the blacksmith, has the most famous {{temper}} — temper meaning the state of the mind with regard to passion; and in daily use, the short and quick kind of it — in three parishes; not the worst, the valley is careful to explain to strangers, but the famousest, which is a different ranking and a higher one. His father had it before him, and his grandfather before that, the forge having passed the {{mood}} — a mood being the mind's weather of the hour, its barometer and its sky — down the family like the anvil. The valley has organized itself around the fact for forty years: errands to the forge are run in the morning, dogs are excused themselves, the Mercury's chess correspondent does not mention the kingside, and the church clock keeps a wary two minutes, Curnow having once, in the old days, {{frown}}ed — to frown meaning to draw the brows together, the face's own weather-glass — at it across the square for a fortnight and reduced the congregation by nerves alone.

The rages themselves were rare, brief and architectural, and the valley can give you the catalogue. There was the {{anger}} — anger being the heat of the mind against a hindrance or a wrong — of the axle week, when three rims came back from Lampford gas-cut and Curnow could be heard explaining the properties of iron to the whole of Fore Street; there was the full {{rage}} — rage being anger at flood, the mind's storm entire — of the show day, over the man who let the yearling loose in the road, which is still dated from ("the year of the yearling") and which the yearling survived; and there was the {{furious}} — furious meaning full of rage, as a sea in a gale — week of the beer money, when the wages came short and the paymaster learned what the valley had paid school fees to learn, that Curnow's {{mad}} — mad meaning angry, in the valley's use of it; and beyond that use, of unsound mind — is never about the money and always about the principle, the sum being merely where the principle keeps its boots.

The occasions were as regular as the causes. Bad iron {{irritate}}d — to irritate meaning to provoke, to rub the temper raw, as a boot rubs a heel — him; wasted coal {{vex}}ed — to vex meaning to anger, to trouble the peace of — him; the boy who left the tongs in the water, the apprentice who mended a gate by paint, the customer who {{bother}}ed — to bother meaning to trouble, to take up a man's time with a small matter urged as a large one — him with a watch strap in July: these were the fuels of the ordinary weather. What brought the storms was different every time, and the same every time: carelessness where another body's safety stood on the work — the cracked trace, the soft link, the weld on the braking bar — and against that his {{excessive}} — excessive meaning beyond measure, past the due and decent amount — standards were, the valley has decided, the correct ones, being exactly as long as a horse's life and a car's load; and the man who took a liberty with either received from Curnow a {{vicious}} — vicious meaning savage; given to ill will, and of a blow, of the kind that does not warn — sentence of an {{insult}} — an insult being a rudeness that wounds, an offence given to the face — in the old language of the trade, of which the Mercury has printed, in sixty years, eleven words, and those by accident.

The doctor's view of the temper was the county's mildest scandal. An {{emotion}} — an emotion being a movement of the mind; feeling that moves, and moves us — was, he told the Women's Institute, neither a sin nor a weather, but an instrument, to be kept in tune and not in a drawer; the {{impulse}} — an impulse being a spring of the mind, acting before counsel arrives — that made a man snatch his hand from the fire was the same spring that made him snatch a child from the road; the {{unstable}} — unstable meaning unsteady, apt to shift without notice — patient of the valley's gossip was, in his account, simply tuned sharp, an instrument that sounded at a touch others needed a blow for; the {{volatile}} — volatile meaning light and quick to fly off, as the spirits in the bottle are — temperament was the temper of all craftsmen written large, the rage being the forge's own weather moving indoors; and the question of whether Curnow was {{mental}}ly — mental meaning of the mind, its faculties and its health — sound was settled by the doctor with a question of his own, namely whether the valley preferred its iron worked by a man whose {{mind}} — the mind being that which thinks, wills and feels; the seat of a man's government — was on the job or at lunch: {{sane}} — sane meaning of sound mind, whole in the judging part — being, in the doctor's book, mostly a matter of what a man is sane about. The valley, which had called the {{insane}} — insane meaning of unsound mind, mad — work of an afternoon "Harry being Harry" for forty years, adopted the doctor's paragraph at the Institute with a vote of thanks and no alteration of practice whatsoever.

The great storm of the new century came over the tractor, and the valley dates that one too. The museum people came down from the county to buy the old forge's hand-made stock, and spoke, over Curnow's own tea, of the pieces as "quirky" and of the trade itself as "a {{crazy}} — crazy meaning wild, beside itself, of a piece with madness — survival"; and Curnow, who had buried the trade with his own hands and did not propose to have it insulted over its own grave, grew {{indignant}} — indignant meaning angry at a wrong, anger with its dignity on — by degrees, like a tide, and delivered the address of his life on the difference between a craft that died of the world's laziness and one that died of its own, with the {{disgust}} — disgust being the mind's rejection of a thing, the turning of the whole body from it — of a man showing visitors the door by pure prose. The {{unpleasant}} — unpleasant meaning not pleasing, disagreeable to be near — half-hour that followed was the talk of the winter; the visitors left {{uncomfortable}} — uncomfortable meaning ill at ease, at odds with one's chair — and wrote the piece anyway; and the Mercury, which had sent a reporter expecting to be {{liable}} — liable meaning likely, subject to a thing; apt — for once in its history to a scene, printed her copy entire with the observation that the temper, like the trade, was the last of its line and both were the county's loss.

He retired at seventy-three, anvil and all, the last of the forges in the valley closing on the same afternoon; and the valley discovered, in the quiet that followed, that it missed the weather. Errands to his cottage are run in the morning still, out of respect rather than information; the church clock keeps its wary two minutes; and the young farrier who comes out from Lampford on Thursdays, having heard the legends and being {{bother}}ed by none of them, asked Curnow, at their first meeting, what the temper had actually been for. "For the iron," said Curnow. "Everything else managed itself."
tr:
铁匠哈里·科诺拥有三个教区里最有名的脾气（temper，temper 指心之于激情的状态；日常用法指短而急的那种）——不是最坏的，河谷向生人解释时很谨慎，而是最有名的：那是另一个名次，还是更高的一个。他父亲传给他，祖父传给他父亲，这间铁匠铺把心情（mood，mood 指心在一小时里的天气、它的晴雨表与天空）连同铁砧一起世代相传。四十年来，全村围绕这一事实安排自己：去铁匠铺的差事都在上午办，狗被允许自行回避，《信使报》的国际象棋专栏不提王翼，教堂的钟也谨慎地慢两分钟——因为早年间科诺曾对着广场上的它皱眉（frown，frown 指双眉拢起、脸自带的晴雨表）两个星期，仅凭 nerves 就让会众减了员。

发作本身罕见、短促、且结构严谨，全村能给你开列清单。有车轴那一周的怒（anger，anger 指心对阻碍或委屈而生的热），三只轮圈从兰普福德气割回来，科诺向整条前街讲解铁的性质，人人听得见；有展览日那场全怒（rage，rage 指怒到洪峰、心里的整场风暴），为的是那个把一岁马驹放到大路上的人——这一场至今被当作纪年（“马驹那一年”），马驹也活了下来；还有啤酒钱那狂怒（furious，furious 指盛怒的，如大风浪里的海）的一星期，工资发短了，出纳员于是领教了全村早交过学费的那一课：科诺的火（mad，mad 在河谷的用法里指生气的；再往外指精神失常的）从来不为钱，永远为道理——钱只是道理放靴子的地方。

发作的时机与起因一样规律。坏铁磨他（irritate，irritate 指激惹、把脾气蹭破皮，如靴子磨脚跟）；浪费的煤恼他（vex，vex 指使恼怒、搅扰心神之安宁）；把火钳留在水里的学徒、靠刷漆修门的伙计、七月里拿一根表带缠他（bother，bother 指打搅、拿小事当大事占人时间）的顾客——这些都是寻常天气的燃料。而招来风暴的，每次不同，每次相同：在别人的安全担在活计上的地方马虎——裂开的辕、软的链环、刹车杆上的焊口——对此，他的超标准的（excessive，excessive 指超出分量的、过了应有限度的）标准，全村公认是对的，那长度正好是一匹马的命、一辆车的载重；在这两样上头随便的人，会从科诺嘴里领到一句狠的（vicious，vicious 指凶狠的、怀恶意的，指一下不先打招呼的那种打击）斥骂（insult，insult 指伤人的粗鲁、当面给的冒犯），用的是这行当的老话——《信使报》六十年里登过其中十一个词，还都是失手。

医生对这脾气的看法，是全县最温和的一桩公案。情绪（emotion，emotion 指心的一个动作、会推动人的感受），他告诉妇女协会，既不是罪也不是天气，而是一件器械——要保养在调上，而不是收进抽屉；使人把手从火上抽回的那股冲动（impulse，impulse 指心里的弹簧、在理智赶到之前先行动的那种），与使人把孩子从大路上拽开的，是同一根弹簧；村里闲话里那个反复无常的（unstable，unstable 指不稳的、说变就变的）病人，照他的说法只是调得尖些——别人要一记重击才响的，他一碰就响；那火性的（volatile，volatile 指轻扬易挥发的，如瓶中之酒气）性子，是一切匠人的脾气放大了写——风暴本是铁匠铺的天气搬进了屋；至于科诺精神（mental，mental 指心的、心智及其健康的）上健全不健全，医生用他自己的一个问题结了案：全村是愿意铁出自一个心神（mind，mind 指思想、意愿与感受之所在、一个人统辖的中枢）在活计上的匠人之手，还是出自一个想着午饭的？健全（sane，sane 指心智健全、判断的部分完好无损），照医生的账本，多半看一个人对什么事健全。全村把一下午的“发疯”（insane，insane 指精神失常的、疯的）活计称作“哈里就是哈里”叫了四十年，此刻在协会以鼓掌通过采纳了医生那一段——实践上未作分毫更改。

新纪元的大风暴是为了拖拉机，全村对那一场也用了纪年。县博物馆的人下来收购老铁匠铺的手工库存，就着科诺自家的茶，把那些物件说成“怪趣”，把这门手艺本身说成“一个疯癫的（crazy，crazy 指狂乱的、自身失了常度的）孑遗”；科诺亲手埋葬了这门手艺，不打算让人在它坟头上冒犯它，于是像涨潮一样一步步义愤（indignant，indignant 指对不义之事而怒、带着尊严的怒）起来，发表了他此生最长的演说，讲一门死于世界之懒的手艺与一门死于自身之过的手艺有什么分别，其间的嫌恶（disgust，disgust 指心对一物的拒斥、全身从它转开）是一个主人以纯正散文送客的姿态。随后那不愉快的（unpleasant，unpleasant 指不悦人的、不宜亲近的）半个钟头成了整个冬天的谈资；来客坐立不安（uncomfortable，uncomfortable 指不安的、与自己的椅子过不去）地走了，稿子照写；而《信使报》——派去一位记者，本以为是它历史上头一回有现场（liable，liable 指易于……的、有……之虞的）可看——全文照登了她的稿子，并加了一句评论：这脾气和这门手艺一样，都是各自族系的最后一员，两者都是全县的损失。

他七十三岁退休，连铁砧一起，河谷最后一间铁匠铺在同一天下午关了门；随之而来的寂静里，全村发现自己想念那天气。往他小屋跑腿仍在上午去——出于敬意，而非消息；教堂的钟保持着那谨慎的两分钟；从兰普福德来的年轻蹄铁匠每星期四出诊，听了种种传说却一件也不放在心上，初次见面就问科诺：那脾气到底是干什么用的。“为铁用的，”科诺说，“其余的事自己会管自己。”

quiz.q: Harry Curnow has the most famous temper in three parishes — the state of the mind with regard to passion; in daily use, the short and quick kind. A temper is —
o: the mind's weather of the hour
the heat of the mind against wrong
quiz.ex: temper = 脾气；性情。lose one's temper 发脾气；a short temper 急性子。

quiz.q: There was the full rage of the show day, over the yearling let loose — anger at flood, the mind's storm entire. Rage is —
o: a rudeness that wounds the face
the turning of the body from a thing
quiz.ex: rage = 狂怒。fly into a rage 勃然大怒；road rage 路怒。

quiz.q: Bad iron irritated him — to provoke, to rub the temper raw, as a boot rubs a heel. To irritate is to —
o: anger with dignity at a wrong
quiz.ex: irritate = 激怒；刺激。be irritated by noise 被噪音激怒；irritating adj. 恼人的。

quiz.q: The impulse that made a man snatch his hand from the fire was the same that snatched the child from the road — a spring of the mind, acting before counsel arrives. An impulse is —
o: a feeling that moves and moves us
the mind's weather of the hour
light and quick to fly off
quiz.ex: impulse = 冲动。on impulse 一时冲动；impulsive adj. 冲动的。

quiz.q: The volatile temperament was the temper of all craftsmen written large — light and quick to fly off, as the spirits in the bottle are. Volatile means —
o: past the due and decent amount
quiz.ex: volatile = 易变的；反复无常的。a volatile mood 反复无常的情绪；volatile market 飘忽的市场。

quiz.q: Curnow grew indignant, like a tide, over the insult to his trade — angry at a wrong, anger with its dignity on. Indignant means —
o: savage and given to ill will
angry at a wrong, dignity on
ill at ease in one's chair
quiz.ex: indignant = 义愤的；愤慨的。be indignant at an injustice 对不公感到愤慨；indignation n. 愤慨。

quiz.q: He delivered the address with the disgust of a man showing visitors the door — the mind's rejection of a thing, the whole body turning from it. Disgust is —
o: the mind's rejection, the body turning
the state of passion short and quick
quiz.ex: disgust = 厌恶。in disgust 厌恶地；disgusting adj. 令人作呕的。

quiz.q: The Mercury had sent a reporter expecting to be liable to a scene for once — likely, subject to a thing; apt. Liable means —
quiz.ex: liable = 易于……的；有责任的。liable to fly into a rage 动辄大怒；be liable for damages 负赔偿责任。

title: The Cousins
text:
Japhet and Reuben Tregose, cousins, farmed either side of the stream for fifty years, and spoke to each other for thirty-five of them not at all. The feud was the valley's oldest institution after the church and the more consistently attended; its origin had been mislaid by everyone, which did not prevent everyone from having a version; and its conduct, over half a century, had settled into the formality of a liturgy. The fence along the water was mended, every year, on Japhet's side and never on Reuben's, and each knew exactly what the other meant by it; the bull was lent in spring to every farm in the valley but one; the flower show entries were timed, weighed and arranged with an eye across the tent; and the Mercury's letters page stood ready, in any month, to print a boundary dispute with two names withheld and a postcode doing the work of a duel.

The two engines of it, the doctor said — who as a newcomer was permitted to ask — were of the oldest make. {{envy|Envy}} — envy being the grief at another's good, the pain of watching another's field come green — was Reuben's: Japhet's meadow lay on the sun side of the water and cropped a week earlier, which Reuben had counted against him since the year of the ration books. {{jealous|Jealous}} — jealous meaning fearful of losing what is one's own, or bitter at another's having of it — was Japhet's: his mother had loved Reuben best, and had said so, in the hearing of the whole Sunday school, in 1948; and a man who has been measured in public at nine years old measures the world back ever after. The doctor's summary, delivered to the Women's Institute in the tone of a man reading a veterinary report on two valuable animals, was that each cousin kept the other's failing in prime condition, and that {{hatred}} — hatred being hate grown settled and housed, the mind's long winter — was simply love that had lost its occupation and refused to be retrained.

The conduct was, in its way, a craft. Reuben was {{sly}} — sly being cunning in the small way, artful by stealth and never in the open — in the manner of the fox: his gate was left open at the exact hour of Japhet's rams' crossing, his dyke was cleaned on the day of the silage, his show marrows appeared from nowhere a week before the judging; Japhet was {{cunning}} — cunning meaning clever at compassing one's ends, by wit or by crook, on the grander scale — in the manner of the chess player: he took the water board seat to sit on Reuben's abstraction licence, and the church seat to sit on the hymns Reuben's mother had liked. Neither would have stolen so much as a rope's end from the other — the feud was conducted, both would have said with pride, by means strictly legal — but each would {{harass}} — to harass meaning to trouble continually, to wear at by repeated small assaults — the other through every office the valley offered; and the valley, which enjoys a feud the way the coast enjoys weather, kept both of them in posts.

What it cost was visible chiefly at a distance of one generation. Reuben's boy, who farmed with his father and inherited the whole engagement, was by his own account the most {{miserable}} — miserable meaning wretched, unhappy through and through — young farmer in the county: married to a quarrel he had not chosen, keeper of a grudge with no first cause he could discover, and {{guilty}} — guilty meaning having done wrong, and worse, feeling it — at night for the years of it. He had tried neutrality at nineteen and been treated, by both houses, as a defector; he had tried the truth at twenty-five — telling each grandfather-aged cousin, over separate gates, that the whole affair was {{childish}} — childish meaning of a child; and by extension, unworthy of a grown one — and had been answered on one side by a fortnight's silence and on the other by a lecture on the water meadows that had begun in 1911 and finished at dusk. The cousins were not, in the ordinary way, {{unkind}} — unkind meaning wanting in kindness, failing of the common offices — men: Japhet stood the widow's bill at the Stores without a word, and Reuben would plough the sick man's acre before his own; but each kept a room in himself where the other's name was stored with the {{hate}} — hate being the mind's enmity, the steady wish of ill — itself, and the room was cleaned for no one.

The ending, when it came, came from outside. The museum men, pricing the valley's farms for a leaflet, valued Reuben's orchard above Japhet's meadow by a factor that both farmers knew to be nonsense, and each waited for the other to say so; and the silence, for the first time in thirty-five years, {{disappoint|disappointed}} — to disappoint meaning to fail of what was expected, to come short of the hope — them both. The Doctor's wife found them a week later at the same gate, arguing not the feud but the valuation, with the maps of both farms on the top bar and the coats of both men on the same post; and the argument, which began at ten and ended at four, was the first conversation of any kind that either could remember winning. What was said at the end of it the valley has never learned, the gate being a quarter mile from anywhere; but the fence was mended on both sides that autumn, by both men, on the same day, each pretending not to see the other do it; and when the Mercury asked Reuben, that Christmas, whether he repented — {{repent}} — to repent meaning to turn the mind back upon itself; to regret with the intention of amendment — the fifty years, he gave the valley its best line of the decade: "I repent the fence," he said. "The rest of it kept me young."
tr:
贾菲特与鲁本·特雷戈斯是堂兄弟，隔着溪流各务一农，五十年里有三十五年彼此不交一言。这场世仇是河谷仅次于教堂的最古老机构，出席率还更高；起因人人弄丢了，却不耽误人人各有一版；而它的进行方式，半个世纪下来，已定型为一套规规矩矩的仪轨。沿水的栅栏每年都修——修在贾菲特那一侧，从不修在鲁本那一侧，两人都完全清楚对方这是什么意思；公牛春天借遍全谷，独独不借一家；花展的参赛品以眼角余光瞄着帐篷对面来计时、过磅、摆放；《信使报》的读者来信版则随时待命，任何月份都能登一场地界之争——隐去两个名字，用一个邮编完成决斗的全部工作。

医生说——他作为新来者获准提问——这架机器的两台发动机都是最老的型号。嫉妒（envy，envy 指对他人之善的痛心、看着别人的田先绿的那种疼）是鲁本的：贾菲特的草场在水的向阳一侧，早一个星期收割，从配给簿那年起，鲁本就把这笔账记在他头上。妒忌（jealous，jealous 指唯恐失去自己所有的、或见别人有而心怀怨愤的）是贾菲特的：他母亲最爱鲁本，并且当着整个主日学的面这样说过——在一九四八年；一个九岁就在人前被量过尺寸的人，此后会一辈子量回去。医生向妇女协会作的总结，用的是给两头值钱牲口读兽医报告的口吻：两位表亲各自把对方的毛病保养在巅峰状态，而仇恨（hatred，hatred 指恨意安顿落户之后、心里的漫长冬天）不过是失了业又拒绝转行的爱。

这场经营，自有一门手艺。鲁本狐狸般地刁（sly，sly 指小路数的狡黠、鬼祟而从不公开的艺术）：他的大门恰好在贾菲特的公羊过路的钟点敞开，他的沟渠恰好在青贮那天疏浚，他的赛用西葫芦在评审前一星期不知从何处冒出来；贾菲特棋手般地狡（cunning，cunning 指成事的机巧、不论正邪地绕到目的的那一路数，规模更大）：他谋取水董事会的席位，坐镇鲁本的取水执照；又谋取教会的席位，压着鲁本母亲生前喜欢的圣诗。两人谁也不会偷对方一截绳头——这场世仇，两人都会自豪地说，手段严格合法——但每一处河谷提供的公职，都是互相消耗（harass，harass 指不断骚扰、以连绵的小股袭击磨损人）对方的阵地；而河谷像海岸喜欢天气一样喜欢世仇，于是把两人都一直供在职位上。

代价主要隔着一辈人才能看见。鲁本的儿子随父务农，整场恩怨一并继承，据他自述是全谷最愁苦的（miserable，miserable 指凄惨的、由里到外不快乐的）年轻农户：娶了一场自己没挑的争吵，看守着一份查无起因的宿怨，夜里还要为这些年头内疚（guilty，guilty 指做错事的、更糟的是心里有数的）。他十九岁试过中立，两边都把他当叛徒；二十五岁试过讲真话——隔着两扇门分别告诉两位祖父辈的表亲，这整件事孩子气（childish，childish 指孩子似的；引申指配不上一个成年人的）了——一边回敬他两星期的沉默，另一边给他上了一场水草滩讲座，从一九一一年讲起，讲到天黑。这两位表亲在平常并非刻薄（unkind，unkind 指缺乏善意的、不行日常善举的）之人：贾菲特不声不响替寡妇垫了杂货铺的账，鲁本会先犁病人的地再犁自己的；但两人心里各留着一间屋子，那屋里存放的正是恨（hate，hate 指心里的敌意、稳定的恶意之愿），而那间屋子不打扫给任何人看。

结局来的时候，是从外面来的。博物馆的人为一份折页给全谷的农庄估价，把鲁本的果园估得高于贾菲特的草场一个倍数——两位农户都清楚那是胡说，于是各自等着对方先说出口；而那沉默，三十五年来头一回，让两人双双失望（disappoint，disappoint 指辜负了所期待或所指望的）。一星期后，医生的太太在同一扇门前撞见他们：争论的不是世仇，是那份估价，两家的地图摊在门楣上，两件外套挂在同一根门柱上；这场争论从上午十点进行到下午四点，是两人记忆里各自赢下的头一场任何性质的交谈。末尾说了什么，河谷永远无从知晓——那扇门离哪儿都有四分之一英里；但那年秋天，栅栏两侧都修了，两人同一天修的，各自假装没看见对方；圣诞节《信使报》问鲁本，他悔不悔（repent，repent 指把心思转回来、存心改过地追悔）这五十年，他给了河谷这十年最好的一句话：“栅栏我悔，”他说，“其余的，是它让我保持了年轻。”

quiz.q: Envy was Reuben's engine: Japhet's meadow cropped a week earlier — the grief at another's good, the pain of another's field coming green. Envy is —
quiz.ex: envy = 嫉妒；羡慕。green with envy 妒火中烧；envy of sb 对某人的嫉妒。

quiz.q: Jealous was Japhet's engine: his mother had loved Reuben best — fearful of losing what is one's own, or bitter at another's having. Jealous means —
quiz.ex: jealous = 妒忌的。be jealous of sb's success 忌妒某人的成功；jealousy n. 嫉妒。

quiz.q: Each would harass the other through every office the valley offered — to trouble continually, to wear at by repeated small assaults. To harass is to —
o: mend the fence on one side
quiz.ex: harass = 骚扰；侵扰。harass an opponent 烦扰对手；harassment n. 骚扰。

quiz.q: Reuben was sly in the manner of the fox: the gate left open at the exact hour of the crossing — cunning in the small way, artful by stealth. Sly means —
quiz.ex: sly = 狡猾的。a sly fox 狡猾的狐狸；on the sly 偷偷地。

quiz.q: The boy was guilty at night for the years of it — having done wrong, and worse, feeling it. Guilty means —
o: having done wrong and feeling it
quiz.ex: guilty = 内疚的；有罪的。feel guilty about sth 对某事内疚；be found guilty 被判有罪。

quiz.q: He told each cousin the whole affair was childish — of a child; and by extension, unworthy of a grown one. Childish means —
quiz.ex: childish = 幼稚的。a childish tantrum 孩子气的胡闹；注意与 childlike（天真的）区别。

quiz.q: Hatred was simply love that had lost its occupation and refused to be retrained — hate grown settled and housed, the mind's long winter. Hatred is —
o: the steady wish of ill itself
a quarrel with no first cause
quiz.ex: hatred = 仇恨。deep-seated hatred 根深蒂固的仇恨；hate v. 憎恨。

quiz.q: Asked whether he repented the fifty years, he said: 'I repent the fence.' — to turn the mind back upon itself; to regret with the intention of amendment. To repent is to —
o: mourn aloud in the letters page
quiz.ex: repent = 悔悟；忏悔。repent of one's sins 忏悔罪过；repentance n. 悔改。

title: The Likeness
text:
The parish council, wishing to mark Colonel Venning's fifty years as churchwarden, and having been quoted for a stained-glass window a sum approaching the national debt, commissioned a portrait instead — the decision made easier by the arrival, that same month, of a painter wintering at the Beacon: Miss Hartree, of the Slade, who set up her easel in the reading room of the Corn Exchange and gave the valley, over six sittings, an education in what a face is.

She began, as she told the Women's Institute afterwards, with the whole man. "A portrait," she said, "is anatomy with an opinion. You must know what a {{human}} — human meaning of or belonging to man; and as a noun, a member of that unlucky and interesting species — being is before you can know what one looks like; and you must know his {{character}} — character meaning the sum of a person's qualities, moral and otherwise; and by extension, a person in a book or a play — before you know his face. The {{personality}} — personality being that which makes a person himself and no other; the self that shows through — sits for you entire, and arrives in parts." The Colonel's {{manner}} — manner meaning the way a thing is done; and of a person, the way he carries and conducts himself among others — she found military in the mornings and agrarian after lunch; and his {{attitude}} — attitude meaning the posture of the body; and beyond the body, the settled posture of the mind towards a thing — towards the whole enterprise was patience itself, provided the easel faced the window and the tea came at three.

The head she took by quarters. The {{forehead}} — the forehead being the front of the head above the brows, where the weather of a life keeps itself — was "good honest ploughland"; the {{cheek}} — a cheek being the side of the face below the eye — had the particular set of a man who has spent fifty years being agreed with; the {{eyelash}} — an eyelash being the fringe of small hairs at the edge of the lid, which guards the eye and betrays the sitter whenever he believes himself unobserved — she counted, to the Institute's horror and delight, one by one; the {{lip}}s — a lip being either of the two fleshy borders of the mouth, the busiest thing a face owns — she painted shut, the Colonel's being otherwise engaged whenever at rest; the {{tongue}} — the tongue being the organ of taste and of speech, the latter its more dangerous office — did not once, in six sittings, rest, so that the portrait, the valley agreed, was really half a conversation; the {{throat}} — the throat being the passage by which food and breath go down, and the front of the neck that holds it — was cleared on the quarter hour, as a stationmaster clears a platform; the {{chin}} — the chin being the part of the face below the mouth, on which the whole expression finally rests — she called the keystone of the arch; and the {{beard}} — a beard being the hair grown on the lower part of a man's face — had been worn since 1916 and would not now, the Colonel said, be parted from, the Boer War having taken the moustache and the trenches the rest.

The hands took two sittings and were, she said, the portrait's second signature. The {{shoulder}}s — a shoulder being the joint by which the arm is hung upon the trunk; and the place where burdens, literal and otherwise, are customarily laid — she set square; the {{elbow}} — the elbow being the joint of the arm at its middle bend, the sharpest thing a polite man owns — she kept off the arms of the chair by main force; the {{wrist}} — the wrist being the joint by which the hand is set upon the arm — did more talking than the tongue had; the {{thumb}} — the thumb being the short thick finger set apart from the other four, by which a hand becomes a hand and not a paw — was "a shepherd's thumb, forty years in the wool"; the {{palm}} — the palm being the inner face of the hand, the flat of it, where the fortune-tellers do their reading — she declined to read, on professional grounds; the {{finger}}s — a finger being one of the five parted ends of the hand — were given a light of their own; and every {{joint}} — a joint being the place where two bones meet and bend — was asked its history and got its answer, the right hand being, on the Colonel's own account, a weatherglass.

The rest of him was translated rather than painted. The {{limb}}s — a limb being any of the arms or legs, the members by which the body travels and works — were reduced to dark clothes, as the Colonel wished posterity to remember him; the {{waist}} — the waist being the middle of the body, where the trunk narrows above the hips — had been given up for lost in 1953; the {{stomach}} — the stomach being the organ in which the meal is received; and beyond anatomy, the seat of a man's courage, as the valley uses the word — was, on the evidence of the teas, sound; the {{thigh}}s — a thigh being the part of the leg from hip to knee — bore the dog, who attended every sitting upon the {{lap}} — the lap being the flat made by the thighs of one seated, the dog's estate — and was painted in over the Colonel's objections and to the parish's lasting gratitude; the {{knee}}s — a knee being the joint of the leg at its middle, on which supplication and proposal are traditionally made — were crossed; the {{ankle}}s — an ankle being the joint where the foot is set upon the leg — were pronounced sound; the {{heel}}s — a heel being the back of the foot, on which Achilles kept his whole secret — showed the bootmaker's last to advantage; the {{toe}}s — a toe being one of the five parted ends of the foot — escaped both the canvas and the bootmaker's verdict, the portrait ending at three-quarter length by mutual treaty; and as for the {{flesh}} — flesh being the soft substance of the body between skin and bone; and by extension, the body's mortal part, as against its spirit — she painted it warm where the photographs had gone grey, which was, the Colonel allowed, the entire advantage of the undertaking.

What made the likeness, she told the Institute, was none of these. It was the {{space}} — space meaning room, extent, that in which things stand and are placed — between the nose and the lip: "a face is all intervals; get the spaces right and the {{feature}}s — a feature being any part of the face; and beyond faces, a marked quality of anything at all — confess themselves." And it was the one {{trait}} — a trait being a line of character, a distinguishing quality that runs through a person and shows — that the Colonel could not school for the occasion: patience, which is not a pose but a {{virtue}} — a virtue being a moral excellence; a quality counted good in a person — and which shows in paint as nowhere else. The unveiling filled the Corn Exchange. The council, the chapel, the Legion and the dogs having been seated, the sheet came off; and the valley, which had braced itself for flattery, found itself looked at by the Colonel {{really}} — really meaning truly, in fact; and, as the valley itself uses the word, very — as he had looked at the parish accounts: in full, and without hope. The Mercury's review ran to one line, and is cut out and framed in the reading room still: "The picture will do for the window what the window was to have done for the Colonel, at a tenth of the price, and with the dog."

教区议会想给担任教堂执事五十年的文宁上校留个纪念，一问彩绘玻璃窗的价钱，数字直逼国债，于是改请一幅肖像——促成这个决定的是当月恰有一位画家来灯塔山庄过冬：斯莱德美术学校出身的哈特里小姐，她把画架支进谷交所的阅览室，用六次坐姿，给全村上了一堂“脸是什么”的课。

事后她向妇女协会讲了自己的路数。“肖像，”她说，“是带着见解的解剖学。你得先知道一个人类（human，human 指人的、属于人的；作名词指这个倒霉而有趣的物种的一名成员）存在是什么，才能知道他长什么样；你得先知道他的性格（character，character 指一个人诸般品质的总和，道德的与其余的；引申指书里或戏里的一个人物），才能知道他的脸。个性（personality，personality 指使人成其为自己、而非旁人的那点东西；是那个透出来的自我）是整个儿坐下来让你画的，只是分批到场。”上校的举止（manner，manner 指做事的方式；就人而言，指他在众人之间立身行事的那一套）她发现上午是军人的，午后是庄稼人的；而他对整件事的态度（attitude，attitude 指身体的姿态；身体之外，指心智对一事定下的姿态、看法）堪称耐心本身——只要画架对着窗，茶在三点送到。

头部她按方位取。前额（forehead，forehead 指眉以上的头脸前部、一生的风云存放之处）是“老实的好犁地”；面颊（cheek，cheek 指眼睛下方的脸侧）带着一种特殊的定型——一个被人赞同了五十年的人才会有的那种；睫毛（eyelash，eyelash 指眼睑边缘的小毛发帘幕，护着眼，也在画中人自以为无人观看时出卖他）她一根一根数过，让协会又惊又喜；双唇（lip，lip 指嘴的两片肉边、一张脸上最闲不住的东西）她画成闭着的，因为上校的嘴一得空就要开工；舌头（tongue，tongue 指味觉与言语的器官，后者是它更危险的职分）六次坐姿里没有一次歇过，以致全村公认这幅画像其实是半场谈话；喉咙（throat，throat 指食物与呼吸下咽的通道，也指兜着它的脖颈前部）每刻钟清一次，像站长清站台；下巴（chin，chin 指嘴以下的脸的那部分、整个表情最终搁靠之处）她称为拱心石；胡须（beard，beard 指男人下颌上生的须发）则是一九一六年起留的，上校说如今也不会分开——布尔战争带走了髭，战壕带走了其余。

手占去两次坐姿，她说，那是肖像的第二个签名。肩（shoulder，shoulder 指把胳膊挂上身躯的关节；也是担子——实在的与别的——惯常搁放的地方）她摆得端正；肘（elbow，elbow 指臂中弯处的关节、有礼貌的人身上最尖利的东西）她靠强制力请离了椅子扶手；腕（wrist，wrist 指把手安到臂上的关节）比舌头还健谈；拇指（thumb，thumb 指与其余四指分开的短粗手指、靠它一只手才成其为手而非爪子）是“牧人的拇指，在羊毛里泡了四十年”；掌心（palm，palm 指手的里面、平坦的那一面、算命先生做营生的地方）她以职业操守拒绝解读；手指（finger，finger 指手上分开的五端之一）各自领到了一点光；每一个关节（joint，joint 指两骨相接而能弯折之处）都被问了来历、也都得了回答——右手按上校自己的说法，是一具晴雨表。

身体的其余部分是“转译”而非描画。四肢（limb，limb 指臂与腿、身体借以行走与劳作的肢体）压进深色衣裳，遵上校之愿，好教后世这样记他；腰身（waist，waist 指身体的中段、躯干在臀上收窄处）一九五三年就已放弃寻找；胃（stomach，stomach 指受纳饭食的器官；解剖之外，也是河谷用语里胆气的所在）就茶点的证据看还算结实；大腿（thigh，thigh 指腿从髋到膝的那一段）上伏着狗——狗每次坐姿都出席，占着膝头（lap，lap 指人坐下时大腿形成的平面、狗的领地），不顾上校抗议被画了进去，教区为此永远感激；双膝（knee，knee 指腿中段的关节、恳求与求婚按传统要跪的地方）交叠着；脚踝（ankle，ankle 指脚安到腿上的那个关节）经宣布健全；脚跟（heel，heel 指脚的后部、阿喀琉斯藏着他全部秘密的地方）把靴匠的楦头衬得十分体面；脚趾（toe，toe 指脚上分开的五端之一）则逃过了画布，也逃过了靴匠的裁断——画是七分身，经双方协议，到 thigh 为止；至于皮肉（flesh，flesh 指皮与骨之间身体的软质；引申指身体的必朽部分、与精神相对的那一面），她画得温暖，照片里那种灰她不肯给——上校承认，这正是这项工程全部的用处所在。

真正成就这张脸的，她告诉协会，不在以上任何一处。是鼻与唇之间那段空间（space，space 指余地、广度、万物立足与安放之所）：“一张脸全是间隔；间隔摆对了，五官（feature，feature 指脸上的任何部分；脸之外，指任何事物显著的特质）自己就招了。”也是上校为这次场合怎么也训练不出来的那一条特质（trait，trait 指性格里的一道线、贯穿一个人而显出来的独特品质）：耐心——那不是姿势，是美德（virtue，virtue 指道德上的卓越、被人算作好的品质），画进颜料里比在哪儿都藏不住。揭幕那天谷交所坐满了。委员会、礼拜堂、军团和狗们都落了座，布掀开；全村本已摆好挨奉承的架势，结果发现自己被上校真真正正地（really，really 指真正地、事实上；也是河谷嘴里的“非常”）望着——用的是他看教区账目的那种眼神：看全本，不存指望。《信使报》的评论只有一行，至今剪下来裱在阅览室里：“这幅画替那扇窗办了窗本要替上校办的事，价钱是十分之一，还附一条狗。”

quiz.q: You must know his character before you know his face — the sum of a person's qualities, moral and otherwise; and by extension, a person in a book or play. Character is —
o: a line of quality running through a person
that which makes one himself and no other
the sum of a person's qualities
quiz.ex: character = 性格；人物。a man of character 有个性的人；the main character 主角。

quiz.q: The forehead was good honest ploughland — the front of the head above the brows, where the weather of a life keeps itself. The forehead is —
o: the front of the head above the brows
the side of the face below the eye
the part of the face below the mouth
the passage of food and breath
quiz.ex: forehead = 前额。wipe one's forehead 擦前额；forehead thermometer 额温枪。

quiz.q: The palm she declined to read, on professional grounds — the inner face of the hand, where the fortune-tellers do their reading. The palm is —
o: the inner face of the hand
the short thick finger set apart
the joint setting hand on arm
the place where two bones bend
quiz.ex: palm = 手掌。read one's palm 看手相；palm tree 棕榈树。

quiz.q: The dog attended every sitting upon the lap — the flat made by the thighs of one seated, the dog's estate. A lap is —
o: the leg from hip to knee
the middle of the body above the hips
the flat made by the thighs seated
the joint where foot meets leg
quiz.ex: lap = （坐时）大腿的平面；膝上。sit on one's lap 坐在膝上；lap dog 巴儿狗。

quiz.q: The heels showed the bootmaker's last to advantage — the back of the foot, on which Achilles kept his whole secret. A heel is —
o: the sharp bend of the arm
one of the five ends of the foot
the joint of the leg's middle
quiz.ex: heel = 脚跟；鞋后跟。high heels 高跟鞋；Achilles' heel 致命弱点。

quiz.q: It was the space between the nose and the lip that made the likeness — room, extent, that in which things stand and are placed. Space is —
o: any part of the face at all
room, extent, in which things are placed
quiz.ex: space = 空间；空位。parking space 停车位；outer space 外太空。

quiz.q: Patience was the one trait the Colonel could not school for the occasion — a line of character, a distinguishing quality that runs through a person and shows. A trait is —
o: a line of character running through one
the organ of taste and speech
the fringe at the lid's edge
quiz.ex: trait = 特征；特质。personality traits 人格特质；a family trait 家族特征。

quiz.q: Patience is not a pose but a virtue, and shows in paint as nowhere else — a moral excellence; a quality counted good in a person. A virtue is —
o: the way a thing is done
the sum of a person's qualities
a person in a book or play
quiz.ex: virtue = 美德；优点。patience is a virtue 耐心是美德；by virtue of 凭借。

title: The Night Exchange
text:
The telephone exchange came to Millbrook in 1936 and took, for its night hours, Mrs. Payne, who kept them for thirty-one years, in a chair, at a board, under a lamp, with the valley's whole sleeping life arriving at her ears by wire. Her {{habit}} — habit meaning a thing so often done that it does itself without asking — of waking at the first tremor of the bell was not, she insisted, a gift: her {{biorhythm}} — biorhythm being the body's inner clock, its built-in tide of sleeping and waking — had simply been set, like the church clock, by the Post Office. What she had instead of sleep she never named; the doctor's word for it, {{insomnia}} — insomnia being the want of sleep, the night spent awake against the will — she declined as a diagnosis, holding the condition to be rather a vocation.

Her hearing was the valley's hearing, and her report on it was modest. "The board trains an {{aural}} — aural meaning of or for the ear, of hearing — memory the way the chapel trains the musical one," she said; and it was true that she knew the voice before the number, the farm before the voice, and the news before the farm. Of her {{sense}}s — a sense being any one of the body's channels of knowing, the doors by which the world gets in — she claimed no more than ordinary stock, kept in repair; the bell was her {{stimulus}} — a stimulus being whatever stirs a body or a mind to answer, the goad that starts the response — and she answered it as the church answers its own. The doctor, who inspected her yearly as the county inspects a bridge, found the {{nerve}}s — a nerve being one of the fine threads by which feeling travels between body and brain; and beyond anatomy, the stuff of which courage is made — steady, the {{artery}} — an artery being a vessel that carries the blood out from the heart — at her wrist regular as the ringers' rope, the {{pore}}s — a pore being one of the small openings of the skin, by which it breathes and sweats — of the exchange room in August a standing grievance, and the {{hormone}}s — hormones being the body's chemical messengers, carried in the blood to give their orders to distant organs — responsible for the four-o'clock terrors; a verdict on which Mrs. Payne reserved judgement, being awake at four and in a position to know.

The valley's senses were on permanent exhibition at her window. The basket-maker, {{blind}} — blind meaning wanting sight, without the seeing of the eyes — since 1916, wove by touch and by the ear of a room, and wove the tighter for it; the saddler's son, born without speech — the old word for whose condition was {{dumb}} — dumb meaning mute, wanting the power of speech; a word worn bad in long service and since laid down — said more with a pencil in ten seconds than the Legion managed in an evening; the schoolmaster's {{sight}} — sight being the act and the power of seeing — was long, and his {{eyesight}} — eyesight being the seeing power of the eyes, sight in its ordinary keeping — short, a combination he had converted into a career of reading aloud. Mrs. Payne's own {{visual}} — visual meaning of or for the eyes, having to do with seeing — duties were few, being the labels and the lamp; her {{view}} — a view being what is seen from a place; and beyond the eyes, an opinion held and looked out from — of the valley, formed at the window at three in the morning, was the gentlest on record; and her memory of any call made after four was {{vague}} — vague meaning wanting outline, not clear at the edges, as borders, statements and memories can be — by six, which the valley took not as a failing but as tact.

Sleep itself she had watched leave the whole valley and return to it. She kept a private register of the {{awake}} — awake meaning not in sleep, roused and waking — and knew the {{asleep}} — asleep being in sleep, in the holding of it — hours of every house as the vicar knew the unconfessed sins; the {{yawn}} — a yawn being the open-mouthed breath of tiredness or boredom, catching as laughter catches — that went round the vestry at evensong she could hear through two doors and a wall; the harvest dinner ended, every year, in a {{nap}} — a nap being a short sleep, taken by day and by surprise — of agricultural breadth; the {{doze}} — to doze meaning to sleep lightly, on the edge of it, as in a chair after dinner — of the Legion's front room she clocked without comment; and of the {{quiet}} — quiet meaning without noise, still — after midnight she said the truest sentence of her career: "The valley is never silent, only quiet, and quiet is the sound of everybody's luck holding."

The automatic exchange came in 1967, and her last night was the valley's last night of being known. She sat the shift out to the {{weary}} — weary meaning tired past tiredness, worn down to the last coat of paint — end of it, took the final calls with the full ceremony of the old ones, and at dawn walked home through a village that slept on, unaware of the coincidence. The Mercury, at her retirement supper, put it in the terms the valley has kept since: that for thirty-one years it had slept the better for one of itself being awake; and that it could no longer remember how it had ever dared, before her, to close its eyes.
tr:
电话总机一九三六年进米尔布鲁克，夜班交给了佩恩太太，她一看就是三十一年——一把椅子、一面交换台、一盏灯，全村沉睡的生活顺着电线抵达她的耳朵。铃声第一下颤动就醒的那个习惯（habit，habit 指做得太多、不请自来自己就做掉的事），她坚称不是天分：她的生物节律（biorhythm，biorhythm 指身体的内钟、自带的一涨一落的睡与醒）不过是让邮政总局调过，同教堂的钟一个待遇。她拿睡眠换了什么，她自己从不命名；医生给那东西起的名字——失眠（insomnia，insomnia 指睡眠的缺失、违背意愿醒着度过的夜晚）——她拒绝当作诊断，认为那更近乎一种天职。

她的听觉就是全村的听觉，而她自己的汇报很低调。“总机训练的是听觉的（aural，aural 指耳的、属于听觉的）记忆，”她说，“就像礼拜堂训练音乐的那种。”确实，号码还没报完她已认出声音，声音还没开口她已认出农庄，农庄还没说话她已知道新闻。至于她的诸般感官（sense，sense 指身体知晓世界的渠道之一、世界进来的那些门），她自认不过寻常货色、保养得宜；铃是她的刺激（stimulus，stimulus 指任何促使身体或心智起而应答的东西、引发反应的那一鞭），而她应答铃声，如同教堂应答自己的钟。每年给她做体检的医生——那架势像县里检桥——发现她的神经（nerve，nerve 指感觉往返于身体与大脑之间的那些细线；解剖之外，也指胆气的料子）稳定，腕上那条动脉（artery，artery 指把血从心脏运出去的血管）规律得像敲钟人的绳，八月总机房里她皮肤上的毛孔（pore，pore 指皮肤上细小的孔、皮肤借以呼吸和出汗的那些）是一桩常年冤情，而荷尔蒙（hormone，hormone 指身体的化学信使、随血而行、向远处的器官发号施令的）该为凌晨四点的惊惶负责——这一裁断佩恩太太保留意见，因为她四点醒着，有资格知道。

全村的感官常年在她窗口陈列。编篮匠一九一六年起失明（blind，blind 指失明的、没有眼睛之看的），靠手与屋子的耳朵编织，反而编得更密；鞍匠的儿子生来不能言语——从前形容他这状况的旧词是哑（dumb，dumb 指喑哑的、缺失言语能力的；这个词在长期服役里磨损坏了，如今已被放下不用）——铅笔十秒钟写下的意思，比军团一晚上说出来的还多；校长的目力（sight，sight 指看的行为与能力）看得远，视力（eyesight，eyesight 指眼睛看的能力、平常保管着的那种目力）却短，他把这个组合经营成了一项朗读的事业。佩恩太太自己的视觉（visual，visual 指眼的、为看服务的、与看见有关的）事务不多，读读标签、看住油灯而已；她从窗口凌晨三点望出去形成的对河谷的看法（view，view 指从一处所见的东西；眼睛之外，也指持有并据以张望的见解），是有记录以来最宽厚的；而四点以后任何通话的记忆，到六点就模糊（vague，vague 指缺轮廓的、边上不清楚的，形容边界、说法与记忆皆可）了——全村不把这当毛病，当作厚道。

睡眠本身，她看着它离开全村、又看着它回来。醒着（awake，awake 指不在睡里的、被唤起的）的人她心里有一本私册；每户人家睡熟（asleep，asleep 指在睡里、被睡眠持有的）的钟点，她知道得像牧师知道那些没忏悔的罪；晚祷时在圣器室里传开的那口哈欠（yawn，yawn 指疲倦或无聊时张口的深呼吸、像笑声一样会传染的东西），隔着两道门一堵墙她也听得见；丰收宴每年都终结在一场范围惊人的午觉（nap，nap 指白天里短短的、出其不意袭来的一觉）里；军团前厅的打盹（doze，doze 指浅浅地睡、在睡的边上，如晚饭后陷进椅子里那样）她记下时间、不作评论；至于午夜之后的安静（quiet，quiet 指没有噪声的、静止的），她说过一句她职业生涯里最真的话：“河谷从来不寂静，只是安静；而安静，是所有人的运气都在走稳的声音。”

自动交换机一九六七年来了，她的最后一夜，也是全村被知晓的最后一夜。她把这一班守到了困乏（weary，weary 指疲惫过了疲惫的、磨损到只剩最后一层漆的）的尽头，用旧日全套的仪轨接完最后几个电话，天亮时穿过一座照旧酣睡的村子走回家，浑然不觉其中巧合。退休晚宴上《信使报》说出了全村从此保留的那句话：三十一年，全村睡得安稳，因为知道村里有一个自己人醒着；而它已经想不起来，在她之前，自己怎么敢闭眼。

quiz.q: Her habit of waking at the first tremor of the bell — a thing so often done that it does itself without asking. A habit is —
o: the body's inner tide of sleeping
a thing done so often it does itself
the want of sleep against the will
a channel by which the world gets in
quiz.ex: habit = 习惯。get into the habit of 养成……习惯；habitual adj. 惯常的。

quiz.q: The doctor's word for her nights, which she declined as a diagnosis — the want of sleep, the night spent awake against the will. Insomnia is —
o: a short sleep taken by day
light sleep at the edge of it
quiz.ex: insomnia = 失眠。suffer from insomnia 患失眠症；insomniac n. 失眠者。

quiz.q: The board trains an aural memory, the way the chapel trains the musical one — of or for the ear, of hearing. Aural means —
quiz.ex: aural = 听觉的。aural comprehension 听力理解；aural and oral skills 听说能力。

quiz.q: The bell was her stimulus, and she answered it as the church answers its own — whatever stirs a body or mind to answer, the goad that starts the response. A stimulus is —
o: a chemical messenger in the blood
one of the skin's small openings
quiz.ex: stimulus = 刺激（物）。stimulus and response 刺激与反应；复数 stimuli。

quiz.q: The doctor held the hormones responsible for the four-o'clock terrors — the body's chemical messengers, carried in the blood to give orders to distant organs. A hormone is —
o: a chemical messenger of the body
quiz.ex: hormone = 激素；荷尔蒙。growth hormone 生长激素；hormonal adj. 激素的。

quiz.q: The basket-maker, blind since 1916, wove by touch and by the ear of a room — wanting sight, without the seeing of the eyes. Blind means —
quiz.ex: blind = 失明的。the blind 盲人（总称）；go blind 失明；blindness n. 盲目。

quiz.q: Her view of the valley, formed at the window at three in the morning — what is seen from a place; and beyond the eyes, an opinion held and looked out from. A view is —
o: a memory not clear at the edges
the act and power of seeing
the seeing power of the eyes
what is seen; and an opinion held
quiz.ex: view = 景色；见解。in my view 依我看；a room with a view 看得见风景的房间。

quiz.q: The doze of the Legion's front room she clocked without comment — to sleep lightly, on the edge of it. To doze is to —
o: sleep short by day, by surprise
sleep lightly, on the edge of it
quiz.ex: doze = 打瞌睡；小睡。doze off 打起瞌睡来；n. 瞌睡。

title: The Casebook
text:
At the top of the pass, where the parish boundary crosses the drovers' road, there stands a shallow stone bowl on a post, which the Ordnance Survey calls a font and the valley calls the {{plague}} — a plague being any great sickness that spreads abroad through a people; and in the old use, the sickness itself — stone. In the year of the plague, the story runs, the two parishes left money in the bowl and took bread out of it, no face seeing a face; and the arrangement, which was the whole of public health for a season, held: the sickness being {{lethal}} — lethal meaning deadly, having in it the power to kill — and the only medicine on either side of the pass being distance. Dr. Anand, walking up there in his first spring, found the bowl full of rainwater and one ten-pence piece, and said it was the valley's first consultation room, and the fee about right.

The serious cases of every generation since have come down from the quarry. The rockfall of 1963 supplied the worst: three men {{injure}}d — to injure meaning to do harm to the body, to wound it from the outside — past the reach of the first-aid box, one of them {{unconscious}} — unconscious meaning without consciousness, in the dark of oneself, neither waking nor asleep — for nine days; and the {{hurt}} — hurt meaning harm done, of the body or of the feeling, the plain word the valley keeps for both — that mattered most, the men said afterwards, was the waiting, theirs in the kitchen and their wives' at the gate. The {{trauma}} — trauma meaning a wound of the body; and beyond the body, the shock of a blow that outlasts the blow — was treated that year with a word nobody used and a distance everybody kept, which the doctor has spent his career closing. One man was left {{disable}}d — disabled meaning made unable, robbed of the use of a limb or of a faculty — in the right hand, and retrained at the Stores as a bookkeeper with a hand like a signature; and the old words for such a state — {{cripple}} — cripple meaning one lame or otherwise fallen short in limb, a word the valley used for four centuries and has since put away — and {{lame}} — lame meaning halting, wanting the full use of a leg — the doctor keeps in his lectures as the laboratories keep the smallpox: to show what a word can do, and be retired from doing.

The heart's failures came later and to better dinners. The {{heart attack}} — a heart attack being the sudden failing of the heart's muscle, the engine seizing at speed — took the flower-show chairman between the marrow and the cups, and was survived, the doctor happening to stand two feet away at the tea tent; the {{stroke}} — a stroke being the sudden loss of the blood's passage to part of the brain, by which an arm, a word or half a world is taken away — came to the squire at his own breakfast and took his right hand's writing, which he replaced, being the squire, with a left hand's that the Mercury printed for years without comment. Of {{symptom}}s — a symptom being a sign of illness, what the body says of its own trouble, if it is asked in time — the doctor lectured the whole winter: the ache in the jaw that is the heart's, the week of the mouth gone crooked that is the brain's, the cough that outstays its cold; and the valley, which had taken the notifications of its own body on trust for sixty years, learned to read the gauges. What it would not learn, then or since, was the arithmetic of another kind: that the good of the cigarette is a minute's and its {{detriment}} — detriment meaning harm, damage, the being-worse-for — is a lifetime's; a fact the Legion heard annually, agreed with entirely, and set aside with the ashtrays.

The word {{cancer}} — cancer being the sickness of cells that will not stop, growing without office or reason or end — was not said aloud in the valley until Dr. Anand said it, in the third winter, to a room of the Women's Institute, on the grounds that a disease named is a disease half-met; and the room, which had buried the same sickness under a dozen gentler names for a century, sat very still, and then asked better questions than any lecture on the subject had ever got in the county. Against the serious things, the small ones keep their own scale: the {{pimple}} — a pimple being a small swelling of the skin, the adolescent's temporary decoration — that shut the sixth form's leading actress in her room for a week was treated by the whole school with the gravity of a state occasion. Fear itself he filed among the serious things: it can {{paralyse}} — to paralyse meaning to strike with loss of movement; and beyond the body, to fix the mind so that it cannot act — as wholly as any stone, he told them, and is caught the same way, by being known for what it is; and of the {{sorrow}} — sorrow being grief, the mind's mourning for what it has lost or stands to lose — that follows the serious things home, he said the truest sentence of the winter: that it is not a symptom, and must not be treated as one, being the healthy mind's own work.

The Mercury ran the news of the cloned sheep that spring — a {{clone}} — a clone being a living thing grown from the cell of another, its same self arriving late by years — under the headline WHAT THE COUNTY SHOULD KNOW, between the barley prices and a wedding; and the valley, reading it at breakfast, took it calmly, having absorbed in one century the motor car, the National Health and the paraffin heater, and being of the settled opinion that a sheep is a sheep, however it is booked in. Dr. Anand cut the piece out and pasted it in the back of his casebook, where the serious things live, with a note the Mercury never saw: "The century will end by making the copies before the originals are quite finished."
tr:
在山口顶上、教区边界穿过赶牲口大路的地方，立着一根柱子，柱头上凿着一口浅石碗，陆军测量局管它叫洗礼盆，河谷管它叫瘟疫（plague，plague 指在人群中四散传播的大疫；旧义即那场大疫本身）石。相传瘟疫那一年，两侧的教区把钱放进碗里、把面包取出来，没有一张脸见到另一张脸；这套安排就是一个季节的全部公共卫生，而且行之有效——那病是致命的（lethal，lethal 指致命的、内里带着杀人之力的），而山口两侧仅有的药，就是距离。阿南德医生头一个春天走上去看，发现碗里积着雨水和一枚十便士，说这是河谷的第一间诊室，诊金也算公道。

从那以后，每一辈人的重症都是从采石场下来的。一九六三年的塌方提供了最重的一批：三个人受了伤（injure，injure 指使身体受害、自外致伤），伤到急救箱无能为力，其中一个不省人事（unconscious，unconscious 指失去意识的、在自我的黑暗里、既不醒也不睡的）九天；而事后当事人说，最要紧的那种痛（hurt，hurt 指造成的伤害、身体的或心里的，是河谷对两者都通用的那个朴素的词）是等待——他们自己在厨房里的那份，和妻子们在大门口的那份。那一年的创伤（trauma，trauma 指身体的创口；身体之外，指比打击本身活得更久的打击之震荡）是用一个没人说出口的词和一段人人保持的距离治的，而医生这些年一直在做的，就是把这段距离缩短。一个人右手落下残疾（disable，disabled 指被夺去一肢或一种机能之用的），后来在杂货铺再就业做了账房，那只手写得像一枚签名；至于形容这种状态的旧词——瘸子（cripple，cripple 指腿瘸或肢体缺损之人，河谷用了四百年、如今已经收起的词）与瘸（lame，lame 指跛行的、腿不能尽其全用的）——医生在课上还讲，如同实验室封存天花：叫人看看一个词能做什么，又如何功成身退。

心脏的失事来得晚些，专挑丰盛的饭局。心脏病发作（heart attack，heart attack 指心肌的骤然失灵、引擎在高速上咬死）在骨灰坛与奖杯之间放倒了花展主席，人救回来了——多亏医生恰好站在茶帐两英尺外；中风（stroke，stroke 指血液通往脑的通路骤然断绝、一条胳膊、一个词或半个世界就此被取走）在自家早餐桌上找上乡绅，拿走了他右手的字，他又用左手练出一套来——《信使报》登了那手字好些年，一句评论没有。至于症状（symptom，symptom 指疾病的征象、身体就自己的麻烦说的话，只要及时去问），医生讲了一整个冬天：下颌的酸是心脏的，嘴角歪掉的那一星期是脑子的，咳嗽过了感冒还赖着不走的；而把自家身体的通知单信托了六十年的河谷，总算学会了看仪表。它始终不肯学的是另一种算术：香烟的好处是一分钟的，损害（detriment，detriment 指伤害、损耗、“因此更糟”）是一辈子的——这道理军团年年听，完全同意，然后连同烟灰缸一起搁到一边。

癌（cancer，cancer 指不肯停下的细胞之病、无职无由无尽地生长）这个词，是阿南德医生第三年冬天在妇女协会的屋里说出口的，理由是：叫得出名字的病，已经算遇上了一半；满屋子人用一个世纪埋葬过同一种病、底下垫着十几个更温柔的名字，此刻坐得纹丝不动，然后提出的问题比全县任何讲座得到过的都好。大病之侧，小病有自己的度量衡：让六年级头号女演员闭门一星期的丘疹（pimple，pimple 指皮肤上的小肿起、青春期的临时装饰），全校按国典的规格给予了对待。恐惧本身他也归入重症：它能使人的心瘫痪（paralyse，paralyse 指使失去动作；身体之外，指把心固定到动弹不得）之彻底不亚于任何一块石头，他说，而制服它的法子也一样——先认出它是什么；至于跟着重症回家的悲恸（sorrow，sorrow 指哀伤、心智为自己失去的或将要失去的所作的哀悼），他说了那个冬天最真的一句话：它不是症状，不可当症状治——它是健康的心智自己的活计。

那年春天《信使报》登了克隆羊的消息——克隆（clone，clone 指由另一个体的细胞长出的活物、同一个自己迟到若干年才到）——标题是《本县须知》，排在麦价和一场婚礼中间；河谷在早餐桌上读了，心平气和：它在一个世纪里消化了汽车、国民保健和煤油取暖器，而且抱定一个见解——羊就是羊，不管账怎么记。阿南德医生把那条剪下来贴在病历簿末页，重症们都住在那儿，附了一行《信使报》没见过的话：“这个世纪要在原件还没做完之前，先做出拷贝来收尾。”

quiz.q: The sickness being lethal, and the only medicine on either side of the pass being distance — deadly, having in it the power to kill. Lethal means —
quiz.ex: lethal = 致命的。a lethal dose 致死剂量；lethal weapon 致命武器。

quiz.q: Three men injured past the reach of the first-aid box — to do harm to the body, to wound it from the outside. To injure is to —
quiz.ex: injure = 使受伤。the injured 伤员；injury n. 伤害。

quiz.q: One of them unconscious for nine days — without consciousness, in the dark of oneself, neither waking nor asleep. Unconscious means —
o: wanting the use of a leg
quiz.ex: unconscious = 无知觉的；昏迷的。knock sb. unconscious 把某人打昏；subconscious adj. 潜意识的。

quiz.q: The trauma was treated with a word nobody used and a distance everybody kept — a wound of the body; and beyond the body, the shock of a blow that outlasts the blow. Trauma is —
o: a wound, physical or of the mind
quiz.ex: trauma = 创伤（心理或身体）。childhood trauma 童年创伤；traumatic adj. 创伤的。

quiz.q: The heart attack took the flower-show chairman between the marrow and the cups — the sudden failing of the heart's muscle, the engine seizing at speed. A heart attack is —
o: a small swelling of the skin
the loss of blood to the brain
the sudden failing of the heart
quiz.ex: heart attack = 心脏病发作。survive a heart attack 心脏病发作后存活；risk a heart attack 冒心脏病发作之险。

quiz.q: The stroke came to the squire at his own breakfast and took his right hand's writing — the sudden loss of the blood's passage to part of the brain. A stroke is —
o: the loss of blood to part of the brain
the cough that outstays its cold
quiz.ex: stroke = 中风。suffer a stroke 患中风；heat stroke 中暑。

quiz.q: The doctor lectured on symptoms: the ache in the jaw that is the heart's, the crooked mouth that is the brain's — a sign of illness, what the body says of its own trouble. A symptom is —
quiz.ex: symptom = 症状。flu symptoms 流感症状；symptomatic adj. 有症状的。

quiz.q: Fear can paralyse as wholly as any stone — to strike with loss of movement; and beyond the body, to fix the mind so that it cannot act. To paralyse is to —
o: lift a pain for a night
quiz.ex: paralyse = 使瘫痪；使麻痹。be paralysed by fear 被恐惧吓瘫；paralysis n. 瘫痪。

title: The Wing
text:
When Lampford County Hospital announced its appeal for a new wing, the valley subscribed as one man — which is the form its generosity takes — and raised in eighteen months a sum the Mercury printed in figures and the hospital board repeated at dinners for a decade. The {{hospital}} — a hospital being a house set apart for the sick, where they are kept and treated — was no stranger to the valley: its fever sheds had stood at the crossroads for sixty years, put up in the year of the last typhoid, when the county had {{segregate}}d — to segregate meaning to set apart, to put a thing or a people by itself, away from the rest — every infectious case behind its own fence; a policy the valley remembered less for its medicine than for its bread, which was delivered to the fence on a pole, and which was, the old men still said, the best bread in the county's history, being paid for in advance and eaten with a clear conscience.

The wing itself belonged to the surgeon. The {{surgeon}} — a surgeon being one who treats by the knife, medicine's carpenter, who repairs the house from inside — who took the quarry's cases had trained at the old hospital and come back with the new methods and the new manners, the second the more startling; the {{operation}} — an operation being the surgeon's work upon the body, done with the hands and their instruments, the patient mercifully elsewhere — that saved the youngest quarryman was performed at eleven at night and lasted four hours, the church clock striking through it, as the Mercury observed, in the key of the occasion. What the doctor ordered against pain past bearing had not changed since the war: {{morphine}} — morphine being the strong medicine of the poppy, that lifts the pain and lowers the flag — and the {{relief}} — relief meaning the easing of a burden or a pain, the lifting of it, if only for the length of a night — it gave was, he said, the oldest prescription in his bag and the one he was least free with.

The word the wing taught the valley was {{transplant}} — a transplant being the moving of a living part from one body to another, the kidney being the pioneer of it — which the valley learned from the schoolmaster's boy, who went up to Lampford with a failing kidney and came back, two years on, with another man's working in him, and farmed thereafter at a pace his father called ungrateful and his grandfather called a miracle. The {{therapy}} — therapy meaning the treatment of illness or weakness by ordered means, the exercise, the talk, the application — of his first year, the walking and the fluids and the slow miles, was prescribed like medicine and swallowed like it, bitterly and on schedule; the {{treatment}} — treatment meaning the whole of what is done for a patient against his illness, the care entire — he received was, Dr. Anand told the parish meeting, the reason he lived; the {{cure}} — a cure being the restoration to health, the illness ended — was the reason the newspapers wrote about him; and the distinction, the doctor said, was the whole ethics of his profession in one sentence, for which he thanked the meeting. The wing's brochure had called the new ward {{curative}} — curative meaning having the power to cure, of a medicine or a measure — in every paragraph, which the Mercury's proof-reader had corrected, out of superstition, to "comfortable", and had been overruled.

The valley did its own prescribing in the meantime, as valleys will. Every household kept its {{remedy}} — a remedy being a means of curing; and beyond medicine, any means of setting a matter right — of a different make, and defended it with the doctrine of a church; the {{drug}} — a drug being a substance used in medicine; and beyond the prescription, the ones taken for reasons the prescription never mentions — cabinet at the Stores held the lawful sort, and the gossip held the rest; and when the Women's Institute booked a lecturer in {{acupuncture}} — acupuncture being the Chinese art of treating by needles set at points in the skin — the hall was full an hour early, the needles were demonstrated upon the doctor, who had volunteered and afterwards pronounced himself unaccountably {{relax}}ed — to relax meaning to loosen, to let go of a tightness, of the muscle or of the mind — and the vote of thanks was moved on the grounds that the Institute had at last found a speaker it could see through.

The last word the wing gave the valley was the plainest. {{recovery|Recovery}} — recovery meaning the getting back of health, the return journey of an illness, with its own weather — the valley understood as it understood harvest: a season, not a miracle, to be got through with dinners and patience; to {{refresh}} — to refresh meaning to make new in strength, to restore the spent thing, the body or the mind — was the office of Mrs. Tizzard's tea, administered on the hour and without fee; and the {{fitness}} — fitness being the state of the body equal to its work; and in the modern use, the industry raised upon the getting of it — class that met in the Corn Exchange on Tuesdays was taught by the sergeant's widow to an attendance the chapel envied, on the grounds that she promised them less. The wing was opened by the bishop in the rain, the whole valley attending, under the theory that health is the one luxury it cannot farm for itself; and the plaque, when the crowds had gone, was read by the schoolchildren on their way past, and gave several of them, the doctor said, their first English word of any use: the wing was called Recovery, which the bishop had wanted to call Hope, the board had wanted to call the Memorial Wing, and the doctor had proposed, in the minute book, to call Tuesday — on the grounds that it would then always be nearly here.
tr:
兰普福德县医院为新侧楼发布募捐时，全村如一人般认捐——它的慷慨一向取这个形式——十八个月里募得一笔款子，《信使报》登了数字，医院董事会则在晚宴上复述了十年。医院（hospital，hospital 指专门收治病人、予以照护与治疗之所）于河谷并不陌生：它的热病棚在十字路口立了六十年，建于最后一场伤寒那年，当时县里把每一例传染病都隔离（segregate，segregate 指分开、把一人一物置于其本身之内、与其余隔开）在自家的栅栏后面；这道政令留在河谷记忆里的，与其说是医术，不如说是面包——面包用长竿送到栅栏边，而且老人们至今说，那是县史上最好的面包：钱预付了，吃得心安理得。

侧楼本身是属于外科医生的。接手采石场病例的那位外科医生（surgeon，surgeon 指以刀治病的医生、医学的木匠、从屋子里面修缮屋子的人），在老医院受训，回来时带回新方法与新派头，后者更叫人吃惊；救下最年轻采石工的那台手术（operation，operation 指外科医生在病人身体上施行的工作、以双手与器械完成，病人则蒙恩身在别处）夜里十一点开始，做了四个钟头，教堂的钟一路敲着它——用《信使报》的话说，敲的是那场合的调。至于痛到难忍时医生所下的方子，自战争以来没有变过：吗啡（morphine，morphine 指罂粟的烈药、吊起疼痛、降下旗帜的那种），而它给的宽解（relief，relief 指重负或疼痛的纾解、卸下，哪怕只卸一夜的工夫）——他说——是他包里最老的处方，也是他最不肯轻开的一张。

侧楼教给河谷的词是移植（transplant，transplant 指把活的器官从一个身体挪到另一个身体、此道先驱是肾）。这个词条来自校长家的儿子：他带着一颗坏掉的肾去兰普福德，两年后带着另一个人的肾回来了，此后种地的劲头，他父亲说不知感恩，他祖父说是奇迹。他第一年的理疗（therapy，therapy 指以有章法的手段治疗疾病或虚弱——操练、谈话、敷施），走路、补液、慢慢加码的里程，按药方开出来，也按药吞下去，苦，而且准时；他接受的全部治疗（treatment，treatment 指为一个病人对抗疾病所做的一切、照护之全数），阿南德医生告诉教区会议，是他活下来的原因；痊愈（cure，cure 指恢复健康、疾病就此终结）则是报纸写他的原因；而这一分别，医生说，就是他整个行业的伦理、装在一句话里，为此他谢谢大家。侧楼的册子把新病房每一段都写成有疗效的（curative，curative 指药物或措施有治愈之力的），《信使报》的校对出于迷信统统改成“舒适”，没改成功。

与此同时河谷照旧自行开方，河谷向来如此。家家都存着自家配制的药（remedy，remedy 指治愈的手段；医学之外，指把一件事扳正的任何办法），路数各自不同，捍卫起来各有教义；杂货铺的药（drug，drug 指用于医药的物质；处方之外，也指为处方从不提的理由而服下的那些）柜里摆着合法的那部分，闲话里保管着其余；妇女协会订了一场针灸（acupuncture，acupuncture 指以细针刺入皮肤穴位加以治疗的中国医术）讲座，礼堂提前一个钟头就坐满了，针当场扎在自愿报名的医生身上，医生事后自称说不清地放松（relax，relax 指松开、放下紧张——肌肉的或心里的）了；致谢辞的动议理由是：协会总算请到一位能看穿的讲者。

侧楼给河谷的最后一个词最朴素。康复（recovery，recovery 指健康的复得、疾病归程中自带的天气）这件事，河谷像懂收成一样懂它：是一个季节，不是奇迹，要靠晚饭和耐心熬过去；提神（refresh，refresh 指使气力一新、把耗掉的东西——身体的或心的——补回来）是蒂泽德太太的茶的职责，按钟点施与，分文不取；而在谷交所每逢周二开课的健美（fitness，fitness 指身体堪当其事的状态；今义则指围绕获得它而兴起的一门产业）班，由军士的遗孀执教，上座率高得让礼拜堂眼红——理由是她许诺得少。侧楼落成那天，主教在雨里剪彩，全村到场，依据的理论是：健康是它唯一不能自种的奢侈品。人潮散尽后，铭牌被放学的孩子们一路念过去，据医生说，给了其中几个人平生第一个有用的英语词：楼叫“康复”——主教原想叫它“希望”，董事会原想叫“纪念”，而医生在会议记录里提议叫“星期二”，理由是：这样一来，它永远快要到了。

quiz.q: The hospital was no stranger to the valley — a house set apart for the sick, where they are kept and treated. A hospital is —
o: a ward behind an infectious fence
the surgeon's work upon the body
a house for the sick, kept and treated
quiz.ex: hospital = 医院。be taken to hospital 送医院；hospitality n. 好客（同源词）。

quiz.q: The county had segregated every infectious case behind its own fence — to set apart, to put a thing or a people by itself, away from the rest. To segregate is to —
o: move a living part between bodies
set apart, away from the rest
quiz.ex: segregate = 隔离；分开。segregated schools 种族隔离的学校；segregation n. 隔离。

quiz.q: The wing itself belonged to the surgeon — one who treats by the knife, medicine's carpenter, who repairs the house from inside. A surgeon is —
o: one who treats by the knife
quiz.ex: surgeon = 外科医生。a heart surgeon 心外科医生；surgery n. 外科；手术室。

quiz.q: What he ordered against pain past bearing had not changed since the war: morphine — the strong medicine of the poppy, that lifts the pain and lowers the flag. Morphine is —
o: a means of setting matters right
the poppy's strong medicine for pain
the return journey of an illness
quiz.ex: morphine = 吗啡。be given morphine 注射吗啡；morphine drip 吗啡滴注。

quiz.q: The word the wing taught the valley was transplant — the moving of a living part from one body to another, the kidney being the pioneer. A transplant is —
o: the state of body equal to its work
a living part moved between bodies
quiz.ex: transplant = 移植。a heart transplant 心脏移植；v. 移植；移栽。

quiz.q: The cure was the reason the newspapers wrote about him — the restoration to health, the illness ended. A cure is —
o: the easing of a burden for a night
the care done against an illness
the means, any means, of righting
quiz.ex: cure = 治愈；疗法。a cure for cancer 癌症疗法；curable adj. 可治愈的。

quiz.q: The Women's Institute booked a lecturer in acupuncture — the Chinese art of treating by needles set at points in the skin. Acupuncture is —
o: treatment by needles in the skin
quiz.ex: acupuncture = 针灸。acupuncture points 穴位；acupuncturist n. 针灸师。

quiz.q: The fitness class met in the Corn Exchange on Tuesdays — the state of the body equal to its work; and in the modern use, the industry raised upon the getting of it. Fitness is —
o: the body equal to its work
quiz.ex: fitness = 健康；体能。physical fitness 体能；a fitness centre 健身中心。

title: The Centenary
text:
The bridge was a hundred years old that spring, and the parish, having consulted its ledgers and found the bridge still owed it nothing, resolved to celebrate. The committee of management fell at once into its natural halves: Mrs. Tizzard, {{optimistic}} — optimistic meaning inclined to look on the bright side, expecting the best of a thing — as to weather, funds and human nature, all three; and Bill Skidmore, {{pessimistic}} — pessimistic meaning inclined to expect the worst; hope wearing its waterproof — on the same three subjects, with equal consistency. Between them, and owing to them, the arrangements were complete: she decided what would happen, and he decided what would go wrong, and the event took the average.

The committee itself was a study of the valley's temperaments, which the Mercury catalogued in its report of the first meeting. There was the {{passive}} — passive meaning not acting but acted upon; suffering things to happen rather than doing them — member, who agreed warmly with whoever had spoken last, and was treasured by both halves; the {{enthusiastic}} — enthusiastic meaning full of the god within; hot for a cause, burning for it — one, the Sunday-school teacher, who brought nineteen suggestions to every meeting and grieved visibly over the eighteen; the {{indifferent}} — indifferent meaning without interest or concern, neither caring for a thing nor against it — treasurer, who cared only that the books balanced, and balanced they did; and beyond the committee, the {{apathetic}} — apathetic meaning without feeling either way, the still centre of no opinion — valley at large, which received the first month's labours with the warmth of a fencepost and produced, in total, a {{negligible}} — negligible meaning so small it need not be counted, beneath the arithmetic — sum of four pounds ten.

The month before changed everything, as it always does; and the work of it was the {{usual}} — usual meaning such as is commonly seen or done, of the every day — valley's: bunting measured in furlongs, trestle tables tested for wobble and one condemned, the chapel and the Legion electing their respective queens and neither speaking of it, the Mercury printing the programme twice, once correctly; and the money arrived in the shapes money arrives in, some of it from houses that had promised nothing.

The day itself was Mrs. Tizzard's, the sun having decided as she said it would. What the bridge got was a whole valley's {{happiness}} — happiness being the state of the blessed, the mind at ease and glad of the ease — on its banks: {{delight}} — delight being pleasure taken brightly, the high spirits of a moment — in the morning's races; {{fun}} — fun being play and sport, that which makes the laughter — wherever the children were; a {{joke}} — a joke being a thing said or done for laughter, without malice in it — from the chairman, involving the bridge's age and his own, at which the bridge came off better; {{laughter}} — laughter being the sound and the act of laughing, the body's own applause — from the tea tents to the river by three o'clock; and by evening, when the lamps were lit, something steadier, which was {{joy}} — joy being gladness deep set, of the whole heart and not the moment only —.
